variations.name: Classic Chana Dal Tadka
variations.description: This Classic Chana Dal Tadka is a comforting and protein-rich lentil dish, a staple in Indian households. It features tender split Bengal gram simmered in a fragrant onion-tomato gravy, finished with a sizzling tempering of spices in Anveshan Ghee, offering a harmonious balance of earthy and aromatic flavors.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: For a rich, authentic flavor in the tempering.

steps: Rinse 1 cup of chana dal thoroughly under running water. Soak it in 3 cups of fresh water for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours, to aid in faster cooking and better texture.

Drain the soaked dal and transfer it to a pressure cooker. Add 3 cups of fresh water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 0.5 tsp salt. Pressure cook for 4-5 whistles on medium heat, then let the pressure release naturally. The dal should be soft but still hold its shape.

While the dal cooks, prepare the tempering. Heat 1 tbsp of Anveshan Ghee in a separate pan over medium heat. Add 1 tsp cumin seeds and allow them to crackle for a few seconds until fragrant. Then add 0.25 tsp asafoetida and 2 dried red chillies, sautéing for 10-15 seconds.

Add 4 finely chopped garlic cloves and 1 inch grated ginger to the pan. Sauté for 1 minute until their raw aroma disappears. Next, add 1 finely chopped medium onion and cook until it turns translucent and light golden brown, about 5-7 minutes.

Stir in 1 finely chopped medium tomato and cook until it softens and the oil starts to separate from the mixture, approximately 3-5 minutes. Add 0.75 tsp red chilli powder, 0.5 tsp garam masala, and the remaining 0.5 tsp salt, mixing well and cooking for another minute.

Gently pour the cooked dal into the tempering mixture. Stir everything together, ensuring the spices are well incorporated. Add a little hot water if the dal is too thick, aiming for a creamy, pourable consistency. Simmer for 5-7 minutes on low heat, allowing the flavors to meld.

Garnish with 0.25 cup of freshly chopped coriander leaves. For an extra layer of aroma and richness, heat 1 tbsp of Anveshan Ghee in a small pan until shimmering, then pour it over the dal just before serving.
tips: Soaking the chana dal is crucial for even cooking and a creamy texture. Don't skip this step.
Adjust the consistency of the dal by adding hot water as needed. It should be thick enough to coat a spoon but not overly dense.
For a smoky flavor, you can perform a 'dhungar' by placing a small, hot charcoal piece in a small bowl in the dal, drizzling a few drops of Anveshan Ghee over it, and covering for 2-3 minutes.
This dal tastes even better the next day as the flavors deepen. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with steamed Basmati rice, soft rotis, or flaky parathas. A side of pickled onions or a fresh cucumber salad complements its robust flavors beautifully.

variations.name: Punjabi Chana Dal Tadka
variations.description: Embodying the rich culinary traditions of Punjab, this Chana Dal Tadka is known for its hearty texture and generous use of Anveshan Ghee, culminating in a dish that is both comforting and deeply flavorful. The double tempering adds an extra layer of aromatic spices, making it a true Punjabi delight.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Essential for the rich, nutty flavor characteristic of Punjabi cuisine.

steps: Wash 1 cup of chana dal thoroughly and soak it in water for at least 1 hour. Drain the dal and transfer it to a pressure cooker with 3.5 cups of fresh water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 0.75 tsp salt. Cook for 5-6 whistles on medium heat until the dal is very soft and creamy, then let the pressure release naturally.

For the first tempering, heat 1.5 tbsp of Anveshan Ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Add 1 tsp cumin seeds, 0.25 tsp asafoetida, 1 bay leaf, and 2 slit green chillies. Sauté for about 30 seconds until aromatic.

Add 5 finely chopped garlic cloves and 1.5 inches of grated ginger. Cook until the raw smell disappears, about 1-2 minutes. Then add 1 finely chopped large onion and sauté until it turns golden brown, approximately 7-10 minutes.

Stir in 2 finely chopped medium tomatoes. Cook until they soften completely and the Anveshan Ghee begins to separate from the mixture, about 5-7 minutes. Add 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, and the remaining 0.5 tsp salt. Cook for another 2 minutes, stirring constantly.

Gently add the cooked chana dal to the pan with the tempering. Mix well to combine all ingredients. If the dal is too thick, add a splash of hot water to achieve a desired consistency. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.

For the second, final tempering, heat 1.5 tbsp of Anveshan Ghee in a small separate pan. Add 0.5 tsp cumin seeds and let them crackle. Add 0.75 tsp garam masala and 1 tsp kasoori methi (crushed between your palms) and immediately pour this sizzling tempering over the simmering dal.
Stir the dal gently to incorporate the final tempering. Garnish generously with 0.25 cup of fresh coriander leaves before serving hot.
tips: The double tempering (tadka) is key to Punjabi dal's rich flavor. The first tadka forms the base, while the second adds a fresh burst of aroma just before serving.
Ensure the onions are deeply caramelized for a sweeter, more robust base flavor.
Kasoori Methi (dried fenugreek leaves) adds a distinctive earthy aroma. Don't skip it for an authentic Punjabi taste.
If you prefer a smoother dal, you can lightly mash a portion of the cooked dal with the back of a spoon before adding it to the tempering.
variations.servingSuggestion: This hearty Punjabi Chana Dal Tadka pairs perfectly with Amritsari Kulcha, Garlic Naan, or a simple Jeera Rice. A dollop of fresh yogurt or a wedge of lemon on the side enhances the experience.

variations.name: Bengali Chana Dal Tadka
variations.description: This Bengali Chana Dal Tadka offers a unique sweet and savory flavor profile, distinct from other regional variations. Cooked in pungent Anveshan Mustard Oil and finished with a 'panch phoron' tempering, it's a delightful and aromatic dish often enjoyed during festivals and special occasions.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Provides the characteristic pungent flavor essential to Bengali cuisine.

ingredients.name: Panch Phoron
ingredients.note: A Bengali five-spice blend: cumin, fennel, fenugreek, nigella, mustard seeds.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: Adds a subtle sweetness that balances the spices in Bengali dal.

ingredients.name: Fresh Coconut
ingredients.note: Grated or thinly sliced for garnish.

steps: Wash and soak 1 cup of chana dal for at least 2 hours. Drain and pressure cook with 3.5 cups of water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 0.5 tsp salt for 5-6 whistles until soft but not completely mashed. Allow the pressure to release naturally.

Heat 2 tbsp of Anveshan Mustard Oil in a heavy-bottomed pan or kadai over medium heat until it shimmers and just begins to smoke lightly. Reduce the heat and add 1 tsp panch phoron, 2 dried red chillies, and 1 bay leaf. Let them splutter for about 30 seconds.
Add 1 inch of grated ginger and 2 slit green chillies. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Then, stir in 1 finely chopped medium tomato and cook until it softens and breaks down, about 3-4 minutes.
Add 0.5 tsp cumin powder, 0.5 tsp coriander powder, 0.5 tsp red chilli powder, and the remaining 0.5 tsp salt. Cook the spices for 2 minutes, adding a splash of water if needed to prevent burning.

Gently add the cooked chana dal to the spice mixture. Stir well to combine. Add 1 tsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder, which is traditional in Bengali dal to balance the flavors. Simmer the dal for 7-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the dal to thicken slightly.
Stir in 2 tbsp of grated fresh coconut. Garnish with 0.25 cup of freshly chopped coriander leaves. Serve hot.
tips: The pungent aroma of Anveshan Mustard Oil is crucial for authentic Bengali flavor. Ensure it's heated properly before adding spices.
Panch phoron is a key spice blend for Bengali cuisine. If you don't have it, you can make your own by combining equal parts of cumin, fennel, fenugreek, nigella, and mustard seeds.
The addition of Anveshan Jaggery Powder provides a subtle sweetness that perfectly complements the savory and spicy notes, a hallmark of Bengali dal.
Garnish with fresh coconut for added texture and a mild sweetness that enhances the overall profile of the dish.
variations.servingSuggestion: Enjoy Bengali Chana Dal Tadka with fluffy Luchi (fried bread), plain steamed rice, or even with a simple Pulao. A side of 'bhaja' (fried vegetables) or a wedge of lime makes for a complete meal.

variations.name: Kerala Chana Dal Tadka
variations.description: This Kerala-style Chana Dal Tadka is a delightful blend of earthy lentils and the tropical richness of coconut. Infused with curry leaves and tempered in Anveshan Coconut Oil, it offers a distinct South Indian flavor profile that is both comforting and exotic.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: Imparts an authentic tropical flavor to the dal.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.note: Finely chopped.

ingredients.name: Coconut Milk
ingredients.note: Thin coconut milk.

steps: Rinse 1 cup of chana dal and soak it for 30 minutes. Drain and pressure cook with 3 cups of water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 0.5 tsp salt for 4-5 whistles until tender. Let the pressure release naturally.

Heat 1 tbsp of Anveshan Coconut Oil in a pan over medium heat. Add 1 tsp mustard seeds and let them splutter. Then add 15 curry leaves and 2 dried red chillies, sautéing for a few seconds until fragrant.
Add 0.5 cup of finely chopped shallots, 1 inch of finely chopped ginger, and 2 slit green chillies. Sauté until the shallots turn translucent and light golden, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in 0.25 cup of grated coconut and cook for 2-3 minutes until it releases its aroma and turns slightly golden. This adds a lovely texture and flavor to the dal.

Add the cooked chana dal to the pan. Mix well and incorporate the tempering. Pour in 0.5 cup of thin coconut milk and the remaining 0.5 tsp salt. Bring the dal to a gentle simmer and cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the dal to thicken slightly.
Garnish with 0.25 cup of fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot, enjoying the distinct aroma of Anveshan Coconut Oil and curry leaves.
tips: Using Anveshan Coconut Oil is essential for the authentic taste of Kerala Chana Dal. Do not substitute with other oils.
The addition of shallots instead of regular onions provides a milder, sweeter base, typical in Kerala cuisine.
Freshly grated coconut adds a wonderful texture and enhances the tropical flavor. If fresh is unavailable, unsweetened desiccated coconut can be used, rehydrated slightly.
For a richer dal, you can finish with a drizzle of thick coconut milk just before serving, but ensure it doesn't boil to prevent curdling.
variations.servingSuggestion: This Kerala Chana Dal Tadka is best served with Malabar Parotta, Appam, or plain steamed rice. A side of avial or thoran would complete a traditional Kerala meal.

variations.name: Kashmiri Chana Dal Tadka
variations.description: Inspired by the serene valleys of Kashmir, this Chana Dal Tadka is a luxurious and aromatic dish, distinguished by the delicate floral notes of Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron. It's a milder, richer dal, offering a unique blend of warmth and subtle spice, perfect for a special meal.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Provides a rich, traditional base for the Kashmiri flavors.

ingredients.name: Kashmiri Red Chilli Powder
ingredients.note: For color and mild heat.

ingredients.name: Yogurt
ingredients.note: Whisked.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron
ingredients.note: Infuses the dal with a luxurious aroma and subtle color.

ingredients.name: Milk
ingredients.note: Warm milk for saffron.

steps: Wash and soak 1 cup of chana dal for at least 2 hours. Drain and pressure cook with 3.5 cups of water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 0.5 tsp salt for 5-6 whistles until very tender. Let the pressure release naturally. Lightly mash a portion of the dal for a creamier texture.
In a small bowl, soak 10 strands of Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron in 0.25 cup of warm milk for at least 15 minutes to allow the color and aroma to infuse.

Heat 2 tbsp of Anveshan Ghee in a pan over medium heat. Add 1 tsp cumin seeds, 0.25 tsp asafoetida, 3 green cardamom pods, 1 inch cinnamon stick, and 2 cloves. Sauté for about 30-45 seconds until fragrant.
Reduce heat to low. Add 0.75 tsp ginger powder, 1 tsp fennel powder, and 1 tsp Kashmiri red chilli powder. Stir continuously for 30 seconds to prevent burning, ensuring the spices bloom in the ghee.
Gradually whisk in 0.25 cup of plain yogurt, stirring constantly to prevent curdling. Cook for 2-3 minutes until the yogurt is fully incorporated and the mixture thickens slightly.

Add the cooked and lightly mashed chana dal to the pan. Stir well to combine with the spice mixture. Pour in the saffron-infused milk. Add the remaining 0.5 tsp salt. Simmer gently for 7-10 minutes, allowing the dal to absorb the rich Kashmiri flavors.
Garnish with 2 tbsp of fresh mint leaves, finely chopped. Serve hot.
tips: The use of Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron is the hallmark of this dal. Ensure it's soaked in warm milk to extract its full color and aroma.
Kashmiri cuisine often uses dried ginger (sonth) and fennel (saunf) powder for a distinct flavor. Do not substitute with fresh ginger or whole fennel seeds.
When adding yogurt, ensure it's at room temperature and whisked smoothly. Add it gradually while stirring constantly on low heat to prevent curdling.
For an even richer experience, a pinch of crushed dried rose petals can be added along with the saffron for a more pronounced floral note.
variations.servingSuggestion: This elegant Kashmiri Chana Dal Tadka is best savored with steamed Basmati rice or soft Kashmiri Naan. A side of Raita or a simple green salad provides a refreshing contrast to its rich flavors.

variations.name: Goan Chana Dal Tadka
variations.description: Bringing the vibrant flavors of Goa to your table, this Chana Dal Tadka is a tangy and mildly spicy delight. The unique addition of kokum provides a distinctive sourness, beautifully balanced by the rich, aromatic tempering in Anveshan Coconut Oil, creating a truly coastal experience.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: Essential for the authentic coastal flavor of Goan cuisine.

ingredients.name: Goan Red Chilli Powder
ingredients.note: Or regular red chilli powder.

ingredients.name: Kokum
ingredients.note: Soaked in 2 tbsp warm water.

steps: Rinse 1 cup of chana dal and soak it for 1 hour. Drain and pressure cook with 3.5 cups of water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 0.5 tsp salt for 5-6 whistles until soft. Let the pressure release naturally. Soak 3 pieces of kokum in 2 tbsp warm water for 10 minutes.

Heat 2 tbsp of Anveshan Coconut Oil in a pan over medium heat. Add 1 tsp mustard seeds and let them splutter. Then add 10 curry leaves and 2 dried red chillies, sautéing for a few seconds until aromatic.

Add 1 finely chopped medium onion and cook until it turns translucent, about 4-5 minutes. Then add 3 finely chopped garlic cloves and 0.5 inch of grated ginger. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until their raw smell disappears.

Stir in 1 finely chopped small tomato and cook until it softens, about 2-3 minutes. Add 1 tsp Goan red chilli powder (or regular red chilli powder) and 0.5 tsp coriander powder. Cook the spices for 1 minute, stirring well.

Add the cooked chana dal to the pan. Mix everything thoroughly. Squeeze the soaked kokum to extract its juice and add both the juice and the kokum pieces to the dal. Add the remaining 0.5 tsp salt. Simmer for 7-10 minutes, allowing the dal to absorb the tangy kokum flavor and thicken.
Garnish generously with 0.25 cup of fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot, enjoying the unique sweet and sour notes.
tips: Kokum is the star ingredient for Goan dal, providing a distinct tangy flavor. Do not skip or substitute it.
Anveshan Coconut Oil is crucial for the authentic Goan taste. Its mild sweetness and aroma complement the kokum beautifully.
Adjust the amount of kokum based on your preference for tanginess. Start with a smaller amount and add more if desired.
For a thicker consistency, you can mash a portion of the dal against the side of the pan with the back of your spoon while it simmers.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve this tangy Goan Chana Dal Tadka with steamed rice, Goan Pao (bread), or a simple fish curry for a truly authentic Goan culinary experience.

Add 4 finely minced garlic cloves and 1 finely chopped medium onion to the pan. Sauté until the onion turns translucent and light golden, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in 1 finely chopped medium tomato and 2 slit green chillies. Cook until the tomato softens and the oil begins to separate, approximately 8-10 minutes.
Add 1 tsp red chilli powder and 1.5 tsp coriander powder, cooking for 2 minutes to allow the spices to bloom. Then, add the cooked chana dal to the pan, mixing well.

Add 3 pieces of kokum and 0.5 tsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder to the dal. Bring the dal to a gentle simmer and cook for 7-10 minutes, allowing the kokum to release its tanginess and the flavors to meld. Remove the kokum pieces before serving if preferred.
Garnish generously with 0.25 cup fresh chopped coriander leaves before serving.
tips: Kokum is essential for the authentic Goan tang. If unavailable, a small amount of tamarind paste can be used as a substitute, but adjust the quantity carefully as it is more potent.
Anveshan Wood-Pressed Coconut Oil is crucial for the distinct flavor of this Goan dal. Do not substitute with other oils for an authentic taste.
The jaggery balances the sourness of the kokum and the heat of the chillies. Adjust to your preferred sweet-sour balance.
For an extra layer of flavor, you can add a pinch of asafoetida (hing) to the tempering after the mustard seeds.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve this tangy Goan Chana Dal Fry with steamed rice, pav (Goan bread), or crusty sourdough bread. A simple fish curry or a vegetable stir-fry makes for a complete and satisfying Goan meal.

variations.name: Hyderabadi Chana Dal Fry
variations.description: This Hyderabadi Chana Dal Fry is a rich and aromatic delicacy, reflecting the royal culinary heritage of Hyderabad. It features a creamy dal infused with fragrant whole spices, a touch of mint, and the luxurious essence of Anveshan Pure Kashmiri Saffron, creating a truly opulent and flavorful experience.

ingredients.note: Forms the rich, aromatic base for the Hyderabadi tempering.

steps: Rinse 1 cup of Bengal gram thoroughly and soak it in water for at least 1 hour. Drain the water.

In a pressure cooker, combine the soaked Bengal gram, 3.5 cups of water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 1.25 tsp salt. Pressure cook for 5-6 whistles until the dal is very soft and creamy. Allow the pressure to release naturally.
While the dal cooks, soak 20 strands of Anveshan Pure Kashmiri Saffron in 0.25 cup warm milk and set aside to infuse.

Heat 2 tbsp of Anveshan Ghee in a large pan over medium heat. Add 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 inch cinnamon stick, 3 lightly crushed green cardamom pods, 2 cloves, and 1 bay leaf. Sauté until fragrant, about 45 seconds.
Add 1 thinly sliced large onion and cook until it turns golden brown, approximately 8-10 minutes. Stir in 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and sauté until the raw smell disappears, about 2-3 minutes.

Add 2 pureed medium tomatoes and 3 slit green chillies. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes soften and the Anveshan Ghee separates from the masala, about 10-12 minutes. Stir in 1.5 tsp red chilli powder and 2 tsp coriander powder, cooking for 2 minutes.
Add the cooked chana dal to the masala, mashing some of the dal against the side of the pan to achieve a thicker, creamier consistency. Stir well to combine all ingredients.

Pour in the saffron-infused milk and add 0.25 cup chopped fresh mint leaves. Bring the dal to a gentle simmer, add 0.75 tsp garam masala, and cook for 7-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the saffron aroma to fully develop.
Garnish generously with 0.25 cup fresh chopped coriander leaves before serving.
tips: The quality of Anveshan Pure Kashmiri Saffron is paramount for this dish. Ensure it's authentic for the best aroma and color.
Thinly slicing the onions helps them caramelize evenly, which is crucial for the depth of flavor in Hyderabadi cuisine.
Mint leaves add a unique freshness that distinguishes this dal. Do not omit them for an authentic Hyderabadi touch.
For an even richer experience, you can add a tablespoon of fresh cream or cashew paste at the end of cooking.
variations.servingSuggestion: This regal Hyderabadi Chana Dal Fry is best enjoyed with fragrant basmati rice, biryani, or rich Hyderabadi bread like 'naan' or 'sheermal'. A side of Mirchi ka Salan or Baghare Baingan would complete this royal feast.

variations.name: Classic Chana Dal Home-style
variations.description: This quintessential Chana Dal recipe embodies the comforting flavors of a traditional Indian home-cooked meal. Hearty and wholesome, it features tender Bengal gram simmered in a fragrant onion-tomato gravy, brightened with a simple yet aromatic tempering of Anveshan Ghee and spices. It's a staple that offers warmth and nourishment with every spoonful.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: For a rich, nutty flavor in the tempering.

steps: Rinse 1 cup of Bengal gram thoroughly and soak it in water for at least 30 minutes. Drain the water before cooking.

In a pressure cooker, combine the soaked Bengal gram with 3 cups of fresh water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 0.5 tsp salt. Pressure cook for 4-5 whistles on medium heat until the dal is soft and creamy. Allow the pressure to release naturally.
While the dal cooks, prepare the tempering. Heat 2 tbsp of Anveshan Ghee in a separate pan over medium heat. Once hot, add 1 tsp cumin seeds and let them splutter for a few seconds until fragrant.
Add 4 finely minced garlic cloves to the pan and sauté until light golden. Then, add 1 finely chopped medium onion and cook until translucent and soft, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in 1 finely chopped medium tomato and cook until it softens and the oil begins to separate from the mixture, approximately 5-8 minutes.

Pour the cooked dal into the tempering mixture. Add the remaining 0.5 tsp salt and 0.75 tsp red chilli powder. Mix well and simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the dal to thicken slightly.
Garnish generously with 2 tbsp of freshly chopped coriander. Serve hot.
tips: Soaking the chana dal shortens cooking time and helps it cook more evenly, resulting in a creamier texture.
Adjust the consistency of the dal by adding a little hot water if it's too thick, or simmering longer if it's too thin.
For a smoky flavor, you can add a pinch of asafoetida (hing) to the tempering after the cumin seeds.
Leftover dal can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently, adding a splash of water if needed.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve this comforting Classic Chana Dal Home-style with warm rotis, fluffy basmati rice, or even a side of crisp papad and a dollop of Anveshan Ghee for an extra touch of richness.

variations.name: Punjabi Chana Dal Home-style
variations.description: This Punjabi rendition of Chana Dal is known for its robust flavors and rich, buttery finish. The dal is cooked to perfection and then infused with a generous tempering of aromatic spices, garlic, and ginger, all sautéed in Anveshan Ghee, making it a hearty and satisfying dish that truly represents the culinary spirit of Punjab.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Essential for the authentic rich Punjabi flavor and tempering.

steps: Wash 1 cup of Bengal gram and soak it in water for at least 1 hour. Drain well. In a pressure cooker, combine the soaked dal with 3.5 cups of water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 0.75 tsp salt. Cook for 5-6 whistles on medium heat until the dal is very tender. Let the pressure release naturally, then mash it lightly with a ladle for a creamier texture.
Heat 2 tbsp of Anveshan Ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan or kadai over medium heat. Add 1 tsp cumin seeds and allow them to crackle and become fragrant.
Add 5 finely chopped garlic cloves and 1 inch of grated ginger. Sauté until the raw aroma disappears and they turn light golden, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in 1 finely chopped large onion and 2 slit green chillies. Cook until the onion turns golden brown, which will take about 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add 1 finely chopped large tomato and cook until it breaks down completely and the Anveshan Ghee starts to separate from the mixture, about 7-10 minutes. Mash the tomatoes as they cook.
Mix in 1 tsp red chilli powder and 1 tsp coriander powder. Cook the spices for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.

Transfer the cooked and mashed chana dal into the pan with the tempering. Add the remaining 0.5 tsp salt and 0.5 tsp garam masala. Stir everything together, bring to a gentle simmer, and cook for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the dal to absorb all the rich flavors.
Finish with 1 tbsp of fresh Anveshan Ghee, stirring it in for extra richness, and garnish with 3 tbsp of freshly chopped coriander before serving.
tips: For an even richer Punjabi flavor, a small amount of fresh cream or butter can be stirred in at the very end.
Ensure the onions are deeply caramelized to achieve the characteristic rich brown color and sweet undertone of Punjabi dal.
If the dal becomes too thick upon standing, add a splash of hot water to reach the desired consistency when reheating.
This dal pairs wonderfully with garlic naan or Amritsari kulcha, enhancing the overall Punjabi dining experience.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve the hearty Punjabi Chana Dal Home-style hot with buttered naan, tandoori roti, or jeera rice. A side of pickled onions and a dollop of fresh yogurt complement its robust flavors beautifully.

variations.name: Bengali Chana Dal Home-style
variations.description: This Bengali Chana Dal, or 'Cholar Dal', is a delightful balance of sweet and savory, characterized by the unique aroma of 'panch phoron' and the distinct pungency of Anveshan Mustard Oil. Often sweetened with a touch of Anveshan Jaggery and garnished with fried coconut pieces, it offers a comforting and subtly complex flavor profile that is truly unique to Bengali cuisine.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Essential for the authentic pungent flavor of Bengali cuisine.

ingredients.name: Panch Phoron
ingredients.note: A Bengali five-spice blend.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: Adds a characteristic subtle sweetness to the dal.

steps: Rinse 1 cup of Bengal gram and soak it for at least 30 minutes. Drain. In a pressure cooker, combine the dal with 3 cups of water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 0.5 tsp salt. Pressure cook for 4-5 whistles until tender. Allow pressure to release naturally.
Heat 1 tbsp of Anveshan Mustard Oil in a small pan. Fry 0.25 cup of thinly sliced or grated coconut pieces until golden brown and crisp. Remove and set aside for garnish.
In the same pan, add the remaining 1 tbsp of Anveshan Mustard Oil. Once hot, add 1 tsp panch phoron, 1 bay leaf, and 2 dry red chillies. Let them splutter and release their aroma, about 30 seconds.
Add 1 inch of grated ginger and 2 slit green chillies. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Be careful not to burn the spices.
Pour the cooked chana dal into the pan with the tempering. Add the remaining 0.5 tsp salt and 1 tbsp of Anveshan Jaggery Powder. Stir well to combine all the flavors.
Bring the dal to a gentle simmer and cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing the jaggery to dissolve and the dal to absorb the unique flavors of the tempering. The dal should thicken slightly.
Garnish with the fried coconut pieces and 2 tbsp of freshly chopped coriander. Serve hot.
tips: The distinct flavor of Anveshan Mustard Oil is crucial for authentic Bengali Cholar Dal. Do not substitute it with other oils.
Adjust the amount of Anveshan Jaggery Powder according to your preference for sweetness. Some prefer it sweeter, others just a hint.
For a richer dal, you can add a pinch of asafoetida (hing) to the tempering along with the panch phoron.
Ensure the coconut pieces are fried to a golden crisp for the best texture and flavor in the garnish.
variations.servingSuggestion: Bengali Chana Dal is traditionally served with Luchi (fried puffed bread) or porota (paratha). It also pairs wonderfully with steamed rice and a side of vegetable fritters (bhaja).

variations.name: Gujarati Chana Dal Home-style
variations.description: This Gujarati Chana Dal, often called 'Dal Dhokli', is a delightful blend of sweet, sour, and spicy notes, characteristic of Gujarati cuisine. It features tender chana dal simmered with a unique tempering of curry leaves, mustard seeds, and a touch of Anveshan Jaggery, creating a comforting and flavorful dish that is both light and satisfying.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A traditional oil used in Gujarati cooking for its mild flavor.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: Provides the characteristic sweet note in Gujarati dal.

steps: Rinse 1 cup of Bengal gram and soak it in water for 30 minutes. Drain. In a pressure cooker, combine the dal with 3 cups of water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 0.5 tsp salt. Pressure cook for 4-5 whistles until the dal is soft. Allow the pressure to release naturally, then mash lightly.

Heat 2 tbsp of Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a pan over medium heat. Add 1 tsp mustard seeds and let them splutter. Then add 0.5 tsp cumin seeds and 0.25 tsp asafoetida, allowing them to sizzle for a few seconds.
Add 10 curry leaves, 2 slit green chillies, and 1 inch of grated ginger. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, ensuring the ginger is cooked through.
Stir in 1 finely chopped medium tomato and cook until it softens and the oil begins to separate, about 5-7 minutes. Mash the tomato as it cooks.
Add 0.75 tsp red chilli powder and 1 tsp coriander powder. Cook the spices for 1 minute, stirring continuously, until their raw aroma disappears.
Pour the cooked and mashed chana dal into the tempering. Add the remaining 0.5 tsp salt, 1.5 tbsp of Anveshan Jaggery Powder, and 1 tbsp of lemon juice. Mix everything thoroughly.
Bring the dal to a gentle simmer and cook for 7-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the dal to thicken to your desired consistency. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Garnish with 2 tbsp of freshly chopped coriander and serve hot.
tips: The balance of sweet, sour, and spicy is key in Gujarati dal. Adjust Anveshan Jaggery Powder and lemon juice to your taste.
For a thicker dal, you can add a tablespoon of besan (chickpea flour) to the tempering and roast it for a minute before adding tomatoes.
Consider adding a few pieces of boiled bottle gourd (lauki) along with the dal for added nutrition and a subtle sweetness.
This dal tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to deepen. Store in the refrigerator.
variations.servingSuggestion: Gujarati Chana Dal is best enjoyed with soft rotis, bhakri, or steamed rice. A side of fresh salad or a spoonful of plain yogurt complements its complex flavors.

variations.name: Kerala Chana Dal Home-style
variations.description: This Kerala-style Chana Dal, or 'Kadala Curry', is a rich and aromatic dish, deeply infused with the flavors of coconut and curry leaves. The dal is cooked in a creamy coconut milk base and finished with a vibrant tempering of Anveshan Coconut Oil and traditional spices, offering a taste of South India's coastal culinary heritage.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: Imparts the distinctive tropical flavor to the curry.

steps: Rinse 1 cup of Bengal gram and soak it for at least 30 minutes. Drain. In a pressure cooker, combine the dal with 3 cups of water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 0.5 tsp salt. Pressure cook for 4-5 whistles until the dal is very tender. Allow pressure to release naturally.
Heat 1 tbsp of Anveshan Coconut Oil in a pan over medium heat. Add 1 tsp mustard seeds and let them splutter. Then add 2 dry red chillies and 10 curry leaves, frying them until fragrant.

Add 5 finely chopped shallots, 1 inch of grated ginger, 3 minced garlic cloves, and 2 slit green chillies. Sauté until the shallots turn golden brown and the raw aroma of ginger and garlic disappears, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in 1.5 tsp coriander powder, 0.75 tsp red chilli powder, and 0.5 tsp garam masala. Cook the spices for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant. Be careful not to burn them.
Add the cooked chana dal to the spiced mixture. Pour in 0.75 cup of thick coconut milk and the remaining 0.5 tsp salt. Stir gently to combine.

Bring the curry to a gentle simmer and cook for 7-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly. Do not boil vigorously after adding coconut milk to prevent it from curdling.
Garnish with 2 tbsp of freshly chopped coriander and serve hot.
tips: For an authentic taste, use freshly grated coconut and extract your own thick coconut milk. Canned coconut milk works well too.
Adjust the spice level by increasing or decreasing the green chillies and red chilli powder according to your preference.
If you prefer a smoother consistency, you can blend a small portion of the cooked dal before adding it to the tempering.
This curry can be made ahead of time; the flavors deepen overnight. Reheat gently, adding a splash of water if needed.
variations.servingSuggestion: Kerala Chana Dal is a classic accompaniment to Appam, Dosa, or Idiyappam. It is also delicious with steamed rice or Malabar Parotta for a wholesome meal.

variations.name: Kashmiri Chana Dal Home-style
variations.description: This Kashmiri Chana Dal offers a unique blend of aromatic spices and a touch of luxury with Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron. Unlike other regional dals, it often features a rich, yogurt-based gravy and a distinctive tempering that highlights the delicate fragrance of fennel and ginger, creating a truly exquisite and comforting dish.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Used for tempering, adding a rich, traditional Kashmiri flavor.

ingredients.name: Kashmiri Red Chilli Powder
ingredients.note: For vibrant color and mild heat.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron
ingredients.note: Adds a luxurious aroma and subtle color.

steps: Rinse 1 cup of Bengal gram and soak it for at least 1 hour. Drain. In a pressure cooker, combine the dal with 3.5 cups of water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 0.75 tsp salt. Pressure cook for 5-6 whistles until very tender. Allow pressure to release naturally, then mash lightly.
In a small bowl, steep 5 strands of Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron in 2 tbsp of warm water or milk and set aside.
Heat 2 tbsp of Anveshan Ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Add 1 tsp cumin seeds and 0.5 tsp fennel seeds, letting them splutter and become fragrant for about 30 seconds.
Add 0.5 tsp dry ginger powder (saunth) and 0.25 tsp asafoetida. Sauté for a few seconds until aromatic, being careful not to burn the spices.

Add 1 finely chopped medium onion and cook until golden brown, about 7-10 minutes. Then, add 1 finely chopped medium tomato and cook until it softens and the Anveshan Ghee separates, approximately 5-8 minutes.

Stir in 1 tsp Kashmiri red chilli powder and cook for 30 seconds. Reduce heat to low, then gradually whisk in 0.5 cup of plain yogurt, stirring continuously to prevent curdling. Cook for 2-3 minutes until the gravy thickens slightly.

Add the cooked and mashed chana dal to the pan. Stir in the saffron-infused water/milk and the remaining 0.5 tsp salt. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the dal to absorb the richness of the gravy.
Garnish with 2 tbsp of freshly chopped coriander and serve hot.
tips: Ensure the yogurt is at room temperature and whisked smoothly before adding to the hot pan to prevent it from curdling. Stir continuously until it comes to a simmer.
Kashmiri red chilli powder provides a beautiful color without excessive heat; adjust to your preference.
For an authentic touch, a pinch of shahi jeera (caraway seeds) can be added along with cumin and fennel seeds.
This dal pairs exceptionally well with steamed rice or Kashmiri naan. You can also add a few fried paneer cubes for extra richness.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve Kashmiri Chana Dal hot with steamed basmati rice, traditional Kashmiri bread like lavasa, or soft rotis. A side of pickled vegetables or a simple cucumber raita would complement its rich flavors.

variations.name: Classic Chana Dal Punjabi
variations.description: This classic Punjabi Chana Dal is a hearty and comforting dish, featuring split Bengal gram lentils cooked to perfection and tempered with a fragrant blend of spices. It's known for its rich, creamy texture and robust flavor, making it a staple in North Indian cuisine.

steps: Rinse 1 cup of Chana Dal thoroughly under running water. Soak the dal in 3 cups of water for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2 hours, to reduce cooking time and aid digestion.

Drain the soaked dal and transfer it to a pressure cooker. Add 3 cups of fresh water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 1 tsp salt. Pressure cook for 4-5 whistles on medium-high heat, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes. Allow the pressure to release naturally. The dal should be soft but still hold its shape.

While the dal is cooking, prepare the tempering. Heat 2 tbsp of Anveshan Ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan or kadai over medium heat. Once hot, add 1 tsp cumin seeds and let them splutter for a few seconds until fragrant.

Add 1 medium finely chopped onion to the pan and sauté until it turns golden brown, about 5-7 minutes. Then, add 1 tbsp minced garlic and 1 tbsp grated ginger, cooking for another minute until their raw aroma disappears.

Stir in 2 medium finely chopped tomatoes and cook until they soften and the oil begins to separate, approximately 5-7 minutes. Add 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, and the remaining 0.5 tsp salt. Sauté the spices for 1-2 minutes, adding a splash of water if needed to prevent burning.

Gently mash a small portion of the cooked dal to thicken the gravy, then add the cooked dal to the tempering mixture. Mix well and bring to a gentle simmer. Add 0.5 tsp garam masala and 1 tsp crushed Kasuri Methi, stirring to combine.
Simmer the dal for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Adjust consistency by adding a little hot water if it's too thick. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Garnish generously with 2 tbsp fresh chopped coriander before serving.
tips: Soaking the chana dal is crucial for even cooking and a creamier texture. Don't skip this step!
For a richer flavor, you can add a pinch of asafoetida (hing) to the Anveshan Ghee after the cumin seeds splutter.
If the dal becomes too thick after resting, simply add a little hot water and bring it to a simmer before serving.

To enhance the smoky flavor, you can do a dhungar (smoke infusion) by placing a small bowl with a burning charcoal in the dal, drizzling a few drops of Anveshan Ghee over it, and covering immediately for 2-3 minutes.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve this aromatic Classic Chana Dal Punjabi hot with fluffy steamed basmati rice, warm rotis, or flaky parathas. A side of pickled onions and a dollop of Anveshan Ghee can elevate the experience.

variations.name: Gujarati Chana Dal Punjabi with Anveshan Jaggery
variations.description: This Gujarati Chana Dal offers a distinctive sweet, sour, and spicy flavor profile, a hallmark of Gujarati cuisine. The addition of Anveshan Jaggery and a hint of tamarind creates a complex and incredibly satisfying dal that is both comforting and vibrant.

Stir in 1 tsp red chilli powder and 1 tsp coriander powder. Cook for 30 seconds, adding a splash of water if the spices stick to the pan.
Add the cooked chana dal to the tempering. Mix well. Stir in 2 tbsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder, 1 tbsp tamarind pulp, and 1.5 tsp salt. Bring the dal to a gentle boil.

ingredients.name: Fresh Coriander
ingredients.note: chopped, for garnish

steps: Soak 1 cup of Chana Dal for at least 2 hours, then drain. Pressure cook the dal with 3.5 cups of fresh water and 0.5 tsp turmeric powder for 5-6 whistles until it's very tender. Lightly mash a portion of the dal for a thicker consistency.
In a small bowl, soak 10 strands of Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron in 0.25 cup warm milk for at least 15 minutes to infuse its color and aroma.

Heat 2 tbsp of Anveshan Ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Add 1 tsp cumin seeds, 3 lightly crushed green cardamom pods, a 1-inch cinnamon stick, and 2 cloves. Sauté for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add 1 medium finely chopped onion and cook until translucent, about 4-5 minutes. Then, add 1 tbsp ginger paste and 1 tbsp garlic paste, cooking for another 2 minutes until the raw smell disappears.
Stir in 0.5 cup tomato puree, 1.5 tsp Kashmiri red chilli powder, and 1 tsp coriander powder. Cook the masala for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the ghee separates from the sides.
Add the cooked chana dal and 1.5 tsp salt to the pan. Mix well and bring to a gentle simmer. Pour in the saffron-infused milk, stirring gently to combine.
Simmer the dal for 8-10 minutes, allowing the saffron to fully permeate the dish and the flavors to deepen. Adjust the consistency with hot water if necessary.
Garnish generously with 1 tbsp blanched and slivered almonds, 1 tbsp raisins, and 1 tbsp fresh chopped coriander before serving.
tips: Always soak Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron in warm milk or water to extract maximum color and flavor. Never add it directly to hot oil.
For an even richer dal, you can add a tablespoon of fresh cream or cashew paste at the end of cooking.
The use of Kashmiri red chilli powder is key for a vibrant color without excessive heat, characteristic of Kashmiri cuisine.
Ensure the whole spices are gently tempered to release their aromas without burning, which can make the dal bitter.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve this exquisite Kashmiri Chana Dal with fragrant basmati rice, soft naan, or kulcha. A side of Raita (yogurt dip) or a light salad would complement its rich flavors beautifully.

variations.name: Andhra Chana Dal Punjabi with Guntur Red Chilli
variations.description: This Andhra-style Chana Dal is a fiery and tangy delight, characterized by the intense heat of Guntur red chillies and the bright tang of tamarind. It's a robust and flavorful dal that awakens the palate, offering a true taste of Andhra's bold culinary traditions.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A neutral oil perfect for tempering and highlighting the bold spices.

ingredients.name: Guntur Red Chillies
ingredients.note: whole, for intense heat

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.note: finely chopped

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.note: minced

ingredients.name: Tomato
ingredients.note: finely chopped

ingredients.name: Tamarind Pulp
ingredients.note: or to taste

ingredients.name: Fresh Coriander
ingredients.note: chopped, for garnish

steps: Wash 1 cup of Chana Dal thoroughly and soak in water for at least 2 hours. Drain and pressure cook with 3 cups of fresh water and 0.5 tsp turmeric powder for 4-5 whistles until soft. Mash the dal lightly to achieve a slightly coarse consistency.

Heat 2 tbsp of Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a pan over medium heat. Add 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp cumin seeds, and 1 tsp urad dal. Let them splutter and the urad dal turn light golden, about 30-45 seconds.
Add 0.25 tsp asafoetida, 4 whole Guntur red chillies, and 15 curry leaves. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant and the chillies darken slightly.
Add 1 medium finely chopped onion and cook until it turns translucent, about 4-5 minutes. Then, add 1 tbsp minced garlic and sauté for another minute until the raw smell disappears.
Stir in 1 medium finely chopped tomato and cook until it softens and the oil begins to separate, approximately 5-7 minutes. Add 1 tsp red chilli powder and 1.5 tsp salt. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the cooked chana dal and 1.5 tbsp tamarind pulp to the pan. Mix well and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 8-10 minutes, allowing the dal to absorb the tangy and spicy flavors.
Adjust the consistency by adding a little hot water if needed, and taste to adjust the salt and tanginess. Garnish with 2 tbsp fresh chopped coriander before serving.
tips: Guntur red chillies are very potent; adjust the quantity according to your spice preference. For less heat, deseed them.
The urad dal in the tempering adds a lovely crunch and nutty flavor, characteristic of South Indian tadka.
Fresh curry leaves are essential for the authentic Andhra flavor profile. Do not substitute with dried ones if possible.
If you prefer a smoother dal, blend a portion of the cooked dal before adding it to the tempering.
variations.servingSuggestion: This spicy Andhra Chana Dal pairs perfectly with hot steamed rice, dosa, or idli. A dollop of Anveshan Ghee on top and a side of crisp papad or a cooling yogurt raita would complete the meal.

variations.name: Goan Chana Dal Punjabi with Kokum
variations.description: This Goan Chana Dal offers a delightful blend of tanginess from kokum and a subtle sweetness, balanced with aromatic spices. It's a unique take on chana dal, reflecting Goan culinary influences with its bright, refreshing flavors and creamy texture.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: Imparts a distinct tropical aroma and flavor, authentic to Goan cuisine.

ingredients.name: Green Chillies
ingredients.note: slit

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.note: finely chopped

ingredients.name: Tomato
ingredients.note: finely chopped

ingredients.name: Kokum
ingredients.note: dried, soaked in 0.25 cup warm water for 10 minutes

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: Adds a subtle sweetness to balance the tang of kokum.

ingredients.name: Fresh Coriander
ingredients.note: chopped, for garnish

steps: Rinse 1 cup of Chana Dal and soak in water for at least 2 hours. Drain and pressure cook with 3 cups of fresh water and 0.5 tsp turmeric powder for 4-5 whistles until tender. Lightly mash the dal.
Soak 3 pieces of dried kokum in 0.25 cup warm water for 10 minutes. Squeeze the kokum to extract its juice and discard the solids.

Heat 2 tbsp of Anveshan Coconut Oil in a pan over medium heat. Add 1 tsp mustard seeds and 1 tsp cumin seeds, letting them splutter. Add 0.25 tsp asafoetida, 10 curry leaves, and 2 slit green chillies. Sauté for 30 seconds.
Add 1 medium finely chopped onion and cook until translucent, about 4-5 minutes. Then, add 1 tbsp ginger paste and 1 tbsp garlic paste, cooking for another 2 minutes until aromatic.
Stir in 1 medium finely chopped tomato and cook until it softens, about 5-7 minutes. Add 1 tsp red chilli powder and 1.5 tsp salt. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the cooked chana dal to the pan. Pour in the kokum extract and 1 tsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder. Mix everything well and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer the dal for 8-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the dal to thicken slightly. Adjust the consistency with hot water if needed, and taste to balance the sweet and tangy notes.
Garnish with 2 tbsp fresh chopped coriander before serving.
tips: Kokum provides a unique sourness and a beautiful purplish hue. Adjust the quantity based on your preference for tanginess.
Anveshan Coconut Oil is crucial for the authentic Goan flavor. Do not substitute it with other oils if you want the true taste.
For a thicker consistency, you can blend a small portion of the dal before adding it to the tempering.
The subtle sweetness from Anveshan Jaggery Powder balances the tartness of the kokum perfectly.
variations.servingSuggestion: This tangy Goan Chana Dal is best served with steamed rice, Goan pav, or crusty bread. A side of fish curry or a simple vegetable stir-fry would complement this dal wonderfully.

variations.name: Classic Chana Dal Dhaba-style
variations.description: Experience the quintessential taste of Indian highway dhabas with this robust Chana Dal. This hearty, protein-rich lentil preparation, slow-cooked to perfection and finished with a fragrant tempering, embodies comfort food at its best, perfect for a satisfying meal.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Bilona Ghee
ingredients.note: For authentic dhaba flavor and richness.

steps: Rinse 1 cup Chana Dal thoroughly and soak it in water for at least 30 minutes. Drain the water and transfer the dal to a pressure cooker. Add 3 cups fresh water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 0.5 tsp salt. Pressure cook for 4-5 whistles or until the dal is tender yet retains its shape.
While the dal is cooking, prepare the tempering. Finely chop 1 medium onion, mince 2 cloves garlic, and grate 1 inch ginger. Dice 1 medium tomato.

Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Bilona Ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Add 1 tsp cumin seeds and let them splutter. Then add the minced garlic and grated ginger, sautéing until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add the chopped onion to the pan and cook until it turns golden brown, approximately 5-7 minutes. Stir in the diced tomato and cook until it softens and the oil begins to separate, about 5 minutes.
Now, add 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1.5 tsp coriander powder, and the remaining 0.5 tsp salt. Sauté the spices for 1 minute, adding a splash of water if needed to prevent burning.
Gently mash the cooked dal slightly with the back of a spoon to achieve a creamy consistency, leaving some dal grains intact for texture. Pour the cooked dal into the tempering mixture and mix well.
Add 0.5 tsp garam masala and 1 tsp Kasuri Methi, crushed between your palms, to the dal. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Adjust consistency by adding hot water if desired.
Garnish generously with 2 tbsp fresh coriander leaves before serving.
tips: Soaking the chana dal is crucial for even cooking and reducing cooking time. For best results, soak for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours.
Adjust the consistency of the dal by adding hot water as needed. Some prefer a thicker dal, while others like it slightly runnier.

For a smoky dhaba flavor, you can perform a 'dhungar' by placing a small piece of burning charcoal in a small bowl in the dal, drizzling a few drops of Anveshan Bilona Ghee over it, and covering the pan for 2-3 minutes.
This dal tastes even better the next day as the flavors deepen. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve this Classic Chana Dal Dhaba-style hot with fluffy steamed basmati rice, warm rotis, or flaky parathas. A side of pickled onions and a dollop of fresh yogurt complements the rich flavors beautifully.

variations.name: Lauki Chana Dal Dhaba-style (Haryana)
variations.description: A delightful Haryanvi take on Chana Dal, this version incorporates the subtle sweetness and healthy goodness of bottle gourd (lauki). It's a lighter yet equally flavorful variation, perfect for those seeking a nutritious and comforting lentil dish with a unique vegetable twist.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Bilona Ghee
ingredients.note: For a rich, authentic Haryanvi tempering.

steps: Soak 1 cup Chana Dal for at least 30 minutes, then drain. Peel and dice 1.5 cups lauki into 1-inch cubes. In a pressure cooker, combine the soaked dal, lauki, 3.5 cups water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 0.75 tsp salt. Pressure cook for 5-6 whistles or until both the dal and lauki are very soft.
While the dal cooks, prepare the tempering. Finely chop 1 medium onion, dice 1 large tomato, and slit 2 green chillies. Keep 1 tsp garlic paste and 1 tsp ginger paste ready.

Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Bilona Ghee in a separate pan over medium heat. Add 1 tsp cumin seeds and 0.25 tsp asafoetida. Once the cumin seeds splutter, add the chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 4-5 minutes.

Stir in the garlic paste, ginger paste, and slit green chillies. Cook for 1-2 minutes until the raw aroma disappears. Add the diced tomato and cook until it breaks down and releases its juices, about 6-8 minutes.
Add 1 tsp red chilli powder, 2 tsp coriander powder, and the remaining 0.5 tsp salt to the tomato mixture. Sauté the spices for 2 minutes on low heat, ensuring they don't burn.

Once the pressure cooker cools, open it and gently mash the dal and lauki mixture with a ladle to create a slightly chunky consistency. Transfer this cooked dal and lauki into the tempering pan, mixing thoroughly.
Add 0.75 tsp garam masala and 1 tsp Kasuri Methi, crushed, to the dal. Simmer the mixture for 7-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the dal to thicken slightly.
Garnish generously with 3 tbsp fresh coriander leaves and serve hot.
tips: Ensure the lauki is tender and not bitter. Taste a small piece before adding it to the dal.
For a creamier texture, you can blend a small portion of the cooked dal and lauki before combining it with the tempering.
Adjust the spice level by increasing or decreasing the green chillies and red chilli powder according to your preference.
A final drizzle of Anveshan Bilona Ghee just before serving enhances the dhaba-style richness.
variations.servingSuggestion: Lauki Chana Dal Dhaba-style pairs wonderfully with bajra roti (pearl millet flatbread) or makki di roti (cornmeal flatbread), typical Haryanvi accompaniments. It also tastes great with plain rice or whole wheat chapatis.

variations.name: Bengali Chana Dal Dhaba-style (West Bengal)
variations.description: This Bengali-style Chana Dal is a sweet and savory delight, distinctively flavored with Anveshan Wood-Pressed Mustard Oil and a hint of jaggery. It's a rich, aromatic dal, often served during festive occasions, offering a unique blend of textures and tastes that truly stands out.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Wood-Pressed Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Essential for the pungent, authentic Bengali flavor.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: Adds a characteristic subtle sweetness to balance the spices.

ingredients.name: Fresh Coconut
ingredients.note: Grated or thinly sliced

steps: Rinse 1 cup Chana Dal and soak for 30 minutes. Drain and pressure cook with 3 cups water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 0.5 tsp salt for 4-5 whistles until tender but not mushy.

Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Wood-Pressed Mustard Oil in a kadai or heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat until it just begins to smoke. Reduce heat and add 1 bay leaf, 2 dry red chillies, and 1 tsp panch phoron. Let them splutter for about 30 seconds.
Add 1.5 tsp ginger paste and 2 slit green chillies. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in 1 small finely chopped tomato and cook until it softens, about 3-4 minutes.
Add 1 tsp cumin powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, and the remaining 0.5 tsp salt. Sauté the spices for 2 minutes on low heat, adding a tablespoon of water if needed to prevent sticking.
Pour the cooked chana dal into the spiced mixture. Add 1 tsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder and 0.5 tsp garam masala. Mix well and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add 2 tbsp grated or thinly sliced fresh coconut to the dal. Cook for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the dal to thicken slightly to your desired consistency.
Garnish with 2 tbsp fresh coriander leaves before serving.
tips: The use of Anveshan Wood-Pressed Mustard Oil is key to the authentic Bengali flavor. Do not substitute it with other oils for this variation.
Adjust the sweetness by adding more or less Anveshan Jaggery Powder according to your preference.
For an extra layer of flavor, you can lightly toast the fresh coconut before adding it to the dal.
Panch phoron is a Bengali five-spice blend consisting of fenugreek, nigella, cumin, black mustard, and fennel seeds. Do not skip this for the authentic taste.
variations.servingSuggestion: Bengali Chana Dal Dhaba-style is traditionally enjoyed with luchi (deep-fried puffed bread), porota, or steamed rice. It also makes a wonderful accompaniment to kachoris or radhaballabhis.

variations.name: Goan Chana Dal Dhaba-style (Goa)
variations.description: This Goan Chana Dal offers a vibrant, tangy, and subtly spicy flavor profile, characteristic of coastal cuisine. The inclusion of kokum provides a distinctive sour note that beautifully balances the richness of the dal and spices, creating a truly unique and refreshing experience.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Wood-Pressed Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: Imparts an authentic Goan aroma and flavor.

ingredients.name: Kokum
ingredients.note: Dried kokum, soaked in warm water for 10 minutes

steps: Rinse 1 cup Chana Dal and soak for 30 minutes. Drain and pressure cook with 3 cups water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 0.5 tsp salt for 4-5 whistles until tender. Soak 3 pieces of kokum in warm water for 10 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Wood-Pressed Coconut Oil in a pan over medium heat. Add 1 tsp mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add 10 curry leaves and sauté for a few seconds until aromatic.
Add 1 finely chopped medium onion and cook until it turns translucent, about 5 minutes. Add 3 minced garlic cloves and 2 slit green chillies, sautéing for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in 1 finely chopped medium tomato and cook until it softens and the oil begins to separate, about 5-7 minutes.
Add 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1.5 tsp coriander powder, and the remaining 0.5 tsp salt. Sauté the spices for 1-2 minutes on low heat.
Drain the soaked kokum and add it to the tempering. Pour the cooked chana dal into the pan, mixing well. Bring the dal to a gentle simmer.
Add 0.5 tsp garam masala and simmer for 7-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to infuse and the dal to reach a desired consistency. Add a little hot water if the dal becomes too thick.
Garnish with 2 tbsp fresh coriander leaves before serving.
tips: The tanginess from kokum is a signature Goan flavor. Adjust the quantity of kokum based on your preference for sourness.
Anveshan Wood-Pressed Coconut Oil is crucial for the authentic Goan taste. Do not substitute it with other oils.
For a richer flavor, you can add a tablespoon of fresh grated coconut along with the kokum in step 6.
If you don't have kokum, a small amount of tamarind paste can be used as a substitute, but the flavor profile will be slightly different.
variations.servingSuggestion: Goan Chana Dal Dhaba-style is best served with steamed rice, pav (Goan bread), or a simple fish curry for a complete coastal meal. A fresh salad on the side would also be a great addition.

variations.name: Kashmiri Chana Dal Dhaba-style (Jammu & Kashmir)
variations.description: This exquisite Kashmiri Chana Dal is a fragrant and subtly spiced dish, elevated by the luxurious aroma and color of Anveshan Pure Kashmiri Saffron. It's a milder, more aromatic interpretation, offering a delicate balance of flavors that reflect the rich culinary heritage of Kashmir.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Bilona Ghee
ingredients.note: Provides a rich base for the delicate Kashmiri spices.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Pure Kashmiri Saffron
ingredients.note: Infuses a unique aroma, color, and regal touch.

steps: Rinse 1 cup Chana Dal and soak for 30 minutes. Drain and pressure cook with 3 cups water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 0.5 tsp salt for 4-5 whistles until tender. Soak 10 strands of Anveshan Pure Kashmiri Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk or water.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Bilona Ghee in a pan over medium heat. Add 1 tsp cumin seeds and 0.25 tsp asafoetida. Let them splutter for a few seconds.
Add 1 small finely chopped onion and sauté until light golden, about 4-5 minutes. Stir in 1 tsp garlic paste and 1 tsp ginger paste, cooking until the raw smell disappears, about 1 minute.

Add 1 tbsp tomato paste and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly. Then add 1.5 tsp Kashmiri red chilli powder, 1 tsp fennel powder, 0.5 tsp dry ginger powder, and the remaining 0.5 tsp salt. Sauté the spices for 2 minutes on low heat, adding a splash of water if needed.
Pour the cooked chana dal into the spiced mixture. Add the soaked Anveshan Pure Kashmiri Saffron along with its liquid. Mix gently.

Add 0.25 tsp green cardamom powder. Bring the dal to a gentle simmer and cook for 7-10 minutes, allowing the saffron and other spices to infuse thoroughly. Adjust consistency with hot water if necessary.
Garnish with 2 tbsp fresh coriander leaves before serving.
tips: Anveshan Pure Kashmiri Saffron is the star ingredient here; ensure it's of good quality for the best aroma and color.
Kashmiri cuisine often uses less onion and garlic compared to other regions, focusing on aromatic spices. Do not overpower with too much onion.
For an even richer flavor, you can add a pinch of dried mint powder (pudina powder) along with the other dry spices.
This dal is traditionally milder in heat. Adjust Kashmiri red chilli powder for color rather than extreme spiciness.
variations.servingSuggestion: Kashmiri Chana Dal Dhaba-style is best served with steamed basmati rice, Kashmiri naan, or a simple tandoori roti. A side of cucumber raita would provide a cooling contrast.

variations.name: Malwa Chana Dal Dhaba-style (Madhya Pradesh)
variations.description: Hailing from the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh, this Chana Dal is characterized by its nutty flavor and crunchy texture, thanks to the addition of roasted peanuts. It's a hearty and unique variation, offering a delightful contrast of soft dal with the bite of peanuts, making it a truly satisfying meal.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Complements the nutty flavor of the peanuts and is traditional to the region.

ingredients.name: Roasted Peanuts
ingredients.note: Roughly crushed

steps: Rinse 1 cup Chana Dal and soak for 30 minutes. Drain and pressure cook with 3 cups water, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 0.5 tsp salt for 4-5 whistles until tender. Roughly crush 0.25 cup roasted peanuts.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil in a pan over medium heat. Add 1 tsp cumin seeds, 0.5 tsp mustard seeds, and 0.25 tsp asafoetida. Let them splutter for about 30 seconds.
Add 1 finely chopped medium onion and sauté until golden brown, about 5-7 minutes. Add 2 minced garlic cloves and 1 inch grated ginger, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in 1 finely chopped medium tomato and cook until it softens and the oil separates, about 5-7 minutes.
Add 1.5 tsp red chilli powder and 1.5 tsp coriander powder, and the remaining 0.5 tsp salt. Sauté the spices for 2 minutes on low heat, adding a splash of water if needed to prevent burning.
Add the roughly crushed roasted peanuts to the tempering and cook for 2 minutes, allowing them to absorb the flavors. Then, pour in the cooked chana dal and mix well.
Add 0.5 tsp garam masala and 1 tsp Kasuri Methi, crushed between your palms. Simmer the dal for 7-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the dal to thicken to your desired consistency.
Garnish generously with 2 tbsp fresh coriander leaves before serving.
tips: The roasted peanuts are the signature of this Malwa dal. Ensure they are fresh and crunchy for the best texture.
Anveshan Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil enhances the nutty profile of the dish. Avoid using oils with strong competing flavors.
If you prefer a smoother texture, you can lightly mash a portion of the dal before adding it to the tempering.
For an extra kick, you can add a pinch of goda masala (Maharashtrian spice blend) along with the garam masala, though not strictly traditional Malwa, it complements the nutty flavor.
variations.servingSuggestion: Malwa Chana Dal Dhaba-style is delicious with hot phulkas, missi roti (chickpea flour flatbread), or steamed rice. A side of fresh onion salad with a squeeze of lemon would be a perfect accompaniment.

variations.name: Classic Aloo Paratha
variations.description: The quintessential Indian flatbread, Aloo Paratha features a delightful potato filling encased in a soft, whole wheat dough. This classic version celebrates the simple, comforting flavors of spiced mashed potatoes, making it a beloved breakfast or meal across India.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: For a nutritious and wholesome dough with a unique texture.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: For a rich, aromatic dough and perfectly cooked parathas.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.note: Boiled and mashed until smooth.

ingredients.name: Cumin Powder
ingredients.note: Roasted and ground for enhanced flavor.

ingredients.name: Fresh Coriander Leaves
ingredients.note: Finely chopped.

steps: In a large bowl, combine 2 cups of Anveshan Khapli Atta with 0.5 tsp salt. Gradually add 1 cup of water and 1 tbsp of Anveshan Ghee, kneading for 8-10 minutes until a soft, pliable, and non-sticky dough forms. Cover with a damp cloth and let it rest for at least 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, prepare the filling. Peel and mash the 3 medium boiled potatoes thoroughly, ensuring no lumps remain. Add 0.5 tsp salt, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, and 2 tbsp finely chopped fresh coriander leaves to the mashed potatoes. Mix well to combine all the spices evenly.
Divide the rested dough into 8 equal portions. Roll each portion into a smooth ball. Flatten a dough ball slightly with your palm and create a small well in the center using your thumb.

Place about 2 tablespoons of the potato filling into the well. Carefully bring the edges of the dough together over the filling, sealing it completely to form a smooth ball again. Gently flatten the stuffed ball.

Dust the stuffed dough ball lightly with Anveshan Khapli Atta and roll it out gently into a 6-7 inch diameter circle using a rolling pin, applying even pressure to prevent the filling from tearing through.
Heat a tava (griddle) over medium-high heat. Once hot, place the rolled paratha onto the tava. Cook for about 1 minute until small bubbles appear on the surface.
Flip the paratha. Brush the cooked side generously with 0.5 tsp of Anveshan Ghee. Cook for another minute, then flip again and brush the second side with 0.5 tsp of Anveshan Ghee.
Press gently with a spatula, cooking each side until golden-brown spots appear and the paratha is cooked through, about 2-3 minutes per side. Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.
Serve the Classic Aloo Paratha hot, fresh off the tava.
tips: Ensure your mashed potatoes are completely lump-free for a smooth filling that won't tear the dough during rolling.
Don't overfill the parathas; too much filling makes them difficult to roll without tearing. Start with less and adjust as you gain experience.
Resting the dough is crucial for a soft, elastic texture, making it easier to roll and preventing it from shrinking back.
Cook parathas on medium-high heat. If the heat is too low, they will become dry and hard; if too high, they will burn before cooking through.
variations.servingSuggestion: Pair this comforting Classic Aloo Paratha with a dollop of fresh curd, a tangy mango pickle, or a side of homemade mint chutney for a complete and satisfying meal.

variations.name: Punjabi Aloo Paratha
variations.description: Hailing from the heart of Punjab, this Aloo Paratha is renowned for its generous, robustly spiced potato filling and its signature finish with a generous pat of white butter. It's a hearty and flavourful flatbread, embodying the rich culinary traditions of the region.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: For a wholesome and authentic Punjabi paratha base.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: To achieve a soft dough and crisp, golden parathas.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.note: Boiled, peeled, and finely mashed.

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.note: Finely chopped.

ingredients.name: Green Chillies
ingredients.note: Finely chopped, adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.note: Grated.

ingredients.name: Cumin Powder
ingredients.note: Roasted and ground.

ingredients.name: Amchur Powder (Dry Mango Powder)
ingredients.note: For a tangy note.

ingredients.name: Fresh Coriander Leaves
ingredients.note: Finely chopped.

ingredients.name: White Butter
ingredients.note: For serving.

steps: Prepare the dough by combining 2 cups of Anveshan Khapli Atta with 0.5 tsp salt. Gradually add 1 cup of water and 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, kneading thoroughly for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and let it rest for 20 minutes.

For the filling, mash 4 medium boiled potatoes completely. In a separate pan, heat 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee, then sauté 0.5 medium finely chopped onion, 2 finely chopped green chillies, and 1 tsp grated ginger until the onion turns translucent, about 3-4 minutes.

Add the sautéed mixture to the mashed potatoes. Stir in 1 tsp salt, 1.5 tsp red chilli powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, and 0.5 tsp amchur powder. Mix well, then fold in 3 tbsp finely chopped fresh coriander leaves.

Divide the dough into 8 equal portions. Take one portion, flatten it, and create a cup shape. Place 2-3 tablespoons of the potato filling inside, then carefully seal the edges to form a ball. Gently flatten the ball.
Dust the stuffed dough ball with Anveshan Khapli Atta and roll it into a 7-inch diameter circle, ensuring the filling is evenly distributed without tearing the dough.
Heat a tava over medium-high heat. Place the rolled paratha on the hot tava. Cook for about 1 minute until small bubbles appear on the surface.
Flip the paratha. Drizzle 0.5 tsp of Anveshan Ghee around the edges and brush lightly over the surface. Cook for another 1-2 minutes, then flip again and apply another 0.5 tsp Anveshan Ghee.
Press gently with a spatula, cooking until both sides are golden brown and crisp. Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.
Serve each Punjabi Aloo Paratha immediately, topped with a generous dollop of white butter.
tips: The key to a good Punjabi Aloo Paratha is a flavourful, slightly chunky filling. Don't mash the potatoes too finely; a little texture adds to the experience.
Adding finely chopped onions and ginger to the filling provides an extra layer of crunch and pungency, characteristic of Punjabi cuisine.
Ensure your tava is hot enough before placing the paratha to achieve a crisp exterior without making it dry.
For the best flavour, always serve Punjabi Aloo Paratha hot with plenty of white butter, which melts into the warm paratha.
variations.servingSuggestion: Enjoy Punjabi Aloo Paratha with a side of homemade dahi (yogurt), a spicy green chilli pickle, and a tall glass of chilled lassi for an authentic Punjabi breakfast experience.

variations.name: Maharashtrian Aloo Paratha
variations.description: This Maharashtrian take on Aloo Paratha introduces the distinctive warmth and complexity of Goda Masala into its potato filling, offering a unique aromatic profile. It's a comforting and subtly spiced flatbread, reflecting the culinary nuances of Maharashtra.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: For a wholesome and traditional Maharashtrian paratha dough.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee

steps: In a bowl, combine 2 cups of Anveshan Khapli Atta with 0.5 tsp salt. Gradually add 1 cup of water and 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, kneading until a soft, pliable dough is formed (about 8-10 minutes). Cover and let it rest for 15-20 minutes.

Heat 1 tsp Anveshan Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add 0.5 tsp mustard seeds and 0.5 tsp cumin seeds; let them splutter. Add 5 curry leaves, 1 finely chopped green chilli, and 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste, sautéing until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Add the tempered spices to the 3 medium mashed potatoes. Incorporate 0.5 tsp salt, 0.25 tsp turmeric powder, and 1.5 tsp Goda Masala. Mix thoroughly to ensure the spices are well distributed. Fold in 2 tbsp finely chopped fresh coriander leaves.

Divide the dough into 8 equal portions. Take one portion, flatten it slightly, and create a small depression in the center. Fill with 2 tablespoons of the potato mixture, then carefully bring the edges of the dough together to seal.
Dust the stuffed dough ball lightly with Anveshan Khapli Atta and gently roll it out into a 6-7 inch round paratha, applying even pressure.
Heat a tava on medium-high heat. Place the rolled paratha on the hot tava and cook for about 1 minute until small bubbles appear.
Flip the paratha. Brush the cooked side with 0.5 tsp Anveshan Ghee. Cook for another 1-2 minutes, then flip again and brush the second side with 0.5 tsp Anveshan Ghee.
Press gently with a spatula, cooking each side until golden-brown spots appear and the paratha is cooked through. Repeat for the remaining parathas.
Serve the Maharashtrian Aloo Paratha hot.
tips: Goda Masala is the heart of this recipe; ensure it's fresh and aromatic for the best flavour. If unavailable, a good quality garam masala can be a substitute, though the flavour profile will differ.
Tempering the spices in Anveshan Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil before adding to the potatoes enhances their aroma and infuses the filling with a deeper flavour.
To prevent the parathas from becoming soggy, ensure the potato filling is dry and not watery.
For a softer texture, cover the cooked parathas in a clean kitchen towel as you cook the remaining ones.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve Maharashtrian Aloo Paratha with a side of fresh dahi (yogurt) or a spicy Maharashtrian 'thecha' (chilli garlic chutney) for an authentic regional experience.

Add the tempered spices to the 3 medium mashed potatoes. Stir in 0.5 tsp salt, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, and 1 tsp roasted cumin powder. Mix well to combine all ingredients evenly. Finally, fold in 2 tbsp finely chopped fresh coriander leaves.

steps: Steep 10 strands of Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk for at least 15 minutes to allow the colour and flavour to infuse.

In a large bowl, combine 2 cups of Anveshan Khapli Atta with 0.5 tsp salt. Gradually add 1 cup of water and 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, kneading for 8-10 minutes until a soft, pliable dough forms. Cover and let it rest for 15 minutes.

In a separate bowl, combine the 3 medium mashed potatoes with 0.5 tsp salt, 1 tsp fennel powder, 0.5 tsp dry ginger powder, and 0.25 tsp green cardamom powder. Add the saffron-infused milk to the potato mixture and mix gently until well combined. Fold in 1 tbsp finely chopped fresh mint leaves.
Divide the rested dough into 8 equal portions. Roll each portion into a smooth ball. Flatten a dough ball slightly with your palm and create a small well in the center.

Place about 2 tablespoons of the potato-saffron filling into the well. Carefully bring the edges of the dough together over the filling, sealing it completely to form a smooth ball again. Gently flatten the stuffed ball.
Dust the stuffed dough ball lightly with Anveshan Khapli Atta and roll it out gently into a 6-7 inch diameter circle using a rolling pin, applying even pressure.
Heat a tava (griddle) over medium-high heat. Once hot, place the rolled paratha onto the tava. Cook for about 1 minute until small bubbles appear on the surface.
Flip the paratha. Brush the cooked side generously with 0.5 tsp of Anveshan Ghee. Cook for another minute, then flip again and brush the second side with 0.5 tsp of Anveshan Ghee.
Press gently with a spatula, cooking each side until golden-brown spots appear and the paratha is cooked through, about 2-3 minutes per side. Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.
Serve the Kashmiri Aloo Paratha hot.
tips: Always steep Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron in warm milk for sufficient time to extract its full colour and aroma. Avoid boiling it directly.
The spices in Kashmiri cuisine are often subtle. Do not overpower the delicate saffron flavour with too much chilli or strong spices.
Ensure the potato filling is completely cooled before stuffing to prevent the dough from tearing during rolling.
For an extra touch of richness, you can add a pinch of Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron directly to the dough mixture along with the Ghee.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve Kashmiri Aloo Paratha with a side of plain yogurt, a mild Raita, or a simple Kashmiri pickle to complement its subtle, aromatic flavours.

Press gently with a spatula, cooking each side until golden-brown spots appear and the paratha is cooked through, about 2-3 minutes per side. Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.

steps: In a large bowl, combine 2 cups of Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tsp salt and 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee. Gradually add 1 cup of water, kneading until a soft, pliable dough forms. Cover and let it rest for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil 3 medium potatoes until tender. Peel and mash them thoroughly in a bowl, ensuring no large lumps remain.
Heat 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee in a small pan over medium heat. Add 1 tsp cumin seeds and let them splutter for 30 seconds. Add the bloomed cumin seeds to the mashed potatoes.

To the mashed potatoes, add 1 tsp coriander powder, 1/2 tsp garam masala, 1/4 tsp turmeric powder, 1/2 tsp red chilli powder, and salt to taste. Mix in 2 tbsp chopped fresh coriander leaves. Combine everything well to create a uniform filling.

Divide the dough into 8 equal portions. Take one portion, flatten it slightly, and place about 2 tablespoons of the potato filling in the center. Bring the edges of the dough together to seal the filling inside, forming a smooth ball.
Lightly dust your work surface with Anveshan Khapli Atta. Gently roll out each stuffed dough ball into a round paratha, about 6-7 inches in diameter, ensuring even thickness.
Heat a tawa (griddle) over medium-high heat. Place a rolled paratha on the hot tawa. Cook for about 1 minute until small bubbles appear.

Flip the paratha and brush 1/2 tsp Anveshan Ghee on the cooked side. Cook for another minute, then flip again and brush 1/2 tsp Anveshan Ghee on the other side. Press gently with a spatula, cooking each side until golden-brown spots appear and the paratha is cooked through, approximately 2-3 minutes per side.
Repeat with the remaining dough and filling. Serve hot.
tips: Ensure the potato filling is completely cooled before stuffing; warm filling can make the dough sticky and difficult to roll.
For perfectly soft parathas, do not over-knead the dough. A soft, elastic dough is key.
If the filling is too moist, add a tablespoon of roasted besan (chickpea flour) to absorb excess moisture.
To prevent tearing, roll the parathas gently from the center outwards, applying even pressure.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve Classic Masala Aloo Paratha hot with a dollop of Anveshan Ghee, a side of plain yogurt, and your favorite mango pickle for a complete meal.
