tips: Bhut jolokia heat blooms about ten seconds after the bite; warn guests before they take a confident second mouthful.
No ghost pepper available? Two bird's-eye chillies plus a pinch of smoked paprika approximate the flavour at half the danger.
Lemon juice at the end is essential; its acidity brightens the pepper's fruitiness that heat alone hides.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a pool of thick, cold curd and cucumber batons; a side of jaggery cubes is the traditional Assamese emergency exit.

variations.name: Rajasthani Spicy Gobi Paratha
variations.description: Whole Mathania-style dried chillies, soaked and ground with garlic, are cooked down in ghee before coating the gobi, delivering the deep, sun-baked heat Jodhpur is famous for. Amchur and fennel steady the fire with sourness and sweetness in true desert proportion.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: A resilient emmer dough built for Rajasthan's boldest chilli paste

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Frying the red chilli paste in bilona ghee mellows it into a rounded desert warmth

steps: Soak 5 dried red chillies in hot water for 20 minutes until pliable, then grind them with 8 garlic cloves and 1 tbsp of the soaking water into a thick crimson paste.
Grate 1 medium cauliflower finely, salt with 1 tsp salt for 15 minutes, and squeeze the shreds firmly dry in a cloth.
Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and about 3/4 cup water for 8 minutes into a pliant dough; rest it 15 minutes.

Heat 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a kadhai on medium, crackle 1 tsp fennel seeds for 20 seconds, then fry the chilli-garlic paste, stirring, until the ghee beads at the edges and the raw smell fades, about 4 minutes.

Fold the squeezed gobi into the cooked paste with 1 tsp amchur powder, 1/4 tsp turmeric powder and 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, toss off the heat for 1 minute, then cool and finish with 2 tbsp chopped coriander.

Stuff 8 dough balls with 2 tbsp of red-coated gobi apiece, roll into 6- to 7-inch rounds, and roast on a medium tava with 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee per side until crusty, spotted and fragrant, about 2 minutes per side.
tips: The chilli paste must fry until ghee separates; that visual cue marks the difference between raw-hot and warm-hot.
Fennel crackled first sweetens the entire filling; grinding it into the paste instead makes it disappear.
For milder colour-rich results, use Kashmiri dried chillies for three of the five.
variations.servingSuggestion: Present with lasan ki chutney for the fearless, a katori of thick dahi for everyone else, and hot ginger tea in winter.

variations.name: Tamil Spicy Gobi Paratha
variations.description: Heat here comes the Chettinad way, from freshly cracked black pepper and dried chillies bloomed with curry leaves and fennel in gingelly oil. The pepper's sharp, resinous burn is quicker and cleaner than chilli powder, fading fast so the cauliflower's sweetness returns between bites.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Emmer wheat mirrors the wholegrain instincts of old Tamil kitchens

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sesame Oil
ingredients.note: Wood-pressed nallennai gives the peppery filling its Chettinad-style toasted base

steps: Grate 1 medium cauliflower coarsely into about 3 cups of shreds; the pan will handle the moisture, so skip the salting.
Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil and nearly 3/4 cup water for 8 minutes to a smooth, elastic dough; rest 15 minutes.
Crush 1.5 tsp black peppercorns in a mortar until coarsely cracked, keeping visible pieces for the signature Chettinad bite.

Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil on medium, crackle 1/2 tsp fennel seeds and 2 torn dried red chillies for 30 seconds, then add 15 curry leaves, 5 sliced shallots and 1 inch minced ginger and fry until the shallots colour, about 2 minutes.
Add the gobi with 1/2 tsp turmeric powder and 1/2 tsp salt and stir-fry for 6 minutes until dry and tender, then work in the cracked pepper off the heat and cool the filling completely.

Fill 8 dough balls with 2 tbsp of pepper-gobi each, roll softly to 7-inch rounds and roast on a medium tava with 1 tsp Anveshan Sesame Oil per side until crisp-edged and freckled deep gold, about 2 minutes per side.
tips: Add the cracked pepper only after the pan is off the flame; frying pepper long turns its heat bitter and flat.
Shallots, not onions, are worth the extra peeling here; their sweetness against the pepper defines the Chettinad balance.
Grind pepper fresh for this recipe; pre-ground powder has already lost the citrusy top notes that make it sing.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with coconut chutney and sambar for dunking, or roll it around a spoon of podi mixed with gingelly oil for a lunchbox version.

variations.name: Classic Stuffed Aloo Paratha
variations.description: The archetype of North Indian comfort food: a soft khapli-atta shell hiding a generous heart of spiced potato, roasted slowly in bilona ghee until the surface crackles. Balanced rather than fiery, this is the everyday version made in millions of homes each morning.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Khapli wheat's fine bran keeps this everyday paratha tender enough for children and elders alike

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: The caramel notes of bilona ghee are what make a plain aloo paratha taste festive

steps: Boil 4 medium potatoes in salted water for roughly 15 minutes until a knife meets no resistance, then drain, peel while warm and mash to a smooth, dry consistency.

Rub 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee into 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt, then knead in about 3/4 cup water over 8 minutes until you have a soft, satiny dough; cover with a damp cloth and rest for 15 minutes.

Season the mash with 1 finely chopped small onion, 2 minced green chillies, 1 inch grated ginger, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 3/4 tsp red chilli powder, 1/4 tsp turmeric powder, 1/2 tsp salt and 3 tbsp chopped coriander, mixing until every streak of yellow disappears into an even colour.
Divide dough and filling into 8 portions each; press a dough ball into a small bowl shape, spoon in 2 tbsp of filling, draw the edges up over the top and twist off the excess dough to seal.
Flatten each stuffed ball, dust with dry Anveshan Khapli Atta and roll outward from the centre into a 7-inch circle, easing pressure near the edges so the potato layer stays even.

Roast on a medium-hot tava about 90 seconds until the underside speckles, flip, brush 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee across the top, flip again and press gently with a folded cloth until both sides are crisp and golden-brown, around 2 minutes per side.
tips: Squeeze the chopped onion in your fist before adding it to the mash; removing its juice stops the filling from turning watery as it sits.
Rest the rolled parathas no more than a couple of minutes before cooking or the potato moisture starts softening the dough.
For extra-flaky results, cook on medium heat only; a scorching tava browns the outside before the layers cook through.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve stacked with a bowl of sweetened dahi, tangy aam ka achaar and a hot cup of adrak chai for the full North Indian breakfast ritual.

variations.name: Kashmiri Stuffed Aloo Paratha
variations.description: Borrowing its perfume from the Kashmiri wazwan, this paratha seasons the potato with saunf powder, sonth and a saffron-milk soak that stains the filling a pale gold. It is gentle, warming and aromatic, closer to a dum aloo in spirit than to a fiery Punjabi stuffing.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The soft emmer crumb is a natural partner for Kashmir's delicate fennel-and-saffron spicing

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Kashmiri cooking blooms its gentle spices in ghee, and bilona ghee makes them sing

ingredients.name: Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron
ingredients.note: GI-tagged Pampore saffron tints the filling gold and adds its honeyed mountain aroma

steps: Steep 10 strands of Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk and set aside for 15 minutes until the milk blushes deep amber.
Boil 4 medium potatoes for about 15 minutes until soft through the centre, then peel and mash them silky-smooth while hot.
Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and near 3/4 cup water for 8 minutes into a soft, elastic dough and rest it, covered, for 15 minutes.

Warm 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on low heat, stir in 1.5 tsp fennel seed powder, 1 tsp dry ginger powder and 1 tsp Kashmiri red chilli powder for just 20 seconds until fragrant, then pour this spiced ghee over the mash.
Add the saffron milk, 1/4 tsp green cardamom powder, 1/2 tsp salt and 2 tbsp chopped coriander to the potatoes and fold gently until the filling is a uniform pale gold with a heady fennel scent.

Encase 2 tbsp of filling inside each of 8 dough balls, roll carefully to 6- or 7-inch rounds, and roast on a medium tava with 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee per side until softly blistered and golden, about 2 minutes per side.
tips: Powdered spices scorch in seconds, so bloom them in ghee off a low flame and pour immediately over the potatoes.
Crush the saffron strands lightly between your fingers before steeping to release twice the colour into the milk.
This mild filling suits saffron's subtlety; resist adding garam masala, which would bury the fennel-cardamom perfume.
variations.servingSuggestion: Lovely with a bowl of plain curd and a cup of kahwa; for a fuller Kashmiri table, add a spoonful of walnut chutney on the side.

variations.name: Gujarati Stuffed Aloo Paratha
variations.description: In true Kathiawadi spirit this filling walks the sweet-spicy-tangy tightrope: jaggery powder melts into the hot mash alongside green chilli, lemon and toasted sesame. The result eats like a cross between an aloo paratha and a vaghareli khichdi topping, sweet at first bite with heat trailing after.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Khapli's nuttiness deepens the sweet-savoury Kathiawadi flavour balance

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Gujarati theplas and parathas alike get their gloss from a patient ghee roast

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: Chemical-free jaggery powder dissolves into the warm mash for the classic Gujarati sweet note

steps: Boil 4 medium potatoes until yielding, about 15 minutes, then peel and mash them thoroughly while piping hot; the residual heat is needed to melt the jaggery evenly in a later step.
Knead a soft dough from 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and approximately 3/4 cup water, working it for 8 minutes; rest it for 15 minutes under a damp cloth.
Dry-toast 1 tbsp white sesame seeds on a low flame until they turn pale gold and begin to jump in the pan, about 2 minutes, and tip them straight onto the mash.

While the mash is still hot, add 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder, 3 finely chopped green chillies, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric powder, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1/2 tsp salt and 3 tbsp coriander, mixing until the jaggery melts in with no gritty specks.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and fill each with 2 tbsp of the sweet-spicy potato mixture; seal tightly and roll to 7-inch rounds with gentle, even pressure.
Cook on a medium tava, flipping once the base is speckled and then glossing each side with 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee, until both faces show honey-brown patches, around 2 minutes per side.
tips: Taste the filling after mixing; the sweet-sour-hot balance should tug in all three directions, so adjust lemon or chilli before stuffing.
Jaggery makes the crust brown faster, so hold the tava at medium and watch the second side closely.
These keep soft for a full day, making them the best travel paratha in this collection, exactly as Gujarati train food traditions intend.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with chhundo or a bowl of plain dahi and papad; a side of masala chaas turns it into a proper Kathiawadi lunch.

variations.name: Karnataka Stuffed Aloo Paratha
variations.description: This filling is a nod to the potato palya inside a Mysore masala dosa, brightened with a spoon of tamarind and a curry-leaf tempering in groundnut oil. Tangy, mildly sweet and studded with softened onions, it tastes unmistakably of a Bengaluru darshini in paratha form.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Emmer wheat gives this dosa-inspired stuffing a wholesome wholegrain wrapper

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Wood-pressed groundnut oil is the workhorse fat of Karnataka kitchens and crisps the crust beautifully

steps: Boil 4 medium potatoes for around 15 minutes until soft, then peel and break them into a chunky crumble; the palya texture should hold small pieces, not a paste.
Make the dough with 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and roughly 3/4 cup water, kneading 8 minutes to a supple finish; rest for 15 minutes.

Heat 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil on medium, fry 1 tbsp chana dal until golden and nutty, about 90 seconds, then add 12 curry leaves, 3 slit green chillies and 1 inch chopped ginger and sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add 1 sliced medium onion and cook until soft and translucent with browned edges, about 3 minutes, then stir in 1/2 tsp turmeric powder followed by the crumbled potatoes.
Season with 2 tsp tamarind paste and 1/2 tsp salt, fold everything together over low heat for 2 minutes so the tang seeps through, then cool the filling completely before stuffing.

Stuff 8 dough balls with 2 tbsp of palya each, roll softly into 7-inch rounds without pressing the onion chunks through, and toast on a medium tava with 1 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil per side until crisp-edged and golden, about 2 minutes a side.
tips: Cool the filling fully; a warm onion palya steams inside the dough and makes rolling a sticky ordeal.
The chana dal should be truly golden before anything else enters the pan, or it stays hard inside the soft potato.
A pinch of sugar is a very Bengaluru touch if your tamarind is especially sharp.
variations.servingSuggestion: Present with coconut chutney and a small tumbler of strong filter coffee; it also pairs surprisingly well with Mysore-style red chutney spread thinly on top.

variations.name: Malwa Stuffed Aloo Paratha
variations.description: From the poha-and-sev belt of Indore comes this crunchy take, where coarsely crushed roasted peanuts and sev-style seasonings join the potato mash. The peanut crunch against the soft mash is pure Malwa street-food logic, finished with a squeeze of lime and plenty of coriander.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The rustic khapli flavour suits Malwa's earthy peanut-and-potato pairing

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Cooking a peanut-studded filling in wood-pressed groundnut oil doubles down on the nutty Malwa character

steps: Boil 4 medium potatoes for about 15 minutes until tender, drain well, peel and mash them coarsely so a few pea-sized pieces remain for bite.
Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and close to 3/4 cup water into a soft, springy dough over 8 minutes, then let it rest for 15 minutes.
Pulse or pound 1/2 cup roasted peanuts into a coarse rubble, keeping some halves intact; avoid grinding to a powder, which would turn pasty inside the filling.

Warm 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil over medium heat, fry 3 chopped green chillies for 30 seconds, then add 1/2 tsp turmeric powder and immediately tip in the mashed potatoes, stirring for 2 minutes to dry the mixture slightly.

Off the heat, mix in the crushed peanuts, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1/2 tsp fennel seed powder, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp lime juice and 4 tbsp chopped coriander until the filling is speckled generously with nuts.

Fill 8 dough balls with 2 tbsp each of the peanut-potato mixture, roll to 7-inch rounds with a gentle touch so the nut pieces do not pierce through, and roast on a medium tava with 1 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil per side until crunchy and browned, about 2 minutes per side.
tips: Rub the roasted peanuts in a kitchen towel first to shed their papery skins, which otherwise scatter through the filling.
Drying the mash briefly in the pan keeps the lime juice from making the filling wet and hard to seal.
Swap a quarter of the peanuts with roasted daliya for a lighter crunch that children usually prefer.
variations.servingSuggestion: Do as Indore does: serve with hot jeeravan-dusted curd, a handful of nylon sev on top and cutting chai alongside.

variations.name: Classic Cheesy Beetroot Paratha
variations.description: A kid-favourite pink paratha where sautéed spiced beetroot meets a molten core of grated cheese inside a wholesome khapli wheat crust. The trick is chilling the cheese-beet filling briefly so it stays put while rolling, then roasting in ghee until the cheese just begins to ooze at the edges.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Fibre-rich emmer wheat balances the richness of the cheese, making this indulgence a genuinely wholesome breakfast

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee-roasting browns the crust before the cheese overheats, so the core stays stretchy instead of oily

steps: Knead 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and about 1 cup water into a soft, elastic dough; rest it covered for 15 minutes so it rolls without springing back.
Grate 2 medium peeled beetroots finely and wring them out in a clean cloth until barely a drop of juice remains, since cheese will loosen the filling further as it melts.

Warm 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on medium heat, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds for 30 seconds, add 1 inch grated ginger, then the beetroot with 1/2 tsp red chilli powder, 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt. Sauté 5 to 6 minutes until completely dry and cool it fully.
Fold 1 cup grated mozzarella, 1/2 tsp black pepper and 2 tbsp chopped coriander into the cooled beetroot, then refrigerate the filling for 10 minutes so the cheese firms up for easy stuffing.
Split the dough into 8 balls, open each into a small bowl shape and pack in 2 tbsp of the chilled cheesy filling, pinching the seam shut and flattening gently.
Roll each stuffed ball into a 6 inch round with light strokes; stop the moment you see pink shadowing through the dough so the cheese cannot leak.

Roast on a medium-hot tava, about 2 minutes per side with the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee brushed on, until golden spots form and the paratha feels springy where the cheese has melted. Serve straight off the tava.
tips: Chill the cheese-beet filling before stuffing; warm mozzarella smears and rips the dough as you roll.
Keep the tava at medium rather than high so the cheese melts fully before the crust over-browns.
Cut into wedges pizza-style for kids so the molten pink centre shows and cools faster.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with a garlicky tomato ketchup or mint-yogurt dip; the parathas are richest in the first five minutes while the cheese is still stretchy.

variations.name: Punjabi Cheesy Beetroot Paratha
variations.description: Amritsar's paneer-stuffed kulcha spirit meets a cheesy beet filling, punched up with ajwain, crushed kasuri methi and a finishing knob of white butter. It is rolled thick, roasted hard in ghee, and eaten with the unapologetic generosity of a Punjabi breakfast table.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The sturdy khapli crumb shoulders this heavy cheese filling the way a tandoori kulcha would

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Only a hard ghee-roast gets the crackly, blistered shell Punjabis demand before the butter goes on

steps: Work 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and 1/2 tsp salt into 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta, then knead with about 1 cup water for 5 minutes into a smooth dough and rest it for 20 minutes.

Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pan on medium, sizzle 1/2 tsp ajwain for 30 seconds, then add 2 medium grated and squeezed beetroots with 3/4 tsp red chilli powder and 1/2 tsp salt and fry for 6 minutes until dry. Cool completely.
Crumble 1/2 cup paneer and grate 3/4 cup processed cheese into the cooled beet, then rub in 1 tbsp kasuri methi between your palms and 1/2 tsp garam masala until evenly mixed.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and the filling into 8 portions of about 2.5 tbsp each. Stuff, seal with a firm twist at the top, and flatten each ball with your palm.
Roll to a thick 6 inch round, keeping the pressure at the rim so the centre stays cushioned and the cheese cannot break through.
Roast on a medium-high tava for close to 2.5 minutes a side, spooning on the remaining 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, until the crust turns deep brown and crisp at the edges.
Top each hot paratha with 1/2 tbsp white butter and serve immediately while the cheese core is still molten.
tips: Use half paneer and half cheese as listed; all cheese turns greasy on a hot tava while paneer keeps the filling plush.
Rub the kasuri methi between your palms before adding to wake up its aroma.
If serving a crowd, keep roasted parathas wrapped in a cloth-lined casserole and butter them only at the table.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with sweet mango pickle and a tall glass of sweet lassi; the tang of the pickle cuts straight through the double dose of dairy.

variations.name: Tamil Cheesy Beetroot Paratha
variations.description: Borrowing from Chennai's beetroot poriyal, the filling here carries crackled mustard, urad dal, curry leaves and black pepper folded through cheese and beets sautéed in wood-pressed sesame oil. The result is a paratha with the deep nutty perfume of a Tamil tiffin griddle.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The wheat's earthy depth stands up to gingelly oil the way a Tamil kal dosa batter does

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sesame Oil
ingredients.note: Wood-pressed gingelly oil is the traditional Tamil griddle fat and gives the crust its tiffin-shop aroma

steps: Knead 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil and about 1 cup water until soft and stretchy, then rest the dough for 15 minutes under a damp cloth.
Heat the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil on medium, pop 1 tsp mustard seeds fully, then add 1 tsp urad dal and fry for about 1 minute until the dal turns biscuit gold.

Add 12 curry leaves and 2 chopped green chillies, sizzle for 20 seconds, then tip in 2 medium grated and squeezed beetroots with 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt and sauté for 6 minutes until dry. Cool the mixture fully.
Fold in 1 cup grated mozzarella and 3/4 tsp black pepper powder, pressing the filling into a firm mass, and chill it for 10 minutes so it stuffs cleanly.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, stuff each with 2 tbsp of filling, seal well and roll gently to a 6 inch round without pressing the centre.
Roast each paratha on a medium tava for around 2 minutes per side, drizzling a few drops of sesame oil around the rim, until the crust shows toasty brown patches and smells nutty.
tips: Let the urad dal reach a proper golden colour before the beets go in; underdone dal tastes chalky in the filling.
Black pepper, not chilli powder, carries the heat here; grind it fresh for the sharpest bite against the cheese.
A teaspoon of the tempering oil brushed on the finished paratha revives the curry-leaf aroma just before serving.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with coconut chutney and a small tumbler of sweet filter-coffee style milk for the kids; the pairing turns it into a full Chennai tiffin.

variations.name: Rajasthani Cheesy Beetroot Paratha
variations.description: Fiery Mathania-style dried red chillies are bloomed whole in ghee and crushed through the beet-cheese filling, balanced by coriander seeds and a whisper of amchur. It is a desert-state paratha: bold, dry-spiced and built to be eaten with cooling curd.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Hardy khapli wheat mirrors the rustic bajra-and-wheat rotis of Rajasthani thalis while staying soft around the cheese

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: In Rajasthan ghee is the measure of hospitality; it blooms the dried chillies and bastes the crust

steps: Make a soft dough from 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and about 1 cup water, kneading for 5 minutes, and rest it for 15 minutes.

Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on medium, fry 4 whole dried red chillies, 1.5 tsp coriander seeds and 1/2 tsp fennel seeds for about 1 minute until the chillies puff and darken slightly, then lift them out and crush coarsely in a mortar.

In the same ghee, sauté 2 medium grated and squeezed beetroots with 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt for 6 minutes on medium heat until dry, then stir in the crushed chilli-spice mixture and 1/2 tsp amchur and cool completely.
Mix 1 cup grated processed cheese and 2 tbsp chopped coriander into the cooled filling and squeeze it into 8 compact portions of roughly 2 tbsp each.
Stuff 8 dough balls with the portions, twist off the seams, and roll each into a 6 inch round on a floured board with gentle, outward strokes.
Roast on a medium-hot tava, about 2 minutes per side with the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, until the surface blisters deep brown and the chilli aroma lifts off the pan.
tips: Bloom the dried chillies whole and crush them after; adding chilli powder instead flattens the smoky flavour this take depends on.
Deseed two of the four chillies if serving children; the fennel will still carry the Rajasthani character.
This paratha keeps well for travel since the dry filling will not sog the crust, a genuine marwari lunchbox trait.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a big bowl of whisked salted curd and lehsun ki chutney on the side; the cold curd is the intended firewall against the Mathania heat.

variations.name: Gujarati Cheesy Beetroot Paratha
variations.description: In true Gujarati fashion this paratha rides the sweet-spicy line: jaggery powder melts into the beet filling against green chilli and ginger, while cheese pulls it all into a gooey centre. Sesame seeds pressed onto the crust give it the look and crunch of a festive thepla.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Khapli's faint natural sweetness meets the jaggery halfway, keeping this Gujarati take from tasting sugary

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A ghee-basted crust is what separates a festive Gujarati paratha from an everyday thepla

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: Chemical-free jaggery powder dissolves evenly through the hot beets, giving the classic Gujarati gol note without grit

steps: Knead 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and close to 1 cup water into a soft dough; rest 15 minutes while you cook the filling.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on medium and sauté 1 inch grated ginger and 3 minced green chillies for 1 minute until fragrant but not browned.

Add 2 medium grated, well-squeezed beetroots, 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt and cook for 6 minutes until the moisture is gone, then stir in 1 tbsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder and 1 tsp roasted cumin powder and cook 1 more minute until the jaggery melts and glazes the beets. Cool completely.
Fold 1 cup grated mozzarella into the cooled sweet-spicy beets and divide into 8 portions of about 2 tbsp each.
Stuff 8 dough balls, seal firmly, then press the top of each stuffed disc into 2 tbsp sesame seeds so they stud one face before rolling gently to 6 inches.
Roast sesame-side down first on a medium tava for about 2 minutes, flip, brush with the remaining 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and cook 2 minutes more until both sides are golden and the seeds smell toasted.
tips: Add the jaggery powder off the highest heat; if it caramelises hard it will turn the filling chewy instead of glossy.
Press the sesame side down first so the seeds set into the crust and do not scatter on flipping.
These reheat surprisingly well on a dry tava the next morning, making them ideal for Gujarati-style travel nashta.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with chhundo or a mild mango pickle and a small bowl of masala chaas; the sweet pickle doubles down on the jaggery in the best way.

variations.name: Classic Cheesy Carrot Paratha
variations.description: A kid-favourite fusion where sweet sautéed carrot meets a molten pull of grated cheese inside a wholegrain khapli crust. The carrot is cooked bone-dry first so the cheese stays gooey instead of leaking, and a hint of black pepper keeps it from tasting like dessert. Ghee-roasted until the surface blisters, it slices like a stuffed quesadilla.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Fibre-rich emmer wheat balances the indulgent cheese pull

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Roasting in bilona ghee browns the crust before the cheese can leak

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and about 3/4 cup water to a soft, smooth dough; it should not stick to your fingers. Rest under a damp cloth for 20 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on medium, crackle 3/4 tsp cumin seeds for 30 seconds, add 1 inch grated ginger, then 1 1/2 cups grated carrot with 1/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp turmeric.
Sauté the carrot for 6 minutes on medium-high, stirring, until every trace of moisture is gone; any dampness will make the cheese ooze out on the tava. Cool the mixture completely, about 10 minutes.
Toss the cooled carrot with 1 cup grated cheese, 1/2 tsp crushed pepper, 1/2 tsp chilli flakes and 2 tbsp chopped coriander until evenly combined.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, cup each and fill with 2 tbsp of the carrot-cheese mix. Pinch the seams shut firmly, flatten and roll gently into 6-inch rounds without pressing the centre.

Cook on a medium-hot tava for about 1 minute per side until spotted, then brush both sides with the remaining 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and roast 30 to 40 seconds per side until golden-crisp and the middle feels soft when pressed, a sign the cheese has melted.
tips: Mix the cheese into the carrot only after the mixture is fully cool, or it will clump and tear the dough.
Serve within 5 minutes of cooking; the cheese pull is at its dramatic best while piping hot.
For a sharper flavour, swap a third of the mozzarella for grated cheddar.
variations.servingSuggestion: Cut into wedges pizza-style and serve with tomato-garlic chutney or ketchup for kids; adults enjoy it with mint chutney and masala chai.

variations.name: Punjabi Cheesy Carrot Paratha
variations.description: Punjab meets the cheese counter: the filling gains golden fried onion, ajwain-scented dough and a bold garam masala kick, and the finished paratha gets the customary knob of white butter melting over its ghee-crisped crust. Richer and spicier than the classic, it eats like a full dhaba meal.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Hearty stone-ground atta carries the heavy cheese-onion filling without sogging

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Layered in the dough, the bhuna and the tava roast, dhaba style

steps: Work 1/2 tsp crushed ajwain, 1/2 tsp salt and 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee into 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta, then knead with about 3/4 cup water for 5 minutes to a supple dough. Rest for 20 minutes under a damp towel.
Fry 1 finely chopped medium onion in 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on medium flame for 4 minutes until golden at the edges, then add 2 minced green chillies and stir for 30 seconds.

Add 1 1/2 cups grated carrot and 1/4 tsp salt and bhuno on medium-high for 5 to 6 minutes until the pan looks dry and the carrot deepens in colour. Season with 3/4 tsp garam masala, 1/2 tsp red chilli powder and 1 tbsp crushed kasuri methi, then cool fully.
Fold 1 cup grated cheese through the cooled masala carrot so every strand is coated in spice.
Divide the dough into 8 portions, stuff each with a generous 2 tbsp of filling, seal the pleats and flatten. Roll into thick 6-inch rounds, rotating after every few strokes for an even disc.
Roast on a hot tava about 1 minute per side, then spoon 1/2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee around each paratha and fry 40 seconds per side, pressing the edges, until deep golden and crisp.
Top every hot paratha with 1 tsp white butter and serve before it finishes melting.
tips: Bhuno the onion patiently; its sweetness against the salty cheese is what defines this version.
Kasuri methi should be crushed to a powder between your palms so it disperses instead of sitting in bitter flakes.
If the cheese starts leaking on the tava, lower the heat and finish the side that leaked first to seal it with a crust.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with salted churned lassi and sliced onions sprinkled with chaat masala; a side of dal makhani turns it into a full dhaba thali.

variations.name: Gujarati Cheesy Carrot Paratha
variations.description: True to Gujarat's sweet-savoury instinct, this version stirs Anveshan Jaggery Powder and toasted sesame into the carrot before the cheese goes in, so each bite lands sweet first, then salty and nutty. Groundnut oil in the pan keeps the flavour light and thepla-like rather than heavy.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Its gentle wheatiness lets the jaggery-sesame notes shine through

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Wood-pressed peanut oil is the everyday fat of Gujarati griddle breads

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: A spoon of unrefined jaggery gives the classic Gujarati sweet finish

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and about 3/4 cup water into a soft thepla-like dough. Rest for 15 minutes.
Toast 1 tbsp sesame seeds in a dry pan on low for 2 minutes until they turn pale gold and start to pop; set aside.

Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil on medium, sizzle 2 tsp ginger-green chilli paste for 30 seconds, then add 1 1/2 cups grated carrot, 1/4 tsp salt and 1 tsp coriander powder. Cook 5 to 6 minutes until fully dry.

Off the heat, stir in 1 tbsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder and the toasted sesame; the jaggery should just melt into the warm carrot. Cool completely, then mix in 1 cup grated cheese and 2 tbsp chopped coriander.
Shape the dough into 8 balls, stuff each with 2 tbsp of the sweet-savoury filling, seal and roll softly into 6-inch rounds.

Cook on a medium tava about 1 minute per side, then brush with the remaining 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and roast 40 seconds per side until amber-spotted; the jaggery browns faster, so watch the heat.
tips: Add jaggery only off the heat; boiling it makes the filling sticky and hard once cool.
The sweet filling caramelises quickly, so keep the tava at medium rather than high.
These stay soft for hours, making them excellent tiffin-box parathas; wrap in a cloth, not foil, to prevent sweating.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve the Gujarati way with a bowl of chilled sweetened curd, chhundo pickle and fried green chillies on the side.

variations.name: Tamil Cheesy Carrot Paratha
variations.description: Borrowing from Tamil Nadu's kothu and podi traditions, the carrot here is tempered with curry leaves, mustard seeds and urad dal in wood-pressed sesame oil, then laced with cracked pepper before the cheese binds it. The gingelly oil's deep nuttiness against melted cheese is an unexpectedly brilliant pairing.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Emmer's soft bite mimics a parotta crumb without any maida

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sesame Oil
ingredients.note: Wood-pressed gingelly oil is Tamil Nadu's signature tempering fat

steps: Mix 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt and 1 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil, then knead with roughly 3/4 cup water into a smooth, elastic dough. Rest it covered for 20 minutes.

Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil on medium and pop 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, about 30 seconds. Add 1 tsp urad dal and fry until it turns biscuit-gold, then drop in 2 torn dried red chillies, 2 sprigs curry leaves and 1/4 tsp asafoetida.
Add 1 1/2 cups grated carrot and 1/4 tsp salt to the sizzling tempering and cook 5 to 6 minutes on medium-high until dry, sweet and flecked with crisped curry leaves.
Season with 3/4 tsp crushed black pepper, spread the filling out to cool completely, then combine with 1 cup grated cheese.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and fill each with 2 tbsp of the tempered carrot-cheese mixture. Seal, flatten and roll into 6-inch discs, dusting lightly with dry atta.
Roast on a medium-hot tava 1 minute per side, brush both sides with the remaining 1 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil and cook 40 seconds more per side until crisp, deep-gold and fragrant with gingelly.
tips: Fry the urad dal to a true golden brown; underdone dal stays chalky inside the filling.
Tear the curry leaves as they go in to release their oils and stop them from flying out of the pan.
A sprinkle of idli podi over the buttered surface just before serving doubles down on the Tamil character.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with coconut chutney and a shot of hot filter coffee; a spoon of tangy tomato thokku on the side cuts the richness of the cheese.

variations.name: Andhra Cheesy Carrot Paratha
variations.description: Fiery Guntur red chillies meet cooling molten cheese in this Andhra rendition, where the carrot is sautéed with garlic and a coarse home-style Guntur chilli-cumin pounding. The cheese tames the burn just enough to keep you reaching for the next wedge, a genuine sweet-heat-cream triangle.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Wholegrain sturdiness stands up to the aggressive Guntur spicing

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee softens the Guntur chilli's sharp edges the Andhra way

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and about 3/4 cup water until soft and stretchy, then rest the dough for 20 minutes under a damp cloth.
Dry-roast 3 Guntur chillies and 1/2 tsp of the cumin seeds in a pan on low for 2 minutes until the chillies darken a shade and smell smoky, then pound them coarsely with a pinch of salt in a mortar.

Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on medium, crackle the remaining 1/2 tsp cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then fry 4 sliced garlic cloves and 1 sprig curry leaves until the garlic edges turn gold, about 1 minute.

Add 1 1/2 cups grated carrot, 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1/4 tsp salt and sauté 5 to 6 minutes on medium-high until bone-dry. Stir in the pounded Guntur chilli-cumin and cook 1 minute, then cool completely.
Fold 1 cup grated cheese and 2 tbsp chopped coriander into the cooled fiery carrot until evenly speckled red and white.

Stuff 8 dough balls with 2 tbsp filling each, seal and roll into 6-inch rounds. Roast on a medium-hot tava 1 minute per side, then finish with the remaining 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, 40 seconds per side, until crusty and deeply spotted.
tips: Pound the roasted chillies coarsely, not to a powder; the little flakes deliver bursts of heat against the mild cheese.
Deseed one of the three Guntur chillies if serving children, keeping the colour but softening the fire.
The garlic must be fried until golden; raw garlic turns acrid trapped inside a sealed paratha.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a dollop of thick curd and a spoon of Andhra gongura or tomato pachadi; buttermilk spiced with ginger completes the meal.

variations.name: Classic Cheesy Gobi Paratha
variations.description: A kid-favourite twist on the winter staple: spiced grated cauliflower is bulked up with melty grated cheese so every tear of the paratha pulls into gooey strands. The khapli wheat crust roasts up crisp in ghee while the inside stays molten and mildly spiced.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Long-fermenting emmer wheat adds fibre that balances the richness of the cheese

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee browns the crust before the cheese inside can leak and scorch

steps: Knead 3 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and roughly 1.25 cups water, added a splash at a time, into a soft pliable dough. Work it 8 minutes until smooth, then rest under a damp cloth for 20 minutes.
Sprinkle 0.25 tsp salt over 2.5 cups grated cauliflower, wait 10 minutes, then squeeze the shreds hard in your fists until they stop dripping; a dry filling is essential once cheese joins it.

Combine the squeezed gobi with 1 cup grated cheese, 1 inch grated ginger, 2 minced green chillies, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 0.75 tsp red chilli powder, 0.25 tsp turmeric and 3 tbsp coriander, mixing lightly so the cheese stays in strands.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and the filling into 8 portions of about 3 tbsp each. Cup a ball in your palm, tuck in one portion, gather the edges above the filling and pinch into a firm seal.
Roll each stuffed ball into a 6.5-inch round with gentle, even pressure; roll these slightly thicker than a plain paratha so the melting cheese cannot burst through.

Cook on a medium tava for about 2 minutes per side, spreading 0.5 tsp Anveshan Ghee on each face after the first flip, until both sides are patched golden-brown and the paratha feels springy where the cheese has melted.
Rest each paratha 1 minute before cutting so the molten cheese thickens slightly instead of gushing out.
tips: Keep the tava at medium, never high; scorched spots form before the cheese melts if the pan is too hot.
A 50-50 mix of mozzarella and processed cheese gives the best pull plus salty flavour.
Seal any thin patch with a pinch of dry atta before it hits the pan - leaked cheese burns instantly.
variations.servingSuggestion: Cut into wedges like a quesadilla and serve with tomato ketchup for kids and green chutney for everyone else, plus a glass of masala chaas.

variations.name: Punjabi Cheesy Gobi Paratha
variations.description: Amritsari indulgence at full volume: the cheesy gobi filling gets ajwain, garam masala and chopped onion, and the roasted paratha is slathered with white butter that mingles with the molten cheese. This is the version highway dhabas would serve if they discovered mozzarella.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Chakki-style khapli flour gives the rustic bite Punjabi parathas are known for

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Dhaba cooks ladle ghee around the edges so the rim fries crisp while the cheese melts inside

steps: Mix 3 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tsp salt and 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, then knead in about 1.25 cups water over 8 minutes until the dough is soft and springs back slowly. Rest 20 minutes under a damp towel.

Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a kadhai on medium, crackle 0.5 tsp ajwain for 20 seconds, then sweat the chopped onion 2 minutes until glassy. Add 2.5 cups grated cauliflower and fry 4 minutes until bone dry.

Season the gobi off the heat with 0.75 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, 1 tsp anardana powder and 0.25 tsp salt, spread on a plate to cool completely, then toss through 1 cup grated cheese.
Portion the dough into 8 balls and the filling into 8 mounds of about 3 tbsp. Stuff each ball, drawing the dough up and over the mound and twisting off the excess so no cheese sits near the seam.
Roll each into a stout 6.5-inch disc on a floured board; a thicker Punjabi-style roll keeps the double filling of gobi and cheese safely inside.

Roast on a medium-high tava roughly 90 seconds a side, spooning 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee around the rim at every flip, until the crust blisters into crisp brown patches and the centre puffs from the melting cheese.
Crown each hot paratha with 1 tbsp white butter and serve before it finishes melting into the crust.
tips: Cool the cooked gobi fully before adding cheese or it will clump and melt prematurely.
Sharp cheddar stands up to garam masala better than mild mozzarella in this version.
Roll seam-side down; the smooth face takes the first sear and holds the cheese better.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with sweet lassi in a steel tumbler, sliced onions dusted with chaat masala and a fiery mirchi ka achaar on the side.

variations.name: Tamil Cheesy Gobi Paratha
variations.description: A Chennai tiffin-room crossover where the cheesy cauliflower filling is tempered with curry leaves, mustard seeds and cracked pepper in wood-pressed sesame oil. The nutty gingelly aroma against stretchy cheese tastes like a masala-toast and a paratha had a delicious child.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The soft khapli crumb soaks up gingelly oil the way a good parotta should

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sesame Oil
ingredients.note: Wood-pressed gingelly oil brings the deep nutty base note of Tamil tiffin cooking

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A ghee finish softens the sesame oil's intensity, temple-prasadam style

steps: Knead 3 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil and about 1.25 cups water for 8 minutes to a supple dough, then cover and rest it for 20 minutes.

Warm 2 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil in a pan over medium heat and pop 0.75 tsp mustard seeds fully, about 30 seconds, before adding 15 shredded curry leaves and 1 inch grated ginger to sizzle for 20 seconds more.

Tip in 2.5 cups grated cauliflower with 1 tsp sambar powder and 0.25 tsp salt and stir-fry 5 minutes on medium until dry and lightly toasted. Cool completely, then fold in 1 cup mozzarella and 1 tsp crushed black pepper.
Shape 8 dough balls, fill each with 3 tbsp of the curry-leaf cheese mixture, and pleat the edges shut over the top like closing a modak, pinching off any excess dough.
Roll the parcels gently into 6.5-inch rounds, keeping them a shade thick so the mozzarella stays contained while it melts.

Cook on a medium tava for 2 minutes per side, drizzling 0.5 tsp Anveshan Sesame Oil around each paratha as it roasts, until deep golden freckles cover both faces and curry-leaf perfume rises from the pan.
Brush each finished paratha with a little Anveshan Ghee while still on the tava for a glossy, aromatic finish.
tips: Let the mustard seeds finish popping before anything else goes in, or they stay bitter and raw.
Any good sambar powder works, but a homemade one with extra coriander seed lifts the whole filling.
Shred curry leaves fine; whole leaves create slippery gaps that let cheese escape while rolling.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve sliced in quarters with coconut chutney and a small tumbler of sweet filter-coffee style chukku kaapi for a proper Tamil tiffin spread.

variations.name: Maharashtrian Cheesy Gobi Paratha
variations.description: Pune-style comfort food where the cheese-flecked gobi is seasoned with smoky-sweet goda masala and toasted groundnut oil, finishing with a scatter of roasted peanut crush. Goda masala's stone-flower and coconut notes give this paratha a warmth no garam masala can copy.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Khapli is an heirloom Maharashtra-grown wheat, making this the most local flour choice possible

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Wood-pressed groundnut oil is the everyday fat of Maharashtrian kitchens and doubles the peanut flavour

steps: Make a soft dough from 3 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and about 1.25 cups water, kneading a full 8 minutes; cover and set aside for 20 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a kadhai on medium and bloom 0.5 tsp cumin seeds for 20 seconds until they darken and smell toasty, then add 2 minced green chillies.

Add 2.5 cups grated cauliflower, 0.25 tsp turmeric and 0.25 tsp salt and sauté 5 minutes until the moisture cooks off. Stir in 1.5 tsp goda masala for the last 30 seconds so it blooms in the oil, then cool the filling fully.
Fold 1 cup grated cheese, 3 tbsp crushed roasted peanuts and 3 tbsp coriander through the cooled gobi so the mixture holds together in a loose crumble.
Stuff 8 dough balls with 3 tbsp filling apiece, sealing the gathered edges with a firm twist, then roll each into a 6.5-inch round with light strokes and a dusting of dry atta.

Roast on a medium tava about 2 minutes per side, spooning 0.5 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil onto each face at the flips, until the surface is mottled deep brown and the peanut aroma turns unmistakably nutty.
tips: Goda masala scorches fast; always add it at the end of sautéing, never to hot oil at the start.
Crush the peanuts to a coarse rubble, not powder, so they stay crunchy against the melted cheese.
No goda masala? Kala masala works, but reduce to 1 tsp as it runs hotter.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a dollop of homemade dahi, spicy thecha on the side and finish the meal with a piece of jaggery, the true Maharashtrian way.

variations.name: Andhra Cheesy Gobi Paratha
variations.description: For serious heat-seekers: fiery Guntur chilli and garlic tempered in groundnut oil charge through the cauliflower, while a full cup of cheese cools each blazing bite just enough to take another. It is the cheese-pull paratha reimagined for the spiciest table in India.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The wholegrain khapli crust tempers Guntur heat better than refined flour ever could

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Andhra kitchens fry their podis and tadkas in groundnut oil; its high smoke point handles the fierce tempering

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A ghee finish is the traditional Andhra mercy that rounds off chilli fire

steps: Knead 3 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and close to 1.25 cups water into a smooth, yielding dough over 8 minutes, then rest it covered for 20 minutes.
Get 2 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil shimmering in a kadhai on medium-high, then fry 6 minced garlic cloves and 10 shredded curry leaves for 40 seconds until the garlic edges turn pale gold.

Lower the heat, add 2.5 cups grated cauliflower with 0.25 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander powder and 0.25 tsp salt, and cook 5 minutes until dry. Sprinkle in 1.5 tsp Guntur chilli powder in the final minute so it toasts without burning, then cool completely.
Mix 1 cup grated mozzarella into the cooled, brick-red filling and divide it into 8 portions of about 3 tbsp each.
Stuff and seal 8 dough balls around the portions, then roll each into a 6.5-inch round, patching any thin spots with dry atta before they reach the pan.

Roast on a medium tava for roughly 2 minutes a side, adding 0.5 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil at each flip, until fierce red-brown blisters cover the crust and the cheese inside feels molten when pressed.
Swipe each paratha with a little Anveshan Ghee as it comes off the heat; the ghee carries the chilli aroma and softens its edge.
tips: Guntur chilli builds heat late - taste the filling after it cools before deciding to add more.
Toasting the chilli powder in oil at the end deepens colour and flavour, but 30 seconds too long turns it acrid.
Serve with chilled curd rather than raita; plain dahi is the classic Andhra fire extinguisher.
variations.servingSuggestion: Plate with a spoon of Andhra tomato pachadi and a katori of chilled thick curd; a slice of raw mango on the side is the local cooling trick.

variations.name: Classic Dal Paratha
variations.description: The everyday North Indian answer to leftover dal: soft-cooked chana dal is spiced, dried out and tucked inside a khapli atta dough, then roasted in ghee until blistered. The emmer wheat gives the crust a nutty sweetness that plain atta never quite manages, while the filling stays fluffy rather than pasty.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: stone-ground emmer wheat kneads into an extensible dough that rolls thin without tearing over the dal filling

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee does triple duty here — in the dough, in the tempering and for roasting the parathas golden

steps: Rinse 3/4 cup chana dal until the water runs clear, then pressure cook it with 1.5 cups water, 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt on medium heat for 4 whistles, until a grain crushes easily between two fingers. Drain off every bit of extra liquid and spread the dal out to cool.

Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, 1/2 tsp salt and about 3/4 cup water into a soft, non-sticky dough, working it for 5 minutes until the surface turns smooth. Cover with a damp cloth and rest for 15 minutes.

Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a kadhai on medium heat and let 1 tsp cumin seeds crackle for 30 seconds until aromatic. Add 1 inch grated ginger and 2 finely chopped green chillies and saute for 1 minute until the raw smell disappears.

Add the cooked dal along with 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1/2 tsp amchur and the remaining 3/4 tsp salt, mashing and stirring on low heat for 3 to 4 minutes until the mixture is dry enough to hold together in a ball. Cool completely, then fold in 3 tbsp chopped coriander leaves.

Divide the dough into 8 equal balls and the filling into 8 portions of roughly 2 tbsp each. Flatten each ball into a 4 inch cup, enclose one portion of filling, pinch the edges shut and roll gently into a 6 to 7 inch round, dusting with dry atta so the dal never breaks through.

Roast each paratha on a hot tava over medium-high heat for about 1 minute per side until brown spots appear, then brush both sides with the remaining 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and cook another 30 seconds per side until golden, crisp-edged and puffed in places.
tips: The filling must be bone-dry before stuffing — if it looks even slightly wet, stir it on low heat 2 more minutes, or the paratha will tear while rolling.
Cook the dal a day ahead and refrigerate; a chilled filling is firmer and much easier to seal and roll.
If a paratha springs a leak on the tava, press a pinch of dry atta over the tear and flip immediately — the flour seals it.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a bowl of thick curd whisked with roasted cumin powder, a spoon of mango pickle and paper-thin onion rings soaked in lime juice.

variations.name: Punjabi Dal Paratha
variations.description: In Punjab this paratha is breakfast fuel: a moong dal filling sharpened with anardana and garam masala, ajwain-scented dough, and a slick of white butter melting on top the moment it leaves the tava. It is heartier and tangier than the classic, built to be eaten with lassi rather than tea.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: khapli's low-gluten stretch keeps these generously stuffed parathas from springing leaks under the rolling pin

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasting in bilona ghee is what gives the Punjabi paratha its dhaba-style toasted aroma

steps: Pressure cook 3/4 cup rinsed split yellow moong dal with 1.25 cups water and 1/2 tsp salt for 3 whistles on medium heat, so the dal is fully soft but not soupy. Drain thoroughly and mash it coarsely with the back of a ladle.

Meanwhile knead a dough from 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta, 1/2 tsp ajwain seeds, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and about 3/4 cup water; it should feel soft and springy after 5 minutes of kneading. Rest it under a damp cloth for 15 minutes.

Warm 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pan over medium heat and sweat 1 finely chopped onion with 2 chopped green chillies for 3 to 4 minutes until the onion turns translucent and lightly golden at the edges.

Stir the mashed dal into the pan with 1 tsp anardana powder, 1 tsp garam masala and the remaining 3/4 tsp salt, and cook on low for 3 minutes, stirring, until the mixture leaves the sides of the pan dry. Cool it fully and mix in 2 tbsp chopped coriander.
Shape 8 dough balls, stuff each with about 2 tbsp of the moong filling, seal firmly and roll out to a thick 6 inch round — Punjabi parathas are rolled slightly thicker so the layers stay soft inside.
Cook on a medium-hot tava for 60 to 90 seconds per side, pressing the edges with a folded cloth, then finish with the last 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee until both faces are deeply golden with dark freckles.
Top each hot paratha with 1/2 tbsp white butter just before it goes to the plate, letting it melt into the crust.
tips: Anardana can be swapped with 1/2 tsp amchur, but toast anardana briefly on a dry tava first for a deeper sour note.
Press the rolled paratha edges with your fingertips before roasting — the rim is where these thick parathas stay raw if ignored.
The filling freezes well for 2 weeks; thaw and re-dry it in a pan for 2 minutes before stuffing.
variations.servingSuggestion: Bring it to the table dhaba-style with a tall glass of salted lassi, sliced radish and a green chilli pickle on the side.

variations.name: Bengali Dal Paratha
variations.description: Modelled on Bengal's beloved dal puri, this version stuffs the paratha with ground yellow matar dal perfumed with roasted fennel, ginger and a whisper of hing, and cooks everything in pungent mustard oil instead of ghee. The result is sharper and more aromatic, with the unmistakable kick of a Kolkata street griddle.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: the wholegrain emmer stands up beautifully to mustard oil's punch, unlike refined maida used in shop-bought dal puri

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed kachi ghani oil, smoked briefly to mellow, is the soul of this Bengali take — do not substitute

steps: Soak 3/4 cup yellow matar dal in hot water for 30 minutes, then pressure cook with 1.25 cups water and 1/2 tsp salt for 3 whistles until completely tender. Drain very well and grind or mash to a thick, coarse paste with no whole grains left.

Make the dough by rubbing 1 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil and 1/2 tsp kalonji seeds into 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt, then adding roughly 3/4 cup water; knead 5 minutes to a supple, soft ball and rest 15 minutes covered.

Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil in a kadhai on medium-high until it just begins to smoke, then lower the heat and let it cool for 30 seconds so the raw pungency mellows. Add 1/4 tsp hing, 1 inch grated ginger and 3 chopped green chillies and fry for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add the dal paste, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp roasted fennel powder, 1/2 tsp sugar and the remaining 3/4 tsp salt, and stir over low heat for 4 to 5 minutes until the mixture tightens into a dry, mouldable mass. Spread it on a plate to cool completely.

Portion the dough into 8 balls and the filling into 8 lots of about 2 tbsp. Cup each ball in your palm, tuck in the filling, twist the top closed and roll out softly to a 6 inch disc, flouring as needed so the fragrant dal stays sealed inside.

Griddle each paratha on a medium-hot tava about 1 minute per side, then drizzle the last 1 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil around the edges and press gently until both sides are lacquered, crisp and speckled deep brown.
tips: Always heat mustard oil to its smoking point once and then cool it slightly before tempering — skipping this leaves the paratha bitter and raw-tasting.
The pinch of sugar is not optional in a Bengali kitchen; it rounds out the mustard and fennel rather than sweetening the dish.
Grind the dal while still warm — cold matar dal turns stiff and refuses to spread evenly inside the dough.
variations.servingSuggestion: Eat as Kolkata does: with a light aloo'r dom or simply a smear of kasundi mustard and sliced cucumber.

variations.name: Rajasthani Dal Paratha
variations.description: A desert-kitchen paratha that borrows its filling from dal kachori: nutty urad dal cooked down with crushed coriander, fennel and fiery dried red chillies. Generous ghee and a coarse, rustic spice crunch make it sturdy enough to travel — this is a paratha built for long days, not delicate plates.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: emmer wheat's rustic chew suits this kachori-style filling far better than soft mill-ground flour

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Rajasthani cooking is unapologetic about ghee — it blooms the whole spices and crisps the crust

steps: Soak 3/4 cup split urad dal for 30 minutes, then pressure cook with 1.25 cups water and 1/2 tsp salt for 3 whistles on medium heat until each grain is soft right through. Drain completely and mash to a coarse, dryish crumble.

Bring together 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, 1/2 tsp salt and about 3/4 cup water and knead for 5 minutes into a smooth, pliable dough. Set it aside under a damp cloth for 15 minutes.

On a dry tava over low heat, toast 2 tsp coriander seeds, 1 tsp fennel seeds and 3 dried red chillies for about 2 minutes until they smell nutty, then pound them coarsely in a mortar — the crunch is the point.

Melt 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a kadhai on medium heat, sizzle 1/4 tsp hing and 1 inch grated ginger for 30 seconds, then add the mashed dal, the pounded spices, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp amchur and 3/4 tsp salt. Roast, stirring, for 4 to 5 minutes until the filling turns sandy and aromatic, then cool fully.

Divide dough and filling into 8 portions each, using about 2 tbsp filling per ball. Seal each stuffed ball carefully and roll out to a 6 inch round with light, even strokes so the coarse dal does not puncture the surface.
Roast on a medium-hot tava for around 90 seconds per side, spooning the remaining 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee over both faces, until the paratha is a deep golden brown with crisp, biscuity edges.
tips: Pound the toasted spices coarse, never fine — the broken bits of coriander and fennel bursting on the tongue define this paratha.
These keep well for a day at room temperature, which is why Rajasthani travellers pack them; re-crisp on a dry tava for 30 seconds a side.
If the urad filling feels sticky, roast it 2 extra minutes; urad turns gluey when underdried and sandy-perfect when done.
variations.servingSuggestion: Pair with fiery lehsun ki chutney, a spoon of churned dahi and raw onion — or crumble it over kadhi the way it is done in Jodhpur homes.

variations.name: Maharashtrian Dal Paratha
variations.description: Toor dal meets goda masala — Maharashtra's smoky, coconut-and-stone-flower blend — with toasted sesame, curry leaves and the faintest touch of jaggery for that signature sweet-spicy balance. It tastes like puran poli's savoury cousin and is often eaten warm with a swipe of thecha.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: khapli wheat is an old Maharashtra-Karnataka heirloom, so this paratha is truly regional grain to grain

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: a goda masala tempering blooms best in slow-churned bilona ghee

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: just enough unrefined sweetness to balance the smoky goda masala, the classic Maharashtrian trick

steps: Cook 3/4 cup rinsed toor dal with 1.5 cups water, 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt in a pressure cooker for 4 whistles until utterly soft, then drain well and mash smooth — this filling should be closer to a thick puran than a crumble.
Work 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, 1/2 tsp salt and about 3/4 cup water into a soft, elastic dough over 5 minutes of kneading, then rest it for 15 minutes under a damp cloth.
Dry-toast 1 tbsp white sesame seeds and 2 tbsp grated dry coconut on a low flame for 2 minutes until pale gold and nutty, and tip them onto a plate before they darken.

Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on medium, pop 1/2 tsp mustard seeds for 20 seconds, add 10 torn curry leaves, then stir in the mashed dal with 2 tsp goda masala, 2 tsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder, 1/4 tsp turmeric and 3/4 tsp salt. Cook 4 minutes on low until thick and glossy, fold in the toasted sesame-coconut and cool completely.
Split the dough into 8 balls and stuff each with about 2 tbsp of the goda masala filling; pinch shut and roll into 6 inch rounds with a gentle hand, dusting with dry atta whenever the dough resists.

Roast on a medium tava for 1 minute per side, then a final 30 seconds per side with the remaining 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee brushed on, until the surface is amber with dark toasted spots and smells faintly of caramel from the jaggery.
tips: Goda masala scorches quickly — always add it off direct high heat and never fry it alone in ghee for more than a few seconds.
If you cannot find goda masala, a mix of 1.5 tsp garam masala with 1/2 tsp toasted sesame powder gets you close, though it misses the stone-flower smokiness.
The smooth puran-like filling spreads best if you roll from the centre outward in short strokes rather than long sweeps.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with green chilli thecha, a katori of mattha (spiced buttermilk) and lime pickle for a proper Maharashtrian thali corner.

variations.name: Classic Mooli Paratha
variations.description: The definitive North Indian winter breakfast: sharp, juicy white radish grated, squeezed dry and folded with roasted cumin and green chilli, then stuffed inside a soft khapli atta shell. Roasted on a hot tava in bilona ghee, the crust turns blistered and crisp while the filling stays peppery and moist. Every bite carries that unmistakable mooli pungency mellowed by slow-roasted wheat.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Emmer wheat's low gluten keeps the stuffed shell tender so the juicy radish filling never toughens it

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Bilona ghee's high smoke point crisps the paratha crust without burning while its nutty aroma tames raw radish sharpness

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and about 3/4 cup water into a soft, non-sticky dough; it should dent easily when pressed. Cover and rest 15 minutes so the emmer wheat hydrates fully.
Toss the 2 cups grated radish with 1/2 tsp salt and set aside for 10 minutes, then squeeze it hard in fistfuls until almost no liquid drips out. This step is what keeps the parathas from tearing.

Mix the squeezed radish with the remaining 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1/2 tsp red chilli powder, 1/4 tsp turmeric, 2 minced green chillies, 1 tsp grated ginger and 3 tbsp coriander until evenly speckled.

Divide the dough into 8 equal balls. Flatten each into a 4-inch cup, place 2 tbsp of filling in the centre, gather the edges over the top and pinch firmly to seal, then dust and gently roll into a 6-inch round without pressing the centre.

Heat a tava on medium-high until a drop of water sizzles instantly. Cook each paratha for about 1 minute until small bubbles rise, flip, spread 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee over the surface, and flip again after 45 seconds.
Press the edges with a spatula and roast both sides another 1 to 2 minutes, brushing with more Anveshan Ghee, until deep golden-brown spots appear and the paratha smells toasty.
tips: If any filling leaks while rolling, pat a pinch of dry khapli atta over the tear and roll only from the edges inward.
Squeezed radish juice is packed with flavour; knead a splash of it into the dough instead of plain water and discard the rest.
Stack cooked parathas in a cloth-lined box; the trapped steam keeps them pliable for up to two hours.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot off the tava with a bowl of thick whisked curd, a wedge of lime pickle and a mug of masala chai for the full Delhi-winter experience.

variations.name: Punjabi Mooli Paratha
variations.description: In Punjab's dhaba tradition the mooli paratha is rolled thick, roasted until the crust crackles, and crowned with a melting spoon of white butter. Ajwain bloomed in ghee and a generous hit of ginger give the filling its warming, digestive edge, made for foggy Amritsar mornings.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Stone-ground khapli gives the thick dhaba-style paratha a rustic bite that refined flour cannot match

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Punjabi parathas are shallow-roasted generously; cultured bilona ghee adds the tang of homemade makkhan

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt and roughly 3/4 cup water into a supple dough that springs back slowly when poked. Rub 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee over it, cover, and rest for 15 minutes.
Salt the 2.5 cups grated radish with 1/2 tsp salt, wait 10 minutes, then wring it out in a muslin cloth until it feels like a dry sponge. Reserve the juice for kneading your next batch.
Warm 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a small pan on low heat and let 1/2 tsp ajwain crackle for about 30 seconds until fragrant. Pour this sizzling tempering over the squeezed radish.
Stir in 2 tsp grated ginger, 2 minced green chillies, 1 tsp anardana powder, 1/2 tsp red chilli powder, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and 3 tbsp coriander; the filling should taste boldly tangy-hot.
Shape 8 dough balls, stuff each with a heaping 2 tbsp of filling, seal the pleats and roll into thick 5-inch rounds so the dhaba-style paratha stays pillowy inside.
Roast on a medium-hot tava for 1 to 2 minutes per side, spooning 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee around the edges each flip, until both faces are mottled deep brown and the crust crackles when pressed.
Slide each paratha onto a plate and immediately top with 1 tsp white butter so it melts into the hot crust before serving.
tips: Anardana powder is the Punjabi secret; if unavailable, use 1/2 tsp amchur but add it only just before stuffing so the radish does not weep.
Roll these thicker than usual; a thin Punjabi mooli paratha dries out and loses its soft, steamy core.
For an authentic dhaba char, finish each paratha directly on a low open flame for 5 seconds per side using tongs.
variations.servingSuggestion: Pair with sweet lassi in a tall brass glass, sliced onions sprinkled with chaat masala, and a spoon of gajar ka achar on the side.

variations.name: Bengali Mooli Paratha
variations.description: Bengal reimagines the mooli paratha with its beloved pairing of pungent mustard oil and smoky nigella seeds. The radish is briefly sauteed in kasundi-style mustard oil so it turns sweet and mellow, and the paratha fries to a deeper, lacquered crust than its ghee-roasted northern cousin.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Khapli's nutty sweetness balances the sharp mustard-oil filling in this Bengali take

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Wood-pressed kachi ghani mustard oil brings the wasabi-like pungency that defines Bengali griddle breads

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A final brush of ghee softens the mustard oil's bite the way Bengali homes finish their porotas

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil and about 3/4 cup water into a smooth, elastic dough. Rest it covered for 15 minutes while you cook the filling.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil in a kadhai on medium-high until it just begins to smoke, then lower the heat and let 1/2 tsp kalonji sputter for 20 seconds.

Add the 2 cups grated radish (no need to squeeze it first), 1/2 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt, and saute on medium heat for 6 to 7 minutes until the moisture evaporates and the radish smells sweet rather than raw.
Fold in 3 minced green chillies, 1 tsp grated ginger and 2 tbsp coriander, spread the filling on a plate and cool it completely for about 10 minutes; a warm filling will steam-burst the dough.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, stuff each with 2 tbsp of the cooled radish, seal and roll into 6-inch rounds, flouring lightly so the moist filling does not stick.
Pan-fry each paratha on a medium tava with 1 tsp Anveshan Mustard Oil per side for about 90 seconds a side, pressing gently, until lacquered reddish-brown spots develop and the edges crisp.
Brush the hot parathas with a little Anveshan Ghee just before serving to round off the mustard oil's sharpness.
tips: Cooking the radish first, Bengali-style, means you can skip squeezing and keep more of its sweetness in the filling.
Let the mustard oil smoke once and cool slightly before tempering; unheated raw mustard oil tastes unpleasantly acrid.
These reheat beautifully on a dry tava; sprinkle a few drops of water and cover for 30 seconds to revive the crust.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with begun bhaja (crisp fried aubergine slices), a smear of kasundi mustard and sweet mango chutney for a proper Kolkata brunch plate.

variations.name: Kerala Mooli Paratha
variations.description: A Malabar-inspired crossover where grated radish meets fresh coconut, curry leaves and a coconut-oil tempering, then gets folded into flaky khapli layers. The filling is sauteed thoran-style, so it is fragrant, faintly sweet and completely dry, giving you a paratha that shatters at the edges like a parotta.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Whole emmer flour turns satisfyingly flaky when laminated with coconut oil, Malabar-style

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: Cold-pressed coconut oil perfumes both the thoran-style filling and the crisp griddled crust

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil and about 3/4 cup water into a soft dough, then rest it under a damp cloth for 15 minutes.

Heat 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil in a pan on medium heat and pop 1/2 tsp mustard seeds for about 20 seconds, then add 12 curry leaves and 4 sliced shallots and fry until the shallots turn translucent, around 2 minutes.
Add the 2 cups grated radish, 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt and saute for 5 to 6 minutes on medium heat until completely dry and lightly caramelised at the edges.
Stir in 1/2 cup grated coconut, 2 minced green chillies and 1/2 tsp crushed black pepper, cook 1 more minute, then cool the thoran-style filling fully on a wide plate.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, cup each one, pack in 2 tbsp of filling, seal tightly and roll to a 6-inch round with light, even strokes so the coconut does not pierce through.
Griddle each paratha on medium heat, drizzling 1/2 tsp Anveshan Coconut Oil per side, for about 90 seconds a side until golden freckles appear and the kitchen smells of toasted coconut.
Rest the parathas 2 minutes under a cloth, then clap each one gently between your palms to loosen the flaky layers before serving.
tips: Do not skip cooling the filling; warm coconut releases oil and makes the dough greasy and impossible to seal.
Fresh coconut works far better than desiccated here; if using frozen, thaw and squeeze it before sauteing.
Leftover filling makes an excellent mooli-coconut thoran side; just reheat with a splash of coconut oil.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a small bowl of coconut chutney, sliced ripe banana and sweet milky filter-style tea for a Malabar tiffin spread.

variations.name: Rajasthani Mooli Paratha
variations.description: Desert kitchens make their mooli paratha fierce and rustic: whole dried Mathania-style red chillies are pounded with coriander seeds and garlic, and the radish is used tops and all. Roasted slowly in generous ghee until almost khasta-crisp, it is built to be eaten with garlic chutney and chaas.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Hardy emmer wheat mirrors the coarse desert attas traditionally milled for khasta parathas

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Rajasthani cooking prizes ghee above all fats; here it slow-roasts the crust to a biscuit-like crunch

ingredients.name: Radish with tender leaves, grated and chopped

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp melted Anveshan Ghee and about 3/4 cup water into a firm-soft dough and rest 15 minutes; a slightly stiffer dough gives the classic khasta bite.

Toast 4 dried red chillies, 2 tsp coriander seeds and 1 tsp fennel seeds on a dry tava over low heat for about 2 minutes until they darken a shade and smell smoky, then pound them coarsely with 4 garlic cloves in a mortar.

Salt the 2.5 cups grated radish and chopped tender leaves with 1/2 tsp salt for 10 minutes, squeeze bone-dry, then mix with the pounded masala, 1 tsp amchur, 1/4 tsp turmeric and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, stuff each with 2 tbsp of the fiery filling, pinch shut and roll into slightly thick 5-inch rounds, patching any tears with a dusting of dry atta.

Roast on a medium-low tava for 2 minutes per side without fat first, then spoon 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee over each side and roast another 1 to 2 minutes until the crust is deeply browned, rigid at the edges and crisp.
Smear a final 1/2 tsp Anveshan Ghee on each hot paratha and crush it lightly between your palms so the flaky crust cracks open.
tips: Using the radish's tender green tops adds a peppery, slightly bitter depth that Rajasthani cooks never waste.
The slow low-heat roast is essential for the khasta texture; rushing on high heat leaves the inside doughy.
The pounded chilli-garlic masala keeps for a week refrigerated and doubles as a base for Rajasthani-style sabzis.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with lehsun ki chutney, a katori of cool chaas spiked with roasted cumin, and a few rings of raw onion for the full desert thali feel.

variations.name: Classic Palak Paratha
variations.description: The everyday North Indian green flatbread where blanched spinach is pureed straight into the dough, giving every bite an even, earthy sweetness. Slow-milled khapli wheat keeps the parathas soft for hours, while a ghee-roasted finish adds a nutty, toasty edge. It is the version most Indian homes reach for on a weekday morning.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Emmer wheat absorbs the spinach puree without turning gummy, so the parathas stay soft

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Bilona ghee for kneading and roasting gives the classic dhaba-style toasted aroma

steps: Wash 200 g spinach, blanch it in boiling water for 90 seconds, then plunge into cold water so it keeps its bright green colour.
Squeeze the spinach dry and blend it with 1 small green chilli and 1 inch ginger into a smooth, thick puree; you should get about 3/4 cup.
In a large bowl combine 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 0.5 tsp ajwain, 0.25 tsp turmeric and 0.5 tsp red chilli powder.
Add the spinach puree and 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, then knead, adding up to 0.25 cup water a spoon at a time, into a soft, non-sticky dough; cover and rest 15 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 equal balls and roll each into a 6-inch round on a lightly floured surface, dusting only as needed so the discs do not dry out.

Roast each paratha on a medium-hot tava for about 1 minute per side until brown spots appear, then brush both sides with the remaining Anveshan Ghee and press the edges until golden and crisp, about 1 more minute.
tips: Squeeze the blanched spinach very well before blending; extra water in the puree makes the dough sticky and hard to roll.
The dough can be made up to 24 hours ahead and refrigerated; bring it to room temperature for 15 minutes before rolling.
If a paratha turns stiff, stack the cooked ones in a cloth-lined box immediately; the trapped steam keeps them pliable.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve two parathas per person with a bowl of thick curd whisked with a pinch of black salt and a wedge of lime pickle on the side.

variations.name: Punjabi Palak Paratha
variations.description: A dhaba-style paratha from Punjab where the spinach is hand-chopped rather than pureed, so flecks of green stay visible in the crumb. Anardana and kasuri methi give it a tangy, smoky depth, and a knob of white butter melting on top is non-negotiable. It is hearty enough to be a full winter breakfast.
