Rest the dish covered off the heat for 3 minutes before serving, letting the curry-leaf and coconut aromas settle into the eggplant.
tips: Slice the coconut into slivers rather than grating it; the slivers stay distinct and chewy instead of disappearing into the mash.
Freshly crushed black pepper, added late, is this dish's main heat — pre-ground pepper will taste flat here.
If your coconut slivers brown unevenly, pull the pan off the heat for 30 seconds and keep stirring; carryover heat finishes them gently.
variations.servingSuggestion: Pair with Kerala matta rice and moru curry, or spoon over hot dosas at breakfast with an extra drizzle of Anveshan Coconut Oil.

variations.name: Classic Garlic Mixed Veg Paratha
variations.description: A thrifty, colourful paratha that turns yesterday's vegetables into today's breakfast star. Carrot, cauliflower, peas and potato are mashed with a garlicky ghee tadka, so the filling is fragrant right through rather than merely spiced on the surface. Each round roasts up golden with flecks of orange and green peeking through the crust.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: High-fibre emmer flour turns this veggie-packed paratha into a genuinely complete meal

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: The garlic tadka blooms in bilona ghee, carrying its aroma through every bit of the mash

steps: Knead 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and about 1 cup water into a soft, non-sticky dough; rest it covered for 20 minutes.
Steam 1 large diced potato, 1 chopped carrot, 1 cup cauliflower florets and 0.5 cup green peas for 10-12 minutes until a knife slides through easily, then drain thoroughly and mash while hot.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pan over medium flame, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then fry 8 minced garlic cloves for about 1 minute until light gold and nutty-smelling.
Tip the tadka over the mashed vegetables along with 1 tsp red chilli powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, 0.5 tsp salt and 3 tbsp chopped coriander, and mix into a dry, cohesive filling. Cool fully.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and the mash into 8 portions of about 2.5 tbsp. Stuff, seal the gathered pleats and roll each into a 6 inch round with soft, even pressure.
Roast on a medium-hot tava for around 2 minutes per side, brushing on the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots deepen and the surface puffs in places.
Wrap the cooked parathas loosely in a cloth for 2 minutes so the crust settles from crisp to tender-crisp before serving.
tips: Mash the vegetables while hot and let the mash steam off for 5 minutes; residual moisture is the main cause of leaking.
This is the ideal home for leftover sabzi: dry it out in a pan first, then mash and stuff.
A pinch of amchur in the mash brightens the whole paratha if your vegetables taste flat.
variations.servingSuggestion: Plate with a swirl of whipped curd, mango pickle and a quick kachumber of cucumber and tomato for crunch.

variations.name: Bengali Garlic Mixed Veg Paratha
variations.description: This version borrows its soul from Bengali labra, the mixed-vegetable mash spiced with panch-style tempering in pungent mustard oil. Nigella seeds, green chillies and garlic fried in kachhi ghani oil give the filling a sharp, smoky edge that plain ghee versions cannot match. A whisper of sugar rounds everything off, as any Bengali kitchen would insist.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The robust emmer grain holds its own against mustard oil the way Bengali whole-wheat ruti does

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Kachhi ghani pungency is the defining flavour here, seasoning the vegetables and crisping the crust alike

steps: Rub 1 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil and 1 tsp salt into 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta, then knead with close to 1 cup water for 7 minutes into a smooth dough. Rest 20 minutes.
Steam 1 large diced potato, 1 cup diced pumpkin, 0.5 cup chopped beans and 1 chopped carrot for 10 minutes until completely tender, then drain well and mash coarsely.
Bring 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil to a light smoke in a kadhai, reduce the flame, and crackle 1 tsp nigella seeds with 3 slit green chillies for about 30 seconds.

Add 8 sliced garlic cloves, fry 1 minute until golden, then fold in the vegetable mash with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 0.5 tsp salt and 0.5 tsp sugar. Cook and stir 3-4 minutes until the mash dries into a thick, scoopable filling; cool fully.
Shape 8 dough balls, fill each with 2.5 tbsp of the labra-style mash, pinch the seams shut and roll gently into 6 inch rounds.
Griddle over medium heat for roughly 2 minutes a side, trickling the remaining 0.5 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil around the edges, until the crust blisters deep amber-brown.
Serve straight off the tava while the mustard aroma is at its peak; this paratha fades faster than ghee-roasted ones.
tips: Pumpkin brings the faint sweetness Bengali vegetable mashes are known for; do not skip it.
Smoke the mustard oil once and then cool it slightly before tempering, or the nigella will scorch instantly.
The filling doubles as a side dish with plain ruti if you make extra.
variations.servingSuggestion: Accompany with tomato khejur chutney or a spoon of kasundi and slit green chillies for the full Bengali table.

variations.name: Odia Garlic Mixed Veg Paratha
variations.description: Odisha's beloved panch phoron, the five-seed blend of cumin, fennel, fenugreek, nigella and mustard, transforms this vegetable paratha. The whole spices are bloomed in hot ghee so each bite delivers little bursts of anise and bitter-sweet fenugreek against the soft mash. It is homely temple-town food, gentle yet deeply aromatic.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The rustic stone-ground texture suits Odisha's understated, grain-forward home cooking

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Panch phoron must bloom in good ghee to release all five aromas; bilona ghee does it without burning

steps: Prepare a soft dough from 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and about 1 cup water, kneading until smooth; rest it for 20 minutes under a damp cloth.
Peel and steam 1 large potato, 1 medium raw banana, 1 carrot and 0.5 cup green peas for 12 minutes until fork-tender, then drain and mash together while warm.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on medium in a pan and bloom 1.5 tsp panch phoron with 2 torn dried red chillies for about 40 seconds until the fennel and cumin crackle and smell sweetly spiced.

Add 6 chopped garlic cloves to the tempering, fry 45 seconds until golden, then combine with the mash, 0.5 tsp turmeric powder and 0.5 tsp salt. Stir over low heat 2 minutes to dry the filling, then cool completely.
Roll the dough into 8 balls, pack each with 2.5 tbsp of the panch-phoron mash, seal the pleats and flatten gently into 6 inch discs with a rolling pin.
Cook on a medium tava for about 2 minutes per side, glossing both faces with the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, until they puff slightly and take on tortoiseshell-brown patches.
Give the parathas a 2 minute rest under a cloth so the whole spices soften slightly and perfume the crumb.
tips: Raw banana is a very Odia touch that makes the mash creamy and slightly starchy; potato alone works if unavailable.
Panch phoron burns quickly because of the fenugreek; pull it off the heat the moment the seeds crackle.
Serve within 30 minutes; the fennel aroma is at its most vivid when fresh off the tava.
variations.servingSuggestion: Pair with dahi baigana (Odia yoghurt-aubergine raita) or plain curd whisked with roasted cumin and a dry mango pickle.

variations.name: Malwa Garlic Mixed Veg Paratha
variations.description: From the wheat bowl of Madhya Pradesh comes a hearty paratha where crushed roasted peanuts are kneaded right into the vegetable mash. The peanuts add crunch, body and a toasty sweetness that plays off garlic and coriander seeds, echoing the region's poha-and-sev love for texture. Roasted in wood-pressed groundnut oil, it is doubly nutty.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Malwa is India's wheat heartland, and heritage khapli honours that lineage in every bite

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Wood-pressed groundnut oil doubles down on the peanut theme, tying crust and filling together

steps: Knead 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and roughly 1 cup water into a pliant dough; cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Steam 1 large diced potato, 1 chopped carrot and 0.5 cup green peas for 10-12 minutes until soft, drain fully and mash to a coarse, chunky texture.

Warm 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a pan over medium heat and sizzle 1.5 tsp crushed coriander seeds for 30 seconds, then fry 8 minced garlic cloves and 2 chopped green chillies for 1 minute until golden.

Stir the tempering into the mash with 0.5 cup crushed roasted peanuts, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 0.5 tsp salt and 3 tbsp chopped coriander; the peanuts should stay pebble-coarse. Cool the filling fully.
Portion into 8 dough balls and 8 mounds of about 2.5 tbsp filling. Stuff, twist the tops closed and roll into 6 inch rounds with gentle strokes so the peanut bits do not puncture the dough.
Roast on a medium tava about 2 minutes per side, painting on the remaining 0.5 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil, until the surface bubbles into crisp golden-brown patches.
Rest 2 minutes before cutting; the peanut-flecked filling firms just enough to hold a clean wedge.
tips: Crush the peanuts in a mortar rather than a mixer to keep uneven, crunchy pieces.
Crushed coriander seeds, not powder, give the authentic Malwa pop of citrusy spice.
These parathas stay pleasantly crunchy for hours, making them excellent lunchbox candidates.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with green coriander-peanut chutney and a bowl of sweetened dahi, with sev sprinkled on top for true Indore spirit.

variations.name: Karnataka Garlic Mixed Veg Paratha
variations.description: Inspired by the tangy-sweet masalas of Karnataka's kadubu and gojju traditions, this paratha carries a tamarind-jaggery note through its vegetable filling. A rasam-style powder, curry leaves and garlic fried in ghee give it a warm, tangy complexity that finishes with the soft sweetness of jaggery. It is the most flavour-layered paratha of the set.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Emmer's mellow grain lets the tamarind-jaggery seasoning shine without competing

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Karnataka temple kitchens finish everything in ghee, and this bilona one lends that festive fragrance

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: A spoon of unrefined jaggery balances the tamarind exactly the way a good gojju does

steps: Make the dough with 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and about 1 cup water, kneading until springy; rest it for 20 minutes.
Steam 1 large diced potato, 0.5 cup chopped beans and 1 chopped carrot for 10-12 minutes until soft, drain and mash coarsely while still warm.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee over medium flame, pop 0.5 tsp mustard seeds for 30 seconds, then fry the leaves of 2 curry sprigs and 8 sliced garlic cloves for 1 minute until the garlic gilds.
Add the mash, 2 tsp rasam powder, 1 tbsp thick tamarind pulp, 2 tsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder and 0.5 tsp salt, and cook 3 minutes, stirring, until the filling turns glossy and dry. Cool it completely.
Divide dough into 8 balls, stuff each with 2.5 tbsp of the tangy filling, seal firmly at the topknot and roll into 6 inch rounds.
Cook on a medium-hot tava for around 2 minutes per side with the remaining 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee brushed over, until burnished brown spots appear and the tamarind caramelises at the surface.
Cool 2 minutes on a rack; the sweet-tangy filling tastes best just below piping hot.
tips: Cook the tamarind and jaggery into the mash rather than mixing raw; heat marries the sweet and sour into one note.
Rasam powder varies in heat between brands, so start with 1.5 tsp and adjust after tasting the filling.
A few white sesame seeds pressed onto the rolled paratha before roasting add a lovely Karnataka-style crunch.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with fresh coconut chutney and a small tumbler of buttermilk seasoned with ginger and curry leaves.

variations.name: Classic Garlic Pyaaz Paratha
variations.description: Golden-fried garlic is the making of this paratha: slivers are crisped in ghee until amber, then folded with squeezed onions so the filling is sweet, savoury and headily aromatic. It is the paratha to make when the kitchen deserves to smell irresistible.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Emmer wheat's mellow nuttiness rounds out the sharp garlic instead of competing with it

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Garlic fried in bilona ghee turns evenly amber and never acrid the way it can in refined oil

steps: Knead 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and about 1 cup water into a soft, springy dough; cover and rest for 20 minutes.

Slice 10 garlic cloves into thin slivers and fry them in 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee over medium-low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until they turn a uniform light amber; lift them out immediately so they do not burn.

Salt and squeeze 3 finely chopped onions dry, then mix with the fried garlic (and its ghee), 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 0.25 tsp turmeric, 2 minced green chillies and 0.25 cup coriander leaves.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, cup each one, spoon in 2 tbsp of the garlicky filling, and pleat the edges closed, pinching off extra dough at the seal.
Roll every stuffed ball into a 7-inch round with light strokes, flipping once midway so both sides roll evenly.
Roast on a medium-hot tava about 90 seconds per side, brushing each face with 0.5 tsp Anveshan Ghee, until crisp golden-brown patches bloom across the surface.
Rest the parathas in a cloth-lined basket for 2 minutes; the garlic aroma deepens noticeably as they sit.
tips: Amber, not brown: garlic keeps cooking off the heat, so pull it a shade earlier than looks right.
Rub a cut garlic clove over the hot cooked paratha for an extra fresh-garlic top note without any harshness.
The fried-garlic ghee left in the pan is liquid gold; brush it on the final parathas instead of plain ghee.
variations.servingSuggestion: Best with a garlicky twist on raita: whisk curd with roasted garlic and mint, and add jaggery-sweetened lemon shikanji to drink.

variations.name: Bihari Garlic Pyaaz Paratha
variations.description: A hat-tip to litti chokha country: roasted sattu is mixed with raw mustard oil, garlic, ajwain-free nimbu-pyaaz masala and stuffed generously into the paratha. The sattu makes the filling hearty and crumbly while kachi ghani mustard oil gives it that unmistakable Bihari kick.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Rustic emmer flour mirrors the coarse hand-milled atta of Bihari village kitchens

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sattu
ingredients.note: Stone-roasted chana sattu is the backbone of this litti-style filling, binding the onions with earthy protein

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Bihari sattu fillings are moistened with raw kachi ghani mustard oil, and its pungent bite is non-negotiable

steps: Knead 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil and roughly 1 cup water into a soft dough; rest it for 20 minutes under a damp cloth.
Mince 8 garlic cloves and 3 green chillies very finely; finely chop 2 onions, salt them lightly and squeeze out the moisture after 10 minutes.
In a bowl, combine 0.75 cup Anveshan Sattu with the garlic, chillies, onions, 0.5 tsp kalonji, 1 tbsp mashed pickle masala, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 0.5 tsp salt and 0.25 cup coriander leaves.
Drizzle in 2 tbsp raw Anveshan Mustard Oil and rub the mixture between your fingers; it should hold together in a loose clump when squeezed, so sprinkle 1 to 2 tsp water if it is too dry.
Fill 8 dough balls with 2.5 tbsp of the sattu masala each; sattu fillings are packed generously in Bihar, so seal carefully and flatten gently before rolling to 6-inch rounds.
Roast on a medium tava for about 2 minutes per side, brushing with 0.5 tsp Anveshan Mustard Oil at each flip, until the crust turns deep golden with dark toasted freckles.
Crush each paratha lightly between your palms before serving to loosen the crumbly filling, litti-style.
tips: The pickle masala (scraped from a jar of mango achar) is the secret Bihari flavour bomb; do not skip it.
If the filling spills while rolling, chill the stuffed balls for 10 minutes; cold sattu binds tighter.
Kalonji goes in raw here by tradition and works because the paratha is thoroughly tava-roasted; never taste the filling before the paratha is cooked.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a rough-mashed baingan-tomato chokha, green chilli, and a raw mustard oil drizzle on top, the way it is eaten beside the Ganga in Patna.

variations.name: Tamil Garlic Pyaaz Paratha
variations.description: Poondu (garlic) meets small-onion masala in this Tamil-style paratha: shallot-sweet onions, curry leaves crisped in gingelly oil and a dusting of milagai podi inside the layers. The sesame oil's toasty depth makes it taste like a cross between a paratha and a podi-smeared dosa.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The wholegrain emmer takes on gingelly oil beautifully, browning into a podi-friendly toasty crust

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sesame Oil
ingredients.note: Wood-pressed gingelly oil is the definitive Tamil cooking fat; its nutty warmth ties the garlic and podi together

steps: Knead 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil and about 1 cup water into a soft dough; rest for 20 minutes.
Heat 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil in a kadhai on medium, splutter 0.5 tsp mustard seeds for 20 seconds, then add 2 torn dried red chillies and 2 sprigs curry leaves and fry until the leaves crisp.
Add 10 sliced garlic cloves and fry for 1 minute until pale gold, then tip in 15 thinly sliced shallots with 0.5 tsp salt and sauté 5 to 6 minutes until soft, sweet and lightly browned.
Stir in 0.25 tsp turmeric, switch off the heat, and cool the masala completely before mixing in 1 tbsp of the idli milagai podi.
Stuff 8 dough balls with 2 tbsp of the shallot-garlic masala each, seal, and roll out to 6-inch rounds with gentle, even pressure.
Cook on a medium tava for about 2 minutes per side, brushing each face with 0.5 tsp Anveshan Sesame Oil, until crisply blistered and deeply aromatic.
While each paratha is still hot, sprinkle a pinch of the remaining 1 tbsp podi over the top so it clings to the oiled surface.
tips: Shallots take longer to brown than big onions but reward you with double the sweetness; do not rush the sauté.
Store-bought podi varies in salt, so taste before adding and cut back the filling salt if needed.
A cast-iron tava mimics the dosa-kal finish; preheat it a full 5 minutes for the best crust.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with coconut chutney and a tumbler of frothy filter coffee, or roll it around a spoon of curd rice for a lunchbox mash-up kids love.

variations.name: Goan Garlic Pyaaz Paratha
variations.description: Goa's kitchen trinity of garlic, kokum and coconut lands inside a paratha: the onions are cooked down with soaked kokum petals until tangy-pink, then brightened with green chilli and a little jaggery balance. It is sour, sweet, garlicky and unlike any paratha north of the Konkan coast.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The emmer's faint sweetness plays against kokum's sharp tang exactly the way Goan pav does against a sour curry

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: Konkan cooking leans on fresh coconut oil, and its aroma carries the kokum-garlic masala perfectly

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: A traditional Goan pinch of goad (jaggery) rounds off the kokum's sourness into a proper agal-dhagal balance

steps: Soak 6 kokum petals in 3 tbsp warm water for 15 minutes, then chop them fine and reserve the deep-pink soaking liquid.
Knead 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil, the kokum soaking water and enough plain water to total about 1 cup, into a soft blush-tinted dough; rest 20 minutes.
Heat 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil on medium, fry 10 chopped garlic cloves for 1 minute until fragrant and pale gold, then add 3 chopped onions and 0.5 tsp salt and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Add the chopped kokum, 3 minced green chillies, 0.25 tsp turmeric, 2 tsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder and 0.25 cup grated coconut; cook 2 more minutes until jammy, then cool fully.
Stuff 8 dough balls with 2 tbsp of the tangy filling each, seal the pleats well, and roll into 6-inch rounds without pressing hard over the centre.
Toast on a medium tava for around 2 minutes a side, brushing on 0.5 tsp Anveshan Coconut Oil per face, until golden with crisp lacy edges.
Let the parathas stand 2 minutes; the kokum filling thickens slightly and its sweet-sour perfume comes forward.
tips: Rinse kokum before soaking; some sun-dried petals carry surface salt that can tip the filling over.
If kokum is unavailable, 1.5 tsp tamarind paste plus a squeeze of lime lands in the same sour neighbourhood.
This filling doubles as a chutney base; loosen leftovers with coconut milk for an instant Konkan dip.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with sol kadhi to drink and a simple cucumber-coconut koshimbir; for a bigger spread, pair with Goan prawn balchao for the full coastal contrast.

variations.name: Malwa Garlic Pyaaz Paratha
variations.description: From the Malwa plateau of Madhya Pradesh, where peanuts and garlic anchor winter food: crushed roasted peanuts and a rustic garlic-chilli pounded masala fill this hearty paratha. Sev-crunchy inside and ghee-crisp outside, it echoes the flavours of Indori namkeen without leaving the tava.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Malwa's wheat belt heritage deserves a heritage grain; khapli gives the paratha its satisfying rustic chew

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Malwi farm kitchens roast parathas in home-churned ghee; bilona ghee brings back that caramel-milk aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A spoon of wood-pressed groundnut oil in the tempering doubles the peanut aroma at the heart of this filling

steps: Knead 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and around 1 cup water into a soft, elastic dough and rest it for 20 minutes.
Toast 3 dried red chillies and 2 tsp coriander seeds in a dry pan on low for 2 minutes until crisp, then pound them in a mortar with 8 garlic cloves and 0.25 tsp salt into a coarse, rustic paste.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in the same pan, fry the pounded paste for 1 minute until the raw garlic smell fades, and take it off the heat.
Crush 0.5 cup roasted peanuts coarsely and mix with 3 finely chopped, salted and squeezed onions, the fried garlic paste, 1 tsp amchur and 0.25 tsp turmeric.
Fill 8 dough balls with 2 tbsp of the peanut-garlic masala each, seal firmly and roll gently into 6-inch rounds so the nutty bits do not puncture the dough.
Roast on a medium tava about 2 minutes per side, adding 0.5 tsp Anveshan Ghee at each flip, until the crust is burnished brown and smells of toasted nuts.
Cool on a rack for 2 minutes; the peanut filling turns crunchier as the steam escapes.
tips: Rub the roasted peanuts in a kitchen towel first to flake off the papery skins, which can taste bitter.
Frying the pounded garlic briefly keeps its punch but removes the raw hotness that can overpower the peanuts.
For an Indori touch, stir a tablespoon of crushed sev into the filling just before stuffing.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with green coriander chutney, a bowl of jeera-spiked chaas, and a few pickled green chillies; on cold Malwa mornings it is eaten with hot sweet milk on the side.

variations.name: Classic Masala Carrot Paratha
variations.description: A spice-forward carrot paratha where a proper masala base of onion, ginger-garlic, garam masala and coriander powder is sautéed with the grated carrot before it is stuffed into khapli atta dough. The cooked filling tastes like a dry carrot sabzi wrapped in a ghee-crisp shell. This is the paratha to make when plain carrot paratha feels too polite.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The sturdy emmer dough seals the masala filling without tearing

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Blooming the garam masala in bilona ghee is what makes this filling sing

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, 0.75 tsp salt and roughly 0.75 cup water into a soft, stretchy dough; rest it covered for 15 minutes while you cook the filling.
Heat 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a kadhai over medium heat and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds for about 20 seconds, then add 1 finely chopped medium onion and fry 3 to 4 minutes until the edges brown.

Stir in 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute until the raw smell goes, then add 1.5 tsp coriander powder, 0.75 tsp red chilli powder, 0.25 tsp turmeric powder and 1 tsp garam masala and toast the spices for 30 seconds.

Add 2 cups grated carrot and 0.5 tsp salt and sauté on medium-high for 5 to 6 minutes until the carrot wilts, dries out and takes on the masala's colour; spread on a plate to cool fully, then divide into 8 portions of about 2 tbsp.
Shape the dough into 8 balls, open each into a small cup, enclose one portion of masala carrot, pinch shut and roll softly into a 6-inch round on a floured surface.

Roast each paratha on a hot tava for about 1 minute per side until brown spots develop, then brush both faces using the remaining 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and cook another 30 seconds per side until crisp and glossy.
tips: The filling must be dry enough to hold in a loose ball; if it glistens with moisture, cook it 2 more minutes.
Cool the filling completely before stuffing; warm filling steams the dough from inside and tears it.
Grate the carrot on the coarse side for this version so it keeps some bite through the sauté.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with boondi raita and sliced onions sprinkled with chaat masala, or wrap around a spoon of curd for a quick roll.

variations.name: Punjabi Masala Carrot Paratha
variations.description: The Amritsari-style upgrade: the carrot masala is spiked with anardana and crushed coriander seeds, the dough carries ajwain, and the finished paratha gets its ritual dollop of white butter. It is roasted until deeply blistered, the way roadside dhabas do over high flame. Expect a tangy, buttery, faintly smoky flatbread that eats like a meal.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Wholegrain kick that stands its ground against dhaba-level spicing

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Generous ghee-basting is the Punjabi signature; bilona ghee crisps without burning

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 0.5 tsp ajwain, 0.75 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and close to 0.75 cup water into a soft dough; cover with a damp cloth and rest 15 minutes.
Coarsely crush 1 tbsp coriander seeds in a mortar; the split seeds should look cracked, not powdered, for that dhaba crunch.
Melt 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pan on medium flame, sizzle the crushed coriander seeds for 30 seconds, then add julienned 1.5 inch ginger and 2 chopped green chillies and fry another 30 seconds.

Add 2 cups grated carrot, 0.5 tsp salt and 0.75 tsp garam masala; cook 5 minutes on medium-high, tossing often, until the carrot is dry and lightly caramelised at the edges. Off the heat, mix in 1 tsp anardana powder and cool the filling before dividing into 8 mounds of about 2 tbsp.
Ball the dough into 8 pieces, stuff each with a mound of filling, seal the pleats downward and roll to a stout 5.5-inch round so the crust bakes up thick and flaky.

Roast on a hot tava at medium-high for about 90 seconds per side, then lavish both sides with the remaining 2.5 tbsp Anveshan Ghee divided across the batch and flip twice until dark blisters form. Crown each hot paratha with 1 tbsp white butter at the table.
tips: Crushed coriander seeds fried in ghee are safe and crunchy; never mix raw whole seeds directly into the filling.
For a smoky dhaba note, finish each paratha 10 seconds directly over the open flame with tongs.
Anardana loses its tang if cooked long, so always stir it in off the heat.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with dahi sprinkled with black salt, punchy mango pickle and a tall glass of sweet lassi to complete the highway-dhaba experience.

variations.name: Odia Masala Carrot Paratha
variations.description: Odisha's five-spice blend, panch phoron, is bloomed in pungent mustard oil and tossed through the carrot masala, giving this paratha bursts of fenugreek bitterness, fennel sweetness and kalonji's oniony edge. A hint of grated ginger and green chilli keeps it fresh rather than heavy. It is a quietly brilliant, homestyle take you rarely see outside Odia kitchens.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Rustic emmer flour matches Odisha's earthy, unfussy flavours

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Kachi ghani pungency is essential for blooming panch phoron the Odia way

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A finishing brush of ghee rounds the mustard oil's sharp edge

steps: Make the dough by rubbing 1 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil and 0.75 tsp salt into 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta, then kneading with about 0.75 cup water until smooth and soft; rest 15 minutes under a bowl.

Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil in a kadhai until faint wisps of smoke appear, lower the flame, and sputter 1.5 tsp panch phoron for about 25 seconds until the fenugreek seeds darken a shade and smell nutty.
Add grated 1 inch ginger and 2 slit green chillies, stir 30 seconds, then tip in 2 cups grated carrot with 0.5 tsp turmeric powder, 1 tsp coriander powder and 0.5 tsp salt.
Sauté on medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes until the carrot collapses and the pan looks dry; fold in 2 tbsp chopped coriander leaves, cool fully, and divide into 8 portions of about 2 tbsp each.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, cup one in your palm, seat a portion of filling inside, pleat closed and roll out gently to a 6-inch circle.

Cook each paratha on a medium-hot tava for around 1 minute per side until freckled brown, then brush lightly with the 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee shared across the batch and toast 30 seconds more per side until crisp.
tips: Do not let the fenugreek in panch phoron blacken; burnt methi seeds turn the whole filling bitter.
Smoking the mustard oil once before tempering softens its raw pungency, an old Odia kitchen rule.
This filling doubles as a side dish; make extra and serve it with dal-rice the next day.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with dahi baigana (Odia yoghurt-eggplant relish) or simply thick curd and a green chilli; a spoon of tomato khajuri chutney makes it festive.

variations.name: Kerala Masala Carrot Paratha
variations.description: The carrot masala here is treated like a Kerala thoran: mustard seeds and curry leaves crackled in coconut oil, then grated coconut and black pepper folded through the spiced carrot. The coconut keeps the stuffing succulent and subtly sweet against the peppery heat. Roasted in virgin coconut oil, the paratha smells of a Malabar kitchen at breakfast time.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Soft emmer wheat wraps the juicy coconut-carrot thoran without splitting

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: Cold-pressed coconut oil is the backbone of thoran flavour, in the pan and on the tava

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil, 0.75 tsp salt and around 0.75 cup water into a supple dough; cover and rest for 15 minutes.

Warm 1 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil in a kadhai over medium heat, pop 0.75 tsp mustard seeds for 20 seconds, then add 12 curry leaves, 4 sliced shallots and 2 chopped green chillies and fry 1 minute until the shallots soften.
Add 2 cups grated carrot, 0.25 tsp turmeric powder and 0.5 tsp salt; sauté for 4 minutes on medium heat until the carrot turns tender and dry.
Fold in 0.5 cup fresh grated coconut and 1 tsp coarsely crushed black pepper and toast 2 minutes more until the coconut smells nutty; cool completely and split into 8 portions of about 2 tbsp.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, flatten each into a cup, tuck a portion of the thoran filling inside, seal firmly and roll into a gentle 6-inch round.
Roast on a medium tava for about 1 minute per side until golden freckles show, then drizzle a share of the last 1 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil over each and crisp for 30 seconds per side.
tips: Squeeze the grated carrot before sautéing so the coconut does not swim in carrot juice.
Fresh-cracked pepper added at the end keeps its bright heat; pre-ground pepper tastes flat here.
The parathas reheat beautifully in a dry pan for 40 seconds per side; avoid the microwave, which softens the crust.
variations.servingSuggestion: Pair with a chilled glass of sambharam (spiced buttermilk) and a wedge of lime pickle, or serve alongside egg roast for a Malabar-style brunch.

variations.name: Malwa Masala Carrot Paratha
variations.description: From the Malwa plateau of Madhya Pradesh comes this rustic version where roasted peanut crush thickens the carrot masala and coriander-fennel spicing gives it a bazaar-style warmth. The peanuts toast further on the tava, so the paratha crackles softly as you tear it. It is farm food: filling, nutty and made for big appetites.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Stone-ground emmer echoes the wholegrain rotis of Malwa farm kitchens

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Wood-pressed groundnut oil deepens the peanut theme from filling to crust

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A final ghee gloss gives the rustic paratha a festive finish

steps: Rub 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and 0.75 tsp salt into 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta and knead with roughly 0.75 cup water into a soft, springy dough; rest it 15 minutes.
Pound 0.5 cup roasted peanuts in a mortar to a coarse rubble with a few larger pieces; set aside.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a kadhai on medium flame, sizzle 1 tsp fennel seeds for 20 seconds until fragrant, then add grated 1 inch ginger and stir for 30 seconds.

Add 2 cups grated carrot, 1.5 tsp coriander powder, 0.75 tsp red chilli powder and 0.5 tsp salt; cook 5 minutes on medium-high until the carrot is dry and jammy at the edges. Mix in the peanut rubble and 3 tbsp chopped coriander, cool, and shape into 8 portions of about 2 tbsp.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, stuff each with one peanut-carrot portion, seal the seams well and roll into a 6-inch round with a light hand so the peanut bits do not poke through.

Roast each paratha on a hot tava for about 1 minute per side until brown patches appear, then brush with a share of the 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and give each side 30 seconds more until crisp and nut-scented.
tips: Keep the peanut crush coarse; fine powder makes the filling dense and dry.
If the filling feels crumbly, a teaspoon of hot water and a quick knead of the mixture brings it together.
These parathas travel well; the peanut filling holds moisture without going soggy for a full day.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with green coriander chutney thinned with curd and a raw mango slaw; in Malwa homes it goes with a tumbler of thick buttermilk.

variations.name: Classic Spicy Mooli Paratha
variations.description: Winter's favourite paratha: sharp white radish squeezed dry, punched up with green chilli, black pepper and ajwain, and sealed inside khapli wheat dough before a ghee roast. Squeezing and re-seasoning the mooli is the whole craft — done right, the paratha is crisp outside and juicy, peppery inside without a hint of sogginess.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Emmer's sturdy crumb resists the moisture that radish inevitably releases on the tava

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A hot ghee roast is what turns sharp raw mooli mellow and sweet inside the crust

steps: Grate 400 g white radish finely, toss with 1/2 tsp salt and rest 15 minutes; meanwhile knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, 1/2 tsp salt and about 3/4 cup water into a soft dough and set it aside covered.
Squeeze the salted radish hard in fistfuls, then again in a muslin cloth, until you extract nearly half a cup of liquid and the shreds feel almost dry.

Season the squeezed mooli with 3 minced green chillies, 3/4 tsp black pepper, 1/2 tsp ajwain, 1/2 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1/4 tsp turmeric and 3 tbsp chopped coriander — no extra salt, the shreds carry enough.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and the filling into 8 portions of 2 tbsp each; cup a ball, pack in the mooli, pleat the edges shut and roll gently into a 6-inch round, dusting whenever it sticks.

Roast on a medium-hot tava for 1 minute until the underside sets, flip, brush 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee per side and cook about 3 minutes total, pressing with a spatula, until both faces are patched golden-brown.
Serve straight off the tava; mooli parathas lose their crispness fastest of all, so roast in the order you eat.
tips: Save the squeezed radish juice — knead the next batch of dough with it for a bonus layer of mooli flavour and zero waste.
Salt the grated radish first and season after squeezing; salting the finished filling draws fresh water and sogs the paratha.
A 1/2 tsp of amchur in the filling brightens dull winter radishes noticeably.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with white butter and gud (jaggery) on the side in true winter style, plus a mug of adrak chai to chase the pepper heat.

variations.name: Punjabi Spicy Mooli Paratha
variations.description: The Ludhiana truck-stop original: radish shreds spiked with ginger, anardana and extra green chilli, stuffed thick, roasted hard in ghee and slathered with white butter while still crackling. Punjabi cooks roll these bigger and stuff them fuller than anyone else dares.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Strong emmer gluten lets you roll the overstuffed Punjabi way without blowouts

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Spooned liberally around the edges so the thick paratha fries through, dhaba fashion

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, 1/2 tsp salt and around 3/4 cup water into a soft, elastic dough; rest 20 minutes so it rolls thin over a fat filling.
Grate 400 g radish, salt it with 1/2 tsp salt for 15 minutes, then wring it dry in a cloth with all your strength — Punjabi parathas fail or fly on this squeeze.
Mix the dry shreds with 1.5 tbsp grated ginger, 4 minced green chillies, 1 tsp anardana powder, 1 tbsp crushed kasuri methi, 1/2 tsp garam masala and 3/4 tsp red chilli powder.
Make 6 larger dough balls (this style rolls to 8 inches) and pack each with a generous 3 tbsp of filling; pleat, twist off the excess dough at the top and flatten firmly.

Roll each to an 8-inch round and roast on a medium-high tava: 1 minute per side dry, then 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee spooned around the edges of each side and about 4 minutes more, pressing hard, until the crust crackles deep brown.
Finish every paratha with a spoon of white butter melting over the ridges before it reaches the plate.
tips: Six big parathas, not eight small — the high filling-to-dough ratio is exactly what makes this taste dhaba-made.
Anardana against sharp radish is the signature Punjabi pairing; skip it and the filling tastes flat.
If the radish is late-season and bitter, blanch the shreds 1 minute in boiling water before squeezing.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a slab of white butter, mango pickle and a steel glass of salted lassi; the classic winter add-on is a bowl of dal makhani for dunking torn edges.

variations.name: Bengali Spicy Mooli Paratha
variations.description: Bengal treats mulo with mustard, and this porota honours that: the radish is sautéed in smoked kachi ghani mustard oil with nigella and green chilli until sweet, then stuffed and roasted. The cooked filling makes this the most forgiving mooli paratha to roll.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Wholegrain emmer gives the porota a rustic bite that suits mustard-cooked vegetables

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Radish sautéed in pungent wood-pressed mustard oil is a straight lift from Bengali mulo bhaja

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: The final ghee brushing rounds off the mustard sharpness with dairy sweetness

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil, 1/2 tsp salt and about 3/4 cup water into a soft dough; rest it 15 minutes under a damp cloth.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil in a kadhai until it just smokes and pales, about 1 minute, drop the heat to medium and crackle 1/2 tsp nigella seeds for 20 seconds.

Add 1 tbsp grated ginger and 3 slit green chillies, then 400 g grated radish with 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp sugar; sauté 8 minutes, stirring often, until the moisture cooks off and the shreds look glossy and dry. Cool fully and fold in 2 tbsp chopped coriander.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, stuff each with 2 tbsp of the cooled mulo filling, pinch the seams tight and roll into 6-inch rounds.
Roast on a medium tava for 1 minute per side until speckled, then brush both faces with the 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, shared across the batch, and cook 2 minutes more until the spots turn mahogany.
Rest the porotas under a cloth 2 minutes so the mustard-sweet filling perfumes the crumb before serving.
tips: Sautéing rather than raw-squeezing the radish is the Bengali advantage — the filling never leaks and tastes caramel-sweet.
Always let the mustard oil smoke briefly first; unsmoked it will dominate everything with raw pungency.
The filling keeps 2 days refrigerated, so make a double batch and roll fresh porotas both mornings.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with begun bhaja and a dab of kasundi; a few slices of cucumber and onion with a squeeze of gondhoraj or regular lime complete the Bengali plate.

variations.name: Rajasthani Spicy Mooli Paratha
variations.description: Desert-style heat: whole dried red chillies are bloomed in ghee and crushed through the radish along with coriander seeds and amchur, echoing the fierce, tangy masalas of Marwar. Radish leaves go into the filling too — Rajasthani thrift wastes nothing.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Hardy emmer wheat suits Rajasthan's rustic griddle breads better than refined flour ever could

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Marwari kitchens measure hospitality in ghee — it blooms the chillies and crisps the crust

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, 1/2 tsp salt and roughly 3/4 cup water into a firm-soft dough; rest 15 minutes.
Grate 400 g radish, finely shred its tender leaves, salt everything with 1/2 tsp salt for 15 minutes, then squeeze relentlessly in a cloth until the shreds are dry.

Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a small pan, bloom 4 broken dried red chillies, 2 tsp coriander seeds and 1 tsp fennel seeds over low heat for 90 seconds until deeply fragrant, then cool and crush coarsely in a mortar.
Toss the crushed masala through the squeezed radish and leaves along with 1 tsp amchur, 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1/4 tsp asafoetida.

Stuff 8 dough balls with 2 tbsp filling each, seal and roll to 6-inch rounds, then roast on a medium tava with 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee brushed per side for about 3 minutes each, pressing until the crust blisters russet-brown.
Stack in a cloth-lined basket; in Rajasthan these travel well and taste just as good at room temperature two hours later.
tips: Blooming the whole spices in ghee before crushing is non-negotiable — raw coriander seeds would stay woody in the filling.
The radish leaves add a peppery mustard-green note; if yours came leafless, add a handful of chopped methi instead.
For an authentic travel meal, roast these with an extra minute per side until crackery — they keep half a day unrefrigerated.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with garlicky lehsun chutney, a katori of plain curd and slivered onions sprinkled with salt and lime — the classic Marwari roadside spread.

variations.name: Kumaoni Spicy Mooli Paratha
variations.description: From the Uttarakhand hills, where jakhya — wild mustard seed with a crackling nuttiness cumin cannot match — is the tempering of choice. Hill radishes are sweeter and hotter at once, and this paratha layers that sharpness with pahadi coriander-chilli notes and a mountain-style ghee finish.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Closest lowland cousin to the hardy hill wheats Kumaoni families grind for their rotis

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Pahadi kitchens finish griddle breads with homestead ghee — bilona is the honest match

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Jakhya seeds are always crackled in mustard oil in Kumaon — the two are inseparable

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, 1/2 tsp salt and about 3/4 cup water into a smooth, soft dough and rest it 15 minutes in a covered bowl.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil in a kadhai until it faintly smokes, lower the heat and crackle 1 tsp jakhya seeds for 30 seconds — they should pop and smell nutty, not scorch.

Add 4 sliced garlic cloves and 3 chopped green chillies, fry 1 minute until the garlic edges gild, then tip in 400 g grated radish with 1 tsp coriander powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt; sauté 7 minutes until dry and sweet-smelling. Cool, then fold in 3 tbsp chopped coriander.
Portion the dough into 8 balls, fill each with 2 tbsp of the jakhya-radish mixture, seal the pleats and roll softly into 6-inch rounds.
Roast on a medium tava, brushing 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee per side, about 3 minutes per paratha until both faces carry toasted brown islands and the jakhya aroma lifts off the griddle.
Serve hot in twos; hill custom pairs each round with a spoon of fresh homemade curd on top rather than on the side.
tips: Jakhya burns two beats faster than cumin — pull the pan the moment the popping peaks.
No jakhya in the pantry? Brown mustard seeds plus a pinch of crushed cumin gets within shouting distance.
Grate the radish coarse for this version; the sauté keeps texture better than fine shreds do.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with bhang ki chutney (hemp-seed chutney) or a lime-mint chutney and hot glasses of buransh squash in season — a true Kumaoni hill breakfast.

variations.name: Classic Cheesy Methi Paratha
variations.description: Fresh fenugreek's pleasant bitterness against stretchy melted cheese is a pairing that converts methi sceptics on the first bite. The chopped leaves are kneaded straight into the khapli dough as well as the filling, so every layer carries that green, faintly maple-like aroma.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Emmer's nutty depth is the classic partner to bitter greens in heritage wheat rotis

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee mellows methi's edge on the tava the way no neutral oil can

steps: Wash and finely chop 2 cups of fresh fenugreek leaves; knead half of them into 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, 1/2 tsp salt and about 3/4 cup water until soft and springy, then rest 15 minutes.
Sauté the remaining chopped methi in 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee over medium heat for 3 minutes until wilted and dry, then cool completely.

Mix the cooled methi with 100 g grated mozzarella, 100 g crumbled paneer, 2 minced green chillies, 1 tbsp grated ginger, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1/2 tsp red chilli powder, 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt.
Divide the green-flecked dough into 8 balls, stuff each with 2 tbsp of filling, pleat closed and roll gently to a 6-inch round.
Roast on a medium tava for 1 minute until bubbles rise, flip, brush 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee per side and cook about 3 minutes total, pressing the edges, until deep golden spots cover both faces.
Rest each paratha 1 minute off the heat so the cheese sets to a pull instead of a spill.
tips: Wilting the filling methi first stops it leaking bitter juices into the cheese as the paratha cooks.
If your methi is very bitter, toss the chopped leaves with a pinch of salt, rest 10 minutes and squeeze before using.
Tender stems chop in fine with the leaves; only the thick lower stalks need discarding.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a bowl of plain curd swirled with a drop of honey and a sharp lemon pickle — sweetness and sour both flatter methi.

variations.name: Gujarati Cheesy Methi Paratha
variations.description: Gujarat's beloved methi-gol pairing, cheesed: jaggery powder is worked into the dough alongside fenugreek exactly as in classic methi na thepla, so every bite runs sweet-bitter-salty before the cheese melt arrives. Sesame seeds toast on the crust for the full thepla character.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Emmer takes to thepla-style spiced dough beautifully, staying soft for hours

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: The sweet counterweight to methi's bitterness that defines Gujarati thepla dough

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Gujarati griddles run on peanut oil — wood-pressed keeps the flavour honest

steps: Dissolve 2 tbsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder in 2 tbsp warm water. Combine 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1.5 cups finely chopped fenugreek leaves, 2 tsp sesame seeds, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 3/4 tsp salt, 1 tbsp grated ginger and 2 minced green chillies.
Add the jaggery water, 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and enough plain water (about 1/2 cup more) to knead a soft, thepla-style dough; rest it 15 minutes so the methi softens into the crumb.
Sauté the remaining 1/2 cup chopped methi in 1 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil for 2 minutes until wilted, cool, and mix with 100 g grated processed cheese and 1/4 tsp salt for the filling.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, cup each around 1.5 tbsp of the cheese-methi mixture, seal the pleats and roll gently into thin 6-inch rounds.

Cook on a medium tava for about 3 minutes per paratha, flipping twice and drizzling 1/2 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil per side, until the surface blisters with amber-brown spots and the sesame smells toasty.
Stack in a covered box; like thepla, these actually improve as they sit, staying soft for hours.
tips: Dissolving the jaggery first is essential — undissolved granules scorch into dark specks on the tava.
Roll these thinner than a standard stuffed paratha; the thepla character lives in the thin, pliable crumb.
They travel superbly: wrap a stack in foil for tiffins or train journeys and eat at room temperature with pickle.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve Gujarati-style with chundo (sweet mango pickle), a bowl of curd and a hot cup of adrak-elaichi chai on the side.

variations.name: Maharashtrian Cheesy Methi Paratha
variations.description: Smoky goda masala and crushed roasted peanuts turn the methi-cheese filling into something closer to a stuffed methi-chi-bhaji flatbread from a Pune wada. The peanuts crunch, the cheese stretches, and goda's stone-flower muskiness ties the bitter greens together.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The Deccan's affection for rustic grains makes emmer a natural for this filling

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Maharashtrian bhaji starts in peanut oil, and this methi filling follows suit

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A spoonful in the dough for softness while the peanut oil handles the griddle

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, 1/2 tsp salt and about 3/4 cup water into a soft dough; rest it 15 minutes under a damp cloth.

Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a kadhai, fry 4 sliced garlic cloves and 2 chopped green chillies for 1 minute until the garlic gilds, then wilt 2 cups chopped fenugreek leaves with 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt for 3 minutes until dry.
Stir 2 tsp goda masala into the hot methi, cook 30 seconds to wake the spices, then cool fully and fold in 100 g grated mozzarella and 3 tbsp coarsely crushed roasted peanuts.
Stuff 8 dough balls with 2 tbsp of filling each, seal the gathers and roll softly into 6-inch rounds.
Roast on a medium tava, drizzling 1/2 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil per side, about 3 minutes per paratha until both faces blister nut-brown and the goda aroma turns smoky-sweet.
Rest a minute so the peanut crunch settles into the melted cheese before cutting.
tips: Bloom the goda masala in the hot greens for those 30 seconds — raw goda tastes dusty, bloomed goda tastes of caramel and stone flower.
Crush the peanuts pebble-coarse; fine powder disappears into the cheese and forfeits the crunch.
No goda masala? Toast 1 tsp sesame, 1 tsp dry coconut and 1/2 tsp cumin, grind, and add a pinch of cinnamon.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a fiery dry lasun (garlic) chutney sprinkled alongside and a glass of mattha — the buttermilk's salt and cumin reset the palate between rich bites.

variations.name: Punjabi Cheesy Methi Paratha
variations.description: Built like a winter sarson-season breakfast in Jalandhar: methi wilted with ginger and green chilli, doubled with kasuri methi for intensity, bound with cheddar and roasted hard in ghee. A knob of white butter melting on the ridges finishes it the only way Punjab knows.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Its strong crumb rolls thick and roasts crisp, the way Punjabi winter parathas demand

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Generous edge-spooned ghee is the engine of the crackling dhaba crust

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, 1/2 tsp salt and roughly 3/4 cup water into a supple dough; rest it 20 minutes.
Wilt 2 cups chopped fenugreek leaves in 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee with 1 tbsp grated ginger and 3 minced green chillies over medium heat for 3 minutes until the pan is dry, then cool.
Crush 1 tbsp kasuri methi between your palms into the cooled greens and mix in 100 g grated cheddar, 1 tsp anardana powder, 1/2 tsp garam masala and 1/2 tsp salt.
Make 6 large dough balls and pack each with a generous 3 tbsp of the double-methi filling; twist the seal shut, flatten and roll to 7-inch rounds.
Roast on a medium-high tava, 45 seconds dry per side, then spoon 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee around the rim of each side and press-roast about 4 minutes until the crust crackles deep brown.
Top each paratha with 1/2 tbsp white butter the instant it leaves the tava so it melts into the ridges.
tips: Fresh plus kasuri methi is the Punjabi doubling trick — fresh gives body, dried gives that dhaba-intense perfume.
Anardana's sourness rescues the filling from bitterness-on-bitterness; amchur substitutes at a pinch.
Roll these thick; a thin shell cannot hold this much filling through the hard ghee roast.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a tall glass of namkeen lassi, gajar ka achaar and, in season, a ladle of sarson ka saag for the complete Punjabi winter table.

variations.name: Tamil Cheesy Methi Paratha
variations.description: Methi meets the Tamil tempering kit: mustard seeds, urad dal, dried red chilli and curry leaves crackled in gingelly oil, folded through the wilted greens with cheese for melt. It tastes like vendhaya keerai poriyal reborn as a griddle bread — bitter, nutty, gently hot.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: A wholegrain canvas for a keerai-style filling, sturdier than any parotta maida

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sesame Oil
ingredients.note: Gingelly oil's toasted depth is the traditional Tamil frame for bitter greens

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A thin finishing film, tiffin-room style, to gloss the roasted crust

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tsp Anveshan Sesame Oil, 1/2 tsp salt and about 3/4 cup water into a smooth, soft dough; rest 15 minutes covered.

Heat the remaining Anveshan Sesame Oil in a kadhai over medium heat, pop 1 tsp mustard seeds completely, then brown 1 tsp urad dal with 2 torn dried red chillies for 40 seconds until the dal turns biscuit-gold.

Crisp 3 sprigs of curry leaves in the same oil, then wilt 2 cups chopped fenugreek leaves with 1/2 tsp salt for 3 minutes until the pan runs dry; cool fully and fold in 100 g grated mozzarella and 1/2 tsp black pepper.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, fill each with 2 tbsp of the tempered methi-cheese, pleat closed and roll into 6-inch rounds with light pressure.
Cook each paratha on a medium tava about 3 minutes, flipping twice and brushing a thin film of Anveshan Ghee per side, until lacy golden-brown spots cover both faces.
Rest briefly under a cloth so the urad crunch and cheese pull reach their best together.
tips: Brown the urad dal properly — its nutty crunch is the counterpoint that makes bitter greens sing in Tamil cooking.
Never cover the wilting methi; trapped steam turns the greens swampy and dulls their colour.
A pinch of asafoetida with the tempering adds authentic keerai-poriyal depth if your pantry has it.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with coconut chutney and a tumbler of thin, peppery rasam for dipping; end with strong filter coffee, tumbler-frothed.

variations.name: Classic Cheesy Mixed Veg Paratha
variations.description: The paratha that gets vegetables past the fussiest eaters: a spiced carrot-pea-potato mash bound with molten mozzarella inside a golden khapli crust. The cheese melts into the mash so every bite is creamy rather than stringy in one spot and dry in another. A ghee roast finishes it with a crisp, fragrant shell.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The fibre-rich emmer crust quietly balances the indulgence of a cheese-filled centre

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Bilona ghee crisps the shell so the contrast with the gooey filling is at its dramatic best

steps: Knead 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and about 1 cup water into a soft, elastic dough. Rest it under a damp cloth for 20 minutes.
Steam 1 large diced potato, 1 chopped carrot, 0.5 cup peas and 0.5 cup corn for 10-12 minutes until soft, then drain very well and mash coarsely, leaving the corn mostly whole.
Season the warm mash with 1 inch of grated ginger, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1 tsp chilli flakes, 0.25 tsp salt and 3 tbsp chopped coriander, then spread it out to cool completely.
Only once cool, fold in 1 cup grated mozzarella; mixing cheese into warm mash makes it melt prematurely and turn the filling sticky.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, cup each one, pack in about 3 tbsp of the cheesy mash, seal the pleats tightly and roll gently to a 6 inch round.
Roast on a medium tava for around 2 minutes per side, brushing on the remaining 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, until golden-brown spots cover both faces and the edges sizzle crisp.
Rest each paratha for a minute before slicing so the cheese thickens to a slow, satisfying pull.
tips: Cool the mash fully before adding cheese; warm mash melts it early and makes rolling messy.
Corn kernels left whole give sweet pops that children especially love.
If rolling tears the dough, patch with a pinch of dry atta and finish with lighter strokes.
variations.servingSuggestion: Cut into quarters and serve with ketchup for kids and spicy mint chutney for the grown-ups, plus a mug of masala chai.

variations.name: Delhi-style Cheesy Mixed Veg Paratha
variations.description: Straight from the spirit of Chandni Chowk's Paranthe Wali Gali, this version loads the cheesy vegetable filling with warm garam masala, chaat masala and slivered ginger. It is roasted darker than most, so the crust develops the toasty street-side character Delhi swears by. Sharp, spicy and made for pairing with tangy banana-tamarind chutney.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Old-Delhi paranthas were always wholegrain; khapli restores that pre-maida authenticity

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Paranthe Wali Gali fries in desi ghee by the ladleful, and bilona ghee recreates that unmistakable aroma

steps: Make a soft dough from 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and roughly 1 cup water; knead well and rest for 20 minutes.
Steam 1 large diced potato, 1 cup cauliflower florets and 0.5 cup peas for 12 minutes until yielding, drain thoroughly and mash to a rough, rubbly texture.

Mix in 1.5 inches of slivered ginger, 2 minced green chillies, 1.5 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp chaat masala, 0.25 tsp salt and 3 tbsp chopped coriander while the mash is warm, then cool it fully on a plate.
Fold 1 cup grated processed cheese through the cooled mash until evenly distributed in salty little pockets.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, stuff each with 3 tbsp of the masala-cheese filling, twist the gathered edges closed and roll to 6 inch rounds.
Roast on a medium-high tava for 2-2.5 minutes per side, generously brushing on the remaining 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, until the crust turns a shade darker than golden with proper toasty brown patches.
Sprinkle a pinch of chaat masala over the hot crust just before serving for that final street-side flourish.
tips: Slivered ginger, not paste, is the Delhi signature; you should meet sharp ginger threads in the bites.
Roast slightly darker than instinct suggests; the extra toast is what evokes the gali flavour.
Processed cheese holds salt better than mozzarella here and will not water down the masala.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve the old-Delhi way with sweet banana-tamarind chutney, spicy aloo sabzi and a small tumbler of sweet lassi.

variations.name: Tamil Cheesy Mixed Veg Paratha
variations.description: A curry-leaf tadka in wood-pressed sesame oil turns this cheesy vegetable paratha unmistakably Tamilian. Mustard seeds, urad dal and sambar powder season the mash so the cheese carries fragrant, earthy spice rather than plain richness. It tastes like the best bits of a vegetable uttapam and a cheese sandwich in one bread.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Emmer's gentle sweetness mirrors the fermented mellowness Tamil griddle batters bring to their toppings

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sesame Oil
ingredients.note: Nallennai, wood-pressed gingelly oil, is Tamil Nadu's heritage fat and gives the crust its toasty depth

steps: Knead 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil and about 1 cup water into a supple dough; let it rest 20 minutes.
Steam 1 large diced potato, 1 chopped carrot and 0.5 cup chopped beans for 10-12 minutes until tender, drain fully and mash coarsely.

Heat 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil on medium, crackle 1 tsp mustard seeds for 30 seconds, add 1 tsp urad dal and fry to a biscuit gold, then sizzle the leaves of 2 curry sprigs and 2 chopped green chillies for 20 seconds.
Add the mash with 2 tsp sambar powder and 0.25 tsp salt, stir over low heat for 2 minutes until the spices cling to the vegetables, then cool completely and fold in 1 cup grated mozzarella.
Shape 8 balls of dough, load each with 3 tbsp of the tadka-cheese mash, pleat and seal firmly, then roll into 6 inch rounds.
Griddle over medium heat for about 2 minutes per side with the remaining 0.5 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil trickled around the edges, until toasty brown speckles bloom and the sesame aroma rises.
Cool a minute on a rack so the base keeps its crunch against the molten centre.
tips: Do not rush the urad dal past biscuit-gold, or a bitter note will run through the entire filling.
Sambar powders vary; taste the seasoned mash before adding cheese and adjust upward if needed.
Day-old parathas revive beautifully on a dry tava with a few drops of sesame oil.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with coconut chutney and piping-hot sambar for dipping, finishing with a strong davara-tumbler filter coffee.

variations.name: Assamese Cheesy Mixed Veg Paratha
variations.description: Assam brings the world's fiercest chilli to the party: a whisper of bhut jolokia laced through a gentle vegetable-cheese mash, mellowed in mustard oil. The trick is restraint, letting the ghost chilli's fruity, smoky heat build slowly under the cool cheese. It is a daring, addictive paratha for committed heat-seekers.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The sturdy wholegrain wrapper tempers the ghost chilli's blaze better than refined flour would

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Assamese kitchens run on pungent mustard oil, whose sharpness frames the bhut jolokia's fruity fire

steps: Knead 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta, 1 tsp salt and 1 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil with about 1 cup water into a smooth dough; rest 20 minutes covered.
Steam 2 diced potatoes, 1 chopped carrot and 0.5 cup peas for 12 minutes until soft, then drain and mash coarsely.

Wearing care with your hands, mince half a small bhut jolokia very finely; heat 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil to a light smoke, cool it slightly, then fry the chilli with 6 sliced garlic cloves and 1 chopped onion for 3-4 minutes until softened and golden.
Combine the tempering with the mash, 0.5 tsp turmeric and 0.25 tsp salt, cook 2 minutes to dry it out, then cool fully and fold in 1 cup grated mozzarella and 3 tbsp chopped coriander.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, fill each with 3 tbsp of the ghost-chilli mash, seal the pleats and roll softly into 6 inch rounds.
Cook on a medium tava for about 2 minutes per side, trickling the remaining 0.5 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil around the rim, until amber-brown blisters spread across the crust.
Let them rest 2 minutes; the heat integrates and the first bite arrives fruity before the slow burn builds.
tips: Half a bhut jolokia for 8 parathas is genuinely enough; you can always serve extra chilli on the side.
Wash hands, knife and board immediately after mincing the chilli, and avoid touching your face.
The cheese is not just indulgence here; its fat actively buffers capsaicin, so do not reduce it.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with cooling cucumber raita and a wedge of lime; a glass of milk on standby is not a joke with this one.

variations.name: Punjabi Cheesy Mixed Veg Paratha
variations.description: A dhaba-style heavyweight where the vegetable-cheese filling is enriched with kasuri methi, ajwain-scented dough and a finishing knob of white butter. Rolled thick and roasted dark in ghee, it has the plush, buttery excess Punjab is loved for. This is weekend-brunch food, best followed by a nap.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Chakki-style stone-ground khapli gives the thick Punjabi round its hearty, rustic crumb

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Repeated ghee bastings on a hot tava build the layered, charred crust every dhaba chases

steps: Knead 1 tsp ajwain and 1 tsp salt into 2.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and about 1 cup water; work it 8 minutes into a plush dough and rest 20 minutes.
Steam 2 diced potatoes, 1 cup cauliflower florets and 0.5 cup peas for 12 minutes until completely soft, drain and mash with visible chunks remaining.
Season the warm mash with 1 tbsp palm-crushed kasuri methi, 1 tsp garam masala, 2 minced green chillies and 0.25 tsp salt, then spread it thin to cool quickly.
Work 1 cup grated cheese through the cooled mash so it clumps into a rich, cohesive stuffing; divide into 8 portions of about 3 tbsp.
Stuff 8 dough balls with the portions, seal the pleats into a topknot and roll into thick 6 inch rounds; thickness keeps the interior fluffy and molten.
Roast on a medium-hot tava for 2-3 minutes per side with the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, pressing the edges down, until dark golden charred patches develop on both faces.
Crown each hot paratha with a share of the 2 tbsp white butter and serve as it melts down the crust.
tips: Crush kasuri methi between your palms over the mash; the friction wakes up its aroma.
A thick roll is deliberate; thin rolling makes this filling burst and the cheese scorch on the tava.
Amul-style processed cheese survives dhaba-level heat better than fresh mozzarella in this version.
variations.servingSuggestion: Plate with dahi, mango pickle and a tall sweet lassi; for full effect add a side of sliced onions and a green chilli.

variations.name: Classic Cheesy Mooli Paratha
variations.description: An unlikely but brilliant pairing: peppery squeezed radish shreds bound with melting cheese, so the filling stays juicy yet never leaks. The cheese cushions mooli's sharpness for children while the khapli crust roasted in bilona ghee keeps it honest breakfast food.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Emmer's tight crumb walls in both the cheese melt and the radish juices

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A steady ghee roast browns the crust before the cheese inside can overheat and split

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, 1/2 tsp salt and about 3/4 cup water into a soft, smooth dough; rest 15 minutes under a cover.
Grate 300 g radish, salt it with 1/4 tsp salt for 15 minutes, then squeeze mercilessly in a muslin cloth until barely damp — cheese and wet radish cannot share a paratha.
Toss the dry shreds with 100 g grated mozzarella, 2 minced green chillies, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1/2 tsp red chilli powder and 3 tbsp chopped coriander.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and the filling into 8 portions of 2 tbsp; stuff, pleat the tops closed and roll each into a 6-inch round with a gentle touch over the centre.
Roast on a medium tava for 1 minute until the base sets, flip, brush 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee per side and cook about 3 minutes total, pressing lightly, until both faces are patched deep gold.
Rest 1 minute so the cheese thickens from liquid to stretchy before you cut in.
tips: Mix cheese into the radish only at stuffing time; standing together they weep and the seams give way.
If rolling feels risky, cook these as folded half-moons instead — same filling, half the blowout danger.
A rasp of lemon zest in the filling is unconventional but lifts the radish beautifully.
variations.servingSuggestion: Cut into quarters and serve with a bowl of tomato-garlic chutney for dipping; a glass of jeera chaas balances the dairy.

variations.name: Punjabi Cheesy Mooli Paratha
variations.description: Dhaba maximalism: ginger-anardana mooli shreds knitted with cheddar, stuffed into an ajwain crust, ghee-roasted until shattering-crisp and buried under melting white butter. The sour anardana keeps all that dairy from cloying — a trick every Punjabi cook knows by heart.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Robust emmer dough takes the heavy cheese-radish stuffing rolled dhaba-thick

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Edge-spooned onto the tava so the thick paratha shallow-fries crisp all the way through

steps: Rub 1/2 tsp ajwain into 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and 1/2 tsp salt, then knead with about 3/4 cup water into a supple dough; rest it 20 minutes.
Grate 300 g radish, salt lightly with 1/4 tsp salt for 15 minutes and wring it dry in a cloth until no drips remain under pressure.
Combine the dry shreds with 100 g grated cheddar, 1 tbsp grated ginger, 3 minced green chillies, 1 tsp anardana powder and 1/2 tsp garam masala, tossing so the cheese threads through evenly.
Shape 6 large balls and pack each with a generous 3 tbsp of filling; twist off excess dough at the seal, flatten firmly and roll to 7-inch rounds.

On a medium-high tava, cook each paratha 45 seconds per side dry, then spoon 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee around the rim of each side and roast about 4 minutes, pressing hard with the spatula, until crackly and mahogany-spotted.
Slide onto plates and crown at once with 1/2 tbsp white butter per paratha so it pools into the crisp ridges.
tips: Cheddar over mozzarella here — its sharpness argues back at the radish where mozzarella just surrenders.
Six thick parathas beat eight thin ones; thickness is the Punjabi signature and the cheese needs the insulation.
Roast a whole green chilli alongside on the tava and serve it blistered on top for the full dhaba flourish.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with sweet lassi in a tall steel glass, mixed-vegetable pickle and slivered radish salad sprinkled with chaat masala.

variations.name: Kerala Cheesy Mooli Paratha
variations.description: A backwater twist: the radish is sautéed thoran-style with grated coconut, curry leaves and mustard seeds in cold-pressed coconut oil, then bound with cheese for melt. Coconut and cheese turn out to be old friends — both rich, both sweet, both perfect against peppery mooli.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Wholegrain emmer plays the sturdy chapati to a thoran-style filling

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: Cold-pressed copra oil gives the crust the toasty scent of a Kerala tea-shop griddle

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil, 1/2 tsp salt and roughly 3/4 cup water into a soft, stretchy dough; rest 15 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil in a kadhai over medium heat, pop 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, then sizzle 2 sprigs of curry leaves and 2 chopped green chillies for 30 seconds.

Add 300 g grated radish with 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1/4 tsp salt; sauté 7 minutes until dry, then fold in 1/2 cup grated coconut and toast 2 minutes more until nutty. Cool completely and mix with 100 g grated mozzarella and 1/2 tsp black pepper.
Portion the dough into 8 balls, fill each with 2 tbsp of the coconut-cheese thoran, pinch closed and roll into 6-inch rounds.
Roast on a medium tava, drizzling 1/2 tsp Anveshan Coconut Oil per side, about 3 minutes per paratha until freckled golden and smelling of toasted coconut.
Rest a minute before slicing so the mozzarella sets into ribbons rather than rivers.
tips: Cool the sautéed radish-coconut fully before the cheese goes in, or the mozzarella melts prematurely into a clump.
Fresh or frozen grated coconut only; desiccated coconut drinks the filling dry.
A pinch of crushed black pepper pressed onto the rolled surface before roasting makes a fragrant peppered crust.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a sharp tomato-onion chammanthi or Kerala-style lime pickle, and cardamom tea rather than coffee to echo the coconut.

variations.name: Delhi Cheesy Mooli Paratha
variations.description: Paranthe-wali-gali energy: a garam-masala-forward mooli filling laced with cheese, rolled thin, and shallow-crisped in ghee till the surface bubbles like the old Chandni Chowk griddles. Amchur and chaat masala give it that unmistakable Delhi street tang.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Swaps the gali's refined flour for heritage emmer without losing the bubbled, crisp shell

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Paranthe-wali-gali parathas are practically shallow-fried — bilona ghee does it without heaviness

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, 1/2 tsp salt and about 3/4 cup water into a soft dough and rest it 15 minutes under a damp cloth.
Grate 300 g radish, salt with 1/4 tsp salt, stand 15 minutes and squeeze in a cloth until the shreds are quite dry.
Season the mooli with 100 g grated processed cheese, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp amchur, 1/2 tsp chaat masala, 2 minced green chillies, 1 tbsp grated ginger and 3 tbsp chopped coriander.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, stuff each with 2 tbsp filling, seal the pleats and roll thinner than usual — a scant 7-inch round — the gali style is wide and crisp.

Roast on a medium-high tava: 40 seconds dry per side, then 1.5 tsp Anveshan Ghee spooned over and around each paratha, pressing and rotating constantly for about 3 minutes until the surface bubbles and crisps deep gold.
Blot briefly on a plate, then serve stacked no more than two high so the shells stay shattery.
tips: Processed cheese is the right call here — it melts calmly and never floods a thin-rolled shell the way mozzarella can.
The double sour hit of amchur plus chaat masala is what says Delhi; halving either flattens the street flavour.
Rotate the paratha constantly during the ghee stage; the gali crispness comes from even contact, not more fat.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve the gali way: with sweet tamarind-banana chutney, spicy mint chutney and a tangle of pickled carrots — chai in a kulhad if you have one.

variations.name: Odia Cheesy Mooli Paratha
variations.description: Panch phoron — Odisha's five-spice of mustard, cumin, fennel, nigella and fenugreek — is bloomed in hot ghee and folded through sautéed radish before the cheese goes in. The fennel's sweetness and fenugreek's whisper of bitterness give this the layered, temple-town depth of an Odia bhaja.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Its earthy sweetness sits naturally beside fennel-led panch phoron

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Panch phoron must bloom in properly hot ghee to unlock all five aromas at once

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: A spoon in the dough nods to Odisha's everyday pressed mustard oil

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil, 1/2 tsp salt and about 3/4 cup water into a soft, elastic dough; rest 15 minutes covered.

Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a kadhai until properly hot, then bloom 1.5 tsp panch phoron for about 30 seconds until the mustard pops and the fennel smells sweet — do not let the fenugreek darken past golden.

Add 1 tbsp grated ginger and 2 chopped green chillies for 30 seconds, then 300 g grated radish with 1/2 tsp turmeric and 1/4 tsp salt; sauté 8 minutes until dry and glossy. Cool fully, then fold in 100 g grated mozzarella and 2 tbsp chopped coriander.
Shape 8 dough balls, tuck 2 tbsp of filling into each, pinch the seams and roll gently into 6-inch rounds.

Roast on a medium tava about 3 minutes per paratha, brushing each side with a share of the remaining Anveshan Ghee, until both faces carry warm brown freckles and the five-spice aroma blooms off the griddle.
Hold under a cloth for 2 minutes; the brief steam melds fennel, fenugreek and cheese into one rounded flavour.
tips: Watch the fenugreek seeds in the blend — they turn bitter the instant they brown past gold, so bloom on medium, never high.
Mixing your own panch phoron in equal parts beats most packet versions, which skimp on fennel.
The sautéed radish base, minus cheese, doubles as a quick Odia-style bhaja side dish for rice the next day.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with tomato khajur khatta (Odisha's tomato-date chutney) or plain sweet curd, and finish with a piece of chhena poda if you are lucky enough to have it.

variations.name: Classic Cheesy Sattu Paratha
variations.description: A clever fusion that solves sattu's one weakness — dryness — with a handful of melting mozzarella and sharp processed cheese.
