ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: steeped in warm milk to bloom colour and honeyed aroma

steps: Crush a pinch of Anveshan Saffron between your fingers and steep it in 3 tbsp warm milk for 10 minutes until the liquid turns deep amber.

Melt 1 cup Anveshan Ghee in a heavy pan on low heat, add 2 cups coarse besan and roast slowly for about 16 minutes, stirring constantly, until pale gold and fragrant but not browned, so the saffron colour stays clear.
Dissolve 1 cup Anveshan Khandsari in 0.5 cup water and simmer to a one-string syrup, about 6 minutes, then stir in the saffron milk, 1 tsp cardamom, 1 tsp rosewater and a pinch of salt.
Off the heat, pour the saffron syrup into the roasted besan and beat briskly for 2 minutes until the mixture turns a glowing gold and leaves the pan sides.
Spread into a greased tray to a 1 cm layer, press 3 tbsp finely chopped pistachios evenly over the surface, and lightly smooth with the back of a spoon.
Cool for 30 minutes until firm-set, then cut into 16 neat diamonds and, if you like, press a single saffron thread into each for a festive finish.
tips: Roast the besan only to pale gold, not brown, or you will muddy the saffron's colour.
A little saffron goes a long way; a true pinch of good Kashmiri saffron is enough to colour the whole batch.
Add the rosewater to the syrup off the boil so its delicate fragrance is not driven off by high heat.
variations.servingSuggestion: Present on a mirror-finish tray dusted with edible rose petals and pair with warm saffron kahwa for an elegant Eid or Diwali spread.

variations.name: Malwa Festive Besan Barfi
variations.description: From the Malwa plateau of Madhya Pradesh comes a rustic besan barfi studded with coarsely crushed roasted peanuts, which add a savoury crunch and a groundnut richness against the sweet fudge. It is a harvest-season treat where peanuts are plentiful and jaggery is the sweetener of choice.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: toasts the besan and binds the crushed peanuts into the slab

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: the plateau's default sweetener, deepening the peanut flavour

steps: Melt 1 cup Anveshan Ghee in a heavy kadhai on low heat, add 2 cups coarse besan and roast, stirring, for about 15 minutes until deeply golden and aromatic, splashing in 3 tbsp milk near the end for a grainy crumb.
Meanwhile melt 1 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder with 0.33 cup water over low heat into a thick syrup that coats a spoon, about 5 minutes, and strain to remove impurities.
Off the heat, stir a pinch of salt, 1 tsp cardamom and 0.5 tsp dried ginger powder into the roasted besan, then pour in the jaggery syrup and beat for 2 minutes until the mass tightens.
Fold in 0.75 cup coarsely crushed roasted peanuts so they scatter evenly through the warm mixture without breaking down to paste.
Press into a greased tray to a 1.5 cm slab, sprinkle 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds over the top and tamp them down with a flat spatula.
Let it set for 25 minutes until firm at the edges, then cut into 16 chunky squares that reveal the peanut speckle in cross-section.
tips: Crush the peanuts coarsely, not to powder, so each bite keeps a distinct crunch.
The dried ginger cuts the richness; leave it out for a sweeter, plainer barfi if serving to children.
Fold the peanuts in off the heat so they stay crisp rather than steaming soft in the hot mixture.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve wedges with a glass of cold buttermilk after a Malwa festive lunch, or crumble over warm gud-milk for a hearty winter dessert.

variations.name: Awadhi Festive Besan Barfi
variations.description: A refined Lucknawi barfi perfumed with kewra water and a whisper of rose, in the fragrant nazakat style of Awadhi mithai. The besan is roasted gently to keep it pale and delicate, then finished with silver vark so it looks as courtly as it tastes.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: kept mild so the kewra perfume leads the aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: a clean sweetness that lets the floral notes stay in front

steps: Warm 1 cup Anveshan Ghee gently in a heavy pan, add 2 cups coarse besan and roast on low heat for about 15 minutes, stirring throughout and adding 3 tbsp milk midway, stopping at a pale straw colour to keep the barfi delicate.
Dissolve 1 cup Anveshan Khandsari in 0.5 cup water and cook to a soft one-string syrup, about 6 minutes, then take it off the heat before adding fragrances.
Stir 1.5 tsp kewra water, 1 tsp cardamom powder and a pinch of salt into the cooled-slightly syrup so the volatile aromas are not boiled away.
Pour the perfumed syrup over the roasted besan off the heat and beat gently for 2 minutes until smooth and just leaving the pan.
Spread evenly into a greased tray to a 1 cm layer, scatter 2 tbsp slivered almonds and lay 2 sheets of silver vark over the surface without pressing hard.
Cool for 30 minutes until set, then cut into 16 delicate diamonds with a clean, lightly greased knife.
tips: Kewra is potent; measure it carefully, as even half a teaspoon too much turns the barfi soapy.
Apply the silver vark with the paper backing facing up and peel gently so it transfers without tearing.
Keep the roast pale for a courtly look; a dark roast fights with the pale-floral Awadhi character.
variations.servingSuggestion: Arrange on a fine porcelain plate with a scatter of dried rose petals and serve after an Awadhi dawat alongside cardamom-scented kahwa.

variations.name: Classic Masala Masala Dosa
variations.description: A restaurant-style masala dosa turned up a notch, with the potato filling perfumed by freshly ground garam masala and coriander powder for a warmer, more aromatic core. The extra spice layer clings to the potatoes so every fold delivers depth beyond the usual turmeric yellow.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Wood-pressed groundnut oil carries the toasted spice aroma into a crackling crust.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee brushed over the spiced filling amplifies the garam masala's warm notes.

steps: Boil 4 medium potatoes until soft, about 15 minutes, then peel and crush them, leaving a few small lumps for texture.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and splutter 1 tsp mustard seeds with 12 curry leaves and 2 slit green chillies for 20 seconds until aromatic.

Add 1 sliced onion and cook until translucent, about 4 minutes, then stir in 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1.5 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp garam masala and toast for 30 seconds off direct heat so the spices do not scorch.
Fold in the crushed potatoes and 1.5 tsp salt with a splash of water and simmer 3 minutes until the masala is moist and evenly spiced.
Heat a tava, wipe it with a damp cloth, then ladle batter and spread it thin in an outward spiral.
Drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and brush a little Anveshan Ghee at the edges, cooking until deep golden and crisp, about 2 minutes.
Spoon 3 tbsp of the spiced potato masala along the centre, fold, and serve hot.
tips: Bloom the garam masala and coriander powder briefly in the residual heat, never in a dry hot pan alone, so they release aroma without turning bitter.
Grind your own garam masala fresh from whole spices if you can; pre-ground blends fade fast and this dish leans on that warmth.
If the masala tastes flat, a squeeze of lime just before filling lifts the whole spice profile.
variations.servingSuggestion: Offer with coconut chutney, a tangy tomato chutney and sambar, plus a small ramekin of extra garam masala for guests who like it stronger.

variations.name: Maharashtrian Goda Masala Dosa
variations.description: A Puneri spin where the potato filling is seasoned with dark, aromatic goda masala instead of standard garam masala, lending sweet-woody notes of dagad phool and sesame. Cooked in groundnut oil, it tastes like a dosa that wandered into a Maharashtrian kitchen.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Groundnut oil is the everyday Maharashtrian cooking fat and echoes the peanut in the filling.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: A whisper of jaggery is the classic Maharashtrian sweet-savoury balance for goda masala.

steps: Boil 4 medium potatoes until tender, peel and crush them, and dry-roast 3 tbsp peanuts until spotty, then crush coarsely.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and splutter 1 tsp mustard seeds with 10 curry leaves and 2 slit green chillies for 20 seconds.
Add 1 sliced onion and saute until soft, about 5 minutes, then stir in 0.5 tsp turmeric and 1.5 tsp goda masala and warm through for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Fold in the crushed potatoes, crushed peanuts, 1 tsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder and 1.5 tsp salt with a little water, then cook 3 minutes until cohesive.
Heat the tava, wipe it, and spread a thin dosa from a ladle of batter.
Drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil at the edges and cook until crisp and golden, about 2 minutes, without flipping.
Fill with 3 tbsp goda-spiced potato masala, fold over and serve hot.
tips: Goda masala varies wildly between households, so add it gradually and taste, since some blends are far more pungent than others.
The coarsely crushed peanuts add welcome crunch; leave them chunky rather than powdering them fully.
The tiny amount of jaggery should be barely detectable, its job is to round the goda masala, not to sweeten the filling.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve Maharashtrian-style with a fresh coconut-coriander chutney and a bowl of thin, peppery amti on the side.

variations.name: Kerala Coconut Masala Masala Dosa
variations.description: The spiced masala dosa softened with grated coconut and cooked in coconut oil, so the garam-masala warmth meets a sweet Malabar creaminess. It is the richest, most aromatic member of this family.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: Cold-pressed coconut oil bridges the coconut filling and the crisp crust seamlessly.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee grounds the sweet coconut with a savoury, roasted finish.

steps: Pressure-cook 4 medium potatoes for 3 whistles, peel and break into chunks.
Warm 2 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil and crackle 1 tsp mustard seeds with 15 curry leaves and 3 slit green chillies for 30 seconds.
Add 1 sliced onion and cook until glassy, about 5 minutes, then stir in 0.5 cup grated coconut and toast 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle in 0.5 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp garam masala, then fold in the potatoes and 1.5 tsp salt with a splash of water and simmer 3 minutes.
Heat the tava, wipe it, and spread a thin dosa.
Drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Coconut Oil and a little Anveshan Ghee at the rim, cooking until lacy and browned, about 2 minutes.
Fill with 3 tbsp coconut-spiced masala, fold and serve hot.
tips: Toast the coconut just until it smells nutty; browning it too far turns the filling dry and slightly bitter.
If coconut oil has solidified, stand the jar in warm water rather than microwaving, which can overheat it.
A few cashews fried in the coconut oil and tossed in at the end make this a festive-feeling version.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with Kerala sambar and a thin coconut-milk chutney, garnishing the plate with a scatter of fried curry leaves.

variations.name: Bihari Mustard Masala Masala Dosa
variations.description: A rustic Bihari treatment where the spiced potato filling gets a sarso kick and everything is cooked in bracing mustard oil, echoing the region's aloo bhujia. The garam masala and mustard together give a homely, pungent warmth.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Kachi ghani mustard oil gives the earthy, pungent base every Bihari aloo dish relies on.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A finishing spoon of ghee softens the mustard oil's sharpness beautifully.

steps: Boil 4 medium potatoes until tender, peel and crush them roughly.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil until it just smokes, lower the heat, then crackle 0.5 tsp nigella seeds with 3 slit green chillies and 4 crushed garlic cloves for 30 seconds.
Add 1 sliced onion and fry until golden, about 5 minutes, then stir in 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp garam masala and warm briefly.
Fold in the crushed potatoes and 1.5 tsp salt with a splash of water, mashing lightly, and cook 3 minutes until the masala holds.
Heat the tava, wipe it with a mustard-oil-dipped cloth, and spread a thin dosa.
Drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Mustard Oil and finish with a little Anveshan Ghee, cooking until crisp and golden, about 2 minutes.
Fill with 3 tbsp mustard-spiced potato masala, roll up and serve hot.
tips: Smoking the mustard oil before you temper is essential to strip its raw bite and leave only a clean pungency.
This filling doubles as a superb paratha stuffing, so make extra and refrigerate for up to two days.
Add the garlic raw into the tempering rather than the filling, so it mellows in the hot oil instead of tasting sharp.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a Bihari-style tomato-garlic chokha on the side instead of the usual chutney for a hearty, regional plate.

variations.name: Delhi Chaat Masala Masala Dosa
variations.description: A cheeky Dilli street reinvention where the spiced potato masala is finished with tangy chaat masala and a sprinkle of pomegranate for that unmistakable chaat-counter zing. It eats like a dosa and a plate of aloo chaat at once.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Clean wood-pressed groundnut oil keeps the crisp base neutral so the chaat flavours pop.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee lends the buttery richness of a Delhi dhaba tava.

steps: Boil 4 medium potatoes, peel and crush them into a chunky mash.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and splutter 1 tsp cumin seeds with 2 chopped green chillies for 20 seconds until aromatic.
Add 1 sliced onion and cook until soft, about 4 minutes, then stir in 0.5 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp garam masala.
Fold in the crushed potatoes and 1 tsp salt, cook 2 minutes, then turn off the heat and sprinkle in 1.5 tsp chaat masala and 3 tbsp pomegranate seeds so they stay bright and juicy.
Heat the tava, wipe it, and spread a thin dosa from a ladle of batter.
Drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and brush a little Anveshan Ghee at the edges, cooking until crisp and golden, about 2 minutes.
Fill with 3 tbsp chaat-spiced potato masala, fold and serve hot with an extra dusting of chaat masala.
tips: Add the chaat masala and pomegranate only off the heat, since cooking dulls the tang and bursts the seeds.
A drizzle of green coriander-mint chutney inside the fold pushes this fully into chaat territory.
Keep the salt low, as chaat masala already carries black salt and can quickly over-season the filling.
variations.servingSuggestion: Plate with tamarind-date chutney and mint chutney in little bowls, chaat-style, and top with a shower of fine sev at the table.

variations.name: Classic Roasted Besan Barfi
variations.description: This version leans hard into the roast: the gram flour is toasted to a deep amber, well past golden, so the barfi tastes almost like roasted-chickpea toffee with a pronounced nutty bitterness balancing the sweet. The extra-long roast gives a firmer, sandier grain than a festive barfi.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: the medium that lets the besan roast dark without catching or burning

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: balances the deep roast without an over-sweet finish

steps: Melt 1 cup Anveshan Ghee in a heavy iron kadhai on low heat, add 2 cups coarse besan and begin a long, patient roast, stirring constantly to keep the colour even.
Roast for a full 22 minutes until the besan turns a deep amber-brown and smells intensely of toasted chickpea, adding 2 tbsp milk in the last few minutes to lock in a sandy crumb.
In another pan, dissolve 1 cup Anveshan Khandsari in 0.5 cup water and simmer to a firm one-string consistency, about 7 minutes, then mix in 1 tsp cardamom and a pinch of salt.
Take the besan off the heat, pour in the hot syrup and beat vigorously for 2 minutes until the darkly roasted mass thickens and cleanly leaves the pan.
Spread into a greased tray to a 1 cm slab, press in 12 slivered almonds and 8 chopped walnuts, and level the surface firmly.
Cool for 35 minutes until the deeper roast sets it firm, then cut into 16 diamonds; expect a crisper snap than a lighter-roasted barfi.
tips: Watch closely past the 18-minute mark: the line between deep amber and burnt is only a minute or two.
If you smell any acrid note, pull it off the heat instantly and stir off-flame to arrest the roast.
A darker roast needs slightly less syrup, so stop adding once the mixture just holds together.
variations.servingSuggestion: Pair the toasty squares with a strong South Indian filter coffee, whose bitterness echoes the deep roast beautifully.

variations.name: Gujarati Roasted Besan Barfi
variations.description: A Gujarati take where the deeply roasted besan meets molasses-rich jaggery, producing a dark, almost mahogany barfi with a double-caramel intensity from both the roast and the gud. A pinch of nutmeg and clove keeps it warming, in the mould of Surti mithai.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: holds the dark roast and jaggery together into a soft slab

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: doubles down on caramel notes alongside the deep roast

steps: In a thick kadhai, melt 1 cup Anveshan Ghee over low heat, add 2 cups coarse besan and roast slowly for about 20 minutes until deeply browned and richly aromatic, adding 2 tbsp milk towards the end.
Separately, melt 1 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder with 0.33 cup water on low heat into a thick, spoon-coating syrup, about 5 minutes, and strain away any sediment.
Off the heat, season the roasted besan with a pinch of salt, 1 tsp cardamom, 0.25 tsp nutmeg and 0.125 tsp clove powder for a warming Surti profile.
Pour the jaggery syrup into the besan and beat hard for 2 minutes until the mahogany-dark mixture thickens and pulls from the sides.
Fold in 12 broken cashews, then press into a greased tray to a 1.5 cm slab and smooth the top while warm.
Rest for 25 minutes until set but still soft, then cut into 16 squares that glow dark amber in the light.
tips: Because both roast and jaggery are dark, judge doneness by aroma rather than colour alone.
Keep the clove restrained; an eighth of a teaspoon perfumes the batch without turning medicinal.
This barfi tastes even better the next day once the spices meld, so make it ahead.
variations.servingSuggestion: Offer with a wedge of aged mysore pak on a festive platter, or serve warm with a spoon of chilled malai for contrast.

variations.name: Kashmiri Roasted Besan Barfi
variations.description: Here the deep-roasted besan is lifted with saffron and a handful of chopped walnuts, the signature nut of Kashmir, for an autumnal barfi that is at once toasty and floral. The saffron milk is added late so its gold survives against the darker roast.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: melds the roasted grain with saffron and walnut oils

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: keeps the sweetness clean so saffron still reads through the roast

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: bloomed in warm milk to tint the darker crumb gold at the edges

steps: Steep a pinch of Anveshan Saffron in 3 tbsp warm milk for 10 minutes until deeply coloured and aromatic.
Melt 1 cup Anveshan Ghee in a heavy pan on low heat, add 2 cups coarse besan and roast for about 20 minutes, stirring, until a rich reddish-brown with a strong nutty scent.
Dissolve 1 cup Anveshan Khandsari in 0.5 cup water and simmer to a one-string syrup, about 6 minutes, then stir in the saffron milk, 1 tsp cardamom and a pinch of salt.
Off the heat, pour the saffron syrup into the roasted besan and beat for 2 minutes until glossy and pulling together, the gold streaking through the darker base.
Fold in 0.33 cup chopped walnuts, then spread into a greased tray to a 1 cm slab and press the surface even.
Cool for 30 minutes until set, then cut into 16 diamonds; the walnuts should show as pale flecks against the amber.
tips: Toast the walnuts lightly first to keep them from tasting raw against the deep-roasted besan.
Bloom the saffron in warm, not boiling, milk to draw out colour without bitterness.
If the roast has gone very dark, add an extra thread of saffron so its colour still shows.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve in autumn with hot noon chai, the pink salted tea of Kashmir, whose savoury edge sets off the sweet barfi.

variations.name: Kerala Roasted Besan Barfi
variations.description: A coastal reinvention where the roasted besan is enriched with fresh grated coconut and finished in fragrant coconut oil, giving a tropical richness and a moist, tender bite quite unlike a plain besan barfi. Toasted coconut flecks run right through the slab.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the besan while the coconut oil finishes the aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: stirred in at the end for an unmistakable Kerala fragrance

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: a mild sweetness that lets the coconut lead

steps: Dry-toast 0.75 cup fresh grated coconut in a pan on low heat for about 4 minutes until it just turns pale gold and smells fragrant, then set aside.
Melt 0.75 cup Anveshan Ghee in a heavy kadhai, add 2 cups coarse besan and roast on low heat for about 18 minutes, stirring, until deep golden, splashing in 3 tbsp milk near the end.
Dissolve 1 cup Anveshan Khandsari in 0.5 cup water and simmer to a one-string syrup, about 6 minutes, then add 1 tsp cardamom and a pinch of salt.
Off the heat, pour the syrup into the besan and beat for 2 minutes, then fold in the toasted coconut, 12 chopped cashews and 2 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil for its coastal perfume.
Spread into a greased tray to a 1 cm slab and smooth the top, letting the coconut speckle show at the surface.
Cool for 30 minutes until set, then cut into 16 squares; the coconut keeps this barfi noticeably moister than the plain roast.
tips: Use fresh or frozen grated coconut, not desiccated, for the moisture that defines this version.
Add the coconut oil right at the end and off the heat so its fragrance is not cooked away.
Because of the coconut's moisture, store this one refrigerated and eat within four days.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve chilled after a Kerala sadya, or alongside a small cup of sweet, milky coconut payasam for a fully tropical dessert course.

variations.name: Malwa Roasted Besan Barfi
variations.description: The Malwa plateau's roasted-besan barfi folds in crushed roasted peanuts and a hint of dried ginger, marrying the deep toast of the flour with groundnut crunch. Sweetened with jaggery, it is a robust, rustic sweet built for cold-season energy.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: carries the double toast of besan and peanut

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: the warming plateau sweetener that suits the peanuts

steps: Melt 1 cup Anveshan Ghee in a heavy kadhai on low heat, add 2 cups coarse besan and roast for about 20 minutes, stirring, until deeply browned and strongly aromatic, adding 2 tbsp milk near the end.
Melt 1 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder with 0.33 cup water on low heat into a thick syrup, about 5 minutes, and strain out any grit.
Off the heat, stir a pinch of salt, 1 tsp cardamom and 0.5 tsp dried ginger into the roasted besan, then pour in the jaggery syrup and beat for 2 minutes until it tightens.
Fold in 0.75 cup coarsely crushed roasted peanuts so they stay chunky and evenly spread through the warm mass.
Press firmly into a greased tray to a 1.5 cm slab, levelling the surface with the back of an oiled spoon.
Let set for 25 minutes until firm, then cut into 16 hearty squares showing the peanut rubble in section.
tips: Keep the peanuts coarse so they crunch rather than blend into the fudge.
The sonth adds gentle heat that suits winter; halve it for a milder sweet.
Wrap portions in butter paper for a sturdy travel snack that survives a journey.
variations.servingSuggestion: Break into rough pieces for a trekking or Sankranti snack box, or serve with warm turmeric milk on a cold plateau night.

variations.name: Classic Cheesy Adai
variations.description: A modern crowd-pleaser where the protein-rich four-dal adai is topped with melting cheese that seeps into its lacy holes. The nutty lentil base and gooey cheese make an unexpectedly satisfying pairing that kids and adults both love.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Groundnut oil crisps the adai base so it stays sturdy under the melting cheese.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A drizzle of ghee adds a buttery aroma that flatters the cheese.

steps: Soak the chana, toor and urad dals with 1 cup raw rice for 3 hours, then drain, and keep 1 cup grated cheese at room temperature.
Grind the soaked mix with 3 green chillies and 1 tsp cumin seeds to a coarse batter, adding water sparingly.
Stir in 1 tsp salt, 12 curry leaves and 1 chopped onion to a thick batter, keeping the salt low since the cheese is salty.
Heat a tava over medium heat, grease with Anveshan Groundnut Oil, and spread a ladle of batter into a thick 7-inch round.
Make a central hole, drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil around it, and cook until the base is golden and crisp, about 3 minutes.
Scatter a quarter of the grated cheese over the top, drizzle a little Anveshan Ghee, cover for a minute so the cheese melts, then flip briefly to set.
Fold and serve the cheesy adai immediately while it stretches.
tips: Use a good melting cheese like mozzarella or a mozzarella-cheddar mix, as hard aged cheeses stay grainy.
Cover the adai for a minute after adding cheese so it melts fully before you fold it.
Keep the batter salt low, since a whole cup of cheese brings plenty of its own.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a tangy tomato chutney and ketchup on the side, so both traditional and younger palates are happy.

variations.name: Punjabi Butter Cheese Adai
variations.description: A rich, dhaba-style adai lavished with butter and cheese and cooked in ghee for a doubly decadent, hearty crepe. The lentil base keeps it filling while the butter and cheese make it indulgent comfort food.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Bilona ghee delivers the buttery Punjabi richness the dish is built on.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A splash of groundnut oil lets the ghee-rich adai crisp without scorching.

steps: Soak the chana, toor and urad dals with 1 cup raw rice for 3 hours, then drain.
Grind the soaked mix with 2 green chillies to a coarse batter, then stir in 0.5 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp salt, 1 chopped onion and 3 tbsp coriander.
Heat a tava over medium heat, grease with a mix of Anveshan Ghee and Anveshan Groundnut Oil, and spread a ladle of batter into a thick 7-inch round.
Make a central hole, drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee around it, and dot the surface generously with butter, cooking until the base is golden, about 3 minutes.
Scatter a quarter of the grated cheese on top, cover for a minute so it melts, then flip briefly to set the cheese side.
Add a final smear of Anveshan Ghee, fold the adai over the gooey cheese, and serve hot.
Repeat with the remaining batter, keeping the cooked adais warm.
tips: Let the butter foam and lightly brown on the tava before spreading batter for that unmistakable dhaba aroma.
Do not skimp on cheese here; unabashed richness is the whole point of the Punjabi version.
Blot any pooling butter with the spatula so the adai crisps rather than steams.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a fresh onion-tomato-mint chutney and a wedge of lime to cut the richness, dhaba-style.

variations.name: Maharashtrian Schezwan Cheese Adai
variations.description: A Mumbai street-cart mashup where fiery schezwan chutney is smeared over the lentil adai under a cap of melting cheese. Indo-Chinese heat meets South Indian protein crunch for an irresistibly messy, moreish bite.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Neutral groundnut oil keeps the base crisp under the tangy chutney and cheese.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A little ghee balances the tangy schezwan heat with richness.

steps: Soak the chana, toor and urad dals with 1 cup raw rice for 3 hours, then drain.
Grind the soaked mix with 2 green chillies to a coarse batter, then stir in 1 tsp salt and 0.5 finely chopped capsicum.
Heat a tava over medium heat, grease with Anveshan Groundnut Oil, and spread a ladle of batter into a thick 7-inch round, then smear 1 tbsp schezwan chutney over the top.
Make a central hole and drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil around it, cooking until the base is crisp, about 3 minutes.
Scatter a quarter of the grated cheese and a sprinkle of spring onion, cover for a minute to melt, then drizzle a little Anveshan Ghee.
Flip briefly to set the cheese, fold, and serve the schezwan cheese adai hot.
Repeat with the remaining batter, keeping the adais warm.
tips: Spread the schezwan thinly and evenly so it cooks slightly into the adai without turning it soggy.
Add the spring onion right at the end for a fresh crunch against the gooey cheese.
Adjust the schezwan to taste, as brands vary widely in heat and salt.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with extra schezwan chutney and a small bowl of sweet chilli sauce, exactly as the Mumbai carts do.

variations.name: Goan Cheese and Kokum Adai
variations.description: A coastal twist where tangy kokum is worked into the lentil batter beneath melting cheese, cooked in coconut oil. The sweet-sour kokum cuts the cheese so the adai stays bright and fresh rather than heavy.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: Coconut oil gives the Goan coastal aroma that pairs with kokum.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A touch of ghee balances the tangy kokum and stringy cheese.

steps: Soak the chana, toor and urad dals with 1 cup raw rice for 3 hours, then drain, and soak 4 kokum petals in 3 tbsp warm water for 10 minutes, then chop finely.
Grind the soaked mix with 3 green chillies to a coarse batter, then stir in the chopped kokum with its soaking liquid, 1 tsp salt, 12 curry leaves and 1 chopped onion.
Heat a tava over medium heat, grease with Anveshan Coconut Oil, and spread a ladle of batter into a thick 7-inch round.
Make a central hole and drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Coconut Oil around it, cooking until the base is golden and crisp, about 3 minutes.
Scatter a quarter of the grated cheese on top, cover for a minute to melt, then drizzle a little Anveshan Ghee.
Flip briefly to set the cheese, fold, and serve the kokum cheese adai hot.
Repeat with the remaining batter, keeping the adais warm.
tips: Kokum is tart, not spicy, so taste as you add it and stop at a gentle sweet-sour tang.
Because the batter is loosened with kokum water, hold back extra water so the adai still crisps.
Use a mild cheese so the coconut and kokum aromas still come through clearly.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a chilled kokum sherbet alongside, echoing the batter's tang for a true Goan finish.

variations.name: Hyderabadi Saffron Cheese Adai
variations.description: A regal Nizami-inspired adai where saffron and fried onions scent the lentil batter under a blanket of melting cheese. The saffron perfume against the cheese lifts this humble crepe into festive territory.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: Kashmiri saffron steeped in warm milk lends the Nizami colour and aroma to the batter.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee fries the onions to a deep birista and enriches the royal adai.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Groundnut oil lets the ghee-rich adai crisp without burning.

steps: Soak the chana, toor and urad dals with 1 cup raw rice for 3 hours, then drain, and steep a pinch of Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk for 10 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and fry 2 thinly sliced onions until deep golden and crisp like birista, about 8 minutes, then reserve half for garnish.
Grind the soaked dals and rice with 2 green chillies to a coarse batter, then stir in the saffron milk, half the fried onions, 0.5 tsp garam masala, 2 tbsp chopped mint and 1 tsp salt.
Heat a tava over medium heat, grease with a mix of Anveshan Ghee and Anveshan Groundnut Oil, and spread a ladle of batter into a thick 7-inch round.
Make a central hole, drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee around it, and cook until the base is golden and crisp, about 3 minutes.
Scatter a quarter of the grated cheese and some reserved fried onions on top, cover for a minute to melt, then flip briefly to set.
Fold and serve the saffron cheese adai hot, garnished with a few mint leaves.
tips: Bloom the saffron in warm, not boiling, milk so its colour and aroma release fully without turning bitter.
Fry the onions patiently to a true golden birista; rushing them on high heat makes them bitter rather than sweet.
Choose a mild, creamy cheese so the saffron and mint remain the stars.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a cooling mint raita and a scatter of pomegranate seeds, presenting it like a Hyderabadi feast dish.

variations.name: Classic Cheesy Besan Cheela
variations.description: A café-style gram-flour cheela with a melting layer of grated cheese folded into the hot pancake. Crisp at the edges and gooey in the middle, it turns a humble besan cheela into an irresistible snack.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Wood-Pressed Oil
ingredients.note: Wood-pressed groundnut oil crisps the base so the cheese melts cleanly without a greasy finish.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Bilona Ghee
ingredients.note: A brush of bilona ghee at the fold adds a rich, buttery aroma that plays off the melted cheese.

steps: Whisk 1.5 cups gram flour with 1.5 cups water into a smooth, lump-free batter of thin-cream consistency.
Stir in 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric, 0.5 tsp red chilli powder and 0.75 tsp salt, keeping the salt light because the cheese will add more.
Fold in 1 finely chopped onion, 2 minced green chillies and 3 tbsp coriander, then rest the batter for 10 minutes.
Heat a tava over medium heat and grease it with a film of Anveshan Groundnut Wood-Pressed Oil until it shimmers.
Ladle the batter and spread into a 7-inch round, drizzle 1 tsp oil around the rim, and cook the base until golden, about 3 minutes, then flip.
Scatter 3 tbsp grated cheese over one half, cook 1 to 2 minutes until it melts and the second side sets, brush the fold with Anveshan Bilona Ghee, fold over the cheese and serve hot and molten.
tips: Add the cheese after flipping so it melts against the just-cooked side without sticking to the tava.
Keep the batter salt light, since grated processed cheese is salty and can quickly push the cheela over.
For extra pull, mix a spoon of grated mozzarella into the processed cheese.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a tangy tomato ketchup or a schezwan chutney for dipping, cut into wedges for easy sharing.

variations.name: Punjabi Cheesy Besan Cheela
variations.description: The Punjabi dhaba treatment for a gram-flour cheela: cheese meets butter, cooked richly in ghee and loaded with an amritsari-style masala kick. Indulgent, hearty and made for a lazy brunch.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Bilona Ghee
ingredients.note: Cooking in generous bilona ghee gives the Punjabi richness the dish is loved for and browns the base deeply.

steps: Whisk 1.5 cups gram flour with 1.5 cups water into a smooth, lump-free batter.

Beat in 0.75 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp crushed kasuri methi, 0.5 tsp amchur powder and 0.75 tsp salt, fold in 1 chopped onion, 1 inch grated ginger, 2 minced green chillies and 3 tbsp coriander, and rest 10 minutes.
Heat a tava over medium heat and grease generously with Anveshan Bilona Ghee until it foams and shimmers.
Ladle the batter and spread into a 7-inch round, spoon a little more Anveshan Bilona Ghee around the rim, and cook the base until deep golden, about 3 minutes, then flip.
Scatter 3 tbsp grated cheese over one half, dot 1 tsp butter on top, and cook 2 minutes until the cheese melts and the base is richly browned.
Fold over the melting cheese, smear the top with the remaining butter, and serve hot dhaba-style.
tips: Cooking in ghee and finishing with butter gives this cheela its unmistakable dhaba richness, so do not stint.
Brown the base a shade darker than usual for the deep, toasty flavour Punjabis favour.
Rest the cooked cheela for thirty seconds before folding so the molten cheese sets just enough to hold.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a raw onion-lachha salad, a lime wedge and a side of mint chutney for a rich Punjabi brunch.

variations.name: Gujarati Cheesy Besan Cheela
variations.description: A gentle sweet-savoury Gujarati cheesy puda where a touch of jaggery in the batter balances the salty cheese and ginger-chilli heat. Soft, mild and thoroughly crowd-pleasing.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sunflower Wood-Pressed Oil
ingredients.note: Light wood-pressed sunflower oil keeps the puda soft and lets the jaggery-cheese balance come through.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: A little jaggery powder offsets the salty cheese for the classic Gujarati sweet-savoury balance.

steps: Whisk 1.5 cups gram flour with 0.25 cup whisked curd and 1.25 cups water into a smooth, thin, pourable batter.

Stir in 1.5 tsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder, 1.5 tsp ginger-green chilli paste, 0.5 tsp roasted cumin powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric and 0.5 tsp salt until the jaggery dissolves, keeping the salt low for the cheese.
Fold in 3 tbsp coriander and rest the batter 10 minutes so the curd and jaggery meld.
Heat a tava over medium-low heat and grease it thinly with Anveshan Sunflower Wood-Pressed Oil until it just glistens.
Ladle the batter and spread into a thin 7-inch round, drizzle 1 tsp oil around the rim, and cook the base gently until pale gold, about 3 minutes, then flip.
Scatter 3 tbsp grated cheese over one half, cook 2 minutes on low until melted without browning the jaggery, then fold and serve warm.
tips: The spoon of curd makes the puda especially soft while adding a tang that balances the jaggery and cheese.
Keep the flame low, since the jaggery in the batter scorches quickly over high heat.
Taste and adjust so the sweetness sits gently behind the savoury cheese rather than upfront.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a fresh coriander-mint chutney and a glass of chaas, or pack it warm into a lunchbox where it stays soft.

variations.name: Maharashtrian Cheesy Besan Cheela
variations.description: A Mumbai street-food mashup where goda masala and finely chopped capsicum meet gooey cheese in a gram-flour cheela, echoing the city's beloved cheese-loaded snacks. Warm-spiced and full of character.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Wood-Pressed Oil
ingredients.note: Groundnut oil is the classic Maharashtrian street-food fat and keeps the cheesy cheela crisp and light.

steps: Whisk 1.5 cups gram flour with 1.5 cups water into a smooth, lump-free batter of thin-cream consistency.

Beat in 1 tsp goda masala, 0.5 tsp roasted cumin powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric and 0.75 tsp salt, fold in 1 chopped onion, 0.5 finely chopped capsicum, 2 minced green chillies and 3 tbsp coriander, and rest 10 minutes.
Heat a tava over medium heat and grease it with a film of Anveshan Groundnut Wood-Pressed Oil until it shimmers.
Ladle the batter and spread into a 7-inch round, drizzle 1 tsp oil around the rim, and cook the base until golden with the goda masala fragrant, about 3 minutes, then flip.
Scatter 3 tbsp grated cheese over one half and cook 2 minutes until it melts and the vegetables soften.
Fold over the cheese, press gently, and serve hot with the cheese oozing at the edges.
tips: Chop the capsicum very fine so it cooks through in the short griddle time and does not stay raw.
Keep the goda masala at 1 tsp so it complements the cheese rather than overpowering it.
A dusting of chaat masala over the folded cheela adds a Mumbai street-food tang.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a garlicky dry chutney and buttered pav on the side for a full Mumbai-style snack plate.

variations.name: Bengali Cheesy Besan Cheela
variations.description: An unusual fusion where pungent mustard oil and nigella-scented gram-flour batter meet melting cheese. The sharp mustard cuts the richness for a grown-up cheesy cheela.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Wood-Pressed Oil
ingredients.note: Smoked kachi ghani mustard oil brings a sharp pungency that cuts cleanly through the melted cheese.

steps: Whisk 1.5 cups gram flour with 1.5 cups water into a smooth, pourable batter.

Warm 1 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Wood-Pressed Oil until it just smokes, cool briefly, and whisk it into the batter with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 0.5 tsp roasted cumin powder and 0.5 tsp salt, keeping the salt low for the cheese.
Fold in 2 minced green chillies, 2 chopped spring onions and 3 tbsp coriander, then rest 10 minutes.
Heat a tava over medium heat, film it with more Anveshan Mustard Wood-Pressed Oil, and scatter a pinch of nigella onto the greased surface to toast.
Pour the batter over the seeds and spread into a 7-inch round, cook the base until deep golden, about 3 minutes, then flip.
Scatter 3 tbsp grated cheese over one half, cook 2 minutes until melted, then fold over the cheese and serve hot with the mustard aroma still lively.
tips: Smoke the mustard oil before mixing it in so its bite mellows into fragrance without turning bitter under the cheese.
Pair the sharp mustard with a mild cheese so neither element overwhelms the other.
Toast the nigella on the tava only moments before pouring the batter to keep it from burning.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a light cucumber-tomato kachumber and a spoon of kasundi for those who want to double down on the mustard.

variations.name: Classic Cheesy Masala Dosa
variations.description: The kid-favourite street version, where a generous handful of melting cheese blankets the potato masala inside a crisp golden dosa. The cheese pulls into long strands as you break it, marrying comfort-food gooeyness with South Indian crunch.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Groundnut oil crisps the base so it stays sturdy under the melting cheese.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee brushed on the crust adds a buttery aroma that pairs beautifully with cheese.

steps: Boil 3 medium potatoes until soft, peel and crush them coarsely, and keep 1 cup grated cheese ready at room temperature so it melts fast.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and splutter 1 tsp mustard seeds with 0.25 tsp asafoetida, 10 curry leaves and 2 slit green chillies for 20 seconds.
Add 1 sliced medium onion and cook until soft, about 4 minutes, then stir in 0.5 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt.
Fold in the crushed potatoes with a splash of water and cook 3 minutes into a moist masala; keep warm.
Heat the tava, wipe it, spread a thin dosa, then drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and brush a little Anveshan Ghee at the edges and cook until golden, about 2 minutes.
Scatter a quarter of the grated cheese across the dosa while still on the tava so it melts, then spoon 3 tbsp potato masala over one half.
Fold the dosa over the melting cheese and serve immediately while it stretches.
tips: Use a good melting cheese like processed mozzarella or a mozzarella-cheddar mix; hard aged cheeses stay grainy and refuse to string.
Scatter the cheese while the dosa is still on the heat so it melts fully before folding.
Keep the salt low in the potato masala since the cheese brings its own saltiness.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a tangy tomato ketchup for younger eaters alongside coconut chutney, so both traditional and modern palates are happy.

variations.name: Punjabi Amul-Butter Cheesy Masala Dosa
variations.description: A rich, dhaba-style indulgence where the dosa is lavished with butter and layered with cheese for a doubly decadent bite. Cooked and finished in ghee, it eats like a cheese-stuffed grilled sandwich crossed with a dosa.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Bilona ghee delivers the buttery Punjabi richness the dish is built on.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A splash of groundnut oil lets the ghee-rich dosa crisp without scorching.

steps: Boil 3 medium potatoes until soft, peel and crush them coarsely.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and splutter 1 tsp cumin seeds for 20 seconds until aromatic.
Add 1 sliced medium onion and cook until golden, about 5 minutes, then stir in 0.5 tsp turmeric and 0.5 tsp garam masala.
Fold in the crushed potatoes and 1 tsp salt with a splash of water and cook 3 minutes; keep warm.
Heat the tava, wipe it, spread a thin dosa, then drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and dot generously with butter, cooking until golden and crisp, about 2 minutes.
Scatter a quarter of the grated cheese over the dosa to melt, spoon 3 tbsp potato masala on top, then add a final smear of Anveshan Ghee.
Fold over the gooey cheese and serve hot and glistening.
tips: For that dhaba look, let the butter foam and lightly brown on the tava before spreading the batter over it.
Do not skimp on cheese here; the whole point of the Punjabi version is unabashed richness.
Blot excess butter with the spatula edge if it pools, so the dosa crisps rather than steams.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a fresh onion-tomato-mint chutney and a wedge of lime to cut through the richness, dhaba-style.

variations.name: Goan Cheese and Kokum Masala Dosa
variations.description: A coastal twist where tangy kokum brightens the potato masala beneath a layer of melting cheese, cooked in coconut oil. The sweet-sour kokum cuts through the cheese so the dosa stays fresh rather than heavy.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: Coconut oil gives the unmistakable Goan coastal aroma that pairs with kokum.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A touch of ghee balances the tangy kokum and stringy cheese.

steps: Boil 3 medium potatoes until soft, peel and crush them, and soak 4 kokum petals in 3 tbsp warm water for 10 minutes, then chop finely and reserve the soaking liquid.
Warm 2 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil and splutter 1 tsp mustard seeds with 10 curry leaves and 2 slit green chillies for 30 seconds.
Add 1 sliced medium onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes, then stir in 0.5 tsp turmeric, the chopped kokum and its liquid.
Fold in the crushed potatoes and 1 tsp salt and simmer 3 minutes until tangy and moist; keep warm.
Heat the tava, wipe it, spread a thin dosa, then drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Coconut Oil and a little Anveshan Ghee at the edges and cook until crisp, about 2 minutes.
Scatter a quarter of the grated cheese to melt, then spoon 3 tbsp kokum potato masala over one half.
Fold over the cheese and serve hot while stretchy.
tips: Kokum is tart, not spicy, so taste as you add it and stop when the filling has a gentle sweet-sour tang.
Reserve a little kokum water to brush over the finished dosa for an extra glossy tang if you like it sharper.
Coconut oil and cheese are an unusual but delicious pairing; use a mild cheese so the coconut aroma still comes through.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a chilled kokum sherbet on the side, echoing the filling's tang and giving the plate a true Goan finish.

variations.name: Hyderabadi Saffron Cheese Masala Dosa
variations.description: A regal Nizami take where the potato masala is scented with saffron and fried onions, then crowned with melting cheese for a rich, festive dosa. The saffron perfume against the cheese makes it feel like biryani reimagined as a crepe.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: Kashmiri saffron steeped in warm milk lends the Nizami colour and aroma to the filling.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee fries the onions to a deep birista and enriches the royal masala.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Groundnut oil lets the ghee-rich dosa crisp without burning.

steps: Boil 3 medium potatoes until soft, peel and crush them, and steep a pinch of Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk for 10 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and fry 2 thinly sliced onions until deep golden and crisp like birista, about 8 minutes, then remove half for garnish.
To the remaining onions add 2 slit green chillies, 0.5 tsp turmeric and 0.5 tsp garam masala, then fold in the crushed potatoes and 1 tsp salt.
Stir in the saffron milk and 2 tbsp chopped mint and cook 3 minutes until fragrant and moist; keep warm.
Heat the tava, wipe it, spread a thin dosa, then drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and a little Anveshan Ghee and cook until golden, about 2 minutes.
Scatter a quarter of the grated cheese to melt, spoon 3 tbsp saffron potato masala over one half and top with the reserved fried onions.
Fold over and serve hot, garnished with a few extra mint leaves.
tips: Bloom the saffron in warm, not boiling, milk so its colour and aroma release fully without turning bitter.
Fry the onions patiently to a true golden birista; rushing them on high heat makes them bitter, not sweet.
A mild, creamy cheese lets the saffron and mint stay the stars rather than being overpowered.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a cooling mint raita and a sprinkle of pomegranate, presenting it like a Hyderabadi feast dish rather than a snack.

variations.name: Maharashtrian Cheese Schezwan Masala Dosa
variations.description: The beloved Mumbai street-cart mashup, slathered with fiery schezwan chutney under a cap of melting cheese. Indo-Chinese heat meets South Indian crunch in a dosa that defines Bombay's dosa-gaadi culture.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Neutral groundnut oil is the street-cart choice and keeps the crust crisp under the chutney.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A brush of ghee balances the tangy heat of the schezwan with richness.

steps: Boil 3 medium potatoes until soft, peel and crush them coarsely.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and cook 1 chopped medium onion and 0.5 chopped capsicum until softened, about 4 minutes.
Stir in 0.5 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt, then fold in the crushed potatoes and cook 3 minutes; keep warm.
Heat the tava, wipe it, spread a thin dosa, then smear 1 tbsp schezwan chutney across the surface with the ladle.
Drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and brush a little Anveshan Ghee at the edges and cook until crisp, about 2 minutes.
Scatter a quarter of the grated cheese to melt, spoon 3 tbsp potato masala over one half and sprinkle with chopped spring onion.
Fold over the cheese and serve hot, street-cart style.
tips: Spread the schezwan chutney thinly and evenly so the sauce cooks slightly into the dosa without making it soggy.
Add the spring onion right at the end for a fresh crunch that contrasts the gooey cheese.
Adjust the schezwan quantity to taste, as store-bought brands vary a lot in heat and salt.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with extra schezwan chutney and a small bowl of sweet chilli sauce on the side, exactly as the Mumbai carts do.

variations.name: Classic Cheesy Moong Dal Cheela
variations.description: A kid-friendly, café-style cheela where a melting layer of grated cheese is folded into the hot moong dal pancake. Crisp at the edges and gooey in the middle, it turns a healthy dal cheela into an irresistible treat.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Wood-Pressed Oil
ingredients.note: Wood-pressed groundnut oil crisps the base so the cheese melts cleanly without a greasy finish.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Bilona Ghee
ingredients.note: A brush of bilona ghee at the fold adds a rich, buttery aroma that plays off the melted cheese.

steps: Soak 1 cup split green gram for 3 hours, drain, and grind with 2 green chillies and about 0.75 cup water into a smooth, thick batter.
Stir in 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric, 0.5 tsp red chilli powder and 0.75 tsp salt, keeping the salt light because the cheese will add more.
Fold in 1 finely chopped onion and 3 tbsp coriander, then rest the batter for 15 minutes.
Heat a tava over medium heat and grease it with a film of Anveshan Groundnut Wood-Pressed Oil until it shimmers.
Ladle the batter and spread into a 7-inch round, drizzle 1 tsp oil around the rim, and cook the base until golden, about 3 minutes, then flip.
Scatter 3 tbsp grated cheese over one half, cook 1 to 2 minutes until it melts and the second side is set, brush the fold with Anveshan Bilona Ghee, fold over the cheese and serve hot and molten.
tips: Add the cheese after flipping so it melts against the just-cooked side without sticking to the tava.
Keep the batter salt light; grated processed cheese is salty and can easily push the cheela over.
For extra pull, mix in a spoon of grated mozzarella with the processed cheese.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a tangy tomato ketchup or a schezwan chutney for dipping, cut into wedges for easy sharing.

variations.name: Punjabi Cheesy Moong Dal Cheela
variations.description: The Punjabi dhaba treatment: cheese meets butter, with the cheela cooked and finished richly, then loaded with an amritsari-style masala kick. Indulgent, hearty and made for a lazy weekend brunch.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Bilona Ghee
ingredients.note: Cooking in generous bilona ghee gives the Punjabi richness the dish is loved for and browns the base deeply.

steps: Soak 1 cup split green gram for 3 hours, drain, and grind with 2 green chillies and about 0.75 cup water into a smooth, thick batter.
Beat in 0.75 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp crushed kasuri methi, 0.5 tsp amchur powder and 0.75 tsp salt, then fold in 1 chopped onion, 1 inch grated ginger and 3 tbsp coriander and rest 15 minutes.
Heat a tava over medium heat and grease generously with Anveshan Bilona Ghee until it foams and shimmers.
Ladle the batter and spread into a 7-inch round, spoon a little more Anveshan Bilona Ghee around the edge, and cook the base until deep golden, about 3 minutes, then flip.
Scatter 3 tbsp grated cheese over one half, dot 1 tsp butter on top, and cook 2 minutes until the cheese melts and the base is richly browned.
Fold over the melting cheese, smear the top with the remaining butter, and serve hot dhaba-style.
tips: Cooking in ghee and finishing with butter is what gives this cheela its unmistakable dhaba richness, so do not stint.
Brown the base a shade darker than usual for the deep, toasty flavour Punjabis favour.
Rest the cooked cheela for thirty seconds before folding so the molten cheese sets just enough to hold.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a raw onion-lachha salad, a wedge of lime and a side of mint chutney for a rich Punjabi brunch.

variations.name: Maharashtrian Cheesy Moong Dal Cheela
variations.description: A Mumbai street-food mashup where goda masala and a Kolhapuri-style spice meet gooey cheese, echoing the city's famous cheese-loaded snacks. Warm-spiced, cheesy and full of character.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Wood-Pressed Oil
ingredients.note: Groundnut oil is the classic Maharashtrian street-food fat and keeps the cheesy cheela crisp and light.

steps: Soak 1 cup split green gram for 3 hours, drain, and grind with 2 green chillies and about 0.75 cup water into a smooth, thick batter.
Whisk in 1 tsp goda masala, 0.5 tsp roasted cumin powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric and 0.75 tsp salt, then fold in 1 chopped onion, 0.5 finely chopped capsicum and 3 tbsp coriander and rest 15 minutes.
Heat a tava over medium heat and grease it with a film of Anveshan Groundnut Wood-Pressed Oil until it shimmers.
Ladle the batter and spread into a 7-inch round, drizzle 1 tsp oil around the rim, and cook the base until golden with the goda masala fragrant, about 3 minutes, then flip.
Scatter 3 tbsp grated cheese over one half and cook 2 minutes until it melts and the vegetables soften.
Fold over the cheese, press gently, and serve hot with the cheese oozing at the edges.
tips: Chop the capsicum very fine so it cooks through in the short griddle time and does not stay raw and crunchy.
Goda masala and cheese are an unexpected but delicious pair; keep the goda at 1 tsp so it complements rather than fights the cheese.
A dusting of chaat masala over the folded cheela adds a Mumbai street-food tang.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a garlicky dry chutney and buttered pav on the side for a full Mumbai-style snack plate.

variations.name: Gujarati Cheesy Moong Dal Cheela
variations.description: A gentle sweet-savoury Gujarati cheesy cheela where a touch of jaggery in the batter balances the salty cheese and green-chilli heat. Soft, mild and thoroughly crowd-pleasing.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sunflower Wood-Pressed Oil
ingredients.note: Light wood-pressed sunflower oil keeps the cheela soft and lets the jaggery-cheese balance come through.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: A little jaggery powder offsets the salty cheese for the classic Gujarati sweet-savoury balance.

steps: Soak 1 cup split green gram for 3 hours, drain, and grind with about 0.75 cup water into a smooth, pourable batter.
Dissolve 1.5 tsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder in 1 tsp lemon juice and whisk it into the batter with 1.5 tsp ginger-green chilli paste, 0.5 tsp roasted cumin powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric and 0.5 tsp salt.
Fold in 3 tbsp coriander and rest the batter 15 minutes, keeping the added salt low because the cheese is salty.
Heat a tava over medium-low heat and grease it thinly with Anveshan Sunflower Wood-Pressed Oil until it just glistens.
Ladle the batter and spread into a thin 7-inch round, drizzle 1 tsp oil around the rim, and cook the base gently until pale gold, about 3 minutes, then flip.
Scatter 3 tbsp grated cheese over one half, cook 2 minutes on low until melted without browning the jaggery, then fold and serve warm.
tips: Keep the flame low throughout, since the jaggery in the batter scorches quickly over high heat.
Dissolving jaggery in lemon juice first avoids gritty bits and blends the sweetness evenly.
Taste and adjust; a pinch more salt keeps the sweet note in the background rather than upfront.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a fresh coriander-mint chutney and a glass of chaas, or pack it for a lunchbox where it stays soft.

variations.name: Bengali Cheesy Moong Dal Cheela
variations.description: An unusual but delicious fusion where pungent mustard oil and nigella-scented batter meet melting cheese. The sharp mustard cuts the richness of the cheese for a grown-up cheesy cheela.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Wood-Pressed Oil
ingredients.note: Smoked kachi ghani mustard oil brings a sharp pungency that cuts cleanly through the melted cheese.

steps: Soak 1 cup split green gram for 3 hours, drain, and grind with 2 green chillies and about 0.75 cup water into a smooth batter.
Warm 1 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Wood-Pressed Oil until it just smokes, cool briefly, and whisk it into the batter with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 0.5 tsp roasted cumin powder and 0.5 tsp salt.
Fold in 2 chopped spring onions and 3 tbsp coriander, then rest 15 minutes, keeping the salt low to allow for the cheese.
Heat a tava over medium heat, film it with more Anveshan Mustard Wood-Pressed Oil, and scatter a pinch of nigella onto the greased surface to toast.
Pour the batter over the seeds and spread into a 7-inch round, cook the base until deep golden, about 3 minutes, then flip.
Scatter 3 tbsp grated cheese over one half, cook 2 minutes until melted, then fold over the cheese and serve hot with the mustard aroma still lively.
tips: Smoke the mustard oil before mixing it in so its bite mellows into fragrance without turning bitter under the cheese.
The sharpness of mustard is the whole point here; pair it with a mild cheese so neither overwhelms the other.
Toast the nigella on the tava only moments before pouring the batter to keep it from burning.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a light cucumber-tomato kachumber and a spoon of kasundi for those who want to double down on the mustard.

variations.name: Classic Cheesy Onion Uttapam
variations.description: A kid-friendly fusion where the soft, thick uttapam is crowned with sweet onions and a blanket of melting cheese. The spongy base drinks up the gooey cheese while the onion crust stays golden, making it an instant cafe-style favourite.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed oil for cooking that crisps the base so it stays light under the cheese

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee brushed on to finish, giving the cheesy top a fragrant gloss

steps: Stir 0.5 tsp salt, 1 tsp cumin and 0.5 tsp crushed pepper into 2.5 cups fermented dosa batter, loosening with water to a thick, spreadable mix.
Finely chop 2 onions and 2 green chillies and mix them with 3 tbsp coriander for the topping.
Heat a tava on medium and grease it with 0.5 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil wiped across until it shimmers.
Pour a ladle of batter and spread it into a thick 5-inch round, then press a handful of the onion topping into the surface and drizzle 1 tsp oil around the edge.
Cover and cook 3 minutes until the base is golden, scatter 0.25 cup grated cheese over the onions, and cover again for 1 minute so it melts into strings.
Brush the top with 0.5 tsp Anveshan Ghee, fold in half or serve open-faced, and eat at once while the cheese pulls.
tips: Melt the cheese on the topping side rather than flipping it onto the tava, or it sticks and burns.
Grate the cheese fresh for a quick, even melt; packet shreds can stay stubbornly firm.
A brief cover traps just enough steam to melt the cheese without turning the base soggy.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a tangy tomato-garlic chutney and a little ketchup on the side for younger eaters.

variations.name: Punjabi Cheesy Onion Uttapam
variations.description: Punjab makes it richer, finishing the cheesy uttapam with ghee-fried onions and a glossy smear of Anveshan Ghee. Hearty, golden and indulgent, it is a dhaba-style spin that eats almost like a stuffed cheese paratha in uttapam form.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee for frying the onions and finishing, the source of the dhaba richness

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed oil to grease the tava so the base crisps before the ghee finish

steps: Finely chop 2 onions and fry them in 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee with 2 chopped green chillies until soft and golden, then set aside.
Stir 0.5 tsp salt and 0.5 tsp garam masala into 2.5 cups fermented dosa batter, loosening with water to a thick, spreadable mix.
Heat a tava on medium and grease it with 0.5 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil, then spread a ladle of batter into a thick 5-inch round.
Press a handful of the ghee-fried onions into the surface, drizzle 1 tsp oil around the edge, cover and cook 3 minutes until the base is golden.
Scatter 0.25 cup grated cheese over the onions with 1 tsp crushed kasuri methi and cover for 1 minute so the cheese melts into strings.
Brush the top with 0.5 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, scatter 3 tbsp coriander over, and serve glossy and hot.
tips: Caramelise the onions slowly in ghee for sweetness; rushing them leaves a raw, sharp bite under the cheese.
A light dusting of garam masala over the cheese before serving deepens the North Indian aroma.
Keep the finishing ghee for the very end so its fragrance stays fresh rather than cooking away.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with mint-coriander chutney and pickled onions, dhaba-style, with a tall glass of lassi.

variations.name: Maharashtrian Cheesy Onion Uttapam
variations.description: This Mumbai street-cart style loads the cheesy uttapam with goda-spiced onions and a shower of cheese, the way college-gate stalls serve it. Earthy goda masala against gooey cheese makes for an addictive, hearty city snack.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: the everyday Maharashtrian oil for the goda onions and the tava

steps: Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil, pop 1 tsp mustard seeds and 12 curry leaves, add 2 chopped onions and 2 green chillies, and fry until soft, then stir in 1.5 tsp goda masala and set aside.
Season 2.5 cups fermented dosa batter with 0.5 tsp salt, loosening with water to a thick, spreadable mix.
Heat a tava on medium and grease it with 0.5 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil until it shimmers.
Spread a ladle of batter into a thick 5-inch round, press a handful of the goda onions into the surface, drizzle 1 tsp oil around the edge, cover and cook 3 minutes.
Scatter 0.25 cup grated cheese over the top and cover for 1 minute so it melts into strings.
Scatter 3 tbsp coriander over the cheese and serve hot straight off the tava.
tips: Toast the goda masala in the oil with the onions so its roasted aroma blooms before the cheese goes on.
Goda masala and cheese pair surprisingly well; keep the goda at 1.5 tsp so it supports rather than dominates.
For a true stall touch, smear a little butter over the cheese just before serving for extra gloss.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a garlic chutney and schezwan sauce on the side for dipping, Mumbai cart-style.

variations.name: Kerala Cheesy Onion Uttapam
variations.description: The Malabar version pairs melting cheese with fresh coconut and a curry-leaf crackle, all cooked in aromatic Anveshan Coconut Oil. Sweet coconut and salty cheese play off each other over the soft, spongy base for a coastal fusion.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: cold-pressed coconut oil for cooking that layers coconut aroma against the cheese

steps: Season 2.5 cups fermented dosa batter with 0.5 tsp salt, loosening with water to a thick, spreadable mix.
Finely chop 2 onions, 2 green chillies and 1 tbsp ginger, then combine with 0.33 cup grated coconut, 15 chopped curry leaves and 3 tbsp coriander.
Heat a tava on medium and grease it with 0.5 tsp Anveshan Coconut Oil wiped across until it shines.
Spread a ladle of batter into a thick 5-inch round, press a handful of the coconut-onion topping into the surface, drizzle 1 tsp coconut oil around the edge, cover and cook 3 minutes.
Scatter 0.25 cup grated cheese over the topping and cover for 1 minute so it melts into strings.
Serve open-faced and hot while the coconut aroma and cheese are at their peak.
tips: Balance coconut and cheese by keeping the coconut light so neither flavour drowns the other.
Use fresh grated coconut so it toasts sweet under the cheese rather than turning dry.
Keep the coconut oil gently warm for easy greasing, as it solidifies when it cools.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a roasted coconut chutney and a small bowl of drumstick sambar for a coastal plate.

variations.name: Andhra Cheesy Onion Uttapam
variations.description: Andhra spikes the cheesy uttapam with a Guntur-chilli and garlic onion topping, so the molten cheese tames a serious heat. Cooked in nutty Anveshan Sesame Oil, it is the spicy cheese lover's dream from a Vijayawada tiffin cart.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sesame Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed til oil, the Andhra staple, giving a nutty base to the chilli and cheese

steps: Stir 0.5 tsp salt and 1 tsp cumin into 2.5 cups fermented dosa batter, loosening with water to a thick, spreadable mix.
Finely chop 2 onions and mince 4 garlic cloves, then toss them with 1.5 tsp Guntur red chilli powder, 12 chopped curry leaves and 3 tbsp coriander.
Heat a tava on medium and season it with 0.5 tsp Anveshan Sesame Oil rubbed across the surface.
Spread a ladle of batter into a thick 5-inch round, press a handful of the fiery onion-garlic topping into it, drizzle 1 tsp sesame oil around the edge, cover and cook 3 minutes.
Scatter 0.25 cup grated cheese over the topping and cover for 1 minute so it melts and cools the heat.
Serve open-faced and blazing hot, with plenty of curd on the side.
tips: The cheese is the built-in coolant, so do not skimp on it if you have used the full 1.5 tsp Guntur chilli.
Mince the garlic fine so it threads a savoury note through the heat as the topping cooks.
Toss the chilli into the raw onions so it clings and mellows slightly on the tava.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a cooling cucumber raita and a gunpowder podi loosened in sesame oil for the brave.

variations.name: Classic Cheesy Rava Dosa
variations.description: A crowd-pleasing fusion where the crisp semolina lace cradles a molten layer of melted cheese folded into its centre. The contrast of shattering edges and gooey cheese makes it an instant favourite with children and cafe menus alike.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: a whole-grain swap for maida that keeps the lace crisp under the melting cheese

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed oil for greasing and crisping so the dosa stays light beneath the cheese

steps: Whisk 1 cup fine semolina, 0.5 cup rice flour, 0.25 cup Anveshan Khapli Atta and 1 tsp salt, then add 3 cups water gradually to a thin, lacy batter.
Stir in 1 tsp cumin, 0.5 tsp crushed pepper, 2 chopped green chillies, 10 torn curry leaves and 3 tbsp coriander, then rest the batter for 15 minutes.
Heat a tava on medium-high and grease it with 0.5 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil rubbed across with a cloth until it shimmers.
Stir the batter and pour it in a lacy ring from the outer edge inward, then drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil around the rim.
When the base is nearly golden after about 3 minutes, scatter 0.25 cup grated cheese over the centre and cover for 30 seconds so it melts into strings.
Fold the dosa over the melted cheese, press for 10 seconds, and serve at once while it pulls; stir the batter before each new one.
tips: Grate the cheese fresh so it melts quickly and evenly; pre-shredded packet cheese can stay stubbornly firm.
Add the cheese only near the end so it melts without weeping oil and greasing the crisp lace.
A quick cover with a lid traps just enough steam to melt the cheese without softening the dosa base.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a tangy tomato-garlic chutney and a squeeze of lime; kids love it with a small bowl of ketchup on the side.

variations.name: Punjabi Cheesy Rava Dosa
variations.description: Punjab makes it richer still, finishing the cheesy dosa with a glossy smear of Anveshan Ghee and a scatter of amul-style butter-fried onions. It is indulgent, golden and unapologetically hearty, a dhaba-style spin on the southern crisp.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: an ancient-wheat swap for maida that adds a nutty richness under the cheese

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee for finishing that gives the dosa its glossy dhaba-style richness

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed oil to grease the tava so the base crisps before the ghee finish

steps: Whisk 1 cup semolina, 0.5 cup rice flour, 0.25 cup Anveshan Khapli Atta, 1 tsp salt and 0.5 tsp garam masala, then thin with 3 cups water to a lacy batter and rest 15 minutes.
Finely chop 1 onion and fry it in 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee until golden and sweet, then set aside for topping.
Stir 1 tsp cumin, 2 chopped green chillies and 3 tbsp coriander into the rested batter and mix well.
Grease a hot tava with a little Anveshan Groundnut Oil, stir the batter, and pour it in a lacy ring from the edge inward.
After about 3 minutes when the base is golden, scatter 0.25 cup grated cheese and a spoon of the fried onions over the centre and cover for 30 seconds to melt.
Brush the crisp surface with 0.5 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, fold over the cheese, and serve glossy and hot.
tips: Finishing with ghee rather than oil is what gives this dosa its rich Punjabi aroma, so add it right at the end.
Caramelise the onions slowly in ghee for sweetness; rushing them on high heat leaves them raw and sharp.
A light dusting of garam masala over the cheese just before folding deepens the North Indian character.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with mint-coriander chutney and a side of pickled onions, dhaba-style, with a tall glass of lassi.

variations.name: Maharashtrian Cheesy Rava Dosa
variations.description: This street-cart favourite from Mumbai loads the cheesy dosa with schezwan-spiced goda masala butter and a shower of cheese, the way college-gate stalls serve it. Earthy goda warmth meets gooey cheese for an addictive city snack.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: a rustic swap for maida that suits the goda-spiced street style

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: the everyday Maharashtrian oil for greasing and crisping the dosa base

steps: Whisk 1 cup semolina, 0.5 cup rice flour, 0.25 cup Anveshan Khapli Atta and 1 tsp salt, then thin with 3 cups water to a lacy batter and rest 15 minutes.
Stir in 1.5 tsp goda masala, 3 tbsp crushed roasted peanuts, 1 tsp cumin, 2 chopped green chillies, 1 finely chopped onion and 3 tbsp coriander until evenly combined.
Heat a tava on medium-high and grease it with 0.5 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil rubbed on until it shimmers.
Stir the batter and pour it in a lacy ring from the outer edge inward, then drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil around the rim.
When the base is golden after about 3 minutes, scatter 0.25 cup grated cheese over the centre and cover for 30 seconds to melt into strings.
Fold the dosa over the cheese, press briefly, and serve hot; stir the batter before pouring the next.
tips: Add the chopped onion straight into the batter so it steams sweet and soft as the dosa cooks.
Goda masala and cheese are an unexpected but great pair; keep the goda at 1.5 tsp so it supports, not overwhelms.
For a true street-stall touch, smear a little butter over the cheese before folding for extra gloss.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a garlic chutney and schezwan sauce on the side for dipping, Mumbai cart-style.

variations.name: Kerala Cheesy Rava Dosa
variations.description: The Malabar version marries melting cheese with fresh coconut and a curry-leaf crackle, all cooked in aromatic Anveshan Coconut Oil. Sweet coconut and salty cheese play off each other for a coastal spin on the fusion favourite.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: a light whole-grain swap for maida that stays crisp with cheese and coconut

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: cold-pressed coconut oil for cooking that doubles the coconut aroma against the cheese

steps: Whisk 1 cup semolina, 0.5 cup rice flour, 0.25 cup Anveshan Khapli Atta and 1 tsp salt, then thin with 3 cups water to a lacy batter.
Stir in 0.33 cup grated coconut, 1 tsp cumin, 0.5 tsp crushed pepper, 2 chopped green chillies and 15 torn curry leaves, then rest 15 minutes.
Heat a tava on medium-high and grease it with 0.5 tsp Anveshan Coconut Oil rubbed across until it shines.
Stir the batter and pour it in a lacy ring from the outer edge inward, then drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Coconut Oil around it.
When the base turns golden after about 3 minutes, scatter 0.25 cup grated cheese over the centre and cover for 30 seconds to melt.
Fold the dosa over the cheese, press to crisp, and serve; loosen the batter with a splash of water if the coconut thickens it.
tips: Balance the coconut and cheese by keeping the coconut light at a third of a cup so neither drowns the other.
The coconut browns the base faster, so scatter the cheese a touch earlier than you would for a plain dosa.
Use fresh coconut, never desiccated, so the batter keeps its lacy flow rather than turning stiff.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a roasted coconut chutney and a small bowl of sambar for a coastal cheese-dosa plate.

variations.name: Andhra Cheesy Rava Dosa
variations.description: Andhra spikes the cheesy dosa with fiery Guntur chilli and a til-oil crackle, so the molten cheese tames a serious heat. Cooked in nutty Anveshan Sesame Oil, it is the spicy cheese lover's dream from a Vijayawada tiffin cart.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: an earthy swap for maida that holds up to the Guntur heat and cheese

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sesame Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed til oil, the Andhra staple, giving a nutty base to the chilli and cheese

steps: Whisk 1 cup semolina, 0.5 cup rice flour, 0.25 cup Anveshan Khapli Atta and 1 tsp salt, then thin with 3 cups water to a lacy batter and rest 15 minutes.
Stir in 1.5 tsp Guntur red chilli powder, 1 tsp cumin, 3 finely minced garlic cloves, 12 torn curry leaves and 3 tbsp coriander until the batter is evenly fiery.
Heat a tava on medium-high and season it with 0.5 tsp Anveshan Sesame Oil wiped across the surface.
Stir the batter and pour it in a lacy ring from the edge inward, then drizzle 1.5 tsp Anveshan Sesame Oil around the rim.
When the base is rust-gold after about 3 minutes, scatter 0.25 cup grated cheese over the centre and cover for 30 seconds to melt.
Fold the dosa over the molten cheese, press briefly, and serve blazing hot with plenty of curd on the side.
tips: The cheese is the built-in coolant here, so do not skimp on it if you have used the full 1.5 tsp Guntur chilli.
Mince the garlic fine so it crisps on the tava and threads a savoury note through the heat.
Sesame oil smokes fast at this heat, so let it settle a moment before each pour to avoid a bitter edge.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a cooling cucumber raita and a gunpowder podi loosened in sesame oil for the brave.

variations.name: Classic Cheesy Sattu Cheela
variations.description: A kid-friendly, indulgent twist on the protein-packed cheela, where the roasted-gram pancake is folded around a molten layer of grated cheese. Cooked in Anveshan wood-pressed groundnut oil and finished with ghee, it is crisp outside, gooey inside and impossible to resist.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sattu
ingredients.note: Sattu quietly turns a cheesy snack into a high-protein meal without changing the texture.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Groundnut oil crisps the base so the cheese melts before the cheela over-browns.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A ghee finish gives the classic cheesy cheela a golden, glossy top.

steps: Whisk 1.5 cups Anveshan Sattu with 0.75 tsp salt, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric and 0.5 tsp red chilli powder, then beat in 1.5 cups water to a smooth pouring batter; keep the salt light because the cheese is salty.
Fold 1 finely chopped onion, half a chopped capsicum, 2 chopped green chillies and 3 tbsp coriander into the batter and rest 10 minutes.
Heat a tava over medium heat and grease with a little Anveshan Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil until it shimmers.
Ladle on the batter, spread into a 7-inch round, drizzle 0.5 tsp oil around the rim, and cook 2 to 3 minutes until the base is golden and set.
Scatter 3 tbsp grated cheese over one half, flip the bare half over it, press gently and cook another 1 to 2 minutes on low so the cheese melts into strings.
Brush the top with Anveshan Ghee, slide onto a plate and serve at once while the cheese is molten; repeat for the remaining cheela.
tips: Melt the cheese on low heat after folding, not high, or the cheela browns too hard before the cheese goes gooey.
A mix of processed and mozzarella gives both flavour and that satisfying cheese-pull for children.
