Mix the dry mooli with 1 cup grated mozzarella, 1 finely chopped green chilli, 0.5 tsp black pepper powder, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 3 tbsp coriander and 0.25 tsp salt.
Divide dough and filling into 8 each; encase 2 tbsp filling in each ball, seal well and roll gently to a 6-inch round so the cheese stays contained.
Roast on a medium-hot tava for 1-2 minutes per side, brushing with 0.5 tsp ghee, until golden and crisp with the cheese melted inside.
Serve immediately while the centre is molten and stretchy.
tips: Squeeze the radish extra dry; combined with the cheese's moisture, any water will split the paratha.
Go easy on the salt since the cheese is already salty.
Roll these thicker and smaller so the melting cheese does not leak from the edges.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with tomato ketchup for the children and a tangy green chutney for the adults.

variations.name: Classic Mushroom Matar
variations.description: Sliced button mushrooms and sweet green peas simmered in a homely onion-tomato gravy until the mushrooms turn silky and release their earthy juices. The peas add pops of sweetness against the savoury base. A quick, satisfying everyday sabzi that tastes far richer than its effort.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sunflower Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed sunflower oil lets the mushrooms brown cleanly without masking their earthiness

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: a finishing spoon of bilona ghee lifts the aroma of the whole dish

steps: Wipe 300 g button mushrooms clean and slice thick, and keep 1 cup green peas ready; if using dried peas, boil them soft first.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Sunflower Oil in a pan and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then add 2 chopped onions and fry for 7 minutes until golden.

Stir in 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute, then add 3 pureed tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder and 1.5 tsp coriander powder and cook until the oil separates, about 8 minutes.
Add the sliced mushrooms and saute on high heat for 4 minutes until they release their water and it evaporates, concentrating their flavour.
Add the green peas with 1 cup water and 1.25 tsp salt, cover, and simmer for 8 minutes until the peas are tender and the gravy thickens.
Stir now and then so the mushrooms cook evenly and do not stick to the pan.
Finish with 0.75 tsp garam masala and 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, simmer 2 minutes, and garnish with 2 tbsp chopped fresh coriander.
tips: Cook the mushrooms on high heat to drive off their water, or the gravy turns watery and bland.
Wipe mushrooms with a damp cloth instead of washing them, so they brown instead of steaming.
Frozen peas work well here; add them a little later than fresh peas so they do not overcook.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with hot phulka or jeera rice and a wedge of lemon, with a simple kachumber salad alongside for crunch.

variations.name: Masala Mushroom Matar
variations.description: A Rajasthani-leaning take heavy on roasted coriander powder, giving the gravy a warm, earthy body without extra chilli heat. The mushrooms and peas sit in a thicker, spice-forward masala finished with a touch of curd for tang. Robust and full-bodied for the desert palate.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed groundnut oil suits the robust, coriander-heavy Rajasthani masala

steps: Slice 300 g button mushrooms thick and keep 1 cup green peas ready.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds, then fry 2 chopped onions for 7 minutes until golden brown, and add 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute.

Dry-roast 2.5 tsp coriander powder in a small pan for 40 seconds until nutty, then add it with 2 pureed tomatoes, 0.5 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp red chilli powder and cook until the oil separates, about 7 minutes.
Lower the heat and whisk in 0.25 cup curd gradually so it does not split, then cook 2 minutes into a thick masala.
Add the mushrooms and saute on high for 4 minutes until their water evaporates, then add the peas with 0.75 cup water and 1.25 tsp salt.
Cover and simmer for 8 minutes until the peas soften and the gravy clings thick to the mushrooms.
Finish with 2 tbsp chopped fresh coriander stirred through off the heat.
tips: The curd adds a gentle tang that balances the heavy coriander; whisk it in off the boil to avoid curdling.
Roast the coriander powder fresh for the earthy depth that defines this version.
Keep the gravy thick and clinging, as this take is meant to be scooped with bajra roti.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with bajra or missi roti and a dollop of white butter, or with steamed rice and a spoon of garlic chutney for extra heat.

variations.name: Kadai Mushroom Matar
variations.description: A vibrant kadai version where mushrooms and peas are tossed with charred capsicum and a coarse hand-pounded kadai masala. The dish stays semi-dry with a thick, clinging sauce, and the pepper keeps its snap against the silky mushrooms. Smoky, bold and quick to come together.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sesame Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed sesame oil brings a nutty southern aroma that suits the kadai masala

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: a finishing spoon of bilona ghee rounds off the coarse spice and adds gloss

steps: Slice 300 g button mushrooms thick, keep 1 cup peas ready, and cut 1 large capsicum into thick wedges.
Dry-roast 2 tbsp coriander seeds and 3 dried red chillies for 2 minutes until fragrant, cool, and pound to a coarse kadai masala.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil in a kadai and fry 2 diced onions for 6 minutes, then add 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute.
Add 2 chopped tomatoes and 0.5 tsp turmeric and cook until pulpy and the oil separates, about 6 minutes, then stir in most of the pounded kadai masala.
Add the mushrooms and saute on high heat for 4 minutes until their water dries off, then add the peas with 0.5 cup water and 1 tsp salt and cook 6 minutes into a thick gravy.
Toss in the capsicum wedges on high heat for 3 to 4 minutes so they char lightly but stay crunchy.
Crush 1 tsp kasuri methi over the pan, swirl in 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and the reserved kadai masala, and finish with 2 tbsp chopped coriander.
tips: Dry the mushrooms out on high heat before adding water, or the semi-dry kadai will turn soupy.
Add the capsicum last so it keeps its crunch and colour.
Pound the kadai masala coarse so you get little bursts of coriander seed in every bite.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve straight from the kadai with butter naan or laccha paratha and a squeeze of lemon over the top.

variations.name: Handi Mushroom Matar
variations.description: A slow handi mushroom matar perfumed with whole spices bloomed in ghee and finished with a splash of coconut milk for a southern touch. The mushrooms and peas steam gently under a lid so they take on the aroma of cardamom, cloves and cinnamon. Mellow, fragrant and lightly creamy.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: whole spices bloom in bilona ghee and their aroma soaks into the mushrooms on dum

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: a spoon of wood-pressed coconut oil deepens the coconut-milk finish with a Kerala note

steps: Slice 300 g button mushrooms thick and keep 1 cup green peas ready.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and 1 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil in a handi and bloom 1 inch cinnamon, 4 cardamom pods, 4 cloves and 1 bay leaf until fragrant, about 40 seconds.
Add 2 sliced onions and fry for 8 minutes until golden, then stir in 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute.
Add 2 pureed tomatoes and 0.5 tsp turmeric and cook until the fat separates, about 6 minutes, then add the mushrooms and saute on high for 4 minutes until their water evaporates.
Add the peas with 0.75 cup water and 1.25 tsp salt, cover the handi tightly, and dum-cook on low heat for 10 minutes.
Uncover and lower the heat, then stir in 0.5 cup coconut milk and warm through for 2 minutes without boiling hard.
Discard the bay leaf and cinnamon and serve, letting the whole-spice fragrance shine without any powdered masala.
tips: Add the coconut milk at the very end on low heat so it stays smooth and does not curdle.
The whole spices replace garam masala; adding powder would muddy the delicate coconut aroma.
Fish out the bay leaf and cinnamon before serving to avoid a hard whole-spice bite.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with appam, malabar parotta or steamed rice and a side of thoran to complete the southern spread.

variations.name: Punjabi Mushroom Matar
variations.description: The rich Punjabi rendition: mushrooms and peas in a cashew-smooth tomato gravy finished with cream and crushed kasuri methi, with butter swapped for bilona ghee. Plush and mildly sweet, it turns a humble sabzi into a restaurant-worthy dish. A treat for guests.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: replaces butter for the same lush body plus a nutty bilona aroma

steps: Slice 300 g button mushrooms thick and keep 1 cup green peas ready.
Soak 12 cashews in warm water for 15 minutes, then blend with 2 boiled onions and 3 tomatoes to a smooth paste.

Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pan and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds, then add the blended paste with 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp red chilli powder and 1.5 tsp coriander powder and cook for 9 minutes until the ghee separates.
Add the mushrooms and saute on high heat for 4 minutes until their water dries off and they take on colour.
Add the peas with 1 cup water and 1.25 tsp salt, cover, and simmer for 8 minutes until the peas are tender and the gravy turns velvety.
Lower the heat, stir in 3 tbsp cream and 0.75 tsp garam masala, and warm through for 2 minutes without boiling.
Crush 1.5 tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pan and stir it in just before serving.
tips: Saute the mushrooms hard before adding the peas so their moisture does not thin the creamy gravy.
Keep the heat low once cream goes in to stop it from splitting.
Strain the cashew paste for the silkiest, most restaurant-style finish.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with butter naan or ghee pulao, garnished with a cream swirl, kasuri methi and a few sauteed mushroom slices on top.

variations.name: Classic Onion Paratha
variations.description: A stuffed onion paratha done the honest way, where finely diced onions are salted, drained and lightly bound so the filling stays sweet and jammy instead of watery. Roasted cumin and a little chaat masala give it that dhaba tang. Griddled in ghee, the onions caramelise faintly against the khapli crust.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: its supple gluten wraps the moist onion filling without tearing at the seam

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bastes the paratha so the trapped onions steam sweet while the crust turns golden

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with a pinch of salt and about 0.75 cup water for 6 minutes into a soft, non-sticky dough, then cover and rest it for 15 minutes.
Finely dice 2 large onions, toss with 0.5 tsp salt, and set aside 10 minutes; then squeeze out the released juice thoroughly so the filling will not soak through the paratha.
Mix the drained onion with 1 tsp roasted cumin, 1 tsp chaat masala, 0.75 tsp red chilli powder, 3 tbsp coriander, remaining salt and 1.5 tbsp besan, which soaks up any stray moisture.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, roll one into a 4-inch disc, mound 2 tbsp of the onion filling in the centre, pleat the edges shut, and press flat.
Dust with khapli atta and roll gently into a 6-inch round, easing outward from the centre so the seam does not split.
Cook on a medium tava, brushing both faces with Anveshan Ghee, flipping twice, until deep golden spots form and the onion smells sweet, about 3 minutes per paratha.
tips: The besan is a safety net; it binds any onion juice you could not squeeze out and stops the dough turning soggy.
Roll slowly and stop the moment filling threatens to poke through, patching any thin spot with a dab of dough.
Make the filling just before stuffing, since salted onion keeps weeping water the longer it sits.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with thick curd and a spoon of lemon pickle; a side of raw onion rings dusted with chaat masala doubles down on the theme.

variations.name: Masala Onion Paratha
variations.description: A Karnataka-style masala onion paratha where garam masala and coriander powder join the onions, and a curry-leaf tempering in wood-pressed groundnut oil is folded through for a distinctly South Indian aroma. The filling is briefly sauteed rather than raw, giving it a soft, cooked sweetness. It eats like an eriyappa-meets-paratha comfort food.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: gives a soft yet sturdy wrap that holds the cooked masala-onion filling neatly

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: tempers the curry leaves and griddles the paratha with a mellow, nutty South Indian warmth

steps: Bring 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta together with a little salt and roughly 0.75 cup water, kneading 6 minutes into a pliable dough; rest it covered for 15 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil, crackle 0.5 tsp mustard seeds and 12 curry leaves for 20 seconds, then add 2 finely chopped large onions and the minced green chilli.

Saute on medium until the onions turn soft and pale gold, about 5 minutes, then stir in 1 tsp garam masala, 1.5 tsp coriander powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric and remaining salt and cook one minute more; cool completely.
Split the dough into 8 balls, flatten one, spoon 2 tbsp of the cooled masala onion into the middle, draw the edges together, seal, and press down.
Roll the stuffed ball into a 6-inch round on a floured board, working gently so the moist filling stays put.
Griddle on a medium tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Groundnut Oil, turning until richly spotted and fragrant, about 3 minutes per paratha.
tips: Cooking the onion filling first means it will never leak, so this version is the most beginner-proof to stuff.
Let the filling cool fully; warm filling steams the dough from inside and makes it tear.
Double the tempered onion and use the extra as a quick side for rice or dosa.
variations.servingSuggestion: Best with coconut chutney and a small bowl of sambar for dipping, the way a Karnataka tiffin plate would frame it.

variations.name: Spicy Onion Paratha
variations.description: An Andhra-hot onion paratha where slit green chillies and coarsely cracked black pepper set the tone, tempered only slightly by the onion's natural sweetness. Wood-pressed sesame oil, a staple of Andhra kitchens, gives it a toasty, savoury edge. This is the paratha for those who like their food to bite back.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: the robust flour balances the fiery filling with a grounding, wholesome chew

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sesame Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed gingelly oil is the authentic Andhra fat and adds a deep toasted note to the crust

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with a pinch of salt and about 0.75 cup water into a soft dough over 6 minutes, then rest it under a bowl for 15 minutes.
Chop 2 large onions and 4 green chillies very fine, mix with 0.5 tsp salt, wait 10 minutes, and wring out the juice so the fierce filling stays dry.
Fold in 1 tsp cracked black pepper, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp roasted cumin, remaining salt and 2 tbsp besan until the mixture clumps loosely.
Roll the dough into 8 balls, open one into a 4-inch cup, load 2 tbsp of the chilli-onion filling, close the edges over the top, and seal firmly.
Flatten and roll into a 6-inch round, dusting well, and patch any spot where the green chilli threatens to break through.
Cook on a medium-high tava, brushing both faces with Anveshan Sesame Oil, flipping until charred-gold and blistered, about 3 minutes per paratha.
tips: Deseed the green chillies if you want the flavour without full Andhra heat.
Cracked pepper added at the end keeps its perfume, so avoid grinding it to a fine dust.
A dollop of curd worked into the dough softens the finished paratha if you plan to pack it for lunch.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with cool tomato-pachadi and plenty of thick curd to douse the heat, alongside sliced raw onion and lime.

variations.name: Garlic Onion Paratha
variations.description: A Telangana favourite that marries sweet onions with a bold hit of garlic, the garlic first sizzled in ghee so it turns nutty rather than raw and sharp. The two alliums together make an intensely savoury filling with a lingering aroma. It is hearty enough to eat on its own with just curd.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: carries the rich garlic-onion filling with a soft, nutty crumb that stays tender

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: used to bloom the garlic and to baste, marrying the alliums with a buttery finish

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with salt and roughly 0.75 cup water for 6 minutes into a smooth dough, cover, and let it rest 15 minutes.
Mince 12 garlic cloves, warm 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, and fry the garlic on low for about 2 minutes until pale gold and sweet-smelling, then take it off the heat.

Finely chop 2 large onions, salt them, rest 10 minutes, squeeze out the water, and stir in the cooked garlic-ghee, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric and 3 tbsp coriander leaves.
Portion the dough into 8 balls, cup one, spoon in 2 tbsp of the garlic-onion filling, gather and seal the top, and flatten gently.
Roll into an even 6-inch round with light strokes so the juicy filling does not push out at the seam.
Cook on a medium tava, brushing each side with Anveshan Ghee, turning until deeply golden and aromatic, about 3 minutes per paratha.
tips: Frying the garlic before it goes in the filling is what stops the paratha tasting raw and pungent.
Chop rather than paste the garlic, so you get little sweet nuggets in every bite.
The garlic-onion filling can be made a day ahead and refrigerated; drain any liquid before stuffing.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with plain hung curd and a fiery red garlic chutney, plus a wedge of lime to cut the richness.

variations.name: Cheesy Onion Paratha
variations.description: A playful, indulgent version popular in Bihar's small-town cafes, where sharp onions and gooey grated cheese are stuffed together so the sweetness of the onion cuts the richness of the cheese. A pinch of chilli flakes keeps it from feeling flat. It pulls into cheesy strings the moment you tear it.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: forms a forgiving dough that seals tightly around the melting cheese-onion core

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: crisps the outside to gold while the cheese within stays stretchy and molten

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 0.75 tsp salt and about 0.75 cup water for 6 minutes into a soft dough, then rest it covered for 15 minutes.
Finely chop 1 large onion, sprinkle with a little salt, wait 10 minutes, and squeeze out the juice so the cheese filling does not turn watery.
Combine the drained onion with 1 cup grated mozzarella, 0.5 cup grated cheddar, 0.75 tsp chilli flakes, 0.5 tsp black pepper and 2 tbsp coriander.
Divide the dough into 6 balls, roll one into a 4-inch disc, pile 3 tbsp of the cheese-onion mix in the centre, seal the edges over it, and press flat.
Roll out gently to a 6-inch round, keeping pressure light so the cheese stays sealed inside.
Cook on a medium tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee and pressing the centre, until golden and crisp with a molten middle, about 3 minutes per paratha.
tips: Squeeze the onion well; excess onion water is the main reason a cheesy paratha turns soggy.
Eat these fresh off the tava while the cheese still stretches, as it sets quickly on cooling.
Swap half the cheese for grated paneer if you want a lighter, less oily pull.
variations.servingSuggestion: Cut into quarters and serve with a smoky tomato-chilli dip or schezwan sauce, with a crunchy kachumber salad on the side.

variations.name: Classic Palak Paratha
variations.description: A vivid green paratha where blanched spinach is pureed straight into the khapli dough rather than stuffed, colouring it emerald and lacing every layer with iron-rich greens. Blanching keeps the colour bright and strips the raw grassiness. Soft, mildly spiced and ghee-griddled, it is the gentlest way to feed greens to the whole family.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: takes on the spinach puree into a soft green dough that stays supple for hours

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bastes the green paratha to a golden finish and enriches the plain dough

steps: Blanch 3 cups spinach in boiling water for 45 seconds, then plunge it into cold water to lock the colour, drain, and blend to a smooth puree with no added water.
In a bowl combine 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta, the spinach puree, 1 tsp ginger-chilli paste, 1 tsp roasted cumin, 0.5 tsp ajwain, 0.25 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt.
Add 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and knead, splashing in only up to 0.25 cup water if needed, for 6 minutes into a soft, non-sticky green dough; rest it covered 15 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, dust with khapli atta, and roll each into a 6-inch round of even thickness.
Heat a tava on medium and cook the first side 45 seconds until faint bubbles rise, then flip and brush with Anveshan Ghee.
Turn once more, ghee the second side, and press with a spatula until golden-brown spots appear across both faces, about 3 minutes per paratha.
tips: Blanch, do not boil, the spinach; long boiling dulls the green and washes out the nutrients.
Because the puree is watery, add water to the dough only if it feels dry, or it will turn sticky.
The green dough keeps a day in the fridge; a squeeze of lemon in the puree helps hold the colour.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm with a bowl of garlicky curd or plain raita and a spoon of tomato chutney; it also makes a striking green base for a frankie roll.

variations.name: Masala Palak Paratha
variations.description: A heartier Haryanvi take where the spinach dough is built up with garam masala, coriander powder and a spoon of besan for a savoury, rustic bite that suits a farmhouse breakfast. The besan lends body and a faint nuttiness. Cooked in wood-pressed groundnut oil, it is filling enough to power a long morning.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: combines with besan and spinach into a robust, rustic dough with real staying power

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed groundnut oil crisps the paratha with a hearty, nutty aroma

steps: Blanch 3 cups spinach for 45 seconds, cool it in iced water, drain well, and puree until smooth without adding water.
Tip 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta and 0.25 cup besan into a bowl, then add the spinach puree, 1 tsp garam masala, 1.5 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 0.5 tsp ajwain and 1 tsp salt.
Drizzle in 2 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and knead, using up to 0.2 cup water only if needed, for 7 minutes into a firm, pliable dough; rest it 15 minutes.
Shape 8 balls and roll each on a floured board into a 7-inch round a little thicker than usual to carry the hearty dough.
Warm a tava on medium-high, lay a paratha down, and cook 40 seconds until the surface turns matte.
Flip, brush with Anveshan Groundnut Oil, turn again, oil the second side, and press until both faces are deep golden, about 3 minutes per paratha.
tips: Toast the besan lightly in a dry pan beforehand if you want to be sure its raw taste disappears.
Keep this dough firmer than the classic; the besan drinks up moisture as it rests.
These reheat well on a dry tava, making them a good batch-cook option for busy mornings.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a bowl of homemade white butter and a green-chilli pickle, with a tall glass of salted chaas on the side.

variations.name: Spicy Palak Paratha
variations.description: A Delhi street-style green paratha with attitude, the spinach dough spiked with slit green chillies and coarsely cracked black pepper for a bold, warming heat. A little amchur brings the trademark chatpata tang. It is the kind of paratha you find sizzling on a busy Purani Dilli corner at breakfast.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: gives the spicy green paratha a wholesome chew that carries the bold seasoning

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: griddles the paratha crisp and golden, mellowing the sharp chilli heat

steps: Blanch 3 cups spinach 45 seconds, shock it cold, drain, and blend with 4 green chillies to a smooth, flecked green puree.
Mix 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with the spicy puree, 1 tsp cracked black pepper, 1 tsp amchur, 1 tsp roasted cumin and 1 tsp salt until the colour is even.
Add 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and knead, using up to 0.2 cup water only if the dough feels dry, for 6 minutes into a soft dough; rest it covered 15 minutes.
Divide into 8 balls and roll each into a 6-inch round, dusting lightly so the moist dough does not stick.
Cook on a medium tava for 45 seconds until small bubbles form, then flip and brush with Anveshan Ghee.
Turn again, ghee the other side, and press the edges until crisp golden-brown spots cover both faces, about 3 minutes per paratha.
tips: Blend the chillies into the puree rather than chopping them in, so the heat spreads evenly through every bite.
Add the amchur to the dough, not the tava, so its tang runs all the way through.
For extra street-style flavour, sprinkle a little chaat masala over the paratha the moment it comes off the heat.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a bowl of cold, thick dahi and a fiery red-chilli achar, the classic Dilli nashta pairing, plus sliced onion and lime.

variations.name: Garlic Palak Paratha
variations.description: A Telangana-style green paratha where garlic, browned in ghee until sweet, is worked through the spinach dough for a deeply savoury, aromatic result. The garlic and iron-rich greens are a natural, nourishing pairing. Rustic and satisfying, it needs little more than curd alongside.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: holds the garlicky spinach dough together with a soft, wholesome bite

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: browns the garlic to a mellow sweetness and bastes the paratha golden

steps: Blanch 3 cups spinach 45 seconds, cool it in cold water, drain, and puree smooth without adding water.
Warm 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and fry 2 tbsp minced garlic on low for about 2 minutes until pale gold and fragrant, then let it cool a little.
Combine 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with the spinach puree, the garlic-ghee, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, 0.5 tsp roasted cumin and 1 tsp salt.
Knead, adding up to 0.2 cup water only if needed, for 6 minutes into a soft green dough; cover and rest it 15 minutes.
Roll the dough into 8 balls and flatten each into a 6-inch round, dusting so the sticky dough releases cleanly.
Cook on a medium tava, brushing both faces with Anveshan Ghee, flipping until golden and heady with garlic, about 3 minutes per paratha.
tips: Brown the garlic only lightly, since it will cook a little more inside the paratha on the tava.
Reserve a spoon of the garlic-ghee to brush over the finished paratha for an extra aromatic hit.
This dough is best used the same day, as garlic in a raw dough sharpens overnight.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a bowl of plain curd tempered with mustard seeds and curry leaves, and a side of tomato-garlic pachadi.

variations.name: Cheesy Palak Paratha
variations.description: A fun stuffed twist gaining popularity in Jharkhand's towns, where the green spinach dough hugs a molten cheese centre, so a bright emerald crust gives way to a stretchy, savoury core. The mild spinach dough lets the cheese shine. It is a guaranteed way to make greens exciting for children.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: forms a pliable green dough that seals neatly around the cheese without splitting

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: crisps the green crust to gold while keeping the cheese inside soft and stretchy

steps: Blanch 3 cups spinach 45 seconds, refresh it in cold water, drain, and puree smooth without extra water.
Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with the spinach puree and 0.75 tsp salt, adding up to 0.2 cup water only if needed, for 6 minutes into a soft dough; rest 15 minutes.
Mix 1 cup grated mozzarella with 0.5 cup grated processed cheese, 0.5 tsp black pepper and 0.5 tsp chilli flakes for the filling.
Divide the green dough into 6 balls, roll one into a 4-inch disc, place 3 tbsp of the cheese mix in the centre, gather the edges over the top, and seal.
Dust and roll gently into a 6-inch paratha, keeping the pressure even so the cheese does not break the seam.
Cook on a medium tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee and pressing the centre, until golden and crisp with a molten core, about 3 minutes per paratha.
tips: Drain the spinach very well before pureeing; a watery dough will not hold the cheese in.
Serve straight from the tava while the cheese still pulls into strings.
Mix a spoon of finely chopped spinach into the cheese too, for a double dose of green.
variations.servingSuggestion: Cut into wedges and serve with a tangy tomato-basil dip or ketchup for kids, and a cooling mint raita for the grown-ups.

variations.name: Classic Paneer Paratha
variations.description: A rich, protein-packed breakfast paratha where freshly grated paneer is lightly spiced and folded into a soft Anveshan Khapli Atta dough, then griddled in ghee. Grating the paneer fine and keeping the filling barely spiced lets the milky sweetness of the cheese shine through the crisp, nutty crust.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Kneaded into a soft dough; the nutty wholegrain flavour complements the milky paneer.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Bilona Ghee
ingredients.note: One spoon in the dough and the rest for roasting the parathas to a golden, crisp finish.

steps: Knead 3 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Bilona Ghee, 0.5 tsp salt and about 1.25 cups water into a soft, pliable dough; cover and rest 20 minutes.
Grate 250 g paneer finely so there are no lumps, which keeps the filling smooth and easy to roll.
Mix the paneer with 2 finely chopped green chillies, a grated 1-inch piece of ginger, 1.5 tsp roasted cumin powder, 0.75 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp amchur, 4 tbsp coriander and 0.75 tsp salt.
Divide dough and filling into 8 each; flatten a dough ball, place 2 tbsp filling inside, gather and seal, then roll gently to a 7-inch round with a light atta dusting.
Roast on a hot tava for about 1 minute until it blisters, flip and brush with 0.5 tsp ghee, cooking each side 1-2 minutes until golden with brown spots.
Stack the parathas under a cloth so they stay soft while you finish the rest.
tips: Grate the paneer rather than crumbling it; fine strands bind better and prevent tearing.
If using shop paneer that feels firm, soak it in warm water for 10 minutes and pat dry to soften.
Do not over-salt; paneer needs only a light hand so its natural sweetness comes through.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with a bowl of thick curd, a drizzle of white butter and a spoon of tangy pickle.

variations.name: Masala Paneer Paratha
variations.description: A restaurant-style paneer paratha where the filling is enriched with garam masala, coriander powder and a little onion for a fuller, more savoury flavour. The Anveshan Khapli Atta dough and ghee crust turn it into a satisfying, dhaba-worthy meal in itself.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The wholegrain dough base that carries the richly spiced paneer filling.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Bilona Ghee
ingredients.note: Worked into the dough and brushed on the tava for a fragrant, crisp golden crust.

steps: Knead 3 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Bilona Ghee, 0.5 tsp salt and about 1.25 cups water into a soft dough; cover and rest 20 minutes.
Grate 250 g paneer finely and finely chop 1 small onion, then squeeze the onion dry in your hand.
Mix the paneer and onion with 1 tsp garam masala, 1.5 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 2 chopped green chillies, 0.75 tsp red chilli powder, 4 tbsp coriander and 0.75 tsp salt.
Divide dough and filling into 8 each; stuff 2 tbsp filling into each dough ball, seal, and roll gently to a 7-inch round, dusting with atta.
Roast on a hot tava for 1 minute, flip, brush with 0.5 tsp ghee and cook each side 1-2 minutes until golden with crisp brown flecks.
Keep the cooked parathas soft and warm under a cloth as you finish the batch.
tips: Squeeze the chopped onion dry before mixing so its moisture does not make the filling wet.
Bloom the garam masala for a few seconds in a dry pan to deepen its aroma.
Add the onion raw and finely chopped for crunch, or saute it first for a mellower, sweeter note.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a spiced cucumber-mint raita and a wedge of lemon to cut the richness.

variations.name: Spicy Paneer Paratha
variations.description: A bold, fiery paneer paratha where green chillies and coarsely crushed black pepper cut through the mild cheese for a real kick. The creamy paneer tempers the heat just enough, all wrapped in a nutty Anveshan Khapli Atta crust griddled in ghee.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The soft, nutty dough that balances the spicy paneer filling within.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Bilona Ghee
ingredients.note: In the dough and on the tava; its richness softens the heat while crisping the crust.

steps: Knead 3 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Bilona Ghee, 0.5 tsp salt and about 1.25 cups water into a soft dough; cover and rest 20 minutes.
Grate 250 g paneer finely and coarsely crush 1 tsp black peppercorns for a punchy, uneven bite.

Mix the paneer with the crushed pepper, 4 finely chopped green chillies, 1 tsp red chilli powder, a grated 1-inch piece of ginger, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1 tsp crushed kasuri methi, 4 tbsp coriander and 0.75 tsp salt.
Divide dough and filling into 8 each; stuff 2 tbsp filling into each dough ball, seal, and roll gently to a 7-inch round with an atta dusting.
Roast on a hot tava for 1 minute, flip, brush with 0.5 tsp ghee and cook each side 1-2 minutes until golden with crisp spots.
Stack under a cloth to keep the parathas warm and soft while the rest cook.
tips: Crush the pepper fresh for a brighter, more fragrant heat than pre-ground pepper.
The creamy paneer mutes the chilli, so use more than you think for the same kick.
Deseed a couple of chillies if serving to those who prefer milder heat.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a cooling boondi raita and sliced onions dressed in lemon to balance the spice.

variations.name: Garlic Paneer Paratha
variations.description: A garlicky, aromatic paneer paratha where sauteed garlic and a hint of chilli flakes weave through the creamy filling for a savoury, moreish flavour. Ghee-roasting toasts the garlic notes and the Anveshan Khapli Atta gives a hearty, wholesome bite.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Kneaded into the dough; its earthy nuttiness pairs beautifully with toasted garlic and paneer.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Bilona Ghee
ingredients.note: Used to saute the garlic and roast the parathas, layering in a rich toasted-garlic aroma.

steps: Knead 3 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Bilona Ghee, 0.5 tsp salt and about 1.25 cups water into a soft dough; cover and rest 20 minutes.
Finely chop 8 garlic cloves and saute in 1 tbsp Anveshan Bilona Ghee over medium heat for 1-2 minutes until pale gold and fragrant, then cool.
Grate 250 g paneer finely and mix with the sauteed garlic, 1 tsp red chilli flakes, 1 chopped green chilli, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 4 tbsp coriander and 0.75 tsp salt.
Divide dough and filling into 8 each; stuff 2 tbsp filling into each ball, seal, and roll gently to a 7-inch round, dusting with atta.
Roast on a hot tava for 1 minute, flip, brush with 0.5 tsp ghee and cook each side 1-2 minutes until golden with toasty brown spots.
Stack under a cloth to keep soft while you finish the remaining parathas.
tips: Sauteing the garlic first removes the raw bite and gives a sweet, nutty depth that suits paneer.
Add the chilli flakes to the hot ghee with the garlic for a moment to bloom their colour and aroma.
A little grated cheese mixed in makes this even richer if you are cooking for children.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a garlicky yoghurt dip and a simple tomato salad for a light, flavourful meal.

variations.name: Cheesy Paneer Paratha
variations.description: An indulgent double-dairy paratha where grated cheese melts into the paneer filling for a doubly creamy, stretchy centre. The Anveshan Khapli Atta dough griddled in ghee crisps into a golden shell around the molten paneer-cheese core, a guaranteed hit with kids.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The nutty wholegrain dough that crisps around the rich paneer-and-cheese filling.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Bilona Ghee
ingredients.note: A spoon in the dough and the rest for roasting to a crisp, cheese-melting golden crust.

steps: Knead 3 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tbsp Anveshan Bilona Ghee, 0.5 tsp salt and about 1.25 cups water into a soft dough; cover and rest 20 minutes.
Grate 200 g paneer finely and mix with 1 cup grated mozzarella, 1 finely chopped green chilli, 0.5 tsp black pepper powder, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 3 tbsp coriander and 0.5 tsp salt.
Bring the filling together gently; it should be soft but hold a ball without weeping moisture.
Divide dough and filling into 8 each; encase 2 tbsp filling in each ball, seal well and roll gently to a 6-inch round so the cheese stays contained.
Roast on a medium-hot tava for 1-2 minutes per side, brushing with 0.5 tsp ghee, until golden and crisp with the cheese melted inside.
Serve immediately while the centre is molten and stretchy.
tips: Roll these thicker and smaller so the melting cheese does not burst through the seams.
Cook on medium heat so the cheese melts fully before the crust over-browns.
A pinch of oregano or chilli flakes gives a pizza-like twist the kids love.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with tomato ketchup and a tangy green chutney for dipping.

variations.name: Classic Paneer Masala
variations.description: The dependable everyday paneer curry built on a smooth onion-tomato base finished with cream and garam masala. Soft paneer cubes soak up a medium-spiced, subtly sweet gravy, the kind of reliable dish that turns up on weeknight tables and dinner-party menus alike.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: a clean base fat to bhuno the onion-tomato masala without overpowering it

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: swirled in at the end to lend the gravy a restaurant-style aroma

steps: Cube 300 g paneer and soak the cubes in warm water while you make the gravy so they stay soft.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds, then fry 2 chopped onions with 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste for 6 minutes until golden.
Add 3 pureed tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder and 2 tsp coriander powder, cooking 8 minutes until the masala thickens and the oil separates.
Pour in half a cup of water, simmer 3 minutes, then drain and slide in the paneer cubes with 1 tsp salt.
Simmer gently for 4 minutes so the paneer softens and absorbs the gravy without turning rubbery.
Stir in 3 tbsp cream and 0.75 tsp garam masala, swirl in 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee, and cook a final minute.
tips: Soaking paneer in warm water before adding keeps it soft and prevents a chewy texture.
Do not boil hard once the paneer is in; a gentle simmer keeps the cubes tender.
Puree the tomatoes for a smooth gravy, or leave them chopped for a more rustic finish.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with butter roti or jeera rice, garnished with a swirl of cream and a few coriander leaves.

variations.name: Kadai Paneer
variations.description: A robust, semi-dry paneer tossed with chunky onions and capsicum in a freshly pounded kadai masala of coarse coriander and dried red chilli. The aromatic ground spices and crisp peppers make this bold and rustic, worlds apart from a smooth creamy gravy.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: a sturdy fat that carries the coarse kadai masala and stir-fries the peppers

steps: Dry-roast 2 tbsp coriander seeds with 4 dried red chillies for 2 minutes until fragrant, then coarsely pound into a rough kadai masala.
Cube 300 g paneer and cut 1 capsicum and 1 onion into 1-inch chunks, keeping the second onion chopped fine.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil, sear the paneer, capsicum and onion chunks for 3 minutes until lightly charred, then set aside.
In the same pan fry the chopped onion with 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste for 5 minutes, add 3 chopped tomatoes and half the pounded masala, and cook 7 minutes until thick.
Return the seared paneer and vegetables with 1 tsp salt and the rest of the kadai masala, tossing on high for 3 minutes to coat.
Crush 1 tbsp kasuri methi over the top with 0.5 tsp garam masala and toss for a minute until fragrant and semi-dry.
tips: Pounding the coriander and chilli fresh is what gives kadai paneer its signature coarse aroma.
Sear the paneer and peppers separately first so they keep some bite and char.
Keep the dish semi-dry and clinging rather than saucy for an authentic kadai texture.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve sizzling from a kadai or handi with laccha paratha and sliced onions dusted with chaat masala.

variations.name: Butter Paneer
variations.description: The silky restaurant-style paneer makhani in a smooth tomato-cashew gravy enriched with butter and cream. Mildly sweet, glossy and luxurious, the paneer cubes bathe in a velvety sauce balanced with jaggery and a whisper of kasuri methi.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: used to bhuno the tomato base, adding a nutty depth beneath the butter

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: a natural swap for white sugar that balances the tomato tang the makhani way

steps: Simmer 5 roughly chopped tomatoes with 15 cashews, 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and a cup of water for 12 minutes until very soft.
Cool slightly, blend to a smooth puree, then strain through a sieve for that signature silky makhani texture.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee with 2 tbsp butter, add 1.5 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder off the heat, then pour in the strained puree carefully as it will splutter.
Simmer on low for 10 minutes, stirring often, until it thickens, deepens in colour and the fat floats to the top.
Add 1 tsp salt and 1.5 tsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder, then slide in 300 g cubed paneer and simmer 4 minutes.
Finish with 4 tbsp cream, 0.75 tsp garam masala, 1 tbsp crushed kasuri methi and the last tbsp of butter, swirling gently before serving.
tips: Straining the puree is the single biggest step towards restaurant-smooth makhani, so do not skip it.
Balance is everything; if too tangy add a little more jaggery, if too sweet a squeeze of lemon.
For a smoky dhaba touch, place a hot charcoal in a bowl set in the gravy, drizzle with ghee, and cover for two minutes.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with butter naan or jeera rice, a swirl of extra cream on top and julienned ginger for the full restaurant look.

variations.name: Handi Paneer
variations.description: A slow-cooked handi paneer where whole spices bloom in the fat and a yogurt-based gravy simmers gently in a clay pot until fragrant and layered. Bay leaf, cardamom and cloves lend a warming, aromatic depth that sets this apart from the quick tomato gravies.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: the traditional handi fat in which the whole spices bloom slowly

steps: Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a handi and bloom 1 bay leaf, 3 cardamom, 4 cloves and 1 inch cinnamon for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add 3 finely chopped onions with 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and fry on medium for 9 minutes until deep golden.
Lower the heat and whisk in half a cup of yogurt gradually with 1.5 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp red chilli powder, stirring constantly so it does not split.
Cook the gravy for 6 minutes until the ghee separates, then add half a cup of water and 1 tsp salt and simmer 4 minutes.
Slide in 300 g cubed paneer, cover the handi, and simmer on very low for 8 minutes so the flavours meld slowly.
Sprinkle 0.5 tsp garam masala, stir gently, and rest covered for 5 minutes before serving.
tips: Add the yogurt off high heat and whisk constantly to keep the gravy from curdling.
A clay handi holds gentle heat best, but a heavy pan with a tight lid works well too.
Resting the dish covered before serving deepens the whole-spice aroma.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve straight from the handi with sheermal or roomali roti and a side of pickled onions.

variations.name: Punjabi Paneer
variations.description: A rustic Punjabi-style paneer in a robust onion-tomato gravy finished generously with butter and a heavy hand of crushed kasuri methi. Chunky and homely rather than silky, it carries the deep, hearty flavour of a Punjabi household kitchen.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: the pungent base fat that gives this rustic Punjabi gravy its earthy backbone

steps: Cube 300 g paneer and keep it soaking in warm water while you build the gravy.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil to smoking, lower the flame, and fry 3 chopped onions with 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste for 8 minutes until browned.
Add 3 chopped tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1.25 tsp red chilli powder and 2 tsp coriander powder, cooking 7 minutes until pulpy and the oil separates.
Add half a cup of water and 1 tsp salt, simmer 3 minutes, then drain and add the paneer cubes.
Stir in 2 tbsp butter and simmer gently for 5 minutes so the paneer softens into the rich gravy.
Crush 1.5 tbsp kasuri methi generously over the top with 0.75 tsp garam masala and stir for a minute before serving.
tips: Be generous with the kasuri methi here; its aroma is the signature of this Punjabi-style dish.
Keep the gravy chunky and homely rather than blending it smooth.
Mustard oil must be heated to smoking first to mellow its raw sharpness.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with makki di roti or a thick tandoori roti and a glass of chaas for a hearty Punjabi meal.

variations.name: Classic Peas Pulao
variations.description: A comforting matar pulao where sweet green peas are folded through ghee-scented basmati and whole spices. Light, fragrant and quick, it is the everyday festive rice of North Indian homes, with each grain separate and glistening.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee gives the pulao its signature aroma and keeps the grains glossy and separate

steps: Rinse 1.5 cups basmati rice until the water runs clear, soak for 20 minutes, and drain so the grains cook up long and fluffy.
Heat the Anveshan Ghee over medium heat and bloom 1 tsp cumin seeds, 3 cardamom, 3 cloves, a 1 inch cinnamon stick and 1 bay leaf for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the thinly sliced onion and fry for 5 minutes until golden, then add 2 slit green chillies and saute for 30 seconds.
Add 1 cup green peas and saute for 2 minutes, then fold in the drained rice and toss gently for 2 minutes to coat every grain in ghee.
Pour in exactly 3 cups water with 1.5 tsp salt, bring to a rolling boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and fold through 2 tbsp chopped coriander before serving.
tips: If using frozen peas, add them straight in, but blanch fresh peas for 2 minutes first so they cook evenly.
The soaked rice with a 1:2 water ratio keeps the grains distinct and non-sticky.
Rest the pulao before fluffing so the peas and grains settle without breaking.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with cool cucumber raita and a crisp papad, or a simple dal for a light, wholesome meal.

variations.name: Kashmiri Peas Pulao
variations.description: A regal Kashmiri-style matar pulao perfumed with fennel, dry ginger and a whisper of saffron. Warm whole spices and a scatter of nuts give it a gentle, aromatic sweetness suited to the valley's festive tables.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee suits the rich Kashmiri style and carries the warm whole-spice aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: Kashmiri cooking prizes saffron, and a warm-milk soak lends colour and fragrance

steps: Rinse and soak 1.5 cups basmati rice for 20 minutes, drain, and steep 0.25 tsp Anveshan Saffron in 3 tbsp warm milk.
Heat the Anveshan Ghee over medium heat, fry 10 slivered almonds until golden and remove, then add 1 tsp fennel seeds, 4 cardamom, 3 cloves and a 1 inch cinnamon stick and bloom for 30 seconds.
Stir in 0.5 tsp dry ginger powder and 1 cup green peas, and saute for 2 minutes until the spices coat the peas.
Add the drained rice and toss gently for 2 minutes, then pour in 3 cups water with 1.5 tsp salt and bring to a boil.
Drizzle the saffron milk over the top, cover, and cook on the lowest heat for 13 minutes until the water is absorbed and golden threads streak the rice.
Rest for 5 minutes, fluff gently, and scatter the fried almonds over the top before serving.
tips: Fennel and dry ginger are the defining Kashmiri notes, so do not substitute them with generic garam masala.
Bloom the fennel seeds only briefly, as they turn bitter if over-toasted.
Steep the saffron in warm, not boiling, milk to preserve its delicate aroma.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a bowl of Kashmiri dum aloo or a yogurt-based curry, garnished with extra slivered almonds.

variations.name: Himachali Spiced Peas Pulao
variations.description: A mountain-style Himachali pulao where peas share the pot with a bright green paste of mint, coriander and green chilli. Herby and mildly hot, it carries the fresh, brisk character of hill-country cooking.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee cooks the green paste smoothly and keeps the grains glossy

steps: Rinse and soak 1.5 cups basmati rice for 20 minutes and drain, then grind 0.5 cup mint, 0.5 cup coriander and 3 green chillies into a smooth green paste.
Heat the Anveshan Ghee over medium heat, add 1 tsp cumin seeds, 3 cloves and a 1 inch cinnamon stick, and let them crackle for 20 seconds.
Add the sliced onion and fry for 5 minutes until soft, then stir in 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the ground green paste and saute for 3 minutes until the raw smell fades and the ghee separates, then add 1 cup green peas and cook 2 minutes.
Fold in the drained rice and toss for 2 minutes, then pour in 3 cups water with 1.5 tsp salt and bring to a rolling boil.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes, rest for 5 minutes, then fluff gently to reveal the green-flecked, fragrant grains.
tips: Cook the green paste until the ghee separates so the mint loses any raw bitterness.
Adjust the number of green chillies to control the heat of the herby paste.
Blanch fresh peas briefly so they stay bright green against the pale rice.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a tangy yogurt raita or a bowl of rajma, adding sliced onions dressed with lemon on the side.

variations.name: Uttarakhandi Festive Peas Pulao
variations.description: A festive Garhwali-style peas pulao enriched with fried onions, cashews and warm whole spices, dum-cooked until deeply aromatic. It carries the celebratory heft of a hill-wedding rice while keeping the sweetness of fresh peas.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: generous bilona ghee gives this festive pulao its rich aroma and sheen

steps: Rinse and soak 1.5 cups basmati rice for 20 minutes and drain, keeping it ready for the dum.
Heat the Anveshan Ghee over medium heat, fry the thinly sliced onions in batches for 8 minutes until deep golden and crisp, then drain, and fry 15 cashews until pale gold.
In the same ghee bloom 4 cardamom, 1 star anise, 4 cloves and a 1 inch cinnamon stick for 20 seconds, then add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
Stir in 0.25 cup whisked yogurt and 1 cup green peas, cook for 2 minutes, then fold in the drained rice and toss gently for 2 minutes.
Pour in 3 cups water with 1.5 tsp salt, bring to a boil, scatter half the fried onions on top, cover tightly, and dum-cook on the lowest heat for 14 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes, fluff gently, and garnish with the remaining fried onions and cashews before serving.
tips: Fry the onions slowly to a crisp golden birista for the sweet depth this festive rice needs.
Whisk the yogurt well and add on low heat so it enriches without curdling.
Layer half the onions inside and save the rest for a generous, glossy garnish.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve on a festive platter with a spicy chana or a creamy korma, topped with a shower of golden fried onions.

variations.name: Odia Quick Peas Pulao
variations.description: A homely, quick Odia-style peas pulao made in a pressure cooker with a light panch phoron temper. It skips long soaking and heavy spicing, delivering soft, mildly fragrant rice on a busy day.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee gives full pulao aroma even in a fast one-pot cooker method

steps: Rinse 1.5 cups basmati rice well and rest it for just 10 minutes, then drain to keep the dish quick.
Heat the Anveshan Ghee in a pressure cooker over medium heat, add 1 tsp panch phoron and 1 bay leaf, and let the seeds crackle for 20 seconds.
Add the chopped onion, julienned ginger and 2 slit green chillies, and saute for 3 minutes until the onion softens.
Stir in 1 cup green peas and 0.25 tsp turmeric, cook for 2 minutes, then add the drained rice and toss for 1 minute.
Pour in 2.5 cups water with 1.5 tsp salt, close the lid, and cook on medium heat for 2 whistles before turning off the flame.
Let the pressure release naturally for 8 minutes, then open, fluff gently with a fork, and serve hot.
tips: Panch phoron gives an eastern-Indian fragrance, so add it whole and let it splutter fully.
Use slightly less water in the cooker than the open-pot method to avoid mushy grains.
Release the pressure naturally so the peas and rice stay intact.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a simple dalma or a tomato-onion chutney, and a spoon of ghee melting on top.

variations.name: Classic Pyaaz Paratha
variations.description: The dhaba classic: a soft khapli-atta paratha stuffed with sharp, juicy onions seasoned with just cumin, chilli and coriander, roasted until sweet and blistered. The onions half-melt inside the paratha, turning mellow and fragrant against the crisp crust. Simple, punchy and endlessly comforting with a bowl of curd.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Nutty emmer wheat makes a soft dough that seals the juicy onion filling well

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A spoon in the dough and the rest to roast the parathas to a golden crust

ingredients.name: Anveshan Wood-Pressed Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: A little in the dough brings a warm pungency that suits raw onion

steps: Rub 1 tbsp Anveshan Wood-Pressed Mustard Oil into 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 0.5 tsp salt, then knead with about 0.75 cup water into a soft, pliable dough and rest 15 minutes.

Just before stuffing, mix the 2 chopped onions with minced green chilli, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 0.75 tsp red chilli, 0.75 tsp amchur, coriander and 0.5 tsp salt, keeping it dry and not letting it sit.
Flatten a dough ball, place 2 tbsp of the onion mixture in the centre, gather the edges over the top and pinch firmly to seal.
Dust with atta and roll out gently to a 7-inch round, pressing lightly so the juicy onion does not break the seam.
Roast on a hot tava over medium heat for about 1 minute until bubbles rise, then flip and brush with Anveshan Ghee.
Turn once more and press the edges with a spatula, cooking each side 1 to 2 minutes until deep golden blisters form and the onion smells sweet.
tips: Salt the onion only at the last moment, or it will weep and make the filling too wet to seal.
Roll on a lightly floured surface and work quickly so the onion juices do not soften the dough.
If a paratha tears, patch it with a pinch of dry atta and press before flipping.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with a bowl of chilled curd, a spoon of mango pickle and thin slices of raw onion on the side.

variations.name: Masala Pyaaz Paratha
variations.description: A Goan-leaning masala paratha where the onions are cooked down with garam masala and roasted coriander into a soft, savoury-sweet jam before stuffing. Cooking the onions first deepens their flavour and keeps the paratha dry and easy to roll. Warm-spiced and mellow, it eats like a treat.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The hearty emmer crumb pairs well with the spiced onion jam

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: To cook the onion masala and roast the parathas to a golden finish

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 0.5 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and about 0.75 cup water into a soft dough and rest, covered, for 15 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee over medium heat and crackle 0.75 tsp cumin seeds, then add 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste and the 3 chopped onions and fry 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in 1 tsp garam masala, 1.5 tsp roasted coriander powder, 0.75 tsp red chilli, 0.25 tsp turmeric and 0.5 tsp salt, and cook 3 minutes until jammy and dry, then mix in the coriander and cool.
Cup each dough ball, fill with 2 tbsp of the cooled onion masala, pinch the seam shut and pat into a disc.
Roll out to a 7-inch round with even pressure so the soft filling stays enclosed.
Roast on a medium-hot tava, brushing both sides with Anveshan Ghee, for 1 to 2 minutes each until golden-brown and fragrant.
tips: Cook the onions until they look dry and jam-like; a wet filling will burst through as you roll.
Let the masala cool completely before stuffing so the dough stays firm.
The onion jam keeps three days refrigerated and is delicious stirred into an omelette too.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a cooling mint raita and a wedge of lemon, with extra ghee brushed over the top.

variations.name: Spicy Pyaaz Paratha
variations.description: A bracing version built for cold mornings, where raw onion meets plenty of green chilli and coarsely cracked black pepper for a clean, warming heat. A little sesame oil in the dough gives a toasty depth that suits the mountain-style spicing. Sharp, aromatic and genuinely fiery.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Wholegrain emmer balances the sharp chilli-and-pepper onion filling

ingredients.name: Anveshan Wood-Pressed Sesame Oil
ingredients.note: Worked into the dough for a warm, toasted backbone

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: For roasting the parathas to a crisp, golden crust

steps: Rub 1 tbsp Anveshan Wood-Pressed Sesame Oil into 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 0.5 tsp salt, then knead with roughly 0.75 cup water to a supple dough and rest 15 minutes.

Just before filling, toss the 2 chopped onions with minced green chilli, 1 tsp cracked black pepper, grated ginger, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1 tbsp lemon juice, coriander and 0.5 tsp salt, keeping the mix dry.
Flatten each dough ball, place 2 tbsp of the spicy onion in the middle, draw the edges up and pinch tightly to seal.
Roll out gently to a 7-inch round, easing from the centre so the peppery onion stays inside.
Slap onto a hot tava and cook 1 minute until the base sets, then flip and brush with Anveshan Ghee.
Turn once more and roast each side 1 to 2 minutes, pressing lightly, until crisp brown blisters form and the pepper turns aromatic.
tips: Crack the peppercorns fresh for bursts of warmth rather than the flat heat of fine powder.
Add the lemon and salt at the very end so the onion stays crunchy and the filling does not weep.
Deseed one chilli if you want the flavour without the full mountain-style fire.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve piping hot with thick curd or a bowl of kahwa-style spiced tea for a cold-weather breakfast.

variations.name: Garlic Pyaaz Paratha
variations.description: A hearty hill-style paratha where onions and a heavy hand of garlic are cooked together until sweet and sticky, then folded into the dough. The garlic caramelises alongside the onion for a rich, mellow filling that smells incredible off the tava. Rustic, warming and deeply savoury.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The nutty emmer base carries the sweet onion-garlic filling well

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: To cook the onion and garlic down and roast the parathas golden

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 0.5 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and about 0.75 cup water into a soft dough and rest, covered, for 15 minutes.
Heat 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Ghee over medium heat and cook the chopped garlic for 40 seconds until fragrant, then add the 3 chopped onions and fry 8 to 10 minutes until soft and lightly caramelised.
Stir in 0.75 tsp red chilli, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 0.25 tsp turmeric, crushed kasuri methi and 0.5 tsp salt, cook 2 minutes until dry, then mix in the coriander and cool.
Hollow each dough ball, load 2 tbsp of the onion-garlic filling, pinch the seam closed and flatten into a disc.
Roll out to a 7-inch round with gentle pressure so the filling stays sealed inside.
Roast on a medium tava, brushing both faces with Anveshan Ghee, for 1 to 2 minutes each until golden and the garlic smells sweet and toasty.
tips: Add the garlic before the onion so it perfumes the ghee without burning at high heat later.
Cook the mixture until visibly dry; residual moisture will tear the paratha as you roll.
This robust filling keeps well and makes an excellent stuffing for kulchas too.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a bowl of plain curd and garlic pickle, or alongside a simple rajma for a hearty meal.

variations.name: Cheesy Pyaaz Paratha
variations.description: A crowd-pleasing paratha that pairs sweet sauteed onions with a molten cheese core for a gooey, savoury filling. The onions are softened first so the cheese has a mellow, jammy partner rather than raw crunch. Rich, stretchy and a sure hit with children and adults alike.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Wholegrain emmer keeps the cheesy onion paratha from feeling too heavy

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: To soften the onions and roast the parathas to a golden crust

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 0.5 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and around 0.75 cup water into a soft dough and rest it, covered, for 15 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and saute the 2 chopped onions with the minced green chilli for 5 minutes until soft and pale gold, then cool completely.
Mix the cooled onions with 1 cup grated cheese, 0.5 tsp crushed black pepper, 0.5 tsp chilli flakes, coriander and 0.25 tsp salt until well combined.
Flatten each dough ball, place 2 tbsp of the cheesy onion in the centre, seal the edges over the top and pat into a disc.
Roll out slowly to a 7-inch round so the soft cheese filling stays sealed inside.
Cook on a medium tava, brushing with Anveshan Ghee, for 1 to 2 minutes a side until golden and the cheese is just melting at the seams.
tips: Cool the sauteed onions fully before adding cheese, or the cheese will melt too soon and turn the mix greasy.
Chill the filling for ten minutes so it firms up and seals easily inside the dough.
Serve immediately while the cheese is molten and stretchy.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve straight off the tava with tomato ketchup or a tangy tamarind chutney as a snack or light supper.

variations.name: Classic Rajma
variations.description: The homestyle Punjabi rajma every North Indian grew up on: dark red kidney beans simmered until buttery-soft in a thick onion-tomato masala. The trick is boiling the beans until some break down and thicken the gravy on their own. Comforting, earthy and made to be eaten with rice and a spoon.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed mustard oil is the traditional North Indian fat for rajma and lends a warm pungency

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: a final spoon of bilona ghee gives the gravy its homely richness and shine

steps: Soak 1.5 cups rajma overnight in plenty of water, then pressure-cook with 4 cups fresh water and 0.5 tsp salt for 6 to 7 whistles until a bean mashes with no resistance.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil in a heavy pot until it just smokes, lower the heat, and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds for 30 seconds.
Add 2 finely chopped onions and fry over medium heat for 10 minutes until richly browned, then stir in 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add 3 pureed tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder and 1.5 tsp coriander powder, and cook on medium heat until the oil separates and the masala darkens, about 9 minutes.
Tip in the boiled beans with 1.5 cups of their cooking liquid and the remaining 0.75 tsp salt, then simmer uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes, mashing a ladleful of beans to thicken the gravy.
Stir the gravy often as it thickens so it does not catch at the bottom, adding a splash of hot water if it gets too dense.
Finish with 0.75 tsp garam masala and 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, simmer 2 minutes, and scatter over 3 tbsp chopped fresh coriander.
tips: Old beans never soften properly, so use rajma within its season; a pinch of baking soda in the soak water helps stubborn beans along.
Rajma tastes even better the next day once the gravy sets, so make it ahead when you can.
Mashing some beans is essential; it is what gives homestyle rajma its thick, spoon-coating body without any cream.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve the quintessential rajma-chawal over hot steamed rice with a wedge of raw onion, a spoon of pickle and a glass of chaas alongside.

variations.name: Masala Rajma
variations.description: A coriander-forward rajma where a heavy dose of freshly roasted coriander powder builds an earthy, aromatic gravy without extra heat. A curry-leaf and mustard tempering nods to the southern kitchen it comes from. Lighter and more fragrant than the Punjabi classic, with a citrusy lift.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed groundnut oil keeps the coriander-led gravy clean and light on the palate

steps: Pressure-cook 1.5 cups soaked rajma with 4 cups water and 0.5 tsp salt for 6 to 7 whistles until fully tender, reserving the liquid.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a pan on medium heat and pop 0.5 tsp mustard seeds and 0.5 tsp cumin seeds, then add 10 curry leaves and let them crackle for 10 seconds.
Add 1 large chopped onion and saute for 6 minutes until soft and pale, then stir in 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.

Dry-roast 2.5 tsp coriander powder in a separate small pan for 40 seconds until nutty and fragrant, then add it with 3 pureed tomatoes, 0.5 tsp turmeric and 0.75 tsp red chilli powder and cook until the oil surfaces, about 8 minutes.
Add the boiled beans with 1.5 cups reserved liquid and the remaining 0.75 tsp salt, and simmer for 15 minutes until the gravy thickens lightly.
Stir in 2 tbsp grated coconut and cook 3 more minutes so it melts into the gravy and adds a subtle southern sweetness.
Finish with 3 tbsp chopped fresh coriander stirred through off the heat.
tips: Toasting the coriander powder just before use is what carries this version; pre-roast a batch and store it airtight for the week.
Keep this gravy thinner than Punjabi rajma so the fragrant, coriander-heavy broth shines with rice.
Swap grated coconut for 1 tbsp coconut milk if you want a smoother, richer body.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve over hot rice topped with a spoon of the mustard-curry-leaf tempering, alongside a crisp papad and a coconut-mint chutney.

variations.name: Kadai Rajma
variations.description: A bold, semi-dry rajma tossed kadai-style with charred capsicum and a coarse hand-pounded kadai masala. The gravy is thick and rugged, clinging to the beans, with visible flecks of coriander seed and chunks of pepper. Smoky, punchy and unapologetically robust.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: smoked to its haze point, wood-pressed mustard oil gives the kadai its sharp, gutsy base

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: a finishing spoon mellows the mustard oil and glazes the beans

steps: Pressure-cook 1.5 cups soaked rajma with 4 cups water and 0.5 tsp salt for 6 to 7 whistles until soft, then drain and keep the liquid.
Dry-roast 2 tbsp coriander seeds, 3 dried red chillies and 1 tsp cumin seeds over medium heat until aromatic, about 2 minutes, then cool and pound coarse for the kadai masala.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil in a kadai until hazy, reduce the heat, and fry 2 diced onions for 6 minutes until softened and browning at the edges.
Add 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute, then 2 chopped tomatoes and 0.5 tsp turmeric, cooking until pulpy and the oil separates, about 6 minutes.
Stir in most of the pounded kadai masala and the drained beans with only 0.5 cup reserved liquid and the remaining 0.5 tsp salt, and cook on medium-high for 8 minutes until thick and clingy.
Add 1 large capsicum in thick wedges and toss on high heat for 3 to 4 minutes so it chars lightly yet stays crunchy.
Crush 1 tsp kasuri methi over the pan, swirl in 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and the reserved kadai masala, and finish with 2 tbsp chopped fresh coriander.
tips: Keep the beans a touch firmer than for classic rajma so they hold their shape in the thick, tossed gravy.
Add the capsicum last for that signature crunch; overcooking it flattens the whole dish.
Pound the masala coarse just before cooking, as pre-ground shop powder cannot match the texture or aroma.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve sizzling from the kadai with tandoori roti or missi roti and a sharp onion-lachha salad dressed with lemon and chaat masala.

variations.name: Handi Rajma
variations.description: A slow handi rajma from the Awadhi belt where whole spices are bloomed in ghee and the beans steam under a sealed lid to absorb the aroma. There is no powdered garam masala; cinnamon, cloves, cardamom and black cardamom do all the perfuming. Deeply fragrant, gently spiced and meant for unhurried cooking.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: whole spices release their oils into bilona ghee, perfuming the beans as they dum-cook

steps: Pressure-cook 1.5 cups soaked rajma with 4 cups water and 0.5 tsp salt for 6 to 7 whistles until tender, keeping the cooking liquid.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a deep handi and bloom 1 inch cinnamon, 1 black cardamom, 3 green cardamoms, 4 cloves and 1 bay leaf until they swell and turn aromatic, about 40 seconds.
Add 2 sliced onions and fry slowly for 10 minutes until deep golden and soft, letting the whole spices steep in the ghee.
Stir in 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute, then add 3 chopped tomatoes, 0.5 tsp turmeric and 0.75 tsp red chilli powder and cook until the ghee glistens on the surface, about 9 minutes.
Add the boiled beans with 1.5 cups reserved liquid and the remaining 0.75 tsp salt, bring to a gentle simmer, and mash a few beans against the pan.
Cover the handi tightly, drop the heat to its lowest, and dum-cook undisturbed for 20 minutes so the aroma of the whole spices soaks into the beans.
Uncover, discard the bay leaf and black cardamom skin, and finish with 2 tbsp chopped fresh coriander.
tips: Bruise the black cardamom lightly before adding so it releases its smoky note without overpowering the pot.
The slow dum is non-negotiable here; low heat and a sealed lid are what set this apart from a stovetop rajma.
Remove the larger whole spices before serving so no one bites into a clove or cardamom pod.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with soft rumali roti or ghee rice and a side of sliced onions soaked in vinegar to cut through the aromatic richness.

variations.name: Punjabi Rajma
variations.description: The plush, dhaba-luxury rajma: a smooth, cashew-enriched gravy finished with cream and crushed kasuri methi, with butter swapped for aromatic bilona ghee. It is richer and silkier than homestyle rajma, with a mellow buttery-fenugreek finish. A crowd-pleaser for gatherings.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: replaces butter for the same lush body plus the nutty depth of bilona ghee

steps: Pressure-cook 1.5 cups soaked rajma with 4 cups water and 0.5 tsp salt for 6 to 7 whistles until very soft, and reserve the liquid.
Soak 12 cashews in warm water for 15 minutes, then blend with 2 boiled onions into a smooth, pourable paste.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pan and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then add the onion-cashew paste and fry for 6 minutes until thickened and no longer raw-smelling.
Add 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute, then 3 pureed tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder and 1.5 tsp coriander powder, cooking until the ghee separates, about 9 minutes.
Add the boiled beans with 1 cup reserved liquid and the remaining 0.75 tsp salt, and simmer gently for 15 minutes until the gravy turns thick and glossy.
Lower the heat, stir in 3 tbsp cream and 0.75 tsp garam masala, and warm through for 2 minutes without boiling.
Crush 1.5 tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pan and stir it in just before serving.
tips: Strain the cashew-onion paste if you want a truly velvety, restaurant-grade gravy with no graininess.
Keep the flame low once the cream goes in, as high heat can split it and dull the sheen.
This freezes well without the cream; add fresh cream and kasuri methi after reheating for the best texture.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with jeera rice or butter naan, finished with a swirl of cream, a scatter of kasuri methi and thin ginger juliennes on top.

variations.name: Classic Sattu Paratha
variations.description: The rustic Bihari-Purvanchal favourite: a soft khapli-atta paratha stuffed with tangy, mustard-oil-slicked roasted gram sattu that puffs and cracks open to a smoky, savoury filling. The sattu is bound with pickle masala and lemon so every bite is nutty, pungent and bright. Eaten with a knob of white butter and a wedge of mango pickle, it is a meal in itself.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The nutty emmer wheat gives a sturdy dough that holds the moist sattu without tearing

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sattu
ingredients.note: Stone-ground roasted gram is the whole point of this paratha, earthy and protein-rich

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Brushed on the tava to crisp the crust to golden lace

ingredients.name: Anveshan Wood-Pressed Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: The raw pungency of wood-pressed mustard oil is what makes an authentic sattu filling sing

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 0.5 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and about 0.75 cup water into a soft, non-sticky dough, then cover and rest for 15 minutes.

For the filling, mix 1 cup Anveshan Sattu with 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Wood-Pressed Mustard Oil, the chopped onion, minced green chilli, grated garlic, 1 tbsp pickle masala, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, crushed ajwain, coriander and 0.5 tsp salt until it just clumps when pressed, sprinkling in 1 tbsp water if dry.
Divide the dough into 6 balls, flatten each, place a generous 2 tbsp of the sattu filling in the centre, gather the edges over the top and pinch firmly to seal.
Dust with atta and roll out gently to a 7-inch round, easing from the centre so the filling does not burst through the seam.
Roast on a hot tava over medium heat for about 1 minute until pale bubbles rise, flip, and brush the surface with Anveshan Ghee.
Flip again and press the edges with a spatula, cooking each side 1 to 2 minutes until deep golden-brown blisters form and the paratha smells toasty.
tips: If the filling feels too dry to hold, a teaspoon more mustard oil binds it far better than water, which can make it leak.
Seal the stuffed ball by pinching the pleats and rolling with light, even pressure; a heavy hand tears the seam and pushes sattu out.
Leftover parathas reheat beautifully on a dry tava; wrap warm ones in a cloth to keep them supple.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve blistering hot with a smear of white butter, mango or chilli pickle and a bowl of chokha (mashed roasted brinjal) on the side.

variations.name: Masala Sattu Paratha
variations.description: A Maharashtrian-leaning masala version where the sattu is warmed up with homemade garam masala and roasted coriander for a deeper, curry-like aroma. The filling turns fragrant and slightly sweet-spiced rather than sharply pungent, softened with a little grated ginger. It pairs especially well with a cooling boondi raita.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Wholegrain emmer stands up to the spiced, slightly oily filling without going soggy

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sattu
ingredients.note: Roasted gram flour drinks in the garam masala and turns wonderfully aromatic

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Used both to bloom the ground spices and to shallow-roast the parathas

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 0.5 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and roughly 0.75 cup water into a smooth, supple dough and rest it, covered, for 15 minutes.

Warm 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee in a small pan and bloom the grated ginger, 1 tsp garam masala, 1.5 tsp roasted coriander powder, 0.25 tsp turmeric and 0.75 tsp red chilli for 20 seconds until aromatic, then cool briefly.
Stir this spiced ghee into 1 cup Anveshan Sattu along with the chopped onion, coriander leaves and 0.5 tsp salt, adding 2 tbsp water so the mix holds a soft clump.
Roll each dough ball into a small cup, spoon in 2 tbsp of the masala sattu, draw the edges together, pinch shut and flatten.
Dust and roll out to a 7-inch disc with gentle pressure so the seasoned filling stays enclosed.
Cook on a medium-hot tava for about 1 minute a side, brushing with Anveshan Ghee, until both faces carry crisp golden spots and the spices smell toasted.
tips: Blooming the spices in ghee first is what stops the finished paratha from tasting of raw masala.
Keep the onion very finely chopped and squeeze out excess moisture, or the filling will steam and turn the seam soggy.
Make a double batch of the spiced sattu and refrigerate it for up to three days for quick weekday parathas.
variations.servingSuggestion: Best served with chilled boondi raita and a spoon of green chutney, alongside a few slices of raw onion.

variations.name: Spicy Sattu Paratha
variations.description: A fiery Gujarati-style take that leans on fresh green chillies and coarsely cracked black pepper for a clean, building heat rather than dry red chilli. A squeeze of lemon and chopped coriander keep it lively, and wood-pressed groundnut oil in the dough adds a light nuttiness. This is the paratha for those who like a proper kick.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The robust emmer crumb balances the sharp chilli-and-pepper filling

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sattu
