variations.description: Whole scooped apple gourds stuffed with a tangy roasted-spice besan filling, then slow-cooked until the shells turn tender and the stuffing crusts. This stuffed version is a special-occasion pahari treat where every bite carries the fragrant, amchur-laced masala inside.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: used to toast the filling and shallow-cook the stuffed gourds

steps: Peel 8 small apple gourds and make a deep cross-cut in each, keeping the base intact to hold the filling.

Dry-roast 4 tbsp besan with 1.5 tsp fennel for 3 minutes until nutty, then mix in 2 tsp coriander powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1.5 tsp amchur, 0.75 tsp garam masala and 1 tsp salt.
Stir 1 tbsp of the mustard oil into the filling to bind it, then pack about 1.5 tbsp firmly into each gourd.
Heat the remaining 3 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil to smoking, lower the flame, and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds.
Lay the stuffed gourds in the pan, cover, and cook on low for 18 minutes, turning gently every 5 minutes so all sides soften.
Uncover and cook a final 4 minutes on medium to crisp the shells and toast any spilled filling.
tips: Roast the besan well before filling so the stuffing tastes nutty rather than raw and pasty.
Keep the base of each gourd intact so the filling does not fall out during cooking.
Cook covered and low so the shells steam tender before you crisp them at the end.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve the whole stuffed gourds with hot phulkas and a wedge of lemon, letting each be split open at the table.

variations.name: Classic Tori
variations.description: The light everyday ridge-gourd sabzi where peeled tori softens into a naturally juicy, faintly sweet dish that needs very little water of its own. A simple cumin-onion-tomato base lets the vegetable stay the star. Quick, wholesome and easy on the stomach.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A light wood-pressed oil suits the delicate, watery gourd without overpowering it.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A finishing teaspoon adds a soft richness to the juicy sabzi.

steps: Lightly peel the ridged skin off 700 g ridge gourd, leaving some green, and cut the flesh into 2 cm half-moons.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a kadhai on medium and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds with 0.5 tsp ajwain and 2 slit green chillies for 20 seconds.
Add 1 chopped onion and 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and saute for 5 minutes until soft and pale gold.
Add 2 chopped tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 0.75 tsp red chilli powder, 1.5 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp salt and cook for 4 minutes until pulpy.
Add the ridge gourd, cover and cook on low for 12 minutes without adding water, stirring twice, as the gourd releases plenty of its own moisture and turns soft.
Uncover and cook on medium for 2 minutes to reduce the liquid, then stir in 0.5 tsp amchur powder and finish with 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee and 2 tbsp coriander.
tips: Do not add water; ridge gourd is very watery and will turn soupy if you do.
Peel lightly and keep a little green skin on for colour and a pleasant bite.
If the sabzi still looks watery, finish uncovered on high heat for a couple of minutes to concentrate the flavour.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with hot phulkas and a bowl of toor dal, or with plain rice and a spoon of ghee.

variations.name: Masala Tori
variations.description: A Jammu-style masala tori where the juicy gourd is folded into a warm garam-masala base with a touch of fennel for a subtle northern sweetness. The masala thickens against the gourd's moisture into a comforting coat. Fragrant, gently spiced and homely.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Builds a slightly thicker masala that holds against the gourd's moisture.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: The garam masala is bloomed in ghee for a warm northern finish.

steps: Peel 700 g ridge gourd lightly and cut into 2 cm half-moons, keeping the pieces even.
Heat 2.5 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a kadhai on medium and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds with a 1 inch piece of cinnamon, 3 green cardamoms and 3 cloves for 20 seconds.
Add 2 chopped onions and 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and fry for 7 minutes until golden.
Add 2 chopped tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1.5 tsp coriander powder, 0.5 tsp fennel powder and 1 tsp salt and cook for 5 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the ridge gourd, cover and cook on low for 12 minutes in its own moisture until soft and coated in masala.
Warm 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, stir 1.25 tsp garam masala into it for 10 seconds, then fold it through with 3 tbsp coriander.
tips: Fennel powder gives a gentle sweetness typical of the region, so do not skip it here.
Keep the pan covered so the gourd cooks in its own steam and the masala thickens naturally.
Add the garam masala at the end so its aroma stays fresh and fragrant.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with hot tandoori rotis and a side of thin cucumber raita.

variations.name: Spicy Tori
variations.description: An Uttarakhand-style spicy tori where slit green chillies and crushed black pepper give the mild gourd a hill-country kick, tempered in mustard oil for extra pungency. The heat wakes up the vegetable without masking its juiciness. Bold, peppery and bright.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: The pungent hill favourite carries the black-pepper and green-chilli heat.

steps: Peel 700 g ridge gourd lightly and cut into 2 cm half-moons, and slit 4 green chillies lengthways.
Heat 2.5 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil in a kadhai on medium-high until shimmering, then crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds for 15 seconds.
Add 1 chopped onion, the slit green chillies and 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and saute for 5 minutes until the onion softens and the chillies blister.
Add 2 chopped tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1.5 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp salt and cook for 4 minutes until pulpy.
Add the ridge gourd, cover and cook on low for 12 minutes in its own moisture until soft.
Crush 1 tsp black pepper coarsely, stir it in with 3 tbsp coriander and cook uncovered on medium for 2 minutes so the pepper heat blooms and any excess water reduces.
tips: Bring the mustard oil to shimmering first so its raw pungency softens into a clean heat.
Add the crushed pepper at the end to keep its aromatic sharpness intact.
Cook the final stretch uncovered so the pepper flavour concentrates and the sabzi is not watery.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with mandua (finger-millet) rotis and a spoon of plain curd to cool the heat.

variations.name: Dhaba-style Tori
variations.description: An Odisha dhaba-style tori with a kasuri-methi and garam-masala finish and a browned onion-tomato masala thick enough to hold the juicy gourd together. A ghee tempering gives it that unmistakable roadside richness. Herby, hearty and full-flavoured.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A generous pour browns the onions into a glossy dhaba masala.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Kasuri methi crushed into warm ghee gives the classic dhaba finish.

steps: Peel 700 g ridge gourd lightly and cut into 2 cm half-moons, then finely chop 2 onions and 3 tomatoes.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a kadhai and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds, then add the onions and 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste.
Fry the onions for 8 minutes until deep golden brown for a rich dhaba base.
Add the tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 2 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp salt and cook for 6 minutes until thick and the oil separates.
Add the ridge gourd, cover and cook on low for 12 minutes in its own moisture, then uncover and reduce for 2 minutes until the masala clings.
Warm 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, crush 1 tbsp kasuri methi into it, pour over with 1 tsp garam masala and 3 tbsp coriander, and fold through.
tips: Brown the onions well for the deep colour and flavour a dhaba masala is known for.
Because the gourd throws off water, finish uncovered to keep the masala thick and glossy.
Crush kasuri methi between your palms before adding it to the ghee for maximum aroma.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with butter rotis or paratha and a side of sliced onions with lemon and chaat masala.

variations.name: Home-style Tori
variations.description: An Assamese home-style tori kept deliberately light, tempered simply and cooked soft so the gourd's natural juices form a thin, soothing gravy. A hint of green chilli and coriander is all it needs. Minimal, tender and everyday comforting.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: A modest spoon of the everyday Assamese fat lends its gentle pungency.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A last teaspoon softens the mustard oil and rounds the mild sabzi.

steps: Peel 700 g ridge gourd lightly and cut into 1.5 cm half-moons so they cook quickly and stay tender.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil in a kadhai on medium-high until shimmering, then crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds with 1 inch grated ginger and 2 slit green chillies.
Add 1 chopped onion and saute for 4 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add 1 chopped tomato with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 0.5 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp salt and cook for 3 minutes until softened.
Add the ridge gourd, cover and cook on low for 12 minutes in its own juices until very soft and a thin gravy forms.
Turn off the heat, drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee and stir in 2 tbsp coriander before serving.
tips: Keep the tempering and spicing minimal so the mild, juicy character of the gourd shines.
The thin natural gravy is meant to be spooned over rice, so do not reduce it away.
Leftovers thicken as they sit, so loosen with a splash of hot water when reheating.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve over steamed rice with a wedge of lemon and a small helping of khar or dal on the side.

variations.name: Classic Veg Korma
variations.description: A mildly spiced mixed-vegetable korma bound in a luxurious cashew and cream gravy. Soft carrots, beans, peas and potato float in a pale golden sauce that is gently sweet, nutty and fragrant with garam masala.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed groundnut oil sautés the base without overpowering the delicate korma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: a finishing spoon of bilona ghee gives the korma its restaurant-style sheen

steps: Chop the mixed vegetables into even bite-sized pieces and boil or steam them for 6 to 8 minutes until just tender but still holding their shape, then drain and set aside.
Heat the Anveshan Groundnut Oil over medium heat, add 1 tsp cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add the finely chopped onions and cook for 6 minutes until soft and pale gold, then stir in 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and the chopped tomato and cook 4 minutes until pulpy.
Lower the heat, add 3 tbsp cashew paste with 0.5 tsp turmeric and 0.5 tsp red chilli powder, and stir for 3 minutes until the raw cashew smell fades and the masala thickens.
Pour in 1.5 cups water and 1 tsp salt, bring to a gentle simmer, then fold in the cooked vegetables and cook for 8 minutes so they absorb the nutty gravy.
Finish with 3 tbsp cream, 0.5 tsp garam masala and 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, simmer 2 minutes, and garnish with 2 tbsp chopped coriander.
tips: Do not overboil the vegetables, as they should keep a slight bite before joining the gravy.
Soak the cashews in warm water for 15 minutes before grinding for a lump-free paste.
A pinch of crushed cardamom stirred in at the end deepens the classic korma aroma.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with soft butter naan or steamed basmati, topped with a swirl of cream and a scatter of slivered almonds for a festive touch.

variations.name: Jharkhand Masala Veg Korma
variations.description: A robust, everyday korma from Jharkhand kitchens that trades cream for a bold hit of roasted coriander powder. The gravy is earthier and more rustic, letting the vegetables and dry-roasted spices take centre stage.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: pungent wood-pressed mustard oil gives this rustic korma its regional bite

steps: Cut the mixed vegetables into chunks and parboil them for 5 minutes until half-cooked, then drain, keeping them slightly firm for the rustic finish.
Dry-roast 3 tbsp peanuts in a hot pan for 3 minutes until spotty brown, cool, and grind coarsely to a gritty powder that will thicken the gravy.
Heat the Anveshan Mustard Oil until it shimmers and just smokes, then reduce the heat, add 1 tsp cumin seeds and let them splutter for 15 seconds.

Add the chopped onions and fry for 7 minutes until deep brown, then stir in 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and the chopped tomatoes with 2 tsp coriander powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp red chilli powder, cooking 6 minutes until thick.
Add the parboiled vegetables, the ground peanuts, 1 tsp salt and 2 cups water, then simmer uncovered for 12 minutes until the gravy thickens and clings to the vegetables.
Sprinkle 0.5 tsp garam masala and 2 tbsp chopped coriander, stir once, and rest for 3 minutes before serving.
tips: The ground roasted peanuts replace cream here, so grind them just before use for the freshest nutty body.
Blooming the mustard oil to its smoke point first mellows its sharpness into a pleasant warmth.
Add a splash of hot water if the gravy tightens, as this korma should stay pourable.
variations.servingSuggestion: Best mopped up with plain hand-rolled rotis and a side of raw onion rings, or spooned over hot rice with a dollop of yogurt.

variations.name: Punjabi Butter Veg Korma
variations.description: A rich, restaurant-style Punjabi korma where vegetables swim in a buttery, cashew-thickened gravy blushed with tomato. Butter and a whisper of honey make it plush and gently sweet, a true special-occasion dish.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee replaces half the butter for a cleaner, aromatic richness

ingredients.name: Anveshan Honey
ingredients.note: raw honey balances the tomato tang far more naturally than refined sugar

steps: Steam the mixed vegetables for 7 minutes until just tender, then plunge them into cold water to keep their colour bright and set them aside.
Blend the tomatoes to a smooth puree, and heat the Anveshan Ghee with 1 tbsp butter over medium heat before adding 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute.
Pour in the tomato puree with 1 tsp red chilli powder and cook covered for 10 minutes, stirring often, until the raw smell disappears and the fat separates.
Stir in 4 tbsp cashew paste and 1 cup water, and simmer for 5 minutes until the gravy turns glossy and pale red, adjusting thickness with a splash more water if needed.
Fold in the steamed vegetables and 1 tsp salt, simmer for 6 minutes, then add 3 tbsp cream, 1 tsp Anveshan Honey and crushed 1 tsp kasuri methi.
Finish with 0.5 tsp garam masala and the remaining tbsp of butter, cook 2 minutes until the butter melts into a shine, and serve at once.
tips: Blend and strain the tomatoes for the smoothest, most restaurant-like gravy.
The teaspoon of honey rounds the acidity, so add it gradually and taste as you go.
Reserve a spoon of cream to swirl on top just before serving for the classic marbled look.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with garlic naan or jeera rice, finished with a marbled swirl of cream and a light dusting of crushed kasuri methi.

variations.name: Maharashtrian Kadai Veg Korma
variations.description: A spicier Maharashtrian kadai treatment where the korma turns semi-dry, studded with charred capsicum and coated in a coarse, freshly pounded kadai masala. Bold, fragrant and less creamy, it is built for scooping with bhakri or roti.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: the go-to Maharashtrian wood-pressed oil, ideal for high-heat kadai cooking

steps: Dry-roast 2 tsp coriander seeds, 3 dried red chillies and 1 tsp cumin seeds for 90 seconds until aromatic, then cool and pound to a coarse kadai masala.
Parboil the mixed vegetables for 5 minutes so they are firm-tender, and cut the capsicum into thick 3 cm squares to keep it crisp in the toss.
Heat the Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a kadai on high heat, add the cubed onions and capsicum, and sear for 3 minutes until the edges char, then remove and reserve the capsicum.
To the same pan add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and the chopped tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, and cook on high for 6 minutes until the tomatoes break down into a thick masala.
Add most of the pounded kadai masala, the parboiled vegetables, 1 tsp salt and 0.5 cup water, and toss on high heat for 6 minutes until the masala clings and the dish turns semi-dry.
Return the charred capsicum, crush 1 tsp kasuri methi and the reserved kadai masala over the top, add 2 tbsp coriander, and toss once before serving hot.
tips: Grinding the kadai masala fresh is essential for the coarse texture and smoky aroma that define this dish.
Keep the capsicum blistered but crunchy by adding it back only at the end.
This korma is meant to be dry and clingy, so resist adding extra water.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve straight from the kadai with jowar bhakri or phulka, a wedge of lime, and a side of raw onion sprinkled with kadai masala.

variations.name: Gujarati Handi Veg Korma
variations.description: A Gujarati handi korma cooked slow with whole spices and a gentle sweet-sour balance. Vegetables steam in a sealed pot until infused with cardamom and cinnamon, and a touch of jaggery gives the signature Gujarati sweetness.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed groundnut oil is the traditional Gujarati cooking medium for such gravies

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: unrefined jaggery gives the authentic Gujarati sweet-sour note without a chemical aftertaste

steps: Cut the mixed vegetables into even pieces and whisk 0.5 cup yogurt until smooth so it blends into the gravy without curdling.
Heat the Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a heavy handi over medium heat and bloom 3 cardamom, 3 cloves, a 1 inch cinnamon stick and 1 bay leaf for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the chopped onions and fry for 8 minutes until golden, then stir in 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and the chopped tomatoes and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Lower the heat, add the whisked yogurt with 0.5 tsp turmeric, and stir constantly for 3 minutes until the masala thickens and the oil surfaces.
Add the raw vegetables, 1 tsp salt and 1 cup water, seal the handi with a tight lid, and steam on low heat for 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender and infused.
Stir in 1 tsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder until it melts, fold in 2 tbsp coriander, and rest covered for 4 minutes so the sweet-sour balance settles.
tips: Steaming the raw vegetables inside the sealed handi keeps them sweet and lets the whole spices penetrate.
Add the jaggery only at the end and taste, as Gujarati sweetness should be subtle, not dominant.
Keep the flame low throughout so the yogurt gravy stays smooth and never splits.
variations.servingSuggestion: Pair with soft phulka or methi thepla and a spoon of sweet mango chhundo on the side for a complete Gujarati thali feel.

variations.name: Classic Veg Pulao
variations.description: A fragrant one-pot rice where soaked basmati is layered with whole spices, sauteed onions and a medley of vegetables. Every grain stays separate and glossy, perfumed with cardamom and cinnamon and rich with ghee.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee is what gives a classic pulao its unmistakable aroma and shine

steps: Rinse 1.5 cups basmati rice until the water runs clear, then soak it for 20 minutes and drain so the grains cook long and separate.
Heat the Anveshan Ghee in a heavy pot over medium heat and bloom 4 cardamom, 4 cloves, a 1 inch cinnamon stick, 2 bay leaves and 1 tsp cumin seeds for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the sliced onions and fry for 6 minutes until golden, then stir in 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and 2 slit green chillies and cook 1 minute more.
Add 2 cups mixed vegetables and saute for 4 minutes, then fold in the drained rice and toss gently for 2 minutes so each grain coats in ghee without breaking.
Pour in exactly 3 cups water with 1.5 tsp salt, bring to a rolling boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Turn off the heat, let it rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and fold through 2 tbsp chopped coriander before serving.
tips: Soaking the rice and using a strict 1:2 rice-to-water ratio is the surest way to separate grains.
Rest the pulao undisturbed for 5 minutes after cooking so the grains firm up before fluffing.
Toss the rice with a fork, never a spoon, to avoid crushing the delicate cooked grains.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with cool boondi raita and a wedge of lime, topped with a few fried cashews for crunch.

variations.name: Kerala Coconut Veg Pulao
variations.description: A Kerala-style pulao cooked in coconut milk with a tempering of curry leaves and coconut oil. The rice turns silky and faintly sweet, carrying the coastal fragrance of fresh coconut in every mouthful.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed coconut oil deepens the coastal aroma and pairs naturally with coconut milk

steps: Rinse and soak 1.5 cups basmati rice for 20 minutes, then drain, and dilute 1.5 cups coconut milk with 1.5 cups water to make the cooking liquid.
Heat the Anveshan Coconut Oil over medium heat, fry 12 cashews until golden and lift them out, then add 15 curry leaves, 3 cardamom and a 1 inch cinnamon stick and let them crackle for 20 seconds.
Add the thinly sliced onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft, then add julienned ginger and 2 slit green chillies and saute for 1 minute.
Stir in 2 cups mixed vegetables and cook for 3 minutes, then add the drained rice and toss gently for 2 minutes to coat it in the fragrant oil.
Pour in the coconut milk mixture with 1.5 tsp salt, bring to a gentle boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 13 minutes until the liquid is fully absorbed.
Rest covered for 5 minutes, fluff gently, and scatter the fried cashews over the top before serving.
tips: Use thin coconut milk diluted with water rather than thick milk, which can make the rice heavy.
Keep the heat low once the coconut milk goes in so it does not scorch at the base.
Add a slit green chilli whole so you get fragrance without overwhelming heat.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a tangy tomato pachadi or a simple cucumber raita, garnished with extra fried curry leaves.

variations.name: Karnataka Spiced Veg Pulao
variations.description: A vibrant Karnataka-style vegetable pulao built on a fresh green paste of mint, coriander and coconut. The rice takes on a herby, mildly hot character reminiscent of a Bangalorean bhath, fragrant and green-flecked.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee carries the fresh green masala and keeps the grains glossy

steps: Rinse and soak 1.5 cups basmati rice for 20 minutes and drain, then grind 0.5 cup mint, 0.5 cup coriander, 3 tbsp coconut and 3 green chillies into a smooth green paste with a splash of water.
Heat the Anveshan Ghee over medium heat, add a 1 inch cinnamon stick and 3 cloves, and let them sizzle for 20 seconds until aromatic.
Add the sliced onion and fry for 5 minutes until soft and light gold, then stir in 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
Add the ground green paste and saute for 4 minutes until the raw smell disappears and the ghee separates at the edges, then add 2 cups mixed vegetables and cook 3 minutes.
Fold in the drained rice and toss for 2 minutes, then pour in 3 cups water with 1.5 tsp salt and bring to a rolling boil.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes, rest for 5 minutes off the heat, then fluff gently to reveal the green-flecked grains.
tips: Grind the green paste fresh and cook it well so the mint stays fragrant rather than bitter.
Do not skip sauteing the paste until the ghee separates, as this removes any raw sharpness.
For extra heat, leave the green chilli seeds in when grinding the masala.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a cooling onion-tomato raita and a crisp papad, or a bowl of plain curd on the side.

variations.name: Andhra Festive Veg Pulao
variations.description: A celebratory Andhra pulao enriched with saffron, fried onions and cashews for a wedding-feast feel. The rice is layered and dum-cooked so the saffron colour streaks through pale grains, luxurious and aromatic.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: generous bilona ghee gives this festive pulao its rich, celebratory aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: a saffron-milk soak lends the golden streaks and fragrance of a feast-day rice

steps: Rinse and soak 1.5 cups basmati rice for 25 minutes, drain, and warm 3 tbsp milk to steep 0.25 tsp Anveshan Saffron for its colour and aroma.
Heat the Anveshan Ghee over medium heat, fry the thinly sliced onions in batches for 8 minutes until deep golden and crisp, then drain them and fry 15 cashews until pale gold.
In the same ghee bloom 4 cardamom, 1 star anise and a 1 inch cinnamon stick for 20 seconds, then add 2 cups mixed vegetables and saute for 4 minutes.
Stir in 0.25 cup whisked yogurt and cook 2 minutes, then fold in the drained rice and toss gently for 2 minutes to coat the grains.
Pour in 3 cups water with 1.5 tsp salt, bring to a boil, drizzle the saffron milk over the surface, and scatter half the fried onions on top.
Cover tightly and dum-cook on the lowest heat for 14 minutes, rest 5 minutes, then fluff and garnish with the remaining fried onions and cashews.
tips: Fry the onions slowly and evenly for that crisp, sweet birista that defines a festive pulao.
Steep the saffron in warm milk for at least 10 minutes to draw out its full colour.
Layer half the fried onions inside for depth and save the rest for a generous garnish.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve on a broad platter with a rich mirchi ka salan or a bowl of tomato raita for a true festive spread.

variations.name: Telangana Quick Veg Pulao
variations.description: A fuss-free Telangana-style pressure-cooker pulao for busy weeknights, spiced simply and ready in minutes. It skips long soaking yet delivers soft, flavourful rice with a homely, everyday charm.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee delivers full pulao aroma even in a quick one-pot method

steps: Rinse 1.5 cups basmati rice well and let it sit for just 10 minutes while you chop the vegetables, then drain.
Heat the Anveshan Ghee in a pressure cooker over medium heat, add 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 bay leaf and 3 cloves, and let them crackle for 20 seconds.
Add the chopped onion and cook for 3 minutes until soft, then add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and the chopped tomato and cook 2 minutes until pulpy.
Stir in 2 cups mixed vegetables with 0.5 tsp garam masala and 1.5 tsp salt, and saute for 2 minutes to coat them in the masala.
Add the drained rice and 2.5 cups water, stir once, and close the lid, cooking on medium heat for 2 whistles before turning off the flame.
Let the pressure release naturally for 8 minutes, then open, fluff gently with a fork, and serve hot.
tips: Use slightly less water in the cooker than the open-pot method to keep the grains from turning mushy.
Let the pressure drop naturally rather than forcing it, so the grains stay whole.
Skip long soaking here, but do rinse the rice well to keep it from clumping.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve straight from the cooker with a spoon of pickle and plain curd for a quick, satisfying meal.

variations.name: Classic Aloo Gobi
variations.description: The everyday North Indian dry sabzi where potato wedges and cauliflower florets cook down into a soft, golden, spice-coated toss. A cumin-and-tomato base does the work while a finishing spoon of ghee lifts the whole pan with nutty aroma. This is the version that lands on weeknight thalis with hot phulkas.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Its clean, high-smoke-point body sears the florets without turning them soggy.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Stirred in at the end for a bilona-ghee aroma that carries the garam masala.

steps: Peel and cut 3 medium potatoes into 2 cm wedges and break 1 medium cauliflower into bite-size florets; soak the florets in warm salted water for 5 minutes, then drain well so they cook evenly.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a wide kadhai on medium heat and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds with 0.5 tsp ajwain for about 20 seconds until they sizzle and smell toasty.
Add 2 finely chopped onions and 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and saute on medium heat for 6 to 7 minutes until the onions turn soft and pale gold.
Stir in 2 chopped tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1.5 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp salt, and cook for 5 minutes until the oil just begins to separate at the edges.
Tip in the potatoes and cauliflower, toss to coat, then cover and cook on low heat for 15 to 18 minutes, stirring gently every few minutes, until a knife slides through the potato easily.
Uncover, raise the heat for 2 minutes to dry any moisture, then sprinkle 0.75 tsp amchur powder and swirl in 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and 3 tbsp chopped coriander before taking off the heat.
tips: Do not stir too often once the vegetables go in; frequent stirring breaks the cauliflower into mush, so use a gentle fold instead.
If the florets release water and the sabzi looks wet, finish uncovered on high heat for a couple of minutes to get a dry, roasted edge.
Cut potato and cauliflower to a similar size so both turn tender at the same time and you never have crunchy florets beside overcooked potato.
variations.servingSuggestion: Pile it beside a bowl of cool boondi raita and a wedge of lemon, with ajwain parathas to scoop it up.

variations.name: Masala Aloo Gobi
variations.description: A gently spiced Assamese-style take that leans on a warm garam masala bloom rather than heat, giving the potato and cauliflower a rounded, fragrant coat. The masala is toasted in ghee so its aroma seeps into every floret. Comforting, aromatic and mildly rich.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: The whole dish is built on ghee so the toasted garam masala turns nutty rather than sharp.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A splash alongside the ghee stops it browning too fast while the onions cook down.

steps: Cut 3 medium potatoes into wedges and 1 medium cauliflower into florets, then pat both thoroughly dry so they take on colour in the pan.

Warm 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee with 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a heavy pan on medium heat, drop in 1 bay leaf, a 1 inch piece of cinnamon, 3 green cardamoms, 3 cloves and 1 tsp cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add 2 finely chopped onions with 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and fry for 7 minutes until deep golden and jammy at the edges.
Mix in 2 chopped tomatoes, 0.5 tsp turmeric, 0.75 tsp red chilli powder, 1.5 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp salt and cook for 5 minutes until soft and glossy.
Add the potatoes and cauliflower, fold to coat, cover and cook on low for 16 to 18 minutes until fork-tender, lifting the lid to stir gently twice.
Scatter 1.25 tsp garam masala over the top, toss for a final 2 minutes so the aroma blooms, then finish with 3 tbsp chopped coriander.
tips: Toast your garam masala only in the last two minutes; adding it early boils off the volatile aromatics that make this version special.
For a deeper colour, let the onions go a shade past golden before the tomatoes go in, but keep the heat moderate so they never burn bitter.
This sabzi reheats beautifully the next day as the garam masala mellows, so it is a smart make-ahead tiffin dish.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with soft luchis or plain steamed rice and a side of thin tomato-tamarind tokku for tang.

variations.name: Spicy Aloo Gobi
variations.description: A punchy Delhi-style version that gets its kick from slit green chillies and a hit of freshly crushed black pepper rather than only chilli powder. The pepper brings a woody warmth that clings to the crisp-edged florets. Sharp, fiery and made for cold-weather appetites.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Its pungent bite stands up to the black pepper and gives the sabzi a bold, north-Indian edge.

steps: Cut 3 medium potatoes into wedges and 1 medium cauliflower into florets, and slit 4 green chillies lengthways keeping them whole at the stem.
Heat 2.5 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil in a kadhai on medium-high until it just shimmers and loses its raw smell, then lower the heat and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds for 15 seconds.
Add 2 chopped onions, the slit green chillies and 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and fry for 6 minutes until the onions soften and the chillies blister.
Stir in 2 chopped tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1.5 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp salt and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until pulpy.
Add the potatoes and cauliflower, toss well, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes until tender, then uncover and fry on high for 2 minutes to crisp the edges.
Crush 1 tsp black pepper coarsely, sprinkle it over with 3 tbsp chopped coriander, and toss for a final minute so the pepper heat coats everything.
tips: Always heat mustard oil until it shimmers and the sharp raw aroma fades before adding spices, otherwise the dish tastes bitter.
Add the black pepper right at the end; cooking it long dulls the sharp, aromatic heat that defines this version.
For less fire without losing flavour, deseed two of the green chillies but keep them in for their grassy aroma.
variations.servingSuggestion: Best with a stack of hot missi rotis and a slice of raw onion rubbed with salt and lemon on the side.

variations.name: Dhaba-style Aloo Gobi
variations.description: The roadside-dhaba rendition where crushed kasuri methi and a generous garam masala give the sabzi its unmistakable smoky-herbal signature. A slightly heavier tomato-onion masala clings to the vegetables, finished with ghee for that restaurant richness. Robust, herby and deeply satisfying.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A generous pour builds the glossy dhaba masala that coats every floret.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A last spoon of ghee bloomed with kasuri methi delivers the classic dhaba finish.

steps: Cut 3 medium potatoes into wedges and 1 medium cauliflower into florets, and finely chop 3 onions and 3 tomatoes separately.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a kadhai on medium heat and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds for 20 seconds until aromatic.
Add the onions and 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and fry for 8 minutes until richly golden brown, the base of a good dhaba masala.
Add the tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 2 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp salt and cook for 6 minutes until the oil separates and the masala looks thick.
Fold in the potatoes and cauliflower, cover and cook on low for 16 minutes, stirring twice, until the vegetables are tender, then stir in 2 tbsp fresh cream and 1 tbsp butter on low heat.
In a small ladle warm 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, crush 1 tbsp kasuri methi into it off the heat, then pour it over with 1 tsp garam masala and 3 tbsp coriander and fold through.
tips: Crush the kasuri methi between your palms before adding so its aroma releases fully into the ghee.
Brown the onions properly to a deep gold; this single step is what separates a dhaba masala from a pale home sabzi.
A tablespoon of thick curd whisked in with the tomatoes makes the masala even richer if you want a wetter, gravy-like finish.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve steaming with tandoori-style butter rotis and a sliced onion-and-green-chilli salad dressed with lemon.

variations.name: Home-style Aloo Gobi
variations.description: A pared-back everyday Chhattisgarhi kitchen version cooked low and slow with minimal spice so the sweetness of the cauliflower shines. No garam masala, no chilli theatrics, just turmeric, cumin and a slow steam that turns the vegetables silky. The kind of unfussy sabzi that tastes of home.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A light hand of wood-pressed oil keeps this gentle sabzi clean-tasting, not heavy.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Just a teaspoon at the end rounds off the simple spices with a homely aroma.

steps: Cut 3 medium potatoes into small cubes and 1 medium cauliflower into small florets so they steam through quickly and evenly.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a heavy pan on medium heat and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds with 1 inch grated ginger for 20 seconds.
Add 1 chopped onion and cook for 4 minutes until just translucent, keeping the heat gentle so it stays pale.
Stir in 2 chopped tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 0.5 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp salt and cook for 4 minutes until softened.
Add the potato and cauliflower, sprinkle 2 tbsp water, cover tightly and steam on the lowest heat for 18 to 20 minutes, stirring once, until meltingly soft.
Turn off the heat, drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee and scatter 2 tbsp coriander, then rest covered for 2 minutes before serving.
tips: Keep the heat truly low and let the trapped steam do the cooking; this is what gives the vegetables their soft, home-style texture.
Add only a splash of water, since cauliflower releases its own moisture and too much will make the sabzi watery.
Leftovers make a lovely stuffing for the next morning's paratha, mashed lightly with a pinch of extra salt.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve simply with hot phulkas, a spoon of homemade white butter and a side of plain yoghurt.

variations.name: Classic Aloo Matar
variations.description: The comforting everyday curry of soft potato cubes and sweet green peas simmered in a light cumin-tomato masala with just enough gravy to soak into rice or roti. The peas keep it fresh while the potato makes it filling. A quick, crowd-pleasing weeknight staple.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A clean wood-pressed oil forms the base of the everyday gravy.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A finishing spoon of ghee rounds the tomato tang and carries the garam masala.

steps: Peel and cut 3 medium potatoes into 2 cm cubes and keep 1.5 cups shelled green peas ready.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a kadhai on medium and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds with 0.5 tsp ajwain for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add 2 finely chopped onions and 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and fry for 7 minutes until golden.
Add 3 pureed tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1.5 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp salt and cook for 6 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the potatoes and peas, stir to coat, then pour in 1.5 cups hot water, cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the gravy thickens.
Stir in 0.5 tsp amchur powder, swirl in 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and 3 tbsp coriander, and simmer for a final minute.
tips: Pureeing the tomatoes gives a smoother, more even gravy than chopping them.
If using frozen peas, add them in the last 6 minutes so they stay bright and sweet.
Mash one or two potato cubes into the gravy to thicken it naturally without any flour.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with hot puris or jeera rice and a side of pickled green chillies.

variations.name: Masala Aloo Matar
variations.description: A richer, festive Haryana-style masala aloo matar simmered in a fragrant whole-spice gravy rounded with cashew paste and a swirl of cream. Bay leaf, clove, cardamom and cinnamon bloomed in ghee give it a warm, almost korma-like depth far removed from the quick weeknight curry. Fragrant, creamy and generous.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: The whole-spice tarka blooms in ghee so the korma-like base turns nutty, not sharp.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A splash beside the ghee keeps the onions from browning too fast as they caramelise.

steps: Peel and cube 3 medium potatoes into 2 cm pieces, keep 1.5 cups green peas ready, and grind 3 tbsp soaked cashews to a smooth paste.
Warm 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee with 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil and bloom 1 bay leaf, 4 cloves, 3 green cardamom, 1 inch cinnamon and 1 tsp cumin seeds for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add 2 chopped onions with 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and fry on medium for 7 minutes until deep golden.
Stir in 2 pureed tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp Kashmiri red chilli powder and 1 tsp salt, cook 4 minutes, then add the cashew paste and cook 3 minutes until glossy.
Add the potatoes and peas with 1.25 cups hot water, cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the gravy thickens.
Swirl in 3 tbsp fresh cream and 1 tsp garam masala, simmer 2 minutes, and finish with 3 tbsp chopped coriander off the heat.
tips: Grind the cashews very smooth for a silky, restaurant-style gravy rather than a grainy one.
Bloom the whole spices gently in the ghee so the korma-like base stays sweet, not bitter.
Add the cream on low heat and avoid a hard boil so it does not split.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with warm butter naan or saffron pulao and a side of pickled onions.

variations.name: Spicy Aloo Matar
variations.description: A Telangana-style spicy aloo matar where slit green chillies and coarsely crushed black pepper bring sharp heat to the sweet peas, all tempered in pungent mustard oil. The pepper gives a warm, lingering burn against the soft potato. Fiery, aromatic and vivid.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Its pungency stands up to the black pepper and green-chilli heat.

steps: Peel and cube 3 medium potatoes into 2 cm pieces, keep 1.5 cups green peas ready and slit 4 green chillies.
Heat 2.5 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil in a kadhai on medium-high until shimmering, then crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds for 15 seconds.
Add 2 chopped onions, the slit green chillies and 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and fry for 6 minutes until the onions soften and the chillies blister.
Add 3 pureed tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1.5 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp salt and cook for 6 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the potatoes and peas with 1.25 cups hot water, cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Crush 1 tsp black pepper coarsely, stir it in with 3 tbsp coriander and simmer uncovered for 2 minutes so the pepper heat infuses the gravy.
tips: Heat the mustard oil until it shimmers to mellow its raw bite before the tempering.
Add the crushed pepper near the end so its aromatic heat stays bright.
For a thicker, spicier coat, reduce the gravy a couple of minutes longer uncovered.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with steamed rice and a bowl of cool curd, or with hot phulkas and sliced onion.

variations.name: Dhaba-style Aloo Matar
variations.description: A smoky Chhattisgarh dhaba-style aloo matar built on deeply browned onions and a tangy yogurt bhuna, then given a real charcoal dhungar in ghee for that highway-kitchen aroma. Whole black cardamom, crushed kasuri methi and a knob of butter make it dark, herby and robust. Rustic, smoky and satisfying.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A generous pour browns the onions into the glossy, smoky base of a dhaba gravy.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Drizzled over the smoking charcoal for the dhungar that seals in the dhaba aroma.

steps: Peel and cube 3 medium potatoes into 2 cm pieces, keep 1.5 cups green peas ready, and whisk 3 tbsp yogurt smooth with 1 tsp Kashmiri red chilli powder.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a kadhai, crackle 1 whole black cardamom and 1 tsp cumin seeds, then add 3 chopped onions and 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste.
Fry the onions for 9 minutes until deep golden brown for a smoky dhaba base.
Lower the heat, add 3 chopped tomatoes and the whisked yogurt with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 2 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp salt, and bhuna for 6 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the potatoes and peas with 1.25 cups hot water, cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes until the potatoes are soft and the gravy thickens.

Set a lit charcoal in a small bowl in the pan, drizzle 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee over it, cover 2 minutes to smoke, then fold in 1 tbsp crushed kasuri methi, 1 tbsp butter, 1 tsp garam masala and 3 tbsp coriander.
tips: The charcoal dhungar gives the signature dhaba smokiness, so keep the lid tight while it infuses.
Whisk the yogurt smooth and add it on low heat so it melts into the masala without curdling.
Black cardamom brings a smoky-camphor depth, so use just one pod to avoid overpowering the gravy.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with laccha paratha or butter naan and a sliced onion salad with lemon.

variations.name: Home-style Aloo Matar
variations.description: A Jharkhand home-style aloo matar kept simple and light, with a thin everyday gravy, minimal spice and the peas cooked just tender. It is the fuss-free version made on busy evenings when comfort matters more than richness. Gentle, honest and quick.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A light hand of wood-pressed oil keeps this everyday curry clean-tasting.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A last teaspoon of ghee adds a homely aroma to the simple gravy.

steps: Peel and cube 3 medium potatoes into small 1.5 cm pieces and keep 1.5 cups green peas ready.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a kadhai on medium and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds with 1 inch grated ginger for 20 seconds.
Add 1 chopped onion and saute for 4 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add 2 chopped tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 0.75 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp salt and cook for 4 minutes until softened.
Add the potatoes and peas with 2 cups hot water, cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes until the potatoes are soft and a thin gravy forms.
Mash a couple of potato pieces to lightly thicken, finish with 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee and 2 tbsp coriander, and serve hot.
tips: Cut the potatoes small so they cook fast and the everyday curry comes together quickly.
The thin gravy is meant to be soaked up by rice, so keep it loose rather than thick.
Mashing a couple of potato pieces thickens the gravy naturally without any effort.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve over steamed rice with a spoon of ghee, or with soft rotis and a slice of lemon.

variations.name: Classic Mushroom Masala
variations.description: The everyday mushroom sabzi where sliced button mushrooms are seared to release their water, then simmered in a cumin-onion-tomato masala until glossy and semi-dry. Their meaty bite makes this a favourite even with non-vegetarians. Quick, savoury and endlessly versatile.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A high-smoke-point oil sears the mushrooms fast so they brown rather than stew.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A finishing spoon of ghee deepens the earthy mushroom flavour.

steps: Wipe 400 g mushrooms clean with a damp cloth rather than washing, then slice each into thick pieces.

Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a kadhai on medium-high and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds with 0.5 tsp ajwain, then add the mushrooms and saute for 6 minutes until they release their water and it cooks off.
Push the mushrooms aside, add 2 chopped onions and 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and fry for 6 minutes until golden.
Add 2 chopped tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1.5 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp salt and cook for 5 minutes until the oil separates.
Fold everything together and cook uncovered on medium for 4 minutes so the masala coats the mushrooms and turns semi-dry.
Stir in 0.5 tsp amchur powder, swirl in 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and 2 tbsp coriander, and toss for a final minute.
tips: Never soak mushrooms in water; they absorb it and go soggy, so wipe them clean instead.
Cook off the released mushroom water fully before adding the masala so the dish stays glossy, not watery.
A high flame at the start gives the mushrooms a lovely browned, savoury edge.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with hot phulkas or jeera rice and a wedge of lemon on the side.

variations.name: Punjabi Mushroom Masala
variations.description: A rich, makhani-leaning Punjabi mushroom where meaty quartered mushrooms sit in a velvety tomato-cashew gravy finished with butter, cream and crushed kasuri methi. The cashew paste and Kashmiri chilli give it a smooth, glossy body and a deep restaurant-red colour. Buttery, fragrant and made for scooping with naan.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: The makhani gravy is built on ghee for that rich Punjabi buttery depth.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Used to sear the mushrooms fast so they brown and stay meaty in the gravy.

steps: Wipe 400 g mushrooms clean and quarter them, and grind 3 tbsp soaked cashews to a smooth paste.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a kadhai and sear the mushrooms on high for 4 minutes until lightly browned, then lift them out.
Warm 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in the same pan, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds, add 2 chopped onions and 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, and fry for 7 minutes until golden.
Add 3 pureed tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp Kashmiri red chilli powder and 1 tsp salt, cook 5 minutes, then stir in the cashew paste and cook 3 minutes until the ghee separates.
Return the mushrooms with 0.5 cup hot water, cover and simmer on low for 6 minutes until tender and coated in the gravy.
Stir in 2 tbsp fresh cream, 1 tbsp butter, 1 tsp garam masala and 1 tbsp crushed kasuri methi, simmer 2 minutes, and finish with 3 tbsp coriander.
tips: Sear the mushrooms first and add them back later so they stay meaty in the creamy gravy.
Grind the cashews smooth for a silky makhani body rather than a grainy one.
Add the cream on low heat and avoid boiling hard so the gravy stays smooth.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with butter naan or a soft kulcha and a swirl of cream and julienned ginger on top.

variations.name: Spicy Mushroom
variations.description: A fiery mushroom sabzi where slit green chillies and crushed black pepper drive the heat, balanced by a whisper of jaggery in the western style. The peppery bite plays against the mushrooms' earthiness. Bold, sharp and just a touch sweet-hot.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Sears the mushrooms and carries the sharp pepper-chilli heat.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: A teaspoon for the gentle sweet-savoury balance beloved in western India.

steps: Wipe 400 g mushrooms clean and slice thickly, and slit 4 green chillies lengthways.
Heat 2.5 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a kadhai on medium-high, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds, then add the mushrooms and saute for 6 minutes until their water cooks off.
Push them aside, add 2 chopped onions, the slit green chillies and 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and fry for 5 minutes until the onions soften.
Add 2 chopped tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 0.75 tsp red chilli powder, 1.5 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp salt and cook for 4 minutes until pulpy.
Stir in 1 tsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder, let it melt, then fold everything together and cook uncovered for 4 minutes until semi-dry.
Crush 1 tsp black pepper coarsely, stir it in with 3 tbsp coriander and toss for a final minute so the pepper heat blooms.
tips: Let the jaggery melt fully into the masala so its sweetness distributes evenly against the heat.
Cook the mushroom water off before the masala goes in so the sabzi stays glossy.
Add the crushed pepper at the end for a fresh, aromatic burn rather than a dull one.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with methi thepla or hot phulkas and a spoon of plain curd.

variations.name: Dhaba-style Mushroom
variations.description: A smoky Rajasthan dhaba-style mushroom built on deeply browned onions and a tangy yogurt bhuna, then given a charcoal dhungar in ghee for that roadside aroma. Whole black cardamom, crushed kasuri methi and a knob of butter make it dark, herby and robust. Rustic, smoky and full-bodied.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A generous pour browns the onions into the glossy, smoky base of a dhaba masala.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Drizzled over the smoking charcoal for the dhungar that seals in the dhaba aroma.

steps: Wipe 400 g mushrooms clean and quarter them, and whisk 3 tbsp yogurt smooth with 1 tsp Kashmiri red chilli powder and 2 tsp coriander powder.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a kadhai, crackle 1 whole black cardamom and 1 tsp cumin seeds, then add 3 chopped onions and 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste.
Fry the onions for 9 minutes until deep golden brown for a smoky dhaba base.
Lower the heat, add 3 chopped tomatoes and the whisked yogurt with 0.5 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt, and bhuna for 6 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the mushrooms with 0.5 cup hot water, cover and cook on low for 8 minutes until tender and coated in thick masala.

Set a lit charcoal in a small bowl in the pan, drizzle 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee over it, cover 2 minutes to smoke, then fold in 1 tbsp crushed kasuri methi, 1 tbsp butter, 1 tsp garam masala and 3 tbsp coriander.
tips: The charcoal dhungar gives the true dhaba smokiness, so keep the pan tightly covered while it infuses.
Whisk the yogurt smooth and add it on low heat so it melts into the masala without splitting.
Black cardamom brings a smoky-camphor depth, so use just one pod to avoid overpowering the gravy.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with tandoori roti or missi roti and a sliced onion salad dusted with chaat masala.

variations.name: Home-style Mushroom
variations.description: A Bengali home-style mushroom lightly tempered with panch phoron and cooked semi-dry with a gentle spicing that lets the earthy flavour lead. Mustard oil roots it firmly in the east. Simple, aromatic and everyday comforting.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: The everyday Bengali fat gives this simple sabzi its characteristic pungency.

steps: Wipe 400 g mushrooms clean and slice thickly, keeping the pieces even.
Heat 2.5 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil in a kadhai on medium-high until shimmering, then crackle 1 tsp panch phoron with 2 slit green chillies until the seeds pop.
Add the mushrooms and saute for 6 minutes on medium-high until their water releases and cooks off.
Add 2 chopped onions and 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and fry for 5 minutes until soft and light gold.
Add 2 chopped tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 0.75 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp salt and cook for 5 minutes until pulpy and semi-dry.
Stir in 2 tbsp coriander, adjust salt and serve warm.
tips: Let all five seeds of the panch phoron crackle before the mushrooms go in for the true eastern aroma.
Heat the mustard oil to shimmering to soften its raw sharpness first.
Keep the dish semi-dry so the earthy mushroom flavour stays front and centre.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with steamed rice and a drizzle of raw mustard oil, or with hot rotis and dal.

variations.name: Classic Atta Ladoo
variations.description: A wholesome whole-wheat ladoo where khapli atta is slow-roasted in ghee until it smells like fresh-baked biscuit, then bound with jaggery. Nutty, faintly fudgy and far more nourishing than any refined-flour sweet. The everyday energy ladoo that Indian grandmothers keep in a tin for hungry children.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Ancient khapli wheat roasts to a deeper, nuttier flavour and higher fibre than ordinary atta.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee is the roasting medium that cooks off the raw-flour taste and gives the ladoo its melt.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: Fine jaggery blends into the warm atta smoothly and keeps the ladoo unrefined.

steps: Melt 3/4 cup Anveshan Ghee in a heavy kadhai on low heat, add 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta and stir so every bit is coated in the fat.
Roast on low heat for 15 to 18 minutes, stirring constantly, until the atta turns golden brown and gives off a warm, biscuity aroma; do not let it scorch.
Take the pan off the heat and let the roasted atta cool for 8 to 10 minutes until just warm, so the jaggery will not seize into syrup.
Stir in 1 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder and 1 tsp cardamom powder, mixing thoroughly until the mass holds together when pressed.
Fold in 3 tbsp chopped almonds and 2 tbsp cashews, then roll into 12 firm ladoos while the mixture is still warm and pliable.
Rest on a plate for 30 minutes to set before transferring to an airtight jar.
tips: Keep the flame low and stir without pause; khapli atta browns fast at the edges and a scorched batch tastes bitter throughout.
If the ladoos crack while rolling, the mixture has cooled too much; warm it for a minute with a teaspoon of ghee to bring it back.
Roasting the atta a shade darker than you think develops the fullest nutty flavour, so trust your nose over the clock.
variations.servingSuggestion: Tuck one into a school tiffin or serve with warm milk at bedtime; the slow-release wheat makes it a genuinely filling snack.

variations.name: Punjabi Mawa Atta Ladoo
variations.description: A richer Punjabi rendition where crumbled khoya is cooked into the roasted khapli atta, turning the ladoo dense, milky and almost barfi-like. Generous almonds and a hint of saffron make it a wedding-season indulgence. Heavier and more luxurious than the everyday version.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The sturdy khapli grain holds up to the moisture of khoya without going gummy.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee roasts the atta and keeps the khoya from catching as it melts in.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: Its caramel note deepens the milky khoya and keeps the sweet unrefined.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: A few strands bloomed in warm ghee lend the ladoo a festive gold colour and aroma.

steps: Warm 1 tbsp of the Anveshan Ghee and steep a pinch of Anveshan Saffron in it for a few minutes until the ghee turns deep orange, then set aside.
Melt the remaining ghee in a kadhai on low heat and roast 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta for 15 minutes, stirring, until golden and nutty.
Crumble in 3/4 cup khoya and cook together on low heat for 5 to 6 minutes until the khoya melts, coats the atta and the mixture smells of caramelised milk.
Take off the heat, stir in the saffron ghee, and cool for 10 minutes to just warm.
Mix in 1 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder, 1 tsp cardamom powder and 1/4 cup chopped almonds until it binds into a soft, pliable mass.
Roll into 12 ladoos and refrigerate for 20 minutes to firm the khoya before serving.
tips: Use fresh, soft khoya; grainy or dried mawa will not melt smoothly and leaves the ladoo lumpy.
Because of the dairy, store these in the fridge and eat within four to five days rather than keeping them at room temperature.
Bloom the saffron in warm, not hot, ghee; boiling it dulls both the colour and the fragrance.
variations.servingSuggestion: Plate on a silver tray dusted with slivered pistachios for a wedding mithai spread; rich enough to close a festive meal on its own.

variations.name: Uttar Pradesh Panjiri Ladoo
variations.description: The nourishing panjiri ladoo of Uttar Pradesh, traditionally made for new mothers and offered as Janmashtami prasad, loaded with fried edible gum, fennel and dry ginger. Every spoonful is warming and restorative rather than merely sweet. Coarse, crunchy and aromatic with digestive spices.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Whole khapli wheat gives the panjiri its wholesome body and slow-release energy.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: You need extra ghee to both puff the gond and roast the atta for panjiri's crumbly texture.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: Unrefined jaggery suits panjiri's restorative purpose better than white sugar.

steps: Heat 3 tbsp of the Anveshan Ghee in a kadhai on medium heat and fry 1/4 cup edible gum in batches for about 30 seconds each until they puff up and turn white, then lift out and crush coarsely.
Lightly crush 1 tbsp fennel seeds so they release aroma but keep some texture, and set aside.
In the same kadhai add the remaining ghee and roast 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta on low heat for 18 minutes, stirring, until deep golden and biscuity.
Take off the heat and cool for 10 minutes to just warm, then mix in 1 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder, the crushed fennel and 1 tsp dry ginger powder.
Add the crushed gond, 2 tbsp melon seeds and 1/4 cup chopped almonds and fold until the crumbly mixture clumps when pressed.
Shape into 12 sturdy ladoos while warm and let them set for 40 minutes so the gond crunch firms up.
tips: Fry the gond on medium heat only; too hot and it browns and hardens instead of puffing into light, crunchy nuggets.
Crush the fennel rather than leaving it whole so the digestive aroma spreads through every bite without a hard seed to crunch on.
This panjiri keeps for weeks in a cool jar and is meant to be eaten a couple of ladoos at a time as a fortifying snack.
variations.servingSuggestion: Offer as bhog at a Janmashtami puja, then serve warm with a glass of milk; especially soothing on cold mornings.

variations.name: Bihari Sonth Atta Ladoo
variations.description: A Bihari winter ladoo built around a heavier dose of dry ginger and coarse wheat, giving real warmth on frosty Gangetic-plain mornings. A handful of grated dry coconut adds chew and a toasty edge. Rustic, warming and unfussy, the kind kept ready for the whole household.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Coarse khapli wheat gives these ladoos their hearty, rustic bite.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee carries the dry ginger's warmth deep into the roasted flour.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: Jaggery and dry ginger are the classic Bihari winter pairing for heat and sweetness.

steps: Dry-roast 1/2 cup grated dry coconut in a kadhai on low heat for 3 minutes until pale gold and fragrant, then remove.
Add 3/4 cup Anveshan Ghee to the pan and roast 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta on low heat for 16 minutes, stirring, until golden brown and nutty.
Take off the heat and cool for 10 minutes to just warm so the jaggery holds its texture.
Mix in 1 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder, 1.5 tsp dry ginger powder and 1 tsp cardamom powder until the mixture is even and cohesive.
Fold in the toasted coconut and 3 tbsp chopped cashews, then roll into 12 firm ladoos.
Leave to set for 30 minutes; the flavours deepen and the ginger warmth blooms as they rest.
tips: Toast the dry coconut separately and briefly; it burns much faster than the atta and turns bitter if left too long.
The generous sonth is deliberate for warmth, but reduce it to 1 tsp if making these for children who find it too sharp.
Store in a dry jar away from moisture, as the dry coconut can turn if the ladoos pick up humidity.
variations.servingSuggestion: A traditional cold-weather energiser eaten mid-morning with hot ginger tea; also a thoughtful edible gift through the winter months.

variations.name: Multigrain Seed Atta Ladoo
variations.description: A modern, nutrition-forward take using multigrain atta roasted with a mix of toasted seeds for crunch and plant protein. Lightly sweetened with jaggery, it leans wholesome rather than indulgent. A contemporary lunchbox and gym-bag ladoo that still tastes of home.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Multigrain Atta
ingredients.note: The blend of grains and pulses makes these ladoos higher in fibre and protein than plain wheat.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee roasts the mixed grains evenly and rounds their slightly grassy edge.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: A restrained amount keeps this take on the healthy side while still binding well.

steps: Dry-roast 3 tbsp pumpkin seeds, 3 tbsp sunflower seeds and 2 tbsp flax seeds together in a kadhai on low heat for 3 to 4 minutes until they pop and smell toasty, then set aside.
Add 3/4 cup Anveshan Ghee to the pan and roast 2 cups Anveshan Multigrain Atta on low heat for 16 to 18 minutes, stirring, until it darkens to golden and loses any raw smell.
Cool the roasted atta for 10 minutes until just warm so the jaggery does not melt.
Mix in 3/4 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder and 1 tsp cardamom powder until the mixture comes together.
Fold in the toasted seeds and 3 tbsp chopped almonds, then press firmly into 12 ladoos.
Rest for 30 minutes to set; the seeds crisp up and the ladoos hold their shape well for lunchboxes.
tips: Roast the flax seeds only briefly and grind them coarsely if you prefer, since whole flax can pass through undigested.
This mixture is drier than a plain atta ladoo, so add a spoon of extra warm ghee if it refuses to bind.
Keep the jaggery modest as written; the appeal here is a lightly sweet, seed-packed energy ball rather than a rich mithai.
variations.servingSuggestion: Perfect as a mid-workout or afternoon-slump snack; pack two in a small tin with a flask of black coffee for the office.

variations.name: Classic Besan Barfi
variations.description: The melt-in-mouth gram-flour fudge of every Diwali sweet box: coarse besan roasted low and slow in ghee until reddish-gold, bound with a single-thread khandsari syrup and set to a fine, grainy danedar crumb. A splash of milk on the hot besan creates the prized granular texture, and cardamom perfumes every bite.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasting the besan low and slow in pure ghee is what gives barfi its melt-in-mouth grain

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: makes a clean single-thread syrup without the bleaching agents used in refined sugar

steps: Grease an 8-inch tray with a little Anveshan Ghee and keep it ready for setting.

Melt 0.75 cup Anveshan Ghee in a heavy kadai on low heat, add 2 cups coarse besan and roast, stirring without pause, for 12-15 minutes until it turns reddish-gold, loosens into a flowing paste and smells deeply nutty.
Sprinkle 2 tbsp warm milk over the hot besan and whisk quickly; it will splutter and break into fine grains, giving the danedar texture, then switch off the heat and cool for 5 minutes.

In a separate pan, boil 1.5 cups Anveshan Khandsari with 0.5 cup water on medium heat for 5-6 minutes until it reaches a single-thread consistency, when a drop pulled between finger and thumb forms one unbroken string.
Pour the hot syrup into the warm besan in a steady stream, add 1 tsp cardamom and 1 pinch salt, and beat vigorously for 2-3 minutes until the mixture thickens and starts leaving the pan.
Spread at once into the greased tray, smooth the top, scatter 2 tbsp each slivered pistachios and almonds, press lightly and cut into squares after 20 minutes while still warm.
tips: The single-thread syrup is make-or-break: too thin and the barfi never sets, too thick and it turns grainy and rock-hard.
Sprinkling milk onto the roasted besan is the trick for a granular danedar crumb, but do it off a high flame or the besan clumps.
Score the barfi while warm, yet lift the pieces out only once fully cool, or they crumble.
variations.servingSuggestion: Box in a single layer with butter paper between rows as a Diwali gift; they keep two weeks at room temperature and are made for a cup of cutting chai.

variations.name: Uttar Pradesh Mawa Besan Barfi
variations.description: The richer halwai-shop version from UP mithai counters, where grated khoya folded into the roasted besan makes it denser, softer and milkier. Saffron, a hint of ground clove and nutmeg give it a festive warmth, finished with a delicate sheet of silver varak.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: carries the khoya and besan together into a soft, halwai-shop crumb

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: keeps the mawa-rich barfi sweet but not cloying, with a clean finish

ingredients.name: Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron
ingredients.note: bloomed in warm milk to colour and perfume the festive barfi

steps: Soak 15 strands of Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron in 1 tbsp warm milk and grease an 8-inch tray with a little Anveshan Ghee.
Melt 0.5 cup Anveshan Ghee in a kadai on low heat, add 2 cups coarse besan and roast for 12 minutes, stirring constantly, until reddish-gold and nutty.
Lower the flame and mix in 0.75 cup grated khoya, cooking 4-5 minutes until it melts into the besan and the mixture smells rich and milky.
In a separate pan, boil 1.5 cups Anveshan Khandsari with 0.5 cup water for 5-6 minutes to a single-thread syrup, then pour it into the besan-khoya off the heat.
Beat in the saffron milk, 1 tsp cardamom, 0.25 tsp clove powder and 1 pinch nutmeg for 2-3 minutes until the mass thickens and pulls from the sides.
Spread into the tray, press 2 tbsp slivered pistachios and a sheet of silver varak on top, and cut into diamonds after 25 minutes while just warm.
tips: Use fresh, soft khoya; dried-out mawa will turn the barfi crumbly rather than fudgy.
Because the khoya adds moisture, keep the syrup at a firm single thread so the barfi still sets cleanly.
Refrigerate these once cool, as the mawa content means they keep best for about five days.
variations.servingSuggestion: Present on a brass thali at Karva Chauth or Bhai Dooj alongside dry fruits; the varak-topped diamonds look regal next to plainer mithai.

variations.name: Bihar Roasted Besan Barfi
variations.description: A rustic, jaggery-sweetened barfi from Bihari kitchens where the besan is roasted extra deep and cut with crushed fennel and toasted dry coconut. Unrefined jaggery gives it a dark, molasses-rich flavour and a firmer, more old-fashioned bite than the sugar version.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: deep-roasts the coarse besan for a robust, village-style nuttiness

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: gives a dark, molasses-rich sweetness that defines this rustic barfi

steps: Grease an 8-inch tray with a little Anveshan Ghee and set aside for later.
Melt 0.75 cup Anveshan Ghee in a kadai and roast 2 cups coarse besan on low-medium heat for 14 minutes, stirring constantly, until it darkens to a deep reddish-brown and smells strongly nutty.
Add 3 tbsp grated dry coconut and 1 tsp crushed fennel and toast 2 minutes more until fragrant, then take the pan off the heat and cool 5 minutes.
Meanwhile melt 1.25 cups Anveshan Jaggery Powder with 0.5 cup water on low heat and simmer 5 minutes to a thick syrup, straining out any grit.
Pour the warm jaggery syrup into the besan, add 1 tsp cardamom and 2 tbsp chopped cashews, and stir hard for 3 minutes until the mixture thickens and comes together in a mass.
Spread into the greased tray, press flat, and cut into squares after 25 minutes, letting them firm fully before lifting out.
tips: Jaggery scorches faster than sugar, so keep the syrup on low heat and pull it off as soon as it thickens.
The extra-deep roast gives this barfi its rustic edge, but stir constantly in the last minutes so it browns evenly rather than burning in spots.
If the set feels soft, chill for 30 minutes before cutting; jaggery barfi firms up more in the fridge.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve these dense squares with winter tea or pack them for Chhath Puja prasad; the fennel makes them pleasantly digestive after a heavy meal.

variations.name: Gujarati Mohanthal
variations.description: The temple-famous Gujarati sweet built on a ghee-and-milk khees rub that turns the besan gorgeously coarse and grainy before roasting. A firmer two-thread syrup, saffron and nutmeg give mohanthal its dense, sliceable body and unmistakable festive fragrance.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: part is rubbed into the besan as khees for mohanthal's signature coarse grain

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: cooked to a firm two-thread syrup so the mohanthal sets dense and sliceable

ingredients.name: Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron
ingredients.note: bloomed in warm milk to give mohanthal its golden hue and temple aroma

steps: Rub 3 tbsp whole milk and 2 tbsp melted Anveshan Ghee into 2 cups coarse besan with your fingertips until crumbly, rest 15 minutes, then pass through a coarse sieve to make the grainy khees.
Soak 20 strands of Anveshan Kashmiri Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk and grease an 8-inch tray with a little ghee.
Heat the remaining Anveshan Ghee in a kadai and roast the khees on low heat for 12-14 minutes, stirring constantly, until deep golden, aromatic and grainy.
In another pan boil 1.5 cups Anveshan Khandsari with 0.75 cup water for 7-8 minutes to a firm two-thread syrup, when the drop forms two parallel threads between the fingers.
Take the besan off the heat, pour in the syrup with the saffron milk, 1 tsp cardamom and 0.25 tsp nutmeg, and stir 2-3 minutes until it thickens and glosses.
Spread into the tray, scatter 2 tbsp each slivered almonds and pistachios, press gently and cut into squares after 30 minutes once set firm.
tips: The khees rub is the soul of mohanthal; don't skip resting and sieving it, or you lose the characteristic coarse grain.
Mohanthal needs a firmer two-thread syrup than plain barfi so it sets dense enough to slice cleanly.
Let it set at room temperature rather than the fridge, which can make the grainy texture seize.
variations.servingSuggestion: A staple of Gujarati thal and Diwali platters, mohanthal is best served at room temperature in thick squares beside a glass of chaas.

variations.name: Rajasthani Besan Chakki
variations.description: A ghee-drenched Marwari sweet, coarser and richer than everyday barfi, with no khoya to hide behind, just deeply roasted besan carrying its own nutty flavour. Melon seeds and chironji fold through for a subtle crunch, in the generous style of Rajasthani halwais.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: the lavish ghee is what gives Marwari besan chakki its rich, short crumb

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: boiled to a single-thread syrup for a clean sweetness that lets the ghee-roasted besan shine

steps: Grease an 8-inch tray with a little Anveshan Ghee and keep ready.
Melt 1 cup Anveshan Ghee in a heavy kadai and roast 2 cups coarse besan on low heat for 14-15 minutes, stirring constantly, until it turns reddish-gold and the ghee floats free and clear.
Sprinkle 2 tbsp warm milk over the roasted besan and beat quickly so it froths and grains, then stir in 2 tbsp melon seeds and 1 tbsp chironji and take off the heat to cool 5 minutes.
Boil 1.5 cups Anveshan Khandsari with 0.5 cup water for 5-6 minutes to a single-thread syrup, then pour it into the warm besan.
Add 1 tsp cardamom and beat hard for 3 minutes until the batter thickens and starts leaving the sides of the pan.
Spread into the tray, scatter 2 tbsp slivered almonds, press lightly and cut into squares after 25 minutes while still warm.
tips: Watch for the ghee separating and floating clear around the besan; that visual cue means it is roasted enough.
Toast the melon seeds only briefly in the residual heat so they stay nutty rather than popping and burning.
This barfi is richer than most, so cut it into smaller squares than usual to serve.
variations.servingSuggestion: A Marwari wedding-feast favourite, serve these ghee-rich squares warm with kesar milk or as part of a festive sweet platter with ghevar.

variations.name: Classic Besan Cheela
variations.description: The everyday Chhattisgarhi breakfast pancake: a smooth gram-flour batter loosened to a pourable pouring consistency, studded with onion and coriander and griddled in Anveshan Groundnut Oil until lacy and golden. A spoon of Anveshan Khapli Atta in the batter gives the edges an extra crisp bite without weighing it down.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Wood-pressed groundnut oil for greasing the tava and drizzling the edges to a lacy, golden crisp.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: A little nutty emmer-wheat atta whisked in to firm up the batter and crisp the cheela edges.

steps: Whisk 2 cups gram flour with 3 tbsp Anveshan Khapli Atta, 0.5 tsp turmeric, 0.5 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder and 1 tsp salt, then add about 1.75 cups water and beat to a smooth, lump-free pouring batter that coats the whisk thinly.
Stir in 1 finely chopped medium onion, 2 chopped green chillies and 3 tbsp coriander leaves, then rest the batter for 10 minutes so the flour hydrates.
Heat a flat tava over medium heat and rub it with 0.5 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil until a drop of batter sizzles gently on contact.
Pour a ladle of batter into the centre and spread it outward in a spiral into a thin 7-inch round, then drizzle 0.5 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil around the edges.
Cook undisturbed for about 2 minutes until the top looks dry and the underside is golden and lacy, then flip and cook the second side for 1 minute until spotted brown.
Fold the cheela in half, slide it onto a plate and repeat with the rest of the batter, greasing the tava lightly each time.
tips: Rest the batter for 10 minutes so it thickens slightly; if it turns too thick, loosen with a splash of water to keep the cheela thin and lacy.
Keep the heat at medium; too hot and the outside browns before the besan cooks through, leaving a raw taste.
Wipe the tava with a halved onion between cheelas for a naturally non-stick, evenly browned surface.
variations.servingSuggestion: Roll around a smear of green coriander chutney and serve with a bowl of cool boondi raita for a light, protein-rich breakfast.

variations.name: Jharkhand Masala Besan Cheela
variations.description: A robust, spice-forward cheela from the Jharkhand kitchen where garam masala and coriander powder are toasted into the batter for a deep, warming flavour. Grated carrot and capsicum fold through for texture, and Anveshan Mustard Oil lends the pungent backbone that defines eastern-plateau cooking.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Pungent wood-pressed mustard oil that gives the masala cheela its earthy eastern-plateau kick.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Stirred into the batter for a heartier, wholegrain body that holds the grated vegetables.

steps: Combine 2 cups gram flour with 3 tbsp Anveshan Khapli Atta, 1 tsp garam masala, 1.5 tsp coriander powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric, 0.75 tsp red chilli powder and 1 tsp salt in a bowl.
Pour in about 1.75 cups water and whisk hard until you have a smooth, thin pouring batter with no floury streaks, then rest it for 10 minutes.
Grate 1 small carrot, finely chop half a capsicum and grate a 1-inch piece of ginger, then fold them through the batter with 3 tbsp coriander leaves.
Warm a tava over medium heat and smear it with 0.5 tsp Anveshan Mustard Oil, letting the oil lose its raw sharpness for a few seconds until it shimmers.
Ladle the batter on and spread into a thin 7-inch round, drizzle 0.5 tsp Anveshan Mustard Oil around the rim, and cook for 2-3 minutes until the base is deep golden and set.
Flip and press gently with a spatula, cooking for another 1-2 minutes until browned and cooked through, then repeat with the remaining batter.
