Fold in 4 tbsp spring onion, toss once, and serve immediately while hot.
tips: Sear the mushrooms on high heat without stirring too soon, so they brown rather than release water and stew.
Blanch the baby corn for 2 minutes first if it is very firm, so it turns tender-crisp.
The mushroom umami lets you cut back slightly on soy sauce for a cleaner flavour.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with chilli garlic sauce and a light vegetable clear soup for a hearty dinner.

variations.name: Triple Schezwan Rice
variations.description: The indulgent restaurant showpiece that layers schezwan fried rice, saucy schezwan noodles and a thick schezwan gravy in one bowl. It is a complete, over-the-top meal combining three textures and a triple hit of fiery flavour in every spoonful.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: one clean oil for frying the rice, noodles and the fiery gravy

steps: Boil 150 g hakka noodles in salted water for 4 minutes, drain, rinse cold and toss with a little oil; cool 3 cups of cooked rice separately.

Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a wok, fry a third of the minced garlic on high for 30 seconds, add the diced carrot and capsicum and stir-fry 2 minutes, then toss in the rice with 2 tbsp Schezwan sauce, 0.5 tbsp soy sauce and 0.5 tsp salt for 3 minutes; set the fried rice aside.
In the same wok add 1 tbsp oil, fry a third of the garlic, then toss the boiled noodles with 1.5 tbsp Schezwan sauce, 0.5 tbsp soy sauce and 0.5 tsp salt for 2 minutes and set aside.
For the gravy, heat the last 1 tbsp oil, fry the remaining garlic for 30 seconds, then add 1.5 cups vegetable stock, 1.5 tbsp Schezwan sauce, 0.5 tbsp soy sauce and 0.5 tsp salt and bring to a boil.
Slurry 2 tbsp cornflour in 4 tbsp cold water, stir it into the gravy and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until thick and glossy.
To serve, mound the schezwan rice on one side of a plate, the schezwan noodles on the other, ladle the hot gravy over the centre, and garnish with 5 tbsp spring onion.
tips: Cook the rice, noodles and gravy in sequence in the same wok to save time and build layered flavour.
Keep the gravy slightly thin, as it thickens further once ladled over the rice and noodles.
Assemble just before serving so the noodles and rice do not turn soggy under the gravy.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve in a wide shallow bowl as a complete indulgent meal, with extra Schezwan sauce on the side.

variations.name: Classic Jaggery Sweet Dalia
variations.description: This Classic Sweet Dalia roasts broken wheat in ghee and simmers it in milk until creamy, sweetened with mineral-rich jaggery and perfumed with cardamom. Studded with almonds and raisins, it is a warm, nourishing porridge served for breakfast or as a light after-dinner sweet.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasting the dalia in bilona ghee gives this porridge its nutty depth

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: unrefined jaggery sweetens the dalia with a deep caramel warmth

steps: Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a heavy pan over medium heat and roast the 0.75 cup broken wheat for 4 minutes, stirring, until it turns golden and smells toasty.
Add 1 cup water, cover and simmer over low heat for 8 minutes until the dalia is soft and the water is absorbed.
Pour in the 4 cups milk and simmer gently for 10 minutes, stirring often, until the porridge thickens and turns creamy.
Stir in the chopped almonds, cashews and 2 tbsp raisins along with 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and cook for 2 more minutes.
Switch off the heat and let the porridge cool for 3 minutes so it is warm but no longer boiling.
Mix in 0.5 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder until fully dissolved and serve warm.
tips: Always add the jaggery off the heat once the milk has cooled slightly, so it does not curdle.
Roast the dalia patiently until golden, as this is what stops the porridge tasting raw.
Thin with a little warm milk if it thickens too much on standing before serving.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm in bowls with an extra sprinkle of slivered almonds and a drizzle of ghee on top.

variations.name: Shahi Dry-Fruit Sweet Dalia
variations.description: A royal, festive rendition enriched with khoya, saffron and a spoon of dry-fruit paak for a kheer-like decadence. Thick, fragrant and studded with pistachios, this indulgent sweet dalia is meant for celebrations and cold-weather treats.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: extra ghee gives this festive dalia its rich, glossy body

ingredients.name: Anveshan Dry Fruit Paak
ingredients.note: a spoon of dry-fruit paak lends instant nutty richness and gentle sweetness

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: saffron steeped in warm milk gives the porridge its regal colour and aroma

steps: Soak the pinch of Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk and set aside to bloom into a golden infusion.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a heavy pan over medium heat and roast the 0.75 cup broken wheat for 5 minutes until deeply golden and fragrant.
Add 1 cup water, cover and cook over low heat for 8 minutes until the dalia softens fully.
Pour in the 4 cups milk and simmer for 12 minutes, then crumble in the 0.5 cup khoya and stir until it melts into a thick, creamy base.
Add 0.25 cup sugar, the saffron milk, 0.5 tsp cardamom powder, chopped pistachios and almonds, and cook for 3 minutes until glossy.
Switch off the heat, swirl in 3 tbsp Anveshan Dry Fruit Paak, and serve warm garnished with more pistachios.
tips: Crumble the khoya finely so it melts smoothly without leaving lumps in the porridge.
Bloom the saffron in warm milk first to draw out its full colour and perfume.
This version is meant to be thick and rich, so keep the milk generous and simmer slowly.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm in small bowls topped with rose petals and slivered pistachios as a festive dessert.

variations.name: Vegan Coconut-Jaggery Dalia
variations.description: A dairy-free version that simmers broken wheat in creamy coconut milk, naturally sweetened with jaggery and dates and finished in fragrant coconut oil. Lightly tropical and wholesome, it is a plant-based comfort porridge with a mellow caramel sweetness.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: cold-pressed coconut oil roasts the dalia and reinforces the tropical flavour

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: jaggery keeps this dairy-free porridge naturally and richly sweet

steps: Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the 12 cashews until golden, then remove and reserve them.
In the same oil roast the 0.75 cup broken wheat for 4 minutes until fragrant and lightly coloured.
Add 1.5 cups water, cover and simmer over low heat for 9 minutes until the dalia is soft and the water is nearly absorbed.
Pour in the 3 cups coconut milk with the 6 chopped dates and simmer gently for 8 minutes, stirring, until creamy and thick.
Add 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and 3 tbsp desiccated coconut and cook for 2 more minutes, then take off the heat and let it cool for 3 minutes.
Stir in 0.5 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder until dissolved and serve warm topped with the fried cashews.
tips: Simmer the coconut milk gently on low heat so it stays smooth and does not split.
Chop the dates finely so they melt into the porridge and boost the natural sweetness.
Use full-fat coconut milk for a richer, creamier body in this dairy-free version.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm or chilled, topped with toasted coconut flakes and a few extra chopped dates.

variations.name: Apple Cinnamon Sweet Dalia
variations.description: A wholesome fruit-forward version where broken wheat simmers with grated apple and warm cinnamon, sweetened lightly with honey stirred in at the end. Comforting and gently spiced, it is a fibre-rich breakfast bowl that tastes like apple pie in a spoon.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: ghee toasts the dalia and carries the cinnamon-apple aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Honey
ingredients.note: raw honey stirred in off the heat sweetens the porridge without overpowering the apple

steps: Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pan over medium heat and roast the 0.75 cup broken wheat for 4 minutes until golden and nutty.
Add 1 cup water, cover and cook over low heat for 8 minutes until the dalia is tender.
Stir in one grated apple and 0.75 tsp cinnamon powder and cook for 2 minutes until the apple softens and perfumes the pan.
Pour in the 3.5 cups milk and simmer for 8 minutes, stirring, until the porridge is creamy and thick.
Fold in the chopped walnuts and 2 tbsp raisins, then take the pan off the heat and let it cool for 4 minutes.
Stir in 3 tbsp Anveshan Honey and the second apple, grated fresh, and serve warm.
tips: Add the honey only once the porridge has cooled slightly, so its delicate flavour and nutrients survive.
Grate one apple fresh at the end for a crisp bite against the cooked, softened one.
A pinch of nutmeg alongside the cinnamon deepens the warm, dessert-like aroma.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm topped with apple slices, toasted walnuts and a light dusting of cinnamon.

variations.name: Classic Tandoori Roti
variations.description: The blistered, smoky wheat flatbread of every North Indian dhaba, traditionally slapped onto the wall of a clay tandoor until it chars in patches and puffs. This home method uses an inverted tava over a flame to mimic that fierce dry heat. Firmer and more rustic than a chapati, it is built to stand up to hearty gravies without turning soggy.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Brushed over the blistered roti as it comes off the flame, melting into the charred spots

steps: Combine 2.5 cups whole wheat flour, 0.5 tsp baking powder, 0.5 tsp sugar and 1 tsp salt, then add 0.25 cups curd.
Pour in about 0.75 cups warm water and knead 8 minutes into a soft, smooth dough, then cover and rest it 30 minutes.
Divide into 7 balls and roll one into a thick 7-inch round, then brush one side lightly with water.
Slap the wet side onto a very hot heavy tava so it clings, cook 1 minute until large bubbles rise, then invert the tava over the flame so the top chars.
Hold it over the flame until brown-black blisters form, about 40 seconds, then pull the roti off with tongs.
Brush the hot roti with Anveshan Ghee and repeat with the remaining dough, stacking them under a cloth.
tips: The water on the underside is what makes the roti stick to the inverted tava so you can char it over the flame.
Keep the roti thicker than a chapati; a thin one dries out before it can blister.
Rest the dough the full 30 minutes so the roti stays soft inside despite the fierce charring.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with dal makhani or kadai paneer and a side of sliced onion, mint chutney and lemon.

variations.name: Butter Garlic Tandoori Roti
variations.description: A rich dhaba-favourite where the charred roti is showered with chopped garlic, coriander and a lavish brush of ghee-butter the instant it comes off the heat. The garlic sizzles against the hot bread and perfumes the whole table. Indulgent and aromatic, it turns a plain accompaniment into something people order for its own sake.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Melted with the garlic and brushed thickly over each hot roti for a sizzling, aromatic finish

steps: Knead 2.5 cups whole wheat flour, 0.5 tsp baking powder and 1 tsp salt with 0.25 cups curd and about 0.75 cups warm water into a soft dough, then rest it 30 minutes.
Finely chop 8 garlic cloves and 4 tbsp coriander, and gently warm them into 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee to make a fragrant garlic ghee.
Roll a ball into a thick 7-inch round, press some of the chopped garlic and coriander onto the surface, and brush the underside lightly with water.
Slap the wet side onto a very hot heavy tava, cook 1 minute until bubbles rise, then invert the tava over the flame and char the top until blistered.
Pull the roti off with tongs and brush it generously with the warm garlic ghee.
Repeat with the remaining dough, brushing each hot roti with the garlic ghee before stacking.
tips: Warm the garlic in ghee only until fragrant, not browned, so it does not turn bitter on the hot roti.
Press the garlic onto the roti before charring so it toasts against the flame and mellows.
Make a double batch of the garlic ghee; it keeps for days and is superb on rice and dal too.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with paneer butter masala or a smoky dal tadka, letting the garlic bread mop up the rich gravy.

variations.name: Multigrain Tandoori Roti
variations.description: A wholesome version that builds the charred roti from Anveshan multigrain atta, adding fibre and a deeper, grainy character while keeping the dhaba-style blister. A touch of curd and oil keeps the heartier dough soft under the fierce heat. It is the guilt-free order for a rich restaurant meal.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Multigrain Atta
ingredients.note: A blend of grains adds fibre and a nutty aroma while still blistering like a classic tandoori roti

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sunflower Oil
ingredients.note: A light oil kneaded in to keep the grainy dough soft, with a little brushed over the finished roti

steps: Combine 2.5 cups Anveshan Multigrain Atta, 0.5 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp kalonji and 1 tsp salt, then add 0.3 cups curd and 1 tbsp Anveshan Sunflower Oil.
Add about 0.8 cups warm water and knead 8 minutes into a soft dough; the grainy flour drinks a little more water, then rest it 30 minutes.
Roll a ball into a thick 7-inch round, pressing a few kalonji seeds on top, and brush the underside with water.
Slap the wet side onto a very hot heavy tava, cook 1 minute until bubbles form, then invert the tava over the flame to char the top.
Once brown blisters appear, lift the roti off and brush it lightly with Anveshan Sunflower Oil.
Repeat with the remaining dough, keeping the cooked rotis warm under a cloth.
tips: Multigrain dough needs a slightly longer rest and a touch more water to stay soft under the tandoor-style heat.
Do not roll these too thin; the grainy dough crisps and cracks faster than plain wheat.
A little extra curd keeps this fibre-rich roti tender rather than dense.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a protein-rich rajma or chana masala for a wholesome, satisfying plate.

variations.name: Missi Tandoori Roti
variations.description: A Rajasthani-Punjabi crossover where gram flour and warm spices are worked into the tandoori dough, giving a savoury, golden-charred roti with far more flavour than the plain version. The besan lends a nutty richness and the ajwain aids digestion of the hearty bread. Blistered over the flame and brushed with ghee, it needs little more than a raw onion.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Brushed over the spiced roti straight off the flame, deepening the nutty besan flavour

steps: Combine 1.75 cups whole wheat flour, 0.75 cups besan, 1 finely chopped onion, 0.5 tsp ajwain, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 0.5 tsp baking powder and 1 tsp salt.
Add about 0.75 cups warm water and knead a soft dough; the onion adds moisture, so add the last of the water slowly, then rest it 30 minutes.
Roll a ball into a thick 6-inch round and brush the underside lightly with water.
Slap the wet side onto a very hot heavy tava, cook 1 minute until bubbles rise, then invert the tava over the flame to char the top.
When golden-black blisters form and the besan is cooked through, lift the roti off with tongs.
Brush the hot roti with Anveshan Ghee and repeat with the remaining dough.
tips: Char these a few seconds longer than plain tandoori roti so the gram flour cooks fully and loses its raw edge.
Chop the onion very fine so it does not create weak spots that tear as you roll.
Rest the dough well; the besan makes it stiffer, and rest keeps the charred roti from turning hard.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a bowl of dahi, a raw onion-lachcha and a spoon of mango pickle, dhaba-thali style.

variations.name: Classic Bhajani Thalipeeth
variations.description: Thalipeeth is a rustic Maharashtrian flatbread patted from bhajani, a roasted multigrain-and-lentil flour blend, spiked with onion, sesame and spices and roasted in ghee. Its nutty, savoury depth and crisp lace-edged base make it a wholesome breakfast that needs nothing more than white butter.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts each thalipeeth to a crisp, golden, lace-edged base

steps: In a bowl mix 2 cups bhajani flour with finely chopped onion, 2 tbsp sesame, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric, 3 tbsp coriander and 1 tsp salt.
Add about 0.75 cup water a little at a time and knead into a soft, pliable dough that just holds together.
Take a lemon-sized ball and pat it into a thin round directly on a greased sheet or wet palm, making a small hole in the centre.
Heat a tawa on medium, transfer the thalipeeth onto it, and drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee around the edges and into the hole.
Cook covered for 3 to 4 minutes until the base is crisp and golden, then flip and cook another 3 minutes with a little more ghee.
Serve hot off the tawa, patting and roasting the remaining dough the same way.
tips: Pat the dough on a greased sheet rather than rolling, as bhajani has no gluten and will crack under a pin.
Cook covered on medium so the thick flatbread cooks through before the base burns.
The central hole lets ghee reach the middle and helps the thalipeeth crisp evenly.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with a knob of white butter (loni) and a dab of green chilli-garlic thecha.

variations.name: Instant Multigrain Atta Thalipeeth
variations.description: A weeknight shortcut that skips the homemade bhajani and uses ready multigrain atta rounded out with a little jowar and rice flour for crunch. It comes together in minutes yet keeps the earthy, spiced character of the traditional thalipeeth.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Multigrain Atta
ingredients.note: a ready blend of grains that gives an instant, wholesome thalipeeth base

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: roasts the flatbread crisp and keeps it light for an everyday breakfast

steps: Combine 1.5 cups Anveshan Multigrain Atta, 0.5 cup jowar flour and 0.25 cup rice flour with chopped onion, 2 minced green chillies, 0.5 tsp ajwain, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric, 3 tbsp coriander and 1 tsp salt.
Add roughly 0.75 cup water gradually and knead into a soft dough that does not stick to the hands.
Pat a ball into a thin round on a greased sheet, making a hole in the centre for even cooking.
Heat a tawa on medium, place the thalipeeth on it, and drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil around the edges.
Cook covered 3 minutes until the base is crisp, then flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes more with a little oil.
Serve hot and repeat with the rest of the dough.
tips: The rice flour is key for crispness, so do not skip it even though the atta is pre-blended.
Knead just before cooking, as multigrain dough can stiffen if it sits too long.
If the dough cracks while patting, wet your fingers and smooth the edges as you shape.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with thick curd and a spoon of mango pickle for a fast, filling breakfast.

variations.name: Methi Thalipeeth
variations.description: A fragrant version kneaded with fresh fenugreek leaves and a jowar-bajra base that turns pleasantly bitter-savoury and deeply aromatic. The greens keep the flatbread moist inside while the millet flours crisp the base.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: roasts the methi thalipeeth crisp and balances the bitterness of the greens

steps: Wash and finely chop 1.5 cups fenugreek leaves and squeeze out excess water to tame the bitterness.
Mix the methi with 1 cup jowar flour, 0.5 cup bajra flour, 0.5 cup besan, 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp sesame and 1 tsp salt.
Add about 0.5 cup water gradually, kneading into a soft dough; the methi releases moisture so add water carefully.
Pat a ball into a thin round on a greased sheet with a central hole.
Heat a tawa on medium, cook the thalipeeth with 1 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil drizzled around, covered, for 3 to 4 minutes until crisp underneath.
Flip, add a little more oil, cook 3 minutes until golden, and serve hot.
tips: Squeeze the chopped methi well; wet greens make a sticky dough that is hard to pat thin.
A little besan binds the crumbly millet flours and helps the greens hold together.
Balance the natural bitterness with the ginger-garlic and chilli rather than removing the methi flavour.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a bowl of cool curd or a dollop of ghee to offset the earthy methi.

variations.name: Mixed-Vegetable Thalipeeth
variations.description: A colourful, veg-loaded flatbread that folds grated carrot, cabbage and capsicum into a jowar-bajra dough for extra moisture, sweetness and nutrition. It is a clever way to slip vegetables into a hearty single-dish breakfast.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the veg-packed thalipeeth crisp and adds a rich, nutty finish

steps: In a large bowl combine 1 cup jowar flour, 0.5 cup bajra flour and 0.5 cup besan with 0.5 cup grated carrot, 0.5 cup grated cabbage and 0.33 cup chopped capsicum.
Add 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric, 3 tbsp coriander and 1 tsp salt and mix so the vegetables coat with flour.
Add only about 0.33 cup water little by little, as the vegetables release moisture, and knead into a soft dough.
Pat a ball into a thick round on a greased sheet with a hole in the centre.
Heat a tawa on medium, place the thalipeeth on it, drizzle 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee around the edges, and cook covered for 4 minutes until crisp.
Flip, add more ghee, cook 3 minutes until golden, and serve hot with the vegetables cooked through.
tips: Add water sparingly since the grated vegetables give up plenty of moisture as you knead.
Pat these slightly thicker so the vegetables inside steam through without the base burning.
Grate the vegetables fine so they bind smoothly and the thalipeeth does not crack while shaping.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a garlicky curd dip or plain yogurt for a balanced, veg-rich meal.

variations.name: Classic Dum Veg Biryani
variations.description: This Classic Dum Veg Biryani layers fragrant saffron-scented basmati with a spiced medley of vegetables and slow-cooks them sealed on low heat. The dum method lets the aromas mingle into fluffy, separate grains perfumed with whole spices and fried onions.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee gives the biryani its rich aroma and glossy grains

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: steeped in warm milk to give the top layer its golden colour and aroma

steps: Soak 2 cups basmati rice for 30 minutes, then boil in salted water with half the whole spices until 70 percent cooked, about 6 minutes, and drain.
Heat 4 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and fry the thinly sliced onions on medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until deep golden, then remove half for garnish.

To the remaining onions add 1.5 tbsp ginger garlic paste and the rest of the whole spices, saute 1 minute, then add 3 cups mixed vegetables, 2 tbsp biryani masala and 1 tsp salt and cook for 5 minutes.
Lower the heat, stir in 0.75 cup whisked yogurt off the boil so it does not split, and simmer for 3 minutes until the vegetables are just tender and the masala is thick.
Layer the par-boiled rice over the vegetables, scatter the reserved fried onions, mint and coriander, and drizzle the saffron steeped in 3 tbsp warm milk over the top.
Seal the pot with a tight lid or dough, cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes for the dum, rest 10 minutes, then fluff gently and serve.
tips: Par-boil the rice to only 70 percent so it finishes cooking perfectly during the dum without turning mushy.
Always add the yogurt off high heat and stir gently, or it will curdle in the hot masala.
Place a flat tawa under the pot during dum to diffuse the heat and prevent the bottom from burning.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a cooling boondi or onion raita and a wedge of lemon, garnished with extra fried onions.

variations.name: Hyderabadi Kacchi Veg Biryani
variations.description: A rich Hyderabadi-style biryani where marinated vegetables and rice cook together from raw in a sealed pot, so the grains drink up the spiced yogurt marinade. Fiery, aromatic and layered with mint, it is the most decadent and deeply flavoured of the takes.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: layered through the biryani for the signature Hyderabadi richness

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: soaked in warm milk to streak the rice gold in the Hyderabadi style

steps: Marinate 3 cups mixed vegetables and 150 g paneer cubes with 1 cup yogurt, 2 tbsp ginger garlic paste, 1.5 tsp red chilli powder, 4 slit green chillies, half the mint, half the fried onions and 1 tsp salt for 30 minutes.
Soak 2 cups basmati rice for 30 minutes, then boil in salted water with the whole spices until 60 percent cooked, about 5 minutes, and drain.
Spread the marinated vegetables in a heavy pot, drizzle 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, and layer the par-boiled rice evenly on top.
Scatter the remaining fried onions and mint, drizzle the saffron soaked in 3 tbsp warm milk and the last 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee over the rice.
Seal the pot with a tight lid or dough, cook on high heat for 4 minutes to build steam, then lower to the minimum and dum for 25 minutes.
Rest the sealed pot for 10 minutes, then open, fluff gently from the sides, and serve mixing the layers lightly.
tips: In the kacchi method the raw vegetables cook in the steam, so cut them evenly and keep the heat low.
A thick-bottomed pot is essential so the bottom layer does not scorch during the long dum.
Marinate for at least 30 minutes so the yogurt tenderises the vegetables and carries the spice deep.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with mirchi ka salan and a bowl of cooling raita for an authentic Hyderabadi feast.

variations.name: South-Indian Bhuna Veg Biryani
variations.description: A one-pot South-Indian style biryani where the rice and vegetables are bhuna-cooked together with coconut, curry leaves and a coconut-oil tempering. Earthier and more rustic than the dum versions, it carries the warm, nutty flavours of a Chettinad kitchen.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed coconut oil lends the biryani its authentic South-Indian aroma

steps: Soak 2 cups basmati rice for 30 minutes and grind 0.5 cup grated coconut with 3 green chillies and a little water to a smooth paste.
Heat 4 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil in a heavy pot, crackle 1 tsp fennel seeds and 15 curry leaves, then add the sliced onions and saute for 5 minutes until golden.
Add 1.5 tbsp ginger garlic paste and the chopped tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes until pulpy, then stir in the coconut paste and 1.5 tsp garam masala and bhuna for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add 3 cups mixed vegetables and 1.5 tsp salt, toss to coat in the masala, and cook covered for 5 minutes until they soften slightly.
Drain the rice and add it with 3.5 cups hot water and half the mint, stir once gently, and bring to a boil.
Cover, cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed, rest 10 minutes, then fluff with the remaining mint and serve.
tips: Grinding fresh coconut into the masala gives this biryani its distinctive South-Indian body.
Use exactly 1.75 cups water per cup of soaked rice for perfectly separate one-pot grains.
Let it rest undisturbed after cooking so the grains firm up before you fluff them.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a coconut raita and crisp papad, or a simple onion-tomato kachumber salad.

variations.name: Tehri Pulao-Style Veg Biryani
variations.description: A quick Awadhi-inspired tehri where turmeric-tinged rice and vegetables cook together in one pot without layering or dum. Homely, mildly spiced and golden, it is the everyday, no-fuss cousin of the elaborate dum biryani, ready in a single pot.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee carries the whole-spice aroma through the one-pot rice

steps: Soak 2 cups basmati rice for 20 minutes and drain, keeping it aside.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a heavy pot, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds and the 1.5 tbsp whole spices for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the sliced onions and 2 slit green chillies and saute on medium for 5 minutes until golden, then add 1 tbsp ginger garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the chopped tomato, 0.75 tsp turmeric, 1.5 tsp coriander powder and 1.5 tsp salt and cook for 3 minutes, then add 3 cups mixed vegetables and toss for 3 minutes.
Add the drained rice and gently fold for 1 minute, then pour in 3.5 cups hot water and bring to a rolling boil.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed, rest 10 minutes, then fluff with 0.5 cup fresh coriander and serve.
tips: Fold the rice gently so the delicate grains do not break before the water goes in.
The turmeric gives tehri its signature golden hue, so add it evenly with the masala.
Keep the water ratio at 1.75 cups per cup of rice for fluffy, non-sticky grains in one pot.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with plain yogurt, a dollop of pickle and papad for a comforting everyday meal.

variations.name: Classic Mumbai Veg Frankie
variations.description: The Veg Frankie is Mumbai's iconic hand-held roll, a soft griddled wrap hugging a tangy spiced-potato filling, tart vinegar onions and the signature sour-hot frankie masala. Rolled in a nutty khapli wrap, it is a complete, mess-free street meal in every bite.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: kneaded into soft, nutty wraps that stay pliable for rolling the frankie

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: griddles the wraps golden and sautes the spiced potato filling

steps: Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 0.5 tsp salt, 1 tsp oil and about 0.75 cup water into a soft, non-sticky dough and rest it 20 minutes.
Slice 1 onion thin, toss with 2 tsp vinegar and a pinch of salt, and set aside as the tangy frankie onions.

Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil, saute 1 finely chopped onion until soft, add 4 mashed potatoes, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp salt and 3 tbsp coriander, mash to a firm filling, and shape into 4 logs.
Roll the dough into thin rounds and griddle each on a hot tawa with a little oil until soft with golden spots, about 1 minute each side.
Lay a warm wrap flat, smear with 1 tbsp green chutney, place a potato log, top with vinegar onions and a sprinkle of frankie and chaat masala, then roll up tightly.
Sear the rolled frankie seam-side down on the tawa for 30 seconds to seal, then wrap in paper and serve hot.
tips: Keep the dough soft and well-rested so the wraps stay flexible and do not crack when rolled.
The vinegar onions and frankie masala are non-negotiable; they give the signature sour-spicy tang.
Griddle the wrap fresh and fill it warm, as a cold wrap turns stiff and splits.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve wrapped in butter paper with extra frankie masala on the side for a true street feel.

variations.name: Paneer Tikka Frankie
variations.description: A rich version filled with smoky yogurt-marinated paneer tikka and charred capsicum tucked into a soft wrap with mint chutney. The tandoori-spiced paneer gives it a satisfying, restaurant-style heft.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: griddles the wraps and sears the marinated paneer to a golden char

steps: Knead 2 cups whole wheat flour with 0.5 tsp salt and about 0.75 cup water into a soft dough and rest 20 minutes.
Whisk 0.5 cup thick yogurt with 2 tsp tandoori masala, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp red chilli powder and 0.75 tsp salt, then coat 300 g paneer and 1 cup capsicum and marinate 15 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pan and sear the marinated paneer and capsicum on high for 4 to 5 minutes until charred at the edges.
Roll the dough into thin rounds and griddle each on a hot tawa with a little ghee until soft with golden spots.
Smear a warm wrap with 1 tbsp mint chutney, add the paneer tikka, capsicum and a few onion slices, and roll up tightly.
Sear the roll seam-side down for 30 seconds and serve hot in paper.
tips: Use thick, hung yogurt for the marinade so it clings to the paneer instead of sliding off.
Sear the paneer on high heat for the char that defines a tikka; do not overcook or it turns rubbery.
Warm the wrap just before assembling so the ghee-griddled roti stays soft and rollable.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a side of sliced onion, lemon and extra mint chutney for a filling meal.

variations.name: Schezwan Veg Frankie
variations.description: A fusion frankie loaded with schezwan-tossed cabbage, carrot and noodles for a spicy, saucy, slurpy roll. It marries the comfort of a wrap with the punch of street-side Chinese.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sunflower Oil
ingredients.note: griddles the wraps and stir-fries the schezwan filling on high heat

steps: Knead 2 cups maida with 0.5 tsp salt, 1 tsp oil and about 0.66 cup water into a soft dough and rest 20 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Sunflower Oil on high, saute 6 minced garlic cloves for 20 seconds, then stir-fry the cabbage and carrot for 2 minutes so they stay crisp.
Add 3 tbsp schezwan sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce and 0.5 tsp pepper, toss in 1.5 cups boiled noodles and the spring onion, and stir-fry 2 minutes into a dry, saucy filling.
Roll the dough into thin rounds and griddle each on a hot tawa with a little oil until soft with golden spots.
Spread a generous line of the schezwan noodle filling along a warm wrap and roll it up tightly.
Sear the roll seam-side down for 30 seconds and serve hot while the filling is spicy and warm.
tips: Cook the filling until quite dry, as extra sauce will leak and soften the wrap.
Boil the noodles just to al dente and oil them so they do not turn mushy in the filling.
Adjust the schezwan sauce to taste, since brands differ a lot in heat and salt.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with extra schezwan sauce and a cold drink as a fun Indo-Chinese meal.

variations.name: Sattu Frankie
variations.description: A Bihari-inspired protein-packed roll filled with spiced roasted-gram sattu bound with mustard oil, pickle masala and onion, the same filling that flavours litti. Nutty, tangy and satiating, it turns a humble wrap into a wholesome, high-protein meal.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sattu
ingredients.note: roasted-gram flour forms the nutty, high-protein heart of the filling

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: binds the sattu filling with its pungent, authentic Bihari aroma

steps: Knead 2 cups whole wheat flour with 0.5 tsp salt and about 0.75 cup water into a soft dough and rest 20 minutes.
In a bowl mix 1.5 cups Anveshan Sattu with finely chopped onion, 3 minced green chillies, 5 minced garlic cloves, 2 tsp pickle masala, 0.5 tsp ajwain, 1 tsp salt and 3 tbsp coriander.
Drizzle in 3 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil and 1 tbsp lemon juice with a splash of water and mix into a moist, crumbly filling that just holds together.
Roll the dough into thin rounds and griddle each on a hot tawa until soft with golden spots, about 1 minute per side.
Spread a generous line of the sattu filling along a warm wrap and roll it up firmly.
Sear the roll seam-side down for 30 seconds and serve hot with the pungent sattu aroma coming through.
tips: Add the mustard oil and water gradually so the sattu stays crumbly-moist, not a wet paste.
Use fresh sattu; if it smells stale the whole filling turns flat and dull.
A little extra pickle masala or its oil deepens the tangy, authentic flavour of the filling.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with green chilli pickle and a glass of spiced buttermilk for a wholesome, filling lunch.

variations.name: Classic Veg Fried Rice
variations.description: This Classic Veg Fried Rice is the quintessential Indo-Chinese stir-fry of separate, fluffy rice grains tossed on high heat with crunchy diced vegetables and a whisper of soy. Light, non-greasy and smoky, it is the perfect base for any Chinese-style gravy.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sesame Oil
ingredients.note: its nutty aroma gives the rice an authentic Indo-Chinese finish

steps: Use 4 cups of day-old cooked rice, or spread freshly cooked rice on a plate to cool so the grains stay firm and separate.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil in a wide wok until shimmering, add the minced garlic and ginger, and stir-fry on high heat for 30 seconds.
Add the finely diced carrot, capsicum, 0.5 cup french beans and 0.5 cup cabbage and stir-fry on high for 2 to 3 minutes so they stay crunchy.
Push the vegetables aside, add the cooled rice, then pour 1.5 tbsp soy sauce, 0.5 tsp black pepper and 0.5 tsp salt over it.
Toss everything vigorously on high heat for 3 minutes, lifting and folding the rice so each grain gets coated and lightly smoky.
Stir in 4 tbsp chopped spring onion, give a final toss, and serve immediately while hot.
tips: Day-old refrigerated rice is drier and fries into the fluffiest, most separate grains.
Keep the flame high and the wok moving so the rice sears rather than steams.
Dice the vegetables small and uniform so they cook quickly and distribute evenly.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with veg manchurian gravy or chilli paneer ladled alongside for a complete meal.

variations.name: Burnt Garlic Veg Fried Rice
variations.description: A restaurant-style version built on nutty, golden burnt garlic that perfumes the whole dish with a deep, toasty aroma. Earthier and more intense than the classic, the crisp garlic bits add both flavour and a delicate crunch to every spoonful.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: its clean high-heat frying is ideal for crisping garlic to golden brown

steps: Finely chop 15 garlic cloves and cool 4 cups of cooked rice so the grains stay separate.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a wok and fry half the chopped garlic on medium heat for 2 minutes until deep golden and crisp, then scoop out and reserve.
In the same oil add the remaining garlic and stir-fry on high for 20 seconds, then add the diced carrot, capsicum and 0.5 cup sliced mushroom and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add the cooled rice with 1.5 tbsp soy sauce, 0.5 tsp white pepper and 0.5 tsp salt and toss vigorously on high heat for 3 minutes.
Fold in three-quarters of the reserved burnt garlic and 4 tbsp spring onion and toss for 1 minute.
Top with the remaining crisp burnt garlic and serve immediately while aromatic.
tips: Fry the garlic on medium heat and watch closely, pulling it out at deep golden before it blackens.
Reserving some crisp garlic for the top keeps its crunch as a garnish.
White pepper gives a cleaner, more authentic Chinese aroma than black pepper here.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a light vegetable clear soup or chilli garlic sauce on the side.

variations.name: Schezwan Veg Fried Rice
variations.description: A fiery version where the rice is tossed with spicy Schezwan sauce, dry red chillies and extra garlic for a deep-red, tongue-tingling plate. Bolder and hotter than the classic, it is a complete meal on its own for those who love a spicy kick.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: withstands high heat to bloom the Schezwan paste without burning

steps: Cool 4 cups of cooked rice on a plate so the grains stay firm and separate.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a wok, add 3 broken dry red chillies and the minced garlic and fry on high for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add the finely diced carrot, capsicum and 0.5 cup french beans and stir-fry on high heat for 3 minutes to keep them crunchy.
Stir in 3 tbsp Schezwan sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce and 0.5 tsp salt and toss for 1 minute until the vegetables are coated red.
Add the cooled rice and toss vigorously on high heat for 3 minutes so every grain turns fiery and glossy.
Fold in 4 tbsp spring onion, toss once, and serve immediately while steaming.
tips: Add the Schezwan sauce gradually and taste, since it brings both heat and salt.
Keep the rice slightly undercooked and cooled so it does not clump during the fiery toss.
A drizzle of vinegar at the end lifts the deep chilli-garlic flavour.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve as a spicy one-bowl meal with a cooling cucumber raita or manchurian gravy on the side.

variations.name: Paneer Veg Fried Rice
variations.description: A protein-rich version studded with golden pan-tossed paneer cubes alongside the crunchy vegetables. The soft paneer makes it more filling and satisfying than the classic, turning a side dish into a wholesome standalone meal.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sesame Oil
ingredients.note: a nutty base for both searing the paneer and tossing the rice

steps: Cool 4 cups of cooked rice so the grains stay separate, and cut 200 g paneer into small cubes.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil in a wok and sear the paneer cubes on high heat for 2 minutes until golden on the edges, then set aside.
In the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil, stir-fry the minced garlic and ginger on high for 30 seconds, then add the diced carrot, capsicum and 0.5 cup green peas and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add the cooled rice with 1.5 tbsp soy sauce, 0.5 tsp black pepper and 0.5 tsp salt and toss vigorously on high heat for 3 minutes.
Fold in the seared paneer and 4 tbsp spring onion and toss for 1 minute so everything mixes evenly.
Serve immediately while hot with the paneer still soft.
tips: Sear the paneer separately and add it at the end so the cubes stay whole and golden.
Soak firm paneer in warm water for 10 minutes before searing to keep it soft.
Add a handful of roasted cashews for extra richness and crunch if you like.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve as a filling meal with a bowl of hot-and-sour soup or chilli garlic sauce.

variations.name: Classic Veg Manchurian Gravy
variations.description: This Classic Veg Manchurian features crisp-fried vegetable balls of cabbage, carrot and beans simmered in a thick, glossy soy-garlic-chilli gravy. The tender-inside, crisp-outside balls soak up the savoury sauce, making it a restaurant-favourite over rice or noodles.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: its high smoke point fries the veg balls crisp and clean-tasting

steps: Finely grate 2 cups cabbage, 1 cup carrot and 0.5 cup french beans, squeeze out excess moisture, then mix with 4 tbsp cornflour, 3 tbsp all-purpose flour, half the minced garlic and 0.5 tsp salt into a stiff dough.
Shape the mixture into small balls and deep-fry them in 1 cup Anveshan Groundnut Oil at 180 C for 4 to 5 minutes until golden and crisp, then drain.
In 2 tbsp of the oil, stir-fry the remaining minced garlic, ginger and chopped onion on high heat for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in 2 cups vegetable stock, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1.5 tbsp red chilli sauce, 0.5 tsp black pepper and 0.5 tsp salt and bring to a boil.
Mix the remaining 2 tbsp cornflour with 4 tbsp cold water, stir it in, and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the gravy turns thick and glossy.
Add the fried veg balls just before serving, simmer for 1 minute, garnish with 4 tbsp spring onion and serve hot.
tips: Squeeze the grated vegetables well, or the balls will turn soggy and absorb too much oil.
Add the balls to the gravy at the last minute so they keep a little bite inside.
Test-fry one ball first; if it breaks apart, add a spoon more cornflour to bind the dough.
variations.servingSuggestion: Ladle over steamed rice or hakka noodles and finish with a scatter of spring onion greens.

variations.name: Dry Veg Manchurian
variations.description: The semi-dry starter version where the crisp vegetable balls are tossed with peppers and onions in a clingy soy-chilli glaze rather than a gravy. Each ball stays crunchy and coated, making it the perfect pick-with-a-toothpick party appetiser.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sunflower Oil
ingredients.note: a light wood-pressed oil that fries the balls crisp for the dry toss

steps: Grate 2 cups cabbage and 1 cup carrot, squeeze dry, and mix with 3 tbsp cornflour, 2 tbsp rice flour, minced ginger and 0.5 tsp salt to form a firm mixture.
Roll into small balls and deep-fry in 1 cup Anveshan Sunflower Oil at 180 C for 4 to 5 minutes until crisp and golden, then drain.
In 2 tbsp of the oil, stir-fry the minced garlic and 3 green chillies on high heat for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add the cubed onion and capsicum and toss on high for 2 minutes so they stay crunchy with a slight char.
Pour in 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1.5 tbsp green chilli sauce, 2 tbsp ketchup and 0.5 tsp salt, then thicken with 1 tbsp cornflour slurried in 3 tbsp water and cook for 1 minute until glossy.
Add the fried balls, toss on high heat for 1 minute to coat, garnish with 4 tbsp spring onion and serve immediately.
tips: Keep the sauce minimal and glaze-like so the balls stay dry and crisp rather than soggy.
Fry the balls a shade darker than for gravy, since they will not soften in a sauce.
Serve within minutes of tossing to enjoy the balls at their crunchiest.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve as a starter with toothpicks and a bowl of extra chilli sauce for dipping.

variations.name: Schezwan Veg Manchurian
variations.description: A fiery version where the fried vegetable balls simmer in a bold Schezwan gravy packed with dry red chillies and garlic. Spicier and more pungent than the classic, it delivers a deep-red, lip-tingling sauce that clings to every ball.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: withstands the heat needed to fry the balls and bloom the chilli paste

steps: Grate 2 cups cabbage, 1 cup carrot and 0.5 cup beans, squeeze dry, then bind with 4 tbsp cornflour, some minced garlic and 0.5 tsp salt into a firm mixture.
Shape into balls and deep-fry in 1 cup Anveshan Groundnut Oil at 180 C for 5 minutes until crisp, then drain.
In 2 tbsp of the oil, fry 5 broken dry red chillies, the remaining minced garlic and ginger on high heat for 30 seconds until sharply aromatic.

Add the chopped onion and 2 tbsp finely chopped celery, toss for 2 minutes, then stir in 4 tbsp Schezwan sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 0.5 tsp Sichuan pepper powder, 1.5 cups vegetable stock and 0.5 tsp salt and bring to a boil.
Slurry the remaining 2 tbsp cornflour in 4 tbsp cold water, stir it in, and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the fiery gravy turns thick and glossy.
Add the fried balls just before serving, simmer for 1 minute, garnish with 4 tbsp spring onion and serve hot.
tips: Add the balls at the very end so they hold their shape in the spicy gravy.
Balance the heat with a small pinch of sugar if the Schezwan sauce feels too sharp.
Fry the dry red chillies only until fragrant, as burnt ones turn the gravy bitter.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve over schezwan fried rice or plain steamed rice for a fiery Indo-Chinese meal.

variations.name: Baked Veg Manchurian
variations.description: A lighter version where the vegetable balls are oven-baked instead of deep-fried, then folded into a quick low-oil Manchurian gravy. It keeps the comforting flavour of the original with far less oil, making it a wholesome weeknight indulgence.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sesame Oil
ingredients.note: brushed on the balls and used in the sauce for a nutty Indo-Chinese aroma

steps: Preheat the oven to 200 C and grate 2 cups cabbage, 1 cup carrot and 0.5 cup beans, squeezing out all excess moisture.
Mix the vegetables with 3 tbsp cornflour, 3 tbsp chickpea flour, minced garlic, 1 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil and 0.5 tsp salt, and roll into small balls.
Arrange the balls on a lined tray, brush lightly with oil, and bake for 20 to 22 minutes turning once, until firm and golden.
Heat the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil in a wok and stir-fry the ginger and chopped onion on high for 2 minutes.
Add 2 cups vegetable stock, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp green chilli sauce, 0.5 tsp black pepper and 0.5 tsp salt, then thicken with 2 tbsp cornflour slurried in cold water and cook for 3 minutes.
Fold in the baked balls, simmer for 1 minute, garnish with 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds and 4 tbsp spring onion and serve hot.
tips: Chickpea flour helps the baked balls hold together without the binding that frying provides.
Bake the balls until firm and dry so they do not disintegrate in the gravy.
Add the balls to the sauce only when ready to serve, so they keep some texture.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve over brown rice or noodles for a lighter meal, topped with spring onion greens.

variations.name: Classic Veg Spring Roll
variations.description: Veg Spring Rolls are crisp golden cylinders packed with a stir-fried medley of shredded cabbage, carrot and capsicum seasoned Indo-Chinese style. The wrapper shatters at the first bite to reveal a hot, crunchy, savoury filling that never turns soggy.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sunflower Oil
ingredients.note: its high smoke point fries the rolls crisp and golden without burning

steps: Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Sunflower Oil in a wok on high, add 5 minced garlic cloves and grated 1 inch ginger, and stir for 20 seconds until fragrant.

Add the cabbage, carrot and capsicum and stir-fry on high heat for 2 to 3 minutes so they stay crunchy, then season with 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp vinegar, 0.75 tsp pepper and 0.75 tsp salt and toss in the spring onion; cool completely.
Make a paste of 3 tbsp corn flour with a little water for sealing the rolls.
Place a spoon of filling along one edge of a spring roll sheet, fold the sides in, roll tightly, and seal the end with the corn flour paste.
Heat the remaining Anveshan Sunflower Oil to about 180C, and fry the rolls in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until evenly golden and crisp.
Drain on paper and serve hot, cut in half on the diagonal.
tips: Cool the filling fully before rolling, as a warm filling steams and tears the delicate wrappers.
Stir-fry the vegetables on high heat only briefly so they keep their crunch inside the roll.
Seal the final edge well with corn flour paste so the rolls do not unravel or take in oil.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with schezwan sauce or a sweet chilli dip as a starter or party snack.

variations.name: Schezwan Noodle Spring Roll
variations.description: A heartier street-cart roll where slurpy hakka noodles are tossed with fiery schezwan sauce and vegetables before being wrapped and fried. Each bite mixes the crunch of the shell with a spicy, tangy noodle centre.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sunflower Oil
ingredients.note: fries the noodle-filled rolls crisp and is used to toss the filling

steps: Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Sunflower Oil on high, saute 6 minced garlic cloves for 20 seconds, then stir-fry the cabbage and capsicum for 2 minutes.
Add 2 tbsp schezwan sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 0.5 tsp pepper and 0.5 tsp salt, then toss in 2 cups boiled hakka noodles and the spring onion until well coated; cool fully.
Mix 3 tbsp corn flour with a little water into a sealing paste.
Lay a portion of the noodle filling along a spring roll sheet, roll tightly, and seal the edge with the corn flour paste.
Heat the remaining Anveshan Sunflower Oil to about 180C and fry the rolls in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and crisp.
Drain and serve hot, sliced in half to show the spicy noodle centre.
tips: Toss the boiled noodles in a little oil first so they do not clump while filling the rolls.
Keep the noodle filling on the drier side, as excess sauce makes the wrappers soggy and hard to seal.
Roll a little tighter than usual so the loose noodles stay put during frying.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with extra schezwan mayo and a wedge of lemon as a filling street-style snack.

variations.name: Paneer-Corn Cheese Spring Roll
variations.description: A rich, kid-friendly roll stuffed with crumbled paneer, sweet corn and melty cheese laced with chilli flakes and herbs. The creamy, mildly sweet filling turns gooey inside the crisp golden wrapper.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sunflower Oil
ingredients.note: its clean taste keeps the cheesy filling the hero and fries the shell crisp

steps: In a bowl mix 1.5 cups crumbled paneer, 0.75 cup sweet corn, 1 cup grated mozzarella and 0.5 cup chopped capsicum.
Season with 1 tsp chilli flakes, 0.5 tsp oregano, 0.5 tsp pepper and 0.75 tsp salt and mix into a thick, bindable filling.
Make a sealing paste from 3 tbsp corn flour and a little water.
Spoon the filling along a spring roll sheet, fold in the sides, roll snugly, and seal the edge with the paste.
Heat 3 cups Anveshan Sunflower Oil to about 175C and fry the rolls in batches for 3 minutes until golden and crisp.
Drain briefly and serve within a few minutes while the cheese is still melty inside.
tips: Do not overfill, as the cheese expands and can split the wrapper while frying.
Fry at a slightly lower heat so the shell colours gently without the cheese bursting out.
Serve immediately for the best cheese pull, as the filling firms up as it cools.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a tangy tomato-basil dip or garlic mayo as a crowd-pleasing party starter.

variations.name: Baked Khapli-Wrap Spring Roll
variations.description: A wholesome twist using homemade nutty khapli-atta wrappers, filled with stir-fried vegetables and baked with a brush of ghee instead of deep-frying. The result is a lighter, fibre-rich roll with a rustic, satisfying crunch.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: rolled into thin homemade wrappers for a nutty, high-fibre baked roll

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: brushed over the rolls so they crisp and brown in the oven

steps: Knead 1.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with a pinch of salt and about 0.66 cup water into a soft dough, rest 15 minutes, then roll into thin 6-inch rounds.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, saute 5 minced garlic cloves, then stir-fry the cabbage, carrot and beans on high for 3 minutes so they stay crunchy.
Season with 1 tbsp soy sauce, 0.75 tsp pepper and 0.75 tsp salt, toss in the spring onion, and cool the filling completely.
Preheat the oven to 200C, place filling on each round, roll up tightly, and tuck the ends under, sealing with a little water.
Arrange the rolls seam-side down on a lined tray, brush all over with the remaining Anveshan Ghee, and bake for 12 minutes.
Turn the rolls, brush again with ghee, and bake another 10 to 12 minutes until crisp and golden, then serve warm.
tips: Roll the khapli wrappers as thin as possible so they crisp rather than staying bready in the oven.
Cool the filling fully so the homemade wrappers do not turn soggy and tear while rolling.
Brush ghee on both bakes; it is what browns and crisps the wholemeal wrapper.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a coriander-mint chutney or hung-curd dip for a lighter, wholesome snack.

variations.name: Classic Vegetable Yakhni Pulao
variations.description: A subtle, aromatic pulao built on yakhni, a spice-infused stock strained clear and used to cook the rice so every grain carries the perfume of whole garam masala. In this vegetarian version the stock is drawn from a muslin bundle of spices simmered with yogurt, then finished with soft vegetables. It is elegant and restrained, prized for aroma over heat.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Fries the onions and toasts the rice so it cooks up glossy in the fragrant yakhni stock

ingredients.name: Yakhni spice bundle (fennel, coriander seed, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaf)

steps: Tie the yakhni spices in a muslin cloth, simmer with 4 cups water and 1 tsp salt for 20 minutes until the liquid reduces to a fragrant 3 cups, then squeeze and discard the bundle.
Rinse and soak 2 cups basmati for 20 minutes and drain; whisk 0.75 cups yogurt until smooth.
Heat 4 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a heavy pot, fry 2 sliced onions on medium heat for 8 minutes until golden, then add 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and 2 slit green chillies for 1 minute.
Lower the heat, stir in the whisked yogurt slowly so it does not split, add 1 tsp fennel powder and 2 cups vegetables, and saute 4 minutes.
Add the drained rice, toast gently for 2 minutes, then pour in the strained yakhni stock and 0.5 tsp salt and bring to a rolling boil.
Cover and cook on the lowest flame for 12 minutes, rest 10 minutes, then fold in the mint and fluff so the pale, aromatic grains stay separate.
tips: Strain the yakhni thoroughly through muslin so the stock is clear; loose seeds make the finished pulao gritty.
Add the whisked yogurt only after lowering the flame and stir constantly so it blends smoothly instead of curdling.
Keep this pulao pale and aromatic; resist adding chilli powder or tomato, which would mask the delicate yakhni perfume.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a mint-coriander raita and a plate of sliced cucumber and onion to complement its gentle spicing.

variations.name: Kashmiri Wazwan-Style Yakhni Pulao
variations.description: A valley-inspired yakhni built on the wazwan palette of dry ginger, fennel and Kashmiri chilli, with the stock enriched by soft-cooked lotus stem or morel-style mushrooms. The spicing is warmer and the aroma more resinous than the plains version. It captures the meditative, spice-forward character of a Kashmiri feast in a vegetarian pulao.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: The authentic Kashmiri cooking fat, heated to smoking first to mellow it and give the pulao its earthy pungency

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Finishes the rice with richness after the mustard oil has done the frying

ingredients.name: Yakhni spice bundle (cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, black cumin)

steps: Simmer the muslin-tied yakhni spices with 4 cups water and 1 tsp salt for 20 minutes to a clear 3 cups of stock, then squeeze out and discard the bundle.
Soak 2 cups basmati 20 minutes and drain; heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil until it just smokes, then lower the flame to temper its sharpness.
Fry 1 sliced onion in the mustard oil for 6 minutes until golden, add 1.5 cups sliced lotus stem or mushrooms and saute 4 minutes until they take colour.
Whisk 0.75 cups yogurt with 1 tsp dry ginger, 1.5 tsp fennel and 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli, lower the heat and stir it in slowly so it does not split, cooking 3 minutes.
Add the drained rice, toast 2 minutes, then pour in the strained yakhni and 0.5 tsp salt, bring to a boil and cover on the lowest flame for 12 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes, drizzle 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee over the top, and fluff gently so the warmly-spiced grains stay whole.
tips: Always heat mustard oil to smoking point first, then cool it slightly; this removes the raw bite and leaves a mellow nuttiness.
Soak lotus stem slices in warm water beforehand and slice them thin so they turn tender in the pulao's cook time.
Lean on fennel and dry ginger rather than garam masala to keep the distinct Kashmiri aroma intact.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a Kashmiri-style walnut chutney and a bowl of spiced radish yogurt for an authentic valley plate.

variations.name: Awadhi Paneer Yakhni Pulao
variations.description: A courtly Lucknowi rendition where saffron and rose water lift a delicate yakhni, and cubes of fried paneer replace the meat of the original. Kewra and a whisper of mace make it perfumed and refined, the kind of pulao served at a nawabi dawat. Softer and more floral than the classic, it is subtle luxury in a bowl.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Fries the paneer to gold and toasts the rice, giving the nawabi pulao its refined richness

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: Bloomed in warm milk for a pale gold hue and the floral note that defines Awadhi cooking

ingredients.name: Yakhni spice bundle (mace, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, coriander seed)

steps: Simmer the muslin-tied yakhni spices with 4 cups water and 1 tsp salt for 20 minutes to a clear 3 cups stock, then squeeze and discard the bundle.
Soak 2 cups basmati 20 minutes and drain; steep the Anveshan Saffron in 3 tbsp warm milk.
Heat 4 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, fry 200 g paneer cubes for 2 minutes until light gold and lift them into warm salted water, then fry 2 sliced onions for 8 minutes until golden.
Add 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute, lower the heat and stir in the whisked 0.75 cups yogurt slowly so it does not split, cooking 3 minutes.
Add the drained rice, toast 2 minutes, pour in the strained yakhni, saffron milk and 0.5 tsp salt, and bring to a boil.
Slip in the fried paneer, cover on the lowest flame for 12 minutes, rest 10 minutes, sprinkle 0.5 tsp kewra water, and fluff gently.
tips: Soak the fried paneer in warm salted water so the cubes stay soft and creamy in the delicate pulao.
Use kewra and saffron with a light hand; these perfumes should hint rather than overpower the yakhni.
Keep the flame under the sealed pot as low as possible so the refined grains steam evenly without browning.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a rose-scented boondi raita and a mild vegetable korma for a genuinely nawabi vegetarian spread.

variations.name: Soya-Chunk Yakhni Pulao
variations.description: A hearty, protein-rich take where soya chunks soak up the spiced yakhni like sponges, giving a satisfying, meaty bite to a vegetarian pulao. The chunks are squeezed, browned and simmered so they carry the stock's aroma deep inside. It is a filling, everyday version aimed at gym-goers and growing families who want substance with the fragrance.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A robust wood-pressed oil that browns the soya chunks and fries the onions without overpowering the yakhni

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Finishes the pulao with a nutty aroma once the soya has soaked up the stock

ingredients.name: Yakhni spice bundle (fennel, coriander seed, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon)

steps: Simmer the muslin-tied yakhni spices with 4 cups water and 1 tsp salt for 20 minutes to a clear 3 cups stock, then squeeze and discard the bundle.
Boil 1.5 cups soya chunks for 4 minutes, drain, rinse in cold water and squeeze dry, then soak 2 cups basmati 20 minutes and drain.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil, brown the squeezed soya chunks for 3 minutes until golden, and lift them out.

Fry 2 sliced onions in the same oil for 8 minutes until golden, add 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and 2 slit green chillies for 1 minute, then lower the heat and stir in 0.75 cups whisked yogurt and 1 tsp fennel powder.
Return the soya, add the drained rice, toast 2 minutes, then pour in the strained yakhni and 0.5 tsp salt and bring to a boil.
Cover on the lowest flame for 12 minutes, rest 10 minutes, drizzle 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, and fluff so the stock-soaked chunks stay whole.
tips: Squeeze the boiled soya chunks completely dry before browning, or they will steam instead of taking on colour.
Browning the soya before simmering gives it a firmer, meatier bite that holds up in the finished pulao.
Rinse the boiled chunks in cold water to wash away any raw soya smell before they go into the aromatic stock.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a thick garlic raita and a fresh kachumber salad for a filling, high-protein one-bowl meal.

variations.name: Classic Bedmi Puri
variations.description: The famous fried breakfast bread of Delhi, Mathura and Agra: a firm wheat dough kneaded with a coarse paste of soaked urad dal and warm spices, rolled thick and deep-fried until puffed and crunchy. Unlike a plain puri, the dal gives it a savoury, almost crackly bite that holds up in gravy. It is the soul of a bedmi-aloo breakfast.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Its firm, nutty crumb carries the coarse dal paste and fries into a crunchy puri

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Rubbed into the dough as moyan and to bloom the ground spices for aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Wood-pressed oil fries the dense bedmi puri clean and crisp

steps: Soak 1/2 cup urad dal in plenty of water for 3-4 hours, then drain well and grind to a thick, coarse paste with 1 inch ginger and 2 green chillies, using as little water as possible.

Warm 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a small pan, add 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp lightly crushed fennel and 1/4 tsp hing, let them splutter for 20 seconds, then stir in the dal paste with 1/2 tsp red chilli powder and 1/2 tsp salt and cook 3-4 minutes until it thickens and no longer smells raw; cool completely.
Mix 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt and knead together with the cooled dal masala, adding water only a spoon at a time, into a stiff, firm dough; cover and rest 20 minutes.
Divide the dough into 14 balls and roll each into a 3.5-inch disc about 3 mm thick, keeping bedmi puris deliberately thicker than plain puris.
Heat 3 cups Anveshan Groundnut Oil to about 185C, hot enough that a dough scrap surfaces at once with steady bubbles.
Fry one puri at a time, pressing it under the oil until it puffs, then turning and frying both sides to a deep golden and crunchy finish, about 45 seconds total as the dense dough needs longer.
Drain well and serve the bedmi puris hot, when their crackly texture is at its best.
tips: Cook the dal paste until it is dry and no longer raw, or the puris turn heavy and refuse to puff.
Grind the dal coarse, not silky; a little texture is what gives bedmi puri its characteristic bite.
Roll these thicker than ordinary puris and fry a touch longer so the dal cooks through and crisps.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve the Mathura way with khatta aloo ki sabzi, a bowl of spiced pumpkin and a spoon of sweet tamarind chutney.

variations.name: Moong Dal Bedmi Puri
variations.description: A lighter cousin from the eastern UP kitchens where yellow moong dal replaces the heavier urad, giving a gentler flavour and a puri that is easier to digest. The moong paste keeps the crumb soft with just enough crunch, seasoned with fennel and coriander. A milder, breakfast-friendly bedmi that still fries up beautifully golden.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: A wholesome base that keeps the softer moong puri sturdy enough to puff

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sunflower Oil
ingredients.note: Light wood-pressed oil for frying, with a spoon used to cook the dal masala

steps: Soak 1/2 cup yellow moong dal for 3 hours, drain, and grind coarsely with 1 inch ginger and 2 green chillies using minimal water.

Coarsely crush 1 tsp fennel and 1 tsp coriander seeds; heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Sunflower Oil, splutter 1/4 tsp hing and the crushed seeds for 20 seconds, then add the moong paste with 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt and saute 3-4 minutes until dry and fragrant; cool fully.
Knead 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1/2 tsp salt and the cooled moong masala, adding water sparingly, into a firm dough; cover and rest 20 minutes.
Divide into 14 balls and roll each into a 3.5-inch disc about 3 mm thick, keeping them on the thicker side.
Heat 3 cups Anveshan Sunflower Oil to about 185C, hot enough that a dough pinch rises quickly.
Fry each puri, pressing gently under the oil until it puffs, then turning to fry both sides to an even golden, about 40 seconds.
Drain well and serve the moong bedmi puris hot with their soft, mildly spiced crumb.
tips: Moong dal grinds smoother than urad, so keep the paste on the coarser side for texture.
Cook the paste until dry; leftover moisture makes the puris dense and greasy.
These are gentler than urad bedmi, making them a good choice for a lighter breakfast.
variations.servingSuggestion: Best with a runny aloo-tamatar sabzi and a bowl of sweet boondi or a spoon of jaggery-sweetened curd.

variations.name: Mathura Halwai-Style Bedmi Puri
variations.description: The rich sweet-shop version from Mathura's halwai counters, where the urad dal is loaded with saunf, hing and whole spices, and the dough is kneaded with extra ghee for a flakier, restaurant-grade crunch. These puris are thicker, more aromatic and unapologetically indulgent. This is the bedmi puri of temple-town feasts.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: The wholesome base for a rich, ghee-laden halwai-style dough

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A generous ghee moyan gives the halwai-style puri its flaky, crackly crunch

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: Wood-pressed oil for a deep, even fry that stays clean batch after batch

steps: Soak 1/2 cup urad dal for 4 hours, drain, and grind to a thick coarse paste with almost no water.

Coarsely crush 1.5 tsp fennel and 1 tsp coriander seeds; warm 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, splutter 1/2 tsp hing and the crushed spices for 20 seconds, then add the dal paste with 3/4 tsp chilli powder, 1/2 tsp dry ginger powder, 1/2 tsp garam masala and 1/2 tsp salt, and cook 4-5 minutes until thick and dry; cool completely.
Mix 1.75 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta, 1/4 cup semolina and 1/2 tsp salt, then rub in 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee thoroughly until the flour clumps when pressed.
Knead in the cooled dal masala with just enough water to make a stiff, rich dough; cover and rest 25 minutes.
Divide into 14 balls and roll each into a 3.5-inch disc about 3-4 mm thick, keeping them plump like the halwai originals.

Heat 3 cups Anveshan Groundnut Oil to about 180C and fry each puri, pressing until it puffs, then turning and frying slowly until deep golden and crackly, about 50 seconds each as the ghee-rich dough browns gradually.
Drain thoroughly and serve these rich bedmi puris hot from the kadhai.
tips: The extra ghee moyan is the secret to the flaky halwai crunch, so do not skimp on rubbing it in.
Fry a little slower than usual; the rich dough browns fast and can darken before the centre cooks.
A pinch of semolina in the dough adds an extra crispness that survives the ride home from the sweet shop.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve the temple-town feast way with spiced kaddu ki sabzi, aloo curry and a scoop of hot boondi or jalebi alongside.

variations.name: Bihari Sattu Bedmi Puri
variations.description: An eastern twist that trades ground dal for nutty roasted-gram sattu, seasoned Bihar-style with ajwain, garlic and pungent mustard oil. The sattu keeps the puri crackly and deeply savoury with a distinctive toasty aroma, no soaking or grinding required. A quicker, protein-rich bedmi that carries the flavours of a Patna kitchen.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: A hearty base that binds the dry sattu filling into a firm, fryable dough

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sattu
ingredients.note: Roasted gram sattu replaces soaked dal, giving the puri a nutty, savoury crackle with no grinding

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Pungent wood-pressed mustard oil for frying, with a spoon seasoning the sattu

steps: Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil until it just smokes, lower the flame, and splutter 3/4 tsp ajwain and 1/2 tsp kalonji for 20 seconds, then take off the heat and cool.

Mix 3/4 cup Anveshan Sattu with 4 minced garlic cloves, 2 chopped green chillies, 1/2 tsp red chilli powder, 1/2 tsp salt and the cooled tempered oil, rubbing it together until evenly seasoned and just moist.
Combine the seasoned sattu with 2 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta and 1/2 tsp salt, then knead with about 1/2 cup warm water into a stiff, firm dough; cover and rest 15 minutes.
Divide the dough into 14 balls and roll each into a 3.5-inch disc about 3 mm thick, keeping them slightly thick like a bedmi puri.
Heat 3 cups Anveshan Mustard Oil to about 185C, until it stops smoking and a dough scrap rises briskly.
Fry each puri, pressing under the oil until it puffs, then turning to fry both sides to a deep golden and crunchy finish, about 45 seconds.
Drain well and serve the sattu bedmi puris hot, their nutty gram aroma at its peak.
tips: Always temper the ajwain and kalonji in hot mustard oil first; raw seeds in the sattu taste harsh.
Keep the sattu mix just moist, not wet, so the dough stays firm enough to puff.
Let the mustard oil reach smoking point once and cool slightly before frying to mellow its raw pungency.
variations.servingSuggestion: Pair the Bihari way with aloo bharta, a green chilli-garlic chutney and a spoon of mango achaar.

variations.name: Classic Malabar Parotta
variations.description: Kerala's legendary flaky flatbread, built from a long-rested maida dough that is oiled, stretched wafer-thin, coiled into a spiral and rolled out so it bakes into countless shattering layers. The magic is in the resting and the stretching, which develop the ropey strands that pull apart like ribbons. Crisp outside and soft within, it is the beloved partner to Kerala's coconut curries.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: The authentic Kerala fat, used to coat and stretch the dough for its layers and to shallow-fry the parotta crisp

steps: Combine 3 cups maida, 1 tsp sugar and 1 tsp salt, then add 0.5 cups milk and knead in about 0.75 cups warm water for 10 minutes into a very soft, elastic dough.
Rub the dough all over with 1 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil, cover, and rest it at least 2 hours (or the 40 minutes minimum) so the gluten relaxes fully.
Divide into 6 balls, roll one out paper-thin on an oiled surface, brushing the sheet with Anveshan Coconut Oil, then pleat it into a long ribbon and coil it into a tight spiral.
Press the spiral flat, rest it 5 minutes, then roll it gently into a 7-inch round without crushing the coils.
Cook on a medium-hot tava with 0.5 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil per side, pressing lightly, until golden-brown crisp patches form, about 2 minutes a side.
While hot, clap the parotta between your palms to loosen and fluff the layers, then repeat with the rest of the dough.
tips: The long rest is everything; under-rested dough will not stretch thin enough to form the signature layers.
Stretch the sheet until you can see the surface through it, oiling generously so it does not tear.
Clapping or crushing the hot parotta between your hands is what separates the flaky ribbons.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with a Kerala vegetable stew or a spicy kadala (black chana) curry, tearing the parotta to scoop the coconut gravy.

variations.name: Wheat Malabar Parotta
variations.description: A wholesome version that builds the layered parotta from nutty Anveshan khapli atta instead of refined flour, proving the flaky wonder can be made without maida. Curd and a generous rest keep the wholewheat dough supple enough to stretch and coil. The layers are a touch less airy but the flavour is richer and it sits lighter afterward.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: Nutty ancient-wheat flour replaces maida entirely, its fine gluten still stretching into flaky layers

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Brushed between the stretched layers and used to fry the parotta, enriching the wholewheat crumb

steps: Mix 3 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with 1 tsp sugar and 1 tsp salt, then add 0.3 cups curd and knead in about 0.9 cups warm water for 10 minutes into a soft, stretchy dough.
Rub the dough with 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, cover, and rest it at least 1 hour so the wholewheat gluten relaxes.
Roll a ball as thin as possible on a greased surface, brush it with melted Anveshan Ghee, pleat it into a ribbon, and coil it into a spiral.
Flatten the coil, rest 5 minutes, then roll gently into a 7-inch round, keeping the layers intact.
Cook on a medium-hot tava with 0.5 tbsp Anveshan Ghee per side until golden and crisp, about 2-3 minutes a side.
Crush the hot parotta between your palms to open the layers and repeat with the remaining dough.
tips: Wholewheat dough tears more readily, so stretch it slowly and keep the surface well oiled.
Curd tenderises the bran and is what lets this dough coil like a maida parotta; do not skip it.
Rest a little longer than you would for maida, as wholewheat needs extra time to become stretchy.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a Kerala-style veg kurma or a green peas masala for a hearty, wholesome meal.

variations.name: Kothu Parotta
variations.description: The riotous Tamil street-food finale where day-old parottas are shredded and stir-fried on a griddle with onion, tomato, egg-free veg and a punchy salna until every strand soaks up the masala. The rhythmic clang of metal spatulas chopping the parotta is the sound of every Tamil Nadu night market. Spicy, tangy and deeply savoury, it turns leftover parotta into a meal in its own right.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: The South Indian griddle fat, used to fry the masala and toss the shredded parotta until it crackles

steps: Tear or chop 4 cooked parottas into small shreds and set aside; day-old parottas shred best.
Heat 4 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil on a wide tava on medium-high, add 1 sprig curry leaves and 2 chopped onions, and fry until golden, about 5 minutes.
Add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and 2 slit green chillies, fry 1 minute, then stir in 1 chopped tomato and 1 cup diced capsicum and carrot and cook until soft, about 4 minutes.
Sprinkle in 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp garam masala and 0.75 tsp salt, then pour in 0.5 cups salna and simmer 2 minutes.
Add the shredded parotta and toss vigorously, chopping with the spatula, until every strand is coated and the mix is dry and sizzling, about 4 minutes.
Finish with 3 tbsp coriander, toss once more, and serve hot straight off the griddle.
tips: Use parottas from the day before; fresh soft ones turn mushy when tossed with the gravy.
Keep the flame high and chop constantly so the parotta strands crisp and absorb the masala without going soggy.
Add the salna a little at a time; the kothu should be moist and coated, never wet or soupy.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with extra salna on the side and a wedge of lemon, plus a bowl of raita to cool the spice.

variations.name: Classic Dry Aloo Gobi Matar
variations.description: The everyday North Indian dry sabzi of potatoes, cauliflower and green peas cooked together with cumin, turmeric and a simple masala until tender and lightly browned. Homely and fuss-free, it stays dry and glossy with each vegetable holding its shape, ready to roll into a hot roti.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.note: cut into 2 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Cauliflower
ingredients.note: cut into bite-sized florets

ingredients.name: Green peas
ingredients.note: fresh or thawed

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed oil browns the vegetables cleanly for a dry sabzi

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.note: grated

ingredients.name: Green chillies
ingredients.note: slit

steps: Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a kadai on medium heat, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds and 1/4 tsp asafoetida for 30 seconds, then add the grated ginger and 2 slit green chillies for 30 seconds.
Add the potato cubes and cauliflower florets, sprinkle 1/2 tsp turmeric powder, and toss for 3-4 minutes until the vegetables are coated and starting to brown at the edges.
Stir in 3/4 tsp red chilli powder, 1.5 tsp coriander powder and 1 tsp salt, then cover and cook on low heat for 10 minutes, stirring once, until the potatoes are half done.
Add 3/4 cup green peas, stir gently, cover again, and cook for another 8-10 minutes until all three vegetables are tender but still holding their shape.
Uncover, raise the heat to medium and stir-fry for 3 minutes to drive off any moisture so the sabzi turns dry and lightly caramelised.
