ingredients.note: A light warm drizzle of wood-pressed groundnut oil coats the chillies and carries the roasted spices

steps: Wash and dry 150 g green chillies and cut into small 0.5-inch pieces.
Dry-roast 1 tbsp cumin and 0.5 tsp carom seeds on low flame for 1 minute until fragrant, cool, and grind coarse.
Toss the chilli pieces with the ground spices, 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp black salt and 1.5 tbsp salt.
Warm 3 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil until it just shimmers, cool for a minute, and pour it over the chillies.
Add 6 tbsp lemon juice and mix well so every piece is coated and glossy.
Rest 3-4 hours at room temperature before serving; it keeps a week refrigerated.
tips: The generous lemon juice does the softening here, so give it a few hours to work before serving.
Carom seeds add a warm, digestive note that pairs especially well with the raw chilli heat.
Make it in small batches since, without long curing, it is meant to be eaten fresh within days.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve fresh with hot theplas, methi paratha or a simple bowl of dal-rice.

variations.name: Classic Haldi Doodh
variations.description: The age-old Indian golden milk given as medicine at home: warm milk simmered with turmeric, cracked black pepper and a spoon of Anveshan Ghee to carry the curcumin, then sweetened with Anveshan Honey off the heat. Soothing and anti-inflammatory, it is the drink pressed on anyone with a cough, a cold or aching joints.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A little ghee helps the body absorb turmeric's fat-soluble curcumin, the reason it belongs here

ingredients.name: Anveshan Honey
ingredients.note: Stirred in off the heat, raw honey sweetens the milk and soothes a scratchy throat

steps: Heat 0.5 tsp Anveshan Ghee in a small pan on low and stir in 0.75 tsp turmeric powder, toasting it for 20 seconds until it smells earthy.
Pour in 2 cups full-fat milk and add 2 lightly crushed cardamom pods, whisking so no turmeric lumps remain.
Bring the milk to a gentle boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 4-5 minutes so the turmeric infuses fully.
Add 0.25 tsp black pepper powder, which activates the turmeric, and simmer one more minute.
Take the pan off the heat and let it cool for a minute, then stir in 2 tsp Anveshan Honey so its enzymes are not destroyed by boiling.
Strain out the cardamom and pour into 2 cups; serve steaming hot.
tips: The pinch of black pepper is not optional; it multiplies the absorption of curcumin many times over.
Never boil honey into the milk; add it only once the drink has cooled slightly off the flame.
For a stronger remedy during a cold, add a small crushed piece of fresh ginger while it simmers.
variations.servingSuggestion: Drink hot just before bed to ease into sleep, or serve to anyone fighting a cold or sore throat; a light biscuit on the side is all it needs.

variations.name: Turmeric Golden Latte
variations.description: A frothy cafe-style golden latte built on Anveshan Turmeric Latte Mix, whisked into steamed milk until foamy and finished with a dusting of cinnamon. Café-smooth and ready in minutes, it delivers the wellness of haldi doodh in a modern, Instagram-worthy cup.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Turmeric Latte Mix
ingredients.note: The pre-blended latte mix brings turmeric, spices and warmth together for an instant frothy golden latte

ingredients.name: Anveshan Honey
ingredients.note: A touch of honey rounds out the spice blend without overpowering the latte

steps: Warm 2 cups full-fat milk in a saucepan on medium heat until it is steaming but not yet boiling.
Whisk in 3 tsp Anveshan Turmeric Latte Mix and 0.25 tsp vanilla extract until the mix dissolves smoothly.
Simmer gently for 2-3 minutes so the spices bloom into the milk, whisking continuously.
Take the pan off the heat, let it cool for a minute, then stir in 2 tsp Anveshan Honey.
Froth the latte with a handheld frother or by whisking briskly for 30 seconds until a light foam forms on top.
Pour into 2 cups and finish with a dusting of 0.25 tsp cinnamon powder over the foam.
tips: Do not let the milk come to a rolling boil, or you lose the microfoam that makes it latte-like.
For a plant-based latte, swap in oat or almond milk; both froth well with the mix.
Chill any leftover and shake over ice the next day for a golden iced latte.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve mid-afternoon in a wide cup as a caffeine-free pick-me-up, dusted with cinnamon and a few edible dried rose petals for a cafe look.

variations.name: Fresh Turmeric-Ginger Kadha Doodh
variations.description: A potent immunity version simmered with fresh turmeric and ginger roots rather than powders, boiled kadha-style with tulsi and black pepper before being strained into milk and sweetened with Anveshan Jaggery Powder. Sharper, more medicinal and deeply warming, it is the version reached for at the first sign of the flu.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: Jaggery sweetens the sharp kadha naturally and adds its own warming, iron-rich character

steps: Bring 0.5 cup water to a boil in a small pan and add 1 inch grated fresh turmeric, 1 inch grated ginger and 4 crushed peppercorns.
Drop in 6 tulsi leaves and 2 crushed cardamom pods and boil this kadha for 3-4 minutes until the water turns deep yellow and aromatic.
Pour in 2 cups full-fat milk and bring back to a gentle boil, watching so it does not overflow.
Lower the heat and simmer for 4-5 minutes so the fresh roots infuse the milk with colour and pungency.
Strain out the roots and leaves, then let the milk cool for a minute and stir in 2 tsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder until dissolved.
Serve hot in 2 cups, best sipped slowly while it is warm.
tips: Fresh turmeric stains everything it touches, so grate it on a board you do not mind yellowing and rinse tools at once.
Add the jaggery off the heat; dropped into boiling milk it can occasionally cause the milk to split.
Double the ginger and add a clove for a fiercer version when a cold has truly set in.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve at the first sniffle before bed, or offer a small cup on damp monsoon evenings; a spoon of it soothes a sore throat between meals.

variations.name: Vegan Coconut Golden Milk
variations.description: A dairy-free golden milk simmered in creamy coconut milk with turmeric, cinnamon and black pepper, finished with a little Anveshan Coconut Oil to help the body absorb the curcumin. Silky, tropical and soothing, it lets those avoiding dairy enjoy the same anti-inflammatory ritual.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: Cold-pressed coconut oil provides the good fat that makes turmeric's curcumin absorbable

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: Jaggery keeps this vegan golden milk unrefined and balances the coconut's richness

steps: Heat 0.5 tsp Anveshan Coconut Oil in a small pan on low and stir in 0.75 tsp turmeric, toasting for 15 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in 1.5 cups coconut milk and 0.5 cup water, whisking to loosen the coconut milk and dissolve the turmeric.
Add 0.25 tsp cinnamon, 0.25 tsp ground ginger and 0.25 tsp black pepper and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer on low for 4-5 minutes, whisking often, so the spices infuse without the coconut milk splitting.
Take off the heat, cool for a minute, and stir in 2 tsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder until fully dissolved.
Whisk briskly for a light froth and pour into 2 cups to serve hot.
tips: Keep the heat low and never let coconut milk boil hard, or it separates into grainy curds.
Use full-fat coconut milk for a creamy latte; carton coconut drink leaves it thin.
Add a squeeze of lemon at the end for a brighter, more warming winter version.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm to vegan guests as an evening wind-down drink, or chill and blend with a frozen banana for a golden turmeric smoothie.

variations.name: Classic Kaju Katli
variations.description: Kaju katli is the beloved diamond-cut cashew fudge, made by cooking finely ground cashews with a one-string sugar syrup until it forms a smooth, pliable dough that is rolled paper-thin. Melt-in-the-mouth and silver-topped, it is India's most-gifted festive mithai.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: cooked to a one-string syrup that binds the cashew powder into a smooth, sliceable katli

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: greases the surface and hands so the cashew dough rolls thin without sticking

steps: Grind 2 cups cashews to a fine, dry powder in short pulses, taking care not to let them turn oily, then sieve for an even texture.
Boil 0.75 cup Anveshan Khandsari with 0.3 cup water over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes to a sticky one-string syrup.
Lower the heat, stir in the cashew powder and 0.25 tsp cardamom, and cook 5 to 6 minutes, stirring, until it forms a soft, glossy dough that leaves the pan.
Turn the warm dough onto a greased sheet, rub 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee on your palms, and knead briefly until smooth and pliable.
Roll the dough between two greased sheets to an even 3-millimetre thickness and press 2 sheets of silver leaf over the top.
Cool for 15 minutes, then cut into the traditional diamonds with a sharp knife and lift them off once set.
tips: Pulse the cashews in short bursts and keep them cool; over-grinding releases oil and turns the powder into paste.
Judge the one-string syrup carefully, as too thin leaves a sticky katli and too thick makes it crack when rolled.
Knead the dough while still warm; once cold it stiffens and will not roll thin or smooth.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve at room temperature as the classic Diwali gift sweet, the silver-topped diamonds arranged in a decorative mithai box.

variations.name: Mawa Kaju Barfi
variations.description: The milk-rich sweet-shop version binds the cashew powder with khoya so it sets thicker and softer, closer to a classic milk barfi than the thin katli. Denser and creamier, it is the kaju barfi sold in generous cubes at festive counters.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: cooked to a syrup that sweetens the mawa and cashew into a firm milk barfi

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the khoya smooth and keeps the barfi from sticking as it sets

steps: Grind 1.5 cups cashews to a fine, dry powder in short pulses and sieve; grate 1 cup khoya and keep ready.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a heavy pan and roast the grated khoya over low heat for 4 to 5 minutes until it softens and smells rich, then set aside.
Boil 0.75 cup Anveshan Khandsari with 0.25 cup water for 4 minutes to a sticky one-string syrup.
Lower the heat, stir in the cashew powder and roasted khoya, and cook 6 to 7 minutes until the mixture thickens and pulls together into a soft mass.
Add 0.5 tsp cardamom, spread the mixture in a greased tray, and smooth it to an even 1-centimetre slab.
Press sliced pistachios over the top, cool for 20 minutes, and cut into neat cubes once set.
tips: Roast the khoya until smooth before mixing, or the barfi will carry grainy milky lumps.
This barfi is softer than katli, so let the slab cool fully before cutting for clean edges.
Fresh, moist khoya gives the best set; if using dry khoya, add a splash of milk while roasting.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve at room temperature in generous cubes, the pistachio-topped barfi arranged on a festive platter.

variations.name: Kesar Kaju Barfi
variations.description: A regal saffron cashew barfi where bloomed saffron tints the fudge a warm gold and lends a heady floral aroma, studded with slivered pistachios. Softer and more fragrant than plain katli, it is the celebration barfi for weddings and Diwali gifting.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: cooked to a one-string syrup that binds the cashew into a soft saffron barfi

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: bloomed in warm milk to tint the barfi gold and lend its heady floral aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: greases the surface so the saffron dough rolls out smooth and non-sticky

steps: Soak 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk and set aside to bloom while you grind 2 cups cashews to a fine, dry powder.
Boil 0.75 cup Anveshan Khandsari with 0.25 cup water for 4 minutes to a sticky one-string syrup.
Lower the heat, stir in the cashew powder, the bloomed saffron milk and 0.25 tsp cardamom, and cook 5 to 6 minutes until it forms a soft golden dough.
Turn the warm dough onto a greased sheet, rub 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee on your palms, and knead until smooth and pliable.
Roll or press the dough to an even 5-millimetre slab and scatter slivered pistachios over the surface, pressing them in gently.
Cool for 15 minutes, then cut into diamonds and lift them off once set.
tips: Bloom the saffron in warm milk first so the colour disperses evenly instead of streaking the barfi.
The saffron milk adds moisture, so cook a minute longer until the dough leaves the pan cleanly.
Toast the pistachio slivers lightly for a deeper flavour and a prettier green against the gold.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve at room temperature as a wedding or Diwali gift sweet, the golden pistachio-studded diamonds in a silk-lined box.

variations.name: Chocolate Kaju Barfi
variations.description: A modern two-toned barfi that layers plain cashew fudge over a cocoa-spiked cashew layer for a striking dark-and-cream mithai. Rich with cocoa yet still melt-in-the-mouth, it is a fusion favourite that delights children at festive time.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: cooked to a one-string syrup that binds both cashew layers into a smooth barfi

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: greases the sheets and helps the cocoa blend smoothly into the cashew dough

steps: Grind 2 cups cashews to a fine, dry powder in short pulses and sieve for an even texture.
Boil 0.75 cup Anveshan Khandsari with 0.3 cup water for 4 to 5 minutes to a sticky one-string syrup.
Lower the heat, stir in the cashew powder and 0.25 tsp cardamom, and cook 5 minutes until it forms a soft dough, then divide it into two portions.
Knead 2 tbsp cocoa powder and 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee into one portion until evenly dark, keeping the other portion plain.
Roll the cocoa portion into a slab on a greased sheet, lay the rolled plain portion over it, and press the two layers together to bond.
Scatter chopped pistachios on top, cool for 15 minutes, and cut into neat squares or diamonds once set.
tips: Sift the cocoa before kneading so it blends in without leaving bitter dry pockets.
Roll both layers to the same size and press firmly so they do not separate when cut.
Work quickly while the dough is warm, as the two layers bond best before they cool and stiffen.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve at room temperature as a modern festive treat, the two-toned squares arranged to show off the dark-and-cream layers.

variations.name: Classic Kesar Pista Milk
variations.description: A luxurious saffron-and-pistachio milk simmered until fragrant and pale gold, studded with ground pistachios and perfumed with cardamom. Warming and restorative, it is the drink of festive nights and winter evenings, rich enough to feel like a treat yet wholesome to the last sip.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: pure Kashmiri saffron steeped in warm milk gives this drink its glowing gold colour and floral aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari Sugar
ingredients.note: khandsari sweetens the milk cleanly without masking the delicate saffron and pistachio flavours

steps: Steep 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk and set aside so its colour and scent bloom fully.
Blanch 0.33 cup pistachios in hot water for 5 minutes, peel them, and grind most of them into a fine paste with a splash of milk, reserving a few for garnish.
Bring 4 cups full-fat milk to a gentle boil in a heavy pan, then lower the heat and simmer for 8 minutes, stirring, until it reduces slightly and thickens.
Whisk in the pistachio paste and simmer for another 3 minutes until the milk turns pale green-gold and creamy.
Lower the heat and stir in 5 tbsp Anveshan Khandsari Sugar, the saffron milk and 0.5 tsp cardamom powder, simmering just until the sugar dissolves.
Serve hot in cups, or chill and serve cold, garnished with the reserved chopped pistachios and slivered almonds.
tips: Simmer and stir the milk regularly so it reduces evenly and does not catch and scorch at the base.
Blanch and peel the pistachios for the cleanest colour and smoothest paste; skins leave a dull, gritty finish.
Grind the pistachios fine so the milk is silky, and reserve a few chopped for a textured garnish.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve steaming hot on winter nights or icy cold in summer, garnished with pistachio and saffron, as a festive after-dinner drink.

variations.name: Kesar Pista Thandai Milk
variations.description: A cooling summer take that folds a fragrant thandai spice blend of fennel, peppercorn and poppy seeds into the saffron-pistachio milk. More aromatic and complex than the plain version, it is served well chilled as a festive, digestion-friendly cooler.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: saffron steeped in warm milk anchors the thandai spices with its floral gold colour and aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Honey
ingredients.note: raw honey stirred into the cooled spiced milk keeps this thandai version light and floral

steps: Steep 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk and set aside to bloom.
Soak 0.25 cup pistachios, 1 tbsp fennel seeds, 5 white peppercorns and 1 tsp poppy seeds together in warm water for 20 minutes, then peel the pistachios.
Drain and grind the soaked nuts and spices with a little milk into a fine paste, then strain through muslin for a smooth base.
Bring 4 cups milk to a boil, lower the heat, whisk in the strained spice-pistachio milk and simmer for 4 minutes until fragrant, then cool completely.
Once cooled, stir in the saffron milk, 0.5 tsp cardamom powder, 1 tsp rose water and 5 tbsp Anveshan Honey until the honey dissolves.
Chill thoroughly, then serve over 1 cup ice cubes garnished with a few pistachio slivers.
tips: Strain the ground spice paste through muslin so no gritty poppy or fennel bits remain in the smooth milk.
Cool the milk before adding honey so its aroma and benefits stay intact rather than being boiled off.
Make the spiced milk a day ahead — the thandai flavours deepen beautifully overnight in the fridge.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve well chilled over ice with a pistachio garnish, a fragrant festive cooler for Holi, Ram Navami or hot summer evenings.

variations.name: Kesar Pista Badam Milk
variations.description: An extra-rich version enriched with almond paste alongside the pistachios, making a thick, nourishing badam-pista milk fit for growing children and convalescents. Deeply creamy and warming, it is the ultimate bedtime tonic, thickened naturally by the ground nuts rather than any cornflour.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: saffron gives the enriched nut milk its signature amber glow and ties the almond and pistachio together

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: unrefined jaggery adds mineral-rich sweetness and a caramel depth that suits this nourishing nut-thick milk

steps: Steep 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk and set aside to bloom.
Soak 15 almonds and 0.25 cup pistachios in warm water for 20 minutes, peel both, and grind them into a fine paste with a splash of milk, reserving a spoon of chopped nuts for garnish.
Bring 4 cups full-fat milk to a boil in a heavy pan, then simmer on low for 8 minutes, stirring often, until slightly reduced.
Whisk in the almond-pistachio paste and simmer for 5 minutes more until the milk is thick, creamy and pale gold.
Lower the heat and stir in 4 tbsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder off the boil so the milk does not split, along with the saffron milk, 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and 0.125 tsp nutmeg powder.
Simmer gently for 1 minute until everything blends, then serve hot topped with the reserved chopped nuts.
tips: Add the jaggery only after the milk is off the boil; poured into boiling milk it can cause curdling.
The ground almonds thicken the milk naturally, so there is no need for cornflour or any other thickener.
For the smoothest drink, strain the milk once after adding the nut paste if you prefer it without any texture.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot in small cups as a rich bedtime tonic or a strengthening winter drink, garnished with chopped almonds and pistachios.

variations.name: Vegan Kesar Pista Almond Milk
variations.description: A dairy-free rendition where homemade almond milk carries the saffron and pistachio, staying light yet fragrant and completely plant-based. Subtly sweet and delicately golden, it proves this festive classic works beautifully without any dairy.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: saffron infused into warm almond milk gives this dairy-free version its floral aroma and golden hue

ingredients.name: Anveshan Honey
ingredients.note: raw honey sweetens the almond milk gently and is stirred in warm to preserve its delicate flavour

steps: Soak 30 almonds overnight or in warm water for 30 minutes, then peel them for a smooth, white milk.
Blend the peeled almonds with 4 cups water until very fine, then strain through a nut-milk bag to yield smooth almond milk.
Steep 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp of the warm almond milk and set aside to bloom.
Blanch and peel 0.33 cup pistachios, then grind most into a fine paste with a little almond milk, keeping a few aside for garnish.
Warm the almond milk gently with the pistachio paste and 0.5 tsp cardamom powder for 4 minutes on low, stirring, until fragrant, then take it off the heat.
Stir in the saffron milk and 4 tbsp Anveshan Honey once the milk is warm not boiling, then serve warm or chilled, garnished with reserved pistachios.
tips: Strain the almond milk well for a smooth drink and save the pulp to stir into porridge or bake into cookies.
Keep the milk from boiling once the pistachio paste is in, as high heat can make homemade almond milk taste bitter.
Use a store-bought unsweetened almond milk as a shortcut and start from the saffron-steeping step.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm or chilled in glasses topped with pistachio slivers, a plant-based festive drink for those avoiding dairy.

variations.name: Classic Langarwali Dal
variations.description: The humble, soul-warming dal served in gurudwara langars, made from whole black urad and chana dal simmered until creamy and finished with a simple ghee-cumin-ginger tadka. There is no cream or fuss here, just slow-cooked lentils and pure ghee, yet it tastes richer than dals twice its complexity. This is comfort in a bowl.

ingredients.name: Whole black urad (sabut urad)
ingredients.note: soaked 4 hours

ingredients.name: Chana dal
ingredients.note: soaked 4 hours

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee is the only richness in langar dal, so its flavour carries the whole bowl

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.note: finely chopped

ingredients.name: Tomato
ingredients.note: finely chopped

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.note: half grated, half julienned

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.note: finely chopped

ingredients.name: Green chillies
ingredients.note: slit

ingredients.name: Fresh coriander leaves
ingredients.note: chopped

steps: Pressure-cook the soaked urad and chana dals with 3.5 cups water, 1/2 tsp turmeric, the grated ginger and 1 tsp salt for 6-7 whistles until the urad is completely soft and creamy.
Open the cooker once the pressure settles and whisk the dal lightly so it turns thick and holds together, adding a little hot water if it is too stiff.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a small pan on medium heat and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds for 30 seconds.
Add 6 chopped garlic cloves, the julienned ginger and 2 slit green chillies and fry for a minute until the garlic turns pale gold.
Add the chopped onion and cook for 4-5 minutes until golden, then add the chopped tomato and 1 tsp red chilli powder and cook 3-4 minutes until the tomato collapses and the ghee separates.
Pour this tadka into the dal with the remaining 1/4 tsp salt, and simmer together on low heat for 8-10 minutes so the dal deepens in flavour.
Finish with 3 tbsp chopped coriander and serve hot with a last drizzle of ghee.
tips: The secret to langar dal is slow cooking; the longer the whole urad simmers, the creamier and more comforting it becomes.
Keep the spicing minimal and let the ghee and lentils speak, the way it is made in gurudwara kitchens.
A spoon of raw ghee stirred in just before serving lifts the whole dal beautifully.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with tandoori roti or steamed rice and a simple onion-cucumber salad, langar-style.

variations.name: Slow-Simmered Smoky Langar Dal
variations.description: The old-fashioned way where the whole urad simmers for hours over a low flame until impossibly creamy, then takes on a gentle charcoal smokiness through the dhungar method. Deeper and more soulful than the quick version, this is the dal that rewards patience with an almost buttery body from the lentils alone.

ingredients.name: Whole black urad (sabut urad)
ingredients.note: soaked overnight

ingredients.name: Chana dal
ingredients.note: soaked overnight

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: ghee both cooks the tadka and is drizzled on the coal for the dhungar smoke

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.note: grated

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.note: crushed

ingredients.name: Green chillies
ingredients.note: slit

ingredients.name: Charcoal
ingredients.note: for the dhungar smoking

steps: Pressure-cook the overnight-soaked urad and chana with 4 cups water, 1/2 tsp turmeric, the grated ginger, 1 bay leaf and 1 tsp salt for 8-9 whistles until the lentils begin to break down.
Transfer the dal to a heavy pot and simmer it uncovered on the lowest flame for 45-60 minutes, stirring every few minutes and topping up with hot water, until it turns thick and creamy on its own.

Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a small pan on medium heat, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds, add 8 crushed garlic cloves and 2 slit green chillies, and fry until deep golden, then stir in 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder off the heat.
Pour this tadka into the simmering dal with the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and stir well.
Heat the charcoal on a flame until glowing red, set it in a small steel bowl placed on top of the dal, and drizzle the remaining 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee over it so it smokes.
Cover the pot tightly and let the dhungar smoke infuse for 4-5 minutes, then remove the coal and bowl.
Stir the smoky dal once and serve hot.
tips: Long, slow simmering is what gives this dal its buttery body, so resist the urge to rush it with cream.
Keep a kettle of hot water beside the pot to loosen the dal as it thickens during the long cook.
Do not leave the charcoal in for more than five minutes, or the smoke turns bitter instead of gently woody.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with jeera rice or a stack of hot phulkas, with sliced onion and green chilli on the side.

variations.name: Satvik No-Onion Langar Dal
variations.description: The purest temple-kitchen rendering, cooked without onion or garlic and leaning on ginger, green chilli and a generous pinch of asafoetida bloomed in ghee. Clean, gentle and deeply comforting, it is the dal offered as prasad and eaten on fasting days, proof that langar dal needs no aromatics to satisfy.

ingredients.name: Whole black urad (sabut urad)
ingredients.note: soaked 4 hours

ingredients.name: Chana dal
ingredients.note: soaked 4 hours

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: the only fat in this pure-veg dal, so its bilona flavour has to carry the tempering

ingredients.name: Asafoetida
ingredients.note: a generous pinch stands in for the missing garlic

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.note: grated

ingredients.name: Green chillies
ingredients.note: slit

ingredients.name: Tomato
ingredients.note: finely chopped

ingredients.name: Fresh coriander leaves
ingredients.note: chopped

steps: Pressure-cook the soaked urad and chana dals with 3.5 cups water, 1/2 tsp turmeric, half the grated ginger and 1 tsp salt for 6-7 whistles until soft and creamy, then whisk lightly.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pan on medium heat and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds for 30 seconds.
Lower the heat and add 1/2 tsp asafoetida, the remaining grated ginger and 3 slit green chillies, frying for about a minute until fragrant and the kitchen fills with hing.
Add the chopped tomato and 1.5 tsp coriander powder and cook for 4-5 minutes until the tomato collapses and the ghee separates.
Pour this tempering into the dal with the remaining 1/4 tsp salt, and simmer together on low heat for 8-10 minutes.
Stir in 1/2 tsp garam masala and mash a little of the dal for a homely, creamy texture.
Finish with 3 tbsp chopped coriander and serve warm.
tips: Because there is no onion or garlic, bloom a genuinely generous half-teaspoon of asafoetida in the ghee to carry the savoury base.
This dal suits a fasting-friendly or satvik thali and reheats beautifully with just a splash of hot water.
Grate rather than chop the ginger so it melts into the dal and perfumes every spoonful.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve over plain steamed rice or with soft phulkas and a spoon of ghee for a satvik meal.

variations.name: Amritsari Butter Langar Dal
variations.description: A plusher Amritsar-style take where the langar dal is enriched with a tomato-heavy masala, a finish of butter and cream, and a fragrant kasuri methi tadka. It bridges the humble langar dal and the restaurant dal makhani, staying rooted in whole urad but dialling up the indulgence for a special-occasion bowl.

ingredients.name: Whole black urad (sabut urad)
ingredients.note: soaked overnight

ingredients.name: Chana dal
ingredients.note: soaked overnight

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: ghee builds the tadka while butter and cream finish this richer langar dal

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.note: finely chopped

ingredients.name: Tomato
ingredients.note: pureed

ingredients.name: Kasuri methi (dried fenugreek)
ingredients.note: crushed

steps: Pressure-cook the overnight-soaked urad and chana with 4 cups water, 1/2 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt for 7-8 whistles until very soft, then mash a portion so the dal turns thick.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a kadai on medium heat, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds, then add the chopped onions and fry for 6-7 minutes until golden.
Add 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste for a minute, then the tomato puree with 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, and cook for 7 minutes until thick and glossy.
Pour the cooked dal into the masala with 1 cup hot water and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt, and simmer on low heat for 12-15 minutes, stirring so it turns velvety.
Stir in 2 tbsp butter and 3 tbsp cream off the boil, letting them melt into the dal without splitting.
Crush 1 tbsp kasuri methi between your palms and add it with 1/2 tsp garam masala, simmering 3 more minutes.
Serve hot with a swirl of cream and a knob of butter on top.
tips: Mash some of the whole urad while it is hot to release its starch, which gives this richer dal its creamy body.
Add butter and cream only after taking the dal off the boil so the finish stays silky.
This dal, like dal makhani, tastes even better the next day once the flavours have settled.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with butter naan or laccha paratha and a side of pickled onions for a festive spread.

variations.name: Classic Mango Lassi
variations.description: Classic Mango Lassi blends ripe sweet mango pulp with thick yogurt and a hint of cardamom into a smooth, sunshine-yellow drink. Creamy, fruity and gently tangy, it is the beloved summer cooler served in every North Indian home and restaurant when mangoes are in season.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Honey
ingredients.note: adjusts the sweetness naturally depending on how ripe the mangoes are

steps: Peel 2 large ripe mangoes and chop the flesh, discarding the stones, to get about 1.5 cups of pulp.
Blend the mango with 2 cups fresh yogurt and 0.5 cup chilled milk for a minute until completely smooth.
Add 3 tbsp Anveshan Honey and 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and blend again to combine.
Drop in the 6 ice cubes and blend briefly until the lassi is cold and frothy.
Pour into four glasses, leaving a little froth on top of each.
Garnish with chopped pistachios and serve immediately while chilled.
tips: Use fragrant, fully ripe mangoes like Alphonso or Kesar for the best flavour.
Adjust honey to taste since ripe mangoes vary widely in sweetness.
Chill the mango and yogurt beforehand so you need less ice and a thicker lassi.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve as a cooling drink with a spicy meal or as a light dessert on a summer afternoon.

variations.name: Alphonso Malai Lassi
variations.description: A luxurious version made only with Alphonso pulp and enriched with fresh cream and a touch of ghee-fried cashew for a dessert-thick, saffron-hued lassi. Denser and richer than the everyday drink, it showcases the king of mangoes at its most decadent.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: a clean sweetener that lets the Alphonso flavour shine through

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: fries the cashews to a golden aroma that deepens the richness

steps: Fry 2 tbsp cashews in 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee over low heat until golden, then cool and set a few aside for garnish.
Blend 2 cups Alphonso mango pulp with 1.5 cups hung curd and 0.5 cup fresh cream until thick and smooth.
Add 3 tbsp Anveshan Khandsari, most of the fried cashews and 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and blend again.
Blend in the 5 ice cubes briefly so the lassi stays thick rather than watery.
Pour the thick, rich lassi into four chilled glasses, dividing it evenly.
Top each with the reserved fried cashews and serve chilled with a spoon.
tips: Hung curd and cream keep this lassi spoonably thick, so skip extra water.
Use pure Alphonso pulp with no added water for the deepest mango flavour.
Frying the cashews in ghee adds a subtle richness worth the extra minute.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve the thick golden lassi in chilled glasses as a stand-alone summer dessert.

variations.name: Vegan Mango Coconut Lassi
variations.description: A dairy-free take that swaps yogurt for thick coconut yogurt and coconut milk, giving a tropical mango drink with a subtle coconut backdrop. Light, refreshing and fully plant-based, it is perfect for anyone avoiding dairy without losing the creamy lassi feel.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: a plant-based sweetener that adds caramel warmth to the tropical drink

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: toasts the coconut flakes for a fragrant garnish

steps: Toast 2 tbsp coconut flakes in 1 tsp Anveshan Coconut Oil over low heat until golden, then set aside.
Peel and chop 2 large ripe mangoes to get about 1.5 cups of pulp.
Blend the mango with 1.5 cups coconut yogurt and 0.75 cup coconut milk until smooth and creamy.
Add 3 tbsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder, 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and 1 tsp lime juice and blend to combine.
Blend in the 6 ice cubes briefly until the lassi is cold and frothy.
Pour into four glasses and garnish with the toasted coconut flakes before serving chilled.
tips: A squeeze of lime brightens the coconut and stops the drink tasting flat.
Use thick coconut yogurt so the lassi has enough body without dairy.
Chill the coconut milk beforehand for the coldest, creamiest result.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve as a dairy-free welcome drink at a summer gathering, garnished with toasted coconut.

variations.name: Mango Saffron Thandai Lassi
variations.description: A festive fusion that stirs a fragrant thandai nut-and-spice paste and saffron into the mango lassi for a Holi-worthy celebration drink. Spiced with fennel, pepper and rose, it layers the cool mango with warming aromatics for something genuinely special.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: bloomed in warm milk to tie the mango and thandai spices together

ingredients.name: Anveshan Honey
ingredients.note: sweetens the spiced lassi without clashing with the aromatic thandai

steps: Soak 2 tbsp almonds, 1 tsp fennel seeds, 1 tsp poppy seeds and 6 black peppercorns in water for 15 minutes, then grind to a fine thandai paste.
Bloom 0.25 tsp Anveshan Saffron in 3 tbsp warm milk for 10 minutes until golden.
Peel and chop 2 large ripe mangoes and blend with 2 cups fresh yogurt until smooth.
Add the thandai paste, saffron milk and 3 tbsp Anveshan Honey and blend until fully combined and fragrant.
Stir in 0.5 tsp rose water by hand and blend in the 6 ice cubes until cold and frothy.
Pour into four glasses and serve chilled, garnished with a few saffron strands.
tips: Grind the thandai paste very fine so the lassi stays smooth to sip.
Add rose water by hand at the end so its delicate scent is not blitzed away.
Make the thandai paste ahead and refrigerate for a quicker festive drink.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve at Holi in place of plain thandai for a fruity, spiced celebration cooler.

variations.name: Classic North Indian Mixed Vegetable Pickle
variations.description: The winter favourite achar of Punjab and the north, where carrot, cauliflower, turnip and green chilli are briefly blanched, dried, and cured in a coarse fennel-mustard masala under mustard oil. Each vegetable keeps its own crunch while soaking up the tangy spice. A jar made in peak winter carries the season's produce right through the year.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Smoked and cooled, it is the pungent preserving oil that binds the masala to the crunchy vegetables

steps: Cut 250 g carrots, 250 g cauliflower, 150 g turnip and 100 g green chillies into even bite-sized pieces.
Blanch the vegetables in boiling salted water for 2 minutes, drain, and spread on a dry cloth in the sun for 3-4 hours until surface-dry.
Dry-roast 4 tbsp fennel, 3 tbsp mustard seeds and 1 tbsp fenugreek for 2 minutes, cool, and grind coarse.
Toss the dried vegetables with the ground spices, 1 tbsp turmeric, 2 tbsp chilli powder and 4 tbsp salt until well coated.
Heat 1.5 cups Anveshan Mustard Oil until it smokes, cool completely, then mix most of it through the vegetables and pack into a dry jar.
Pour the remaining oil on top to cover, sun the jar 5-6 days shaking daily, until the vegetables soften slightly and turn tangy.
tips: Drying the blanched vegetables thoroughly is critical; any surface moisture will make the pickle spoil.
Blanch only briefly so the carrot and cauliflower keep a pleasant bite rather than going soft.
Keep the vegetables submerged under oil and use a dry spoon each time to make the jar last for months.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with hot parathas and curd, or as a crunchy tangy side to a winter dal-chawal meal.

variations.name: South Indian Vegetable Oorugai
variations.description: A tangy Tamil-style mixed vegetable oorugai finished with a mustard and curry-leaf tempering in gingelly oil, with tamarind lending its characteristic sour depth. The vegetables are cooked briefly rather than sun-cured, giving a softer, saucier pickle. Its fenugreek-forward masala and asafoetida set it clearly apart from the northern jar.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sesame Oil
ingredients.note: Gingelly oil blooms the mustard tempering and preserves this tangy southern pickle

steps: Cut 200 g carrots, 150 g beans and 1 raw mango into small pieces, and soak 2 tbsp tamarind in 0.5 cup warm water, then extract a thick pulp.
Heat 0.75 cups Anveshan Sesame Oil in a kadhai on medium flame, splutter 1 tbsp mustard seeds, add 0.5 tsp asafoetida and 2 sprigs curry leaves.
Add the vegetables with 1 tsp turmeric and 3 tbsp salt, and saute 5 minutes until they just begin to soften.
Pour in the tamarind pulp with 3 tbsp chilli powder and cook 8-10 minutes until the raw smell goes and the mixture thickens.
Stir in 1 tsp fenugreek powder, cook 2 more minutes until the oil separates, and switch off.
Cool completely and store in a dry jar; rest a day before serving so the vegetables absorb the tang.
tips: Use pre-roasted fenugreek powder added at the end so it flavours without turning bitter.
Cook until the oil separates, the reliable sign that the moisture has reduced enough for the pickle to keep.
The raw mango adds natural sourness; if it is out of season, increase the tamarind slightly instead.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with curd rice or lemon rice, or as a tangy side to idli and dosa.

variations.name: Gujarati Sweet and Sour Mixed Pickle
variations.description: A Gujarati-style mixed vegetable pickle where the crunchy veg is cooked in a jaggery syrup balanced with mild spice and a hint of tang, producing a glossy sweet-savoury relish. It has little heat and a mellow, family-friendly flavour beloved across Gujarat. The syrupy coat makes it the perfect sweet accent on a spicy thali.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: Melted into a light syrup, it gives this Gujarati pickle its signature sweet-sour glaze

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A light saute in wood-pressed groundnut oil softens the vegetables before the syrup goes in

steps: Cut 200 g carrots and 150 g cauliflower into small pieces and keep 100 g peas ready.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a pan on medium flame and saute the vegetables with 1 tsp turmeric and 2 tbsp salt for 5 minutes.
Add 1 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder with a splash of water and cook 8 minutes until it melts into a light syrup coating the veg.
Stir in 1 tbsp roasted cumin powder and 1 tbsp chilli powder and simmer 6-8 minutes until the syrup thickens and the vegetables are tender-crisp.
Switch off, cool for a few minutes, and stir in 3 tbsp lemon juice for the sour lift.
Cool completely and store in a dry jar; the flavour rounds out beautifully overnight.
tips: Keep the vegetables tender-crisp rather than soft so they hold their shape in the sweet syrup.
Add the lemon juice off the heat so its fresh sourness is not cooked away.
Cook the syrup only until it lightly coats the veg; boiled too far it sets hard on cooling.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve as a sweet counterpoint to spicy theplas, dhokla, or a full Gujarati thali.

variations.name: Instant Mixed Vegetable Pickle
variations.description: A same-day mixed pickle where the vegetables are tossed with a hot mustard-oil tempering and ground spices, ready to eat in a few hours without any sun-curing. It keeps the fresh crunch of the raw veg while carrying a punchy tang. The quick answer when winter vegetables are on hand but there is no time to mature a jar.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Smoked and slightly cooled, it tempers the spices and lightly wilts the vegetables for a quick pickle

steps: Cut 1 carrot, 150 g cauliflower and 6 green chillies into small even pieces.
Heat 5 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil in a pan until it smokes, then lower the flame to medium.
Splutter 1 tbsp mustard seeds, add 0.25 tsp asafoetida, and let it foam for a few seconds.
Add the vegetables with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp fennel powder, 1 tbsp chilli powder and 2 tbsp salt, and saute 4-5 minutes until just crisp-tender.
Switch off, cool slightly, and stir in 4 tbsp lemon juice to coat everything.
Rest 3-4 hours at room temperature before serving; it keeps a week refrigerated.
tips: Saute only briefly so the carrot and cauliflower stay crunchy, which is the appeal of an instant pickle.
Smoking the mustard oil first mellows its raw pungency even in a quick pickle.
The lemon juice both preserves and tenderises, so give it a few hours to work before serving.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve fresh with hot parathas, khichdi, or a bowl of dal-rice for a quick tangy crunch.

variations.name: Classic Andhra Palli Chutney
variations.description: The beloved Andhra palli chutney, a thick, creamy dip ground from roasted peanuts with dry red chilli, garlic and tamarind. A sesame-oil tempering of mustard, cumin and curry leaves crowns it with fragrance and heat. Rich, sour and spicy, it turns a plate of idli or dosa into something deeply satisfying.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sesame Oil
ingredients.note: Gingelly oil in the tempering deepens the roasted-peanut flavour in true Andhra style

steps: Grind 1 cup roasted peanuts, 4 dry red chillies, 4 garlic cloves, 1.5 tsp tamarind and 0.75 tsp salt with 0.6 cups water to a thick, smooth chutney.
Scrape down the sides and grind again, adding a little more water until it reaches a creamy dropping consistency.
Transfer the chutney to a serving bowl.
Heat 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Sesame Oil in a small pan on medium flame until it shimmers.
Add 1 tsp mustard seeds and 0.5 tsp cumin and let them splutter for 20 seconds, then toss in 10 curry leaves and let them crackle.
Pour the sizzling tempering over the chutney and fold it in just before serving.
tips: Rub the skins off the roasted peanuts before grinding for a smoother, cleaner-tasting chutney.
Grind the peanuts warm; freshly roasted nuts break down into a creamier paste.
It thickens quickly as it stands, so keep a little warm water aside to loosen it before serving.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with hot idli, dosa or pesarattu, or spoon it over steamed rice with a little ghee.

variations.name: Peanut-Coconut Chutney
variations.description: A milder, creamier version where fresh coconut joins the roasted peanuts for a softer, sweeter chutney. Green chillies keep it gently hot rather than fiery, and a coconut-oil tempering ties the two together. This is the version many homes prefer for children and for a cooling everyday breakfast side.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: The tempering fat that complements the fresh coconut and keeps the chutney light

steps: Grind 0.75 cups roasted peanuts, 0.5 cups grated coconut, 3 green chillies, 0.5 inch ginger, 1 tsp tamarind and 0.75 tsp salt with 0.6 cups water to a smooth, creamy chutney.
Transfer to a bowl and loosen with a little water to a soft dropping consistency.
Heat 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil in a small pan on medium flame until it shimmers.
Add 1 tsp mustard seeds and let them pop for 20 seconds, then add 1 tsp urad dal and fry until golden.
Toss in 10 curry leaves, let them crackle for 5 seconds, and pour the tempering over the chutney.
Stir gently and serve fresh.
tips: Use green chillies instead of red for a gentler heat that suits the sweet coconut.
Balance the tamarind carefully; the coconut is delicate and too much sourness will mask it.
Grind everything together while the peanuts are freshly roasted for the creamiest texture.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with soft idlis, ghee dosa or upma for a mild, comforting breakfast plate.

variations.name: Maharashtrian Dry Peanut Chutney
variations.description: The coarse, dry shengdana chutney of Maharashtra, a spiced peanut powder rather than a wet dip. Roasted peanuts are pounded with garlic, red chilli and a whisper of groundnut oil into a crumbly, intensely savoury sprinkle. It keeps for weeks and is the classic partner to poha, thalipeeth and vada pav.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A teaspoon crisps the garlic and binds the dry powder without making it greasy

steps: Heat 1 tsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a small pan and fry 6 sliced garlic cloves on low for 2-3 minutes until pale golden and crisp, then cool them.
Rub the skins off 1 cup roasted peanuts and add them to a dry grinder jar with the fried garlic.
Add 1.5 tsp red chilli powder, 0.5 tsp cumin powder and 0.75 tsp salt to the jar.
Pulse in short bursts to a coarse, crumbly powder, stopping before the peanuts release their oil and clump.
Rub the powder between your fingers to check it is dry and sandy, not pasty.
Cool completely and store in an airtight jar for up to three weeks.
tips: Pulse in short bursts only; over-grinding heats the peanuts and turns the powder into a paste.
Frying the garlic first mellows its raw bite and helps the powder keep longer.
Adjust the chilli powder to taste, as this dry chutney is meant to be boldly spicy.
variations.servingSuggestion: Sprinkle generously over kanda poha or thalipeeth, or stuff a spoon into a vada pav.

variations.name: Peanut-Curd Chutney
variations.description: A cooling, restaurant-style peanut chutney where ground roasted peanuts are folded into whisked curd for a rich, creamy dip with a mild tang. A ghee tempering of mustard, cumin and curry leaves adds warmth and aroma on top. Smoother and less sour than the classic, it soothes the heat of a spicy meal.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A ghee tempering gives this curd-based chutney a nutty, aromatic finish that oil cannot match

steps: Grind 0.75 cups roasted peanuts with 2 green chillies, 0.5 inch ginger and 3 tbsp water to a smooth, thick paste.
Whisk 0.75 cups curd in a bowl until smooth, then fold in the peanut paste and 0.5 tsp salt until well combined.
Loosen with a little water if the chutney is too thick to spoon, keeping it creamy.
Heat 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a small pan on medium flame until it melts and shimmers.
Add 1 tsp mustard seeds and 0.5 tsp cumin and let them splutter for 20 seconds, then toss in 8 curry leaves and let them crackle.
Pour the ghee tempering over the chutney and swirl it in just before serving.
tips: Use fresh, mildly sour curd; over-sour curd will overwhelm the delicate peanut flavour.
Add the tempering just before serving so the ghee aroma stays fragrant.
Chill for 15 minutes before serving for the best creamy, cooling texture.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve as a cooling dip beside spicy pulao or biryani, or with hot phulkas and a dry sabzi.

variations.name: Classic Rajgira Ladoo
variations.description: The airy fasting ladoo of popped amaranth bound in molten jaggery, light as a cloud yet richly sweet, eaten across India during Navratri and Ekadashi vrat. Popping the tiny rajgira seeds on a dry hot pan is the delicate heart of the recipe. Cooked to soft-ball jaggery and rolled fast, they set into crisp, feather-light balls.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: cooked to soft-ball stage so the light puffs bind without going hard

ingredients.name: Anveshan Bilona Ghee
ingredients.note: melts the jaggery smoothly and greases your palms for rolling

steps: Heat a deep dry kadhai until very hot, then add 1 tablespoon of amaranth at a time and swirl for a few seconds until the seeds pop into tiny white puffs; repeat until all 1 cup is popped, sieving out any unpopped seeds.
In a clean pan warm 1 tbsp Anveshan Bilona Ghee, add 0.75 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder and the water, and melt on low heat for 3-4 minutes to a soft-ball syrup.
Test the syrup by dropping a little into cold water; it should gather into a soft pliable ball before proceeding.
Turn off the heat and quickly fold in the popped amaranth, chopped almonds and 0.5 tsp cardamom until every puff is coated.
Grease your palms with the remaining ghee and, working fast while warm, press small portions gently into 14 round ladoos.
Let them set on a greased plate for 15 minutes until firm; handle lightly as they are very delicate.
tips: Pop the amaranth in tiny batches on a very hot dry pan; too much at once or too low a heat leaves them unpopped and hard.
Cook the jaggery only to soft-ball, or the ladoos turn either loose or rock hard.
Press gently, not tightly, so the ladoos keep their airy crunch and don't collapse.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve these light ladoos as vrat food during Navratri and Ekadashi, or as a guilt-free everyday sweet bite.

variations.name: Rajgira Peanut Ladoo
variations.description: A more substantial fasting ladoo where roasted peanuts join the popped amaranth, adding protein, crunch and a satisfying heft suited to a full vrat day. The peanuts and rajgira are both fasting-friendly, making this a favourite for Ekadashi. It is heartier and holds together more firmly than the plain version.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: cooked to soft-ball to bind the heavier peanut-amaranth mix

ingredients.name: Anveshan Bilona Ghee
ingredients.note: melts the jaggery and keeps the mix off your palms

steps: Pop 0.75 cup amaranth in small batches on a very hot dry kadhai until the seeds puff white, then sieve out any unpopped ones.
Coarsely crush the roasted peanuts, leaving some halves for texture.
Warm 1 tbsp Anveshan Bilona Ghee, add 0.75 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder and the water, and melt on low heat for 3-4 minutes to a soft-ball syrup.
Off the heat, fold in the popped amaranth, crushed peanuts, 0.5 tsp cardamom and a pinch of rock salt until evenly coated.
Grease your palms with the remaining ghee and press quickly into 14 firm ladoos while warm.
Cool for 15 minutes until set; the peanuts make these firmer and more filling than the classic.
tips: Use rock salt (sendha namak) so these stay fasting-compliant while still tasting balanced.
Keep some peanuts as halves for extra crunch against the light amaranth.
If the mix hardens before shaping, warm it briefly to soften the jaggery again.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve these protein-rich ladoos as satisfying vrat food, or pack them as a wholesome energy snack for travel.

variations.name: Rajgira Dry-Fruit Ladoo
variations.description: A luxurious festive version studded with almonds, cashews, pistachios and raisins so the light puffs are wrapped in nutty richness. It turns a humble fasting ladoo into a celebratory sweet, still vrat-friendly but far more indulgent. The dry fruit also makes each ladoo more filling and nourishing.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: cooked to soft-ball to bind the nut-heavy mixture

ingredients.name: Anveshan Bilona Ghee
ingredients.note: toasts the dry fruit and melts the jaggery

steps: Pop 0.75 cup amaranth in small batches on a very hot dry pan until puffed white, then sieve out unpopped seeds.
Warm 1 tbsp Anveshan Bilona Ghee and toast the chopped almonds, cashews, pistachios and raisins for 2 minutes until fragrant and the raisins plump.
Add 0.75 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder and the water to the same pan and melt on low heat for 3-4 minutes to a soft-ball syrup.
Off the heat, fold in the popped amaranth and 0.5 tsp cardamom until the puffs and nuts are evenly coated.
Grease your palms with the remaining ghee and press gently into 14 ladoos while warm.
Cool for 15 minutes until firm; the nuts keep them together while the amaranth stays airy.
tips: Toast the dry fruit before adding the jaggery so they stay crisp inside the ladoo.
Chop the nuts small so the delicate amaranth still binds around them.
These make an elegant homemade gift; box them in mini paper cups to protect their fragile shape.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve these nut-rich ladoos on a festive Navratri thali, or offer as an upscale vrat sweet to guests.

variations.name: Rajgira Coconut Honey Ladoo
variations.description: A softer, no-cook-syrup version bound with toasted coconut and a little honey for a mellow, floral sweetness and a chewier bite. Using honey and coconut instead of a hard jaggery set makes these tender and quick, ideal when you want a gentle fasting treat. The coconut adds fragrance and body to the light amaranth.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: a smaller amount melted to a light syrup to start the binding

ingredients.name: Anveshan Honey
ingredients.note: stirred in off the heat for a floral sweetness and softer chew

ingredients.name: Anveshan Bilona Ghee
ingredients.note: toasts the coconut and greases your palms

steps: Pop 0.75 cup amaranth in small batches on a very hot dry pan until puffed white, then sieve out unpopped seeds.
Warm the Anveshan Bilona Ghee and toast the grated copra for 3 minutes until pale gold and fragrant.
Add 0.5 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder and the water and melt on low heat for 2-3 minutes to a loose soft syrup.
Take the pan off the heat, let it cool for a minute, then stir in 2 tbsp Anveshan Honey so its aroma isn't cooked away.
Fold in the popped amaranth and 0.5 tsp cardamom until the puffs and coconut are evenly coated and tacky.
Grease your palms and press gently into 14 soft ladoos while warm, resting 15 minutes to set into a tender chew.
tips: Add the honey off the heat, as boiling honey turns bitter and loses its floral note.
These stay softer than syrup-set ladoos, so eat within a week for the best texture.
Toast the coconut just until pale gold to keep the flavour sweet and nutty, not burnt.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve these tender, honeyed ladoos as a light vrat sweet with fruit, or as a soft treat for children.

variations.name: Classic Gud Rewri
variations.description: Classic Rewri are small round jaggery discs rolled thickly in roasted white sesame, a Lohri and Sankranti essential across Punjab and North India. Crunchy on the outside with a firm chewy jaggery centre, they are traditionally tossed into the Lohri bonfire celebrations.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: forms the firm chewy disc that is rolled in sesame

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: kneaded into the warm jaggery so the discs stay pliable and glossy

steps: Dry-roast 1 cup sesame seeds over low heat for 3 minutes until golden and popping, then spread on a plate.
Melt 1.25 cups Anveshan Jaggery Powder with 2 tbsp water and 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee over low heat and cook to a firm soft-crack stage, about 8 minutes.
Stir in 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and 0.25 tsp dry ginger powder, then pour onto a greased plate to cool for a minute.
While still warm and pliable, pinch off small portions and roll each into a marble, then flatten into a thick disc.
Press both sides of every disc firmly into the roasted sesame so they are fully coated.
Lay the coated rewri on a tray and cool completely until the centres firm up with a crunchy sesame shell.
tips: Work while the jaggery is warm; once cold it cracks instead of shaping into discs.
Keep a bowl of sesame ready so you can coat each disc the moment it is shaped.
Store airtight so the sesame coating stays crunchy for up to two weeks.
variations.servingSuggestion: Pile the sesame discs in a bowl for Lohri night alongside gajak and popcorn.

variations.name: Sugar Rewri
variations.description: The pale, glossy white rewri of Delhi's winter carts, made with pulled khandsari sugar so the discs stay ivory rather than amber. Lighter and more delicate in sweetness than the jaggery version, these are the classic paper-wrapped rewri sold near Jama Masjid.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: pulled while warm it stays pale and glossy for the classic white rewri

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: worked into the warm sugar to keep the discs soft and stretchable

steps: Roast 1 cup sesame seeds until just golden and keep on a plate ready for coating.
Melt 1.25 cups Anveshan Khandsari with 3 tbsp water and 0.25 tsp lemon juice over low heat and cook to hard-ball stage, about 9 minutes.
Pour onto a greased slab, work in 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and 0.5 tsp cardamom powder, and gather into a mass as it cools slightly.
Repeatedly pull and fold the warm sugar mass with greased hands until it turns pale, glossy and stretchy.
Pinch off small pieces, shape into thick discs and press both sides firmly into the roasted sesame.
Cool the coated discs on a tray until they set crisp and hold their pale colour.
tips: The lemon juice stops the sugar from crystallising while you pull it.
Pull the sugar as it cools to trap air, which gives the white rewri its lighter bite.
Grease your hands well; pulled sugar is very hot and sticky to work.
variations.servingSuggestion: Wrap a few discs in paper twists the way winter carts sell them, and serve with chai.

variations.name: Kesar Pista Rewri
variations.description: A festive premium rewri perfumed with saffron and coated in a mix of sesame and finely chopped pistachios for a jewelled green-gold finish. Richer and more aromatic than the plain disc, it is a wedding-season upgrade on the humble Lohri sweet.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: keeps the disc pale so the saffron colour shows through

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: bloomed in warm milk to colour and perfume the discs a warm gold

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: keeps the discs soft and carries the saffron aroma

steps: Soak 0.25 tsp Anveshan Saffron in 1 tbsp warm milk for 10 minutes, and roast 0.75 cup sesame seeds until golden.
Finely chop 0.25 cup pistachios and mix them with the roasted sesame on a coating plate.
Melt 1.25 cups Anveshan Khandsari with 3 tbsp water over low heat to hard-ball stage, then stir in the saffron milk.
Pour onto a greased slab, work in 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and 0.5 tsp cardamom powder, and knead the warm mass until smooth and golden.
Shape small thick discs and press both sides into the sesame-pistachio mix so they are richly coated.
Cool the discs on a tray until firm and serve once fully set.
tips: Bloom saffron in warm milk so it colours the sugar evenly without clumping.
Chop the pistachios finely so they cling to the sticky discs like the sesame.
Reserve a pinch of pistachio to press decoratively on top of each disc.
variations.servingSuggestion: Present on a silver tray at a winter wedding with a scatter of saffron strands.

variations.name: Peanut Gud Rewri
variations.description: A rustic Maharashtrian rewri that presses crushed roasted peanuts alongside the sesame coating for extra crunch and body. Earthier and more filling than the plain sesame disc, it is a village winter-fair favourite with a robust groundnut flavour.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: forms the earthy chewy centre that pairs with roasted peanuts

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: greases the slab and echoes the peanut flavour of the coating

steps: Roast 0.5 cup sesame seeds until golden, then coarsely crush 0.5 cup roasted peanuts and mix the two on a coating plate.
Melt 1.25 cups Anveshan Jaggery Powder with 2 tbsp water over low heat to a firm soft-crack stage, about 8 minutes.
Stir in 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and 0.25 tsp salt, then pour onto a slab greased with the 2 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil.
Once cool enough to handle, pinch off portions and shape each into a thick round disc.
Press both sides firmly into the sesame-peanut mix so the crushed nuts stud the surface.
Lay the discs on a tray and cool completely until the centres set firm and chewy.
tips: Crush the peanuts coarsely so they add visible crunch without falling off.
A pinch of salt balances the strong jaggery and peanut sweetness.
Shape the discs a little thicker to hold the heavier peanut coating.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve the hearty discs as a filling winter snack with a glass of warm milk.

variations.name: Classic Rose Milk
variations.description: The blush-pink chilled milk beloved across South Indian bakeries, where fragrant rose syrup meets cold creamy milk over ice. Simple, floral and gently sweet, it is the drink that cools childhood summers, served frothy in a tall glass with a rose-scented finish.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Honey
ingredients.note: a little raw honey adds gentle body and rounds the rose syrup without over-sweetening the delicate milk

steps: Pour 4 cups chilled full-fat milk into a jug and whisk in 2 tbsp Anveshan Honey and 0.25 tsp cardamom powder until the honey fully dissolves.
Add 6 tbsp rose syrup and whisk vigorously for about 30 seconds until the milk turns an even, pretty blush pink and starts to froth.
Taste and adjust the rose syrup to your liking, adding a touch more for a deeper colour and sweeter, more floral note.
Divide 1.5 cups ice cubes among four tall glasses.
Pour the rose milk over the ice, filling each glass and leaving a little froth on top.
Garnish with 2 tbsp chopped almonds and a scatter of dried rose petals, and serve immediately.
tips: Use full-fat chilled milk for the creamiest body; skimmed milk makes the drink taste thin and watery.
Whisk hard or blend briefly to create the signature froth that makes bakery rose milk so appealing.
Add the rose syrup gradually and taste, since brands vary widely in sweetness and colour strength.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve ice-cold in tall glasses with a straw, garnished with rose petals and nuts, as a nostalgic summer cooler or a light dessert drink.

variations.name: Homemade Gulkand Rose Milk
variations.description: A richer, more aromatic version sweetened with gulkand (rose-petal preserve) instead of bottled syrup, giving a deep natural rose flavour and cooling properties. Flecked with real preserved petals, it is fragrant, mildly earthy-sweet and prized in Ayurveda for beating summer heat.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari Sugar
ingredients.note: khandsari lightly sweetens the milk while letting the natural rose flavour of the gulkand lead

steps: Blend 5 tbsp gulkand with 1 cup of the chilled milk until the preserve breaks down and the milk turns fragrant and speckled with fine petal bits.
Pour this into a jug with the remaining 3 cups chilled milk, then whisk in 3 tbsp Anveshan Khandsari Sugar and 0.25 tsp cardamom powder until dissolved.
Stir in 1 tbsp beetroot juice for a natural rosy tint and 1 tsp rose water to lift the aroma, whisking until frothy.
Taste and adjust sweetness with a little more khandsari if the gulkand is on the mild side.
Divide 1.5 cups ice cubes among four glasses and pour the gulkand rose milk over.
Garnish with 2 tbsp chopped pistachios and serve chilled.
tips: Blend the gulkand with a little milk first so the petals disperse evenly instead of sinking as a clump.
A spoon of beetroot juice gives a natural pink without artificial colour used in bottled syrups.
Gulkand is naturally sweet, so add the khandsari gradually and taste to avoid an over-sweet drink.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve chilled with pistachio slivers floating on top, a naturally flavoured, cooling drink especially soothing on very hot days.

variations.name: Rose Falooda Milk
variations.description: A dessert-in-a-glass version layered with soaked basil seeds, falooda vermicelli and a scoop of the chilled rose milk, closer to a spoonable treat than a drink. Textural and festive, it brings together the cooling crunch of sabja and slippery sev for a full falooda experience.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Honey
ingredients.note: raw honey adds gentle sweetness and gloss to the milk base that ties the falooda layers together

steps: Soak 3 tbsp basil seeds in 0.5 cup water for 15 minutes until they swell and turn jelly-like, then drain.
Boil the falooda sev in water for 5 to 6 minutes until soft, drain, rinse under cold water, and chill.
Whisk 4 cups chilled milk with 6 tbsp rose syrup, 2 tbsp Anveshan Honey and 0.25 tsp cardamom powder until pink and frothy.
In each tall glass, spoon a layer of soaked basil seeds, then a layer of cooked falooda sev, and drizzle a little extra rose syrup down the sides.
Add a few ice cubes and pour the rose milk over the layers, filling the glass most of the way.
Top each with a scoop of vanilla ice cream and 3 tbsp chopped mixed nuts, and serve at once with a long spoon and straw.
tips: Rinse the boiled falooda sev in cold water to stop it cooking and keep the strands separate and slippery.
Soak the basil seeds fresh each time; they should be fully bloomed and gel-like before layering.
Assemble the falooda just before serving so the layers stay distinct and the ice cream does not fully melt.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve in tall sundae glasses with a spoon and straw, a celebratory dessert-drink for parties and Eid or summer feasts.

variations.name: Rose Badam Milk
variations.description: A creamier, more nourishing rose milk enriched with a smooth almond paste and warm spices, drinking somewhere between rose milk and badam milk. Thick, pale rose and lightly nutty, it can be served warm in cool weather or chilled in summer for a richer treat.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: a little unrefined jaggery deepens the almond richness and adds a gentle caramel warmth beneath the rose

steps: Soak 18 almonds in warm water for 20 minutes, peel them, and blend with 0.5 cup of the milk into a very smooth, fine paste.
Warm the remaining 3.5 cups milk in a pan on medium with a pinch of saffron and simmer gently for 4 minutes to infuse colour.
Whisk in the almond paste and simmer on low for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until the milk thickens slightly and turns creamy.
Lower the heat and stir in 3 tbsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder and 0.5 tsp cardamom powder off the boil so the milk does not split, mixing until dissolved.
Cool the milk to room temperature, then whisk in 5 tbsp rose syrup until it turns an even pale rose.
Serve warm as is, or chill and pour over 1 cup ice cubes, garnished with 2 tbsp chopped almonds.
tips: Add the jaggery only after taking the milk off the boil, as jaggery stirred into boiling milk can curdle it.
Blend the almond paste ultra-smooth for a silky drink; any coarse bits settle at the bottom of the glass.
Whisk in the rose syrup only once the milk has cooled, so its delicate aroma is not cooked away.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm on cool evenings or chilled over ice in summer, garnished with almonds and a saffron strand, as a rich, nourishing rose milk.

variations.name: Classic Singhare Ka Halwa
variations.description: Singhare ka halwa is a fasting-day pudding made from water-chestnut flour roasted in ghee until nutty, then swelled with hot sweetened water. Naturally gluten-free and permitted during vrat, it is a smooth, cardamom-scented halwa favoured for Navratri and Ekadashi.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the water-chestnut flour to a nutty gold and gives the fasting halwa its richness

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: dissolved into hot water to sweeten the vrat halwa cleanly

steps: Heat 0.6 cup Anveshan Ghee in a heavy pan and fry 3 tbsp cashews and raisins to golden, about 2 minutes, then lift them out.
Add 1 cup singhara flour to the ghee and roast over low heat, stirring without pause, for 10 to 12 minutes until it darkens slightly and smells nutty.
While it roasts, boil 2.5 cups water with 0.6 cup Anveshan Khandsari until the sugar dissolves, then keep it hot.
Pour the hot syrup into the roasted flour very carefully, standing back from the splutter, and stir hard to break every lump.
Cook on low heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring constantly, until the halwa thickens into a smooth, glossy mass that leaves the pan.
Fold in 0.5 tsp cardamom and the fried nuts, then serve the singhara halwa warm.
tips: Singhara flour scorches faster than atta, so keep the flame low and never leave the pan unstirred.
Sieve the flour before roasting, as it tends to clump and can leave hard lumps in the halwa.
Add the syrup hot and away from your face, as this halwa splutters sharply when the liquid hits.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm during Navratri or Ekadashi fasts, garnished with fried cashews and a pinch of cardamom.

variations.name: Kesar Badam Singhara Halwa
variations.description: A richer fasting halwa cooked in milk with almond powder and bloomed saffron for a creamy, saffron-gold pudding. More luxurious than the water version, it turns a humble vrat sweet into a festive treat for breaking the fast.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the flour and almond powder for a rich, milk-swelled fasting halwa

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: sweetens the warm milk while keeping the saffron colour clear and bright

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: bloomed in warm milk to colour and perfume the rich fasting halwa

steps: Soak 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp of warm milk taken from the 2.5 cups and set aside to bloom.
Heat 0.6 cup Anveshan Ghee, fry 3 tbsp sliced almonds and pistachios to golden, and reserve them.
Add 1 cup singhara flour with 0.25 cup almond powder to the ghee and roast over low heat for 9 to 10 minutes until nutty.
Warm the remaining milk with 0.6 cup Anveshan Khandsari until dissolved, then pour it into the roasted flour, stirring hard to avoid lumps.
Add the bloomed saffron milk and cook on low heat for 4 minutes until the halwa thickens and turns a rich gold.
Fold in the reserved nuts, mix until glossy, and serve the kesar badam singhara halwa warm.
tips: Adding almond powder deepens the nuttiness and gives the fasting halwa a plush, rich body.
Bloom the saffron in warm milk first so its colour disperses evenly through the pudding.
Keep the halwa slightly loose, as milk and almond powder thicken it further as it cools.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm to break a fast, garnished with slivered pistachios and a few saffron strands.

variations.name: Jaggery Singhara Halwa
variations.description: A rustic fasting halwa sweetened with jaggery instead of sugar, giving a darker, earthier pudding with a whisper of dry ginger. Deeper and more warming than the classic, it suits those who prefer unrefined sweeteners on vrat days.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the flour to a nutty gold for a rustic, jaggery-sweetened fasting halwa

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: melted and strained to sweeten the halwa with warming, earthy caramel notes

steps: Heat 0.6 cup Anveshan Ghee in a heavy pan and lightly toast 3 tbsp chopped walnuts for 1 minute, then set them aside.
Add 1 cup singhara flour to the ghee and roast over low heat, stirring constantly, for 10 to 12 minutes until nutty and slightly darkened.
Melt 0.7 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder in 2.5 cups water over low heat, then strain out any grit and keep it hot.
Pour the hot jaggery water into the roasted flour off the boil, standing back from the splutter, and stir hard to break lumps.
Cook on low heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until the halwa thickens into a smooth, glossy mass.
Fold in 0.25 tsp dry ginger, 0.5 tsp cardamom and the toasted walnuts, then serve warm.
tips: Add the jaggery water off the boil so it blends in smoothly without seizing the flour.
Strain the melted jaggery to keep the halwa smooth and free of grit.
Dry ginger adds warmth and aids digestion, making this a comforting choice for cold fasting days.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm on vrat days, garnished with toasted walnuts and a light dusting of cardamom.

variations.name: Singhara Coconut Khoya Halwa
variations.description: A festive fasting halwa enriched with khoya and toasted coconut for a denser, fudgier pudding that eats almost like a mithai. Richer and more textured than the plain version, it is a treat reserved for breaking a long fast.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the flour and toasts the coconut for a rich, mithai-like fasting halwa

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: sweetens the khoya-enriched halwa to a soft, fudgy set

steps: Heat 0.6 cup Anveshan Ghee, fry 3 tbsp cashews to golden, then toast 0.25 cup grated coconut for 1 minute and set both aside.
Add 1 cup singhara flour to the ghee and roast over low heat for 10 minutes until nutty and lightly darkened.
Warm 2 cups milk with 0.6 cup Anveshan Khandsari until dissolved, then pour it into the roasted flour, stirring hard to avoid lumps.
Cook 3 minutes until it thickens, then stir in 0.5 cup grated khoya and cook a further 3 to 4 minutes until it melts in.
Continue on low heat until the halwa turns thick, glossy and fudgy and starts leaving the pan.
Fold in the toasted coconut, cashews and 0.5 tsp cardamom, then serve warm.
tips: Add the khoya after the flour has absorbed the milk, so the halwa binds richly rather than turning loose.
Toast the coconut only until fragrant, as over-browning turns it bitter.
For a set, sliceable version, press the finished halwa into a greased tray and cut into squares once cool.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm to break a fast, garnished with toasted coconut and fried cashews for a festive finish.

variations.name: Classic Sweet Lassi
variations.description: Classic Sweet Lassi is a thick, frothy Punjabi drink of whisked fresh yogurt sweetened naturally and scented with cardamom, served in a tall glass with a cap of foam. Cooling and gently tangy, it is the everyday summer refresher of North Indian homes.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Honey
ingredients.note: sweetens the lassi with a floral note and blends smoothly into cold yogurt

steps: Whisk 3 cups fresh yogurt vigorously with a hand whisk or blender for 2 minutes until completely smooth and lump-free.
Add 4 tbsp Anveshan Honey, 0.5 cup chilled water and 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and blend for another minute until light and frothy.
Blend in the 8 ice cubes briefly so the lassi turns cold and gets a thick foamy top.
Stir in 0.5 tsp rose water gently by hand so the fragrance is not lost.
Pour into four tall glasses, letting the froth settle on top of each.
Garnish with 1 tbsp chopped pistachios and serve immediately while chilled and foamy.
tips: Use fresh, not sour, yogurt for a mild sweet lassi; older curd turns it too tangy.
Whisk well before adding water so the lassi is smooth and not watery.
Add honey to taste depending on how tart your yogurt is.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve alongside a spicy Punjabi meal or on its own as a cooling afternoon drink.

variations.name: Punjabi Malai Lassi
variations.description: The indulgent dhaba-style lassi, blended with fresh cream and a spoon of ghee-fried khoya so it is almost a drinkable dessert. Extra thick and topped with a thick layer of malai, it is the towering glass served in Amritsar's famous lassi shops.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: dissolves into the thick lassi for a clean sweetness without overpowering the malai

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: a touch fried with the crumbled khoya adds a rich dhaba-style aroma

steps: Crumble 3 tbsp khoya and toast it in 1 tsp Anveshan Ghee over low heat for 2 minutes until soft and fragrant, then cool.
Whisk 3 cups fresh yogurt with 0.5 cup fresh cream until thick and smooth.
Add 5 tbsp Anveshan Khandsari, the toasted khoya and 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and blend until fully combined.
Blend in the 6 ice cubes briefly to chill without thinning the lassi too much.
Pour into four glasses and top each with 1 tbsp malai and a sprinkle of chopped almonds.
Serve at once with a spoon, as this lassi is thick enough to eat.
tips: Do not add water; the cream and khoya are what make this lassi luxuriously thick.
Toast the khoya just until soft so it blends smoothly without lumps.
Chill the glasses beforehand so the thick lassi stays cold longer.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve the towering malai-topped glass as a filling stand-alone treat after a light lunch.

variations.name: Rose Falooda Lassi
variations.description: A dessert-forward lassi layered with rose syrup, soaked basil seeds and slippery falooda vermicelli for a drink that eats like a sundae. Pretty pink and full of chewy textures, it is a Hyderabadi-inspired treat for a hot afternoon.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: sweetens the yogurt base with a caramel depth that balances the floral rose
