Fold in the 300 g paneer cubes along with the diced capsicum and onion petals, coat evenly, and rest in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Thread the paneer and vegetables onto skewers and grill on a hot tawa brushed with 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee for 7 minutes, turning until charred at the edges.
Brush the tikka with the remaining ghee, char for 2 more minutes for a glossy finish, and serve hot with sliced onions.
tips: Roast and grind the achari spices fresh rather than using ready pickle masala, as the aroma is far sharper and cleaner.
Use firm, block paneer and pat it dry before marinating so it holds shape and takes a good char.
A pinch of amchur folded into the marinade deepens the pickle-like tang if your curd is mild.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve as a starter with mint-coriander chutney, onion rings and a lemon wedge, or tuck into a kathi roll.

variations.name: Punjabi Sarson Achari Paneer Tikka
variations.description: A robust Punjabi rendition where pungent mustard oil forms the soul of the achari marinade, giving the paneer a bold, dhaba-grill sharpness. Crushed yellow mustard and dry red chillies push the pickle notes to the fore for a fiery, unmistakably North-Indian tikka.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: its pungency is the backbone of the achari marinade and grilling char

steps: Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil to smoking point, then cool it fully so its raw pungency mellows into a nutty sharpness.
Dry-roast 1.5 tbsp yellow mustard, 1 tbsp fennel and 3 dry red chillies for 2 minutes, then grind coarse; toast 1 tbsp besan for a minute until nutty.
Whisk 0.5 cup yogurt with 2 tbsp of the cooled mustard oil, the ground masala, roasted besan, 1.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1.5 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, 1 tsp amchur and 1 tsp salt.
Coat the 300 g paneer cubes and large onion petals thickly in this marinade and rest for 40 minutes so the flavours soak in.
Skewer the paneer and onion and grill over an open flame or on a smoking tawa for 8 minutes, turning until deeply charred.
Drizzle the last 1 tbsp mustard oil over the tikka, sear for 2 minutes more until glossy, and serve piping hot.
tips: Always heat mustard oil to smoking point before cooling and using it raw, or the marinade tastes bitter.
Grind the mustard seeds only coarsely so you get little bursts of pickle heat rather than an even paste.
Rest the marinated paneer at room temperature for the last 10 minutes so it grills evenly without cracking.
variations.servingSuggestion: Plate on a bed of sliced onions with a squeeze of lemon and a side of pickled green chillies.

variations.name: Tandoori Charcoal Achari Paneer Tikka
variations.description: This restaurant-style version finishes the achari tikka with a charcoal dhungar smoke for that unmistakable tandoor-house aroma. A double marination and a cashew-thickened curd coat give an extra-plump, juicy cube wrapped in smoky pickle spice.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: poured over the hot charcoal to release the smoky dhungar aroma into the tikka

steps: Rub the 300 g paneer cubes with 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, 0.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and 0.5 tsp salt and set aside for 15 minutes as a first marination.
Dry-roast 1 tbsp fennel, 1 tsp nigella and 1 tsp cumin for 2 minutes and grind coarse into an achari blend.
Whisk 0.75 cup hung curd with 2 tbsp cashew paste, the ground achari blend, 1 tsp tandoori masala, 0.5 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp chilli powder and 0.5 tsp salt into a thick second marinade.
Coat the pre-marinated paneer in this creamy mix and chill for 30 minutes, then skewer and grill on a ghee-brushed tawa for 8 minutes until charred and plump.
Place the grilled tikka in a deep bowl, set a red-hot charcoal piece in a small steel cup in the centre, and pour 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee over it.
Cover the bowl immediately for 3 minutes to trap the smoke, then uncover and serve the tikka wreathed in tandoori aroma.
tips: The cashew paste keeps the curd coat rich and stops the paneer drying out under high grilling heat.
Heat the charcoal until it glows red and grey-ashed for clean smoke; a half-lit coal gives an acrid taste.
Do not smoke for longer than 3 minutes or the tikka can turn bitter from over-exposure.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve on a sizzler plate with grilled onions and capsicum and a bowl of burnt-garlic dip.

variations.name: Air-Fried Achari Malai Paneer Tikka
variations.description: A lighter, creamy achari tikka crisped in an air fryer with barely a brush of fat, blending the tang of pickle spices with a mild malai richness. It gives a golden, evenly browned cube without deep grilling, ideal for a quick weeknight starter.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: brushed lightly over the tikka so it crisps and browns in the air fryer

steps: Dry-roast 1 tbsp fennel and 0.5 tsp nigella for 2 minutes and crush coarse to release the achari fragrance.

Whisk 0.33 cup hung curd with 3 tbsp cream, 2 tbsp grated cheese, the crushed spices, 0.5 tsp white pepper, 1 tsp green chilli paste, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tbsp cornflour and 0.75 tsp salt into a thick malai marinade.
Coat the 300 g paneer cubes generously and rest in the fridge for 25 minutes so the coating sets and clings.
Preheat the air fryer to 200C for 4 minutes, arrange the paneer in a single layer, and brush the tops with 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil.
Air-fry for 8 minutes, flip the cubes and brush with the remaining oil, then air-fry another 6 minutes until golden and lightly crisp at the edges.
Rest for 2 minutes so the malai coat firms up, then serve warm with a dusting of chaat masala.
tips: The cornflour and cheese together give a coat that browns and crisps without the char of an open grill.
Do not overcrowd the air-fryer basket; a single layer ensures each cube colours evenly.
Keep the marinade thick and spoonable so it does not slide off during air-frying.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve skewered with cherry tomatoes as a party bite, with a cooling mint-yogurt dip alongside.

variations.name: Classic Aloo Ki Kadhi
variations.description: A homely UP-style kadhi where soft-boiled potato chunks simmer in a gently soured besan-yogurt curry until they drink up the tang. No fritters here, just silky gravy and creamy potato, finished with a ghee tempering of cumin and dried red chilli. Comfort in a bowl, made for pooling over steamed rice.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee carries the cumin tempering that defines a classic kadhi

steps: Whisk the sour yogurt and besan together with 3 cups water, turmeric, red chilli powder and salt until completely lump-free and smooth.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a heavy pot, crackle the cumin, fenugreek seeds and grated ginger for 30 seconds until fragrant, then pour in the yogurt-besan mixture.
Bring to a boil while stirring continuously so the yogurt does not split, then lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until the kadhi thickens and loses its raw besan smell.
Slide in the boiled potatoes cut into large chunks and simmer another 8 minutes so they absorb the tang.
Heat the remaining Anveshan Ghee in a small pan, fry the dried red chillies and curry leaves until they splutter, about 30 seconds, then pour this tempering over the kadhi.
Cover for 2 minutes to let the aromas infuse before serving.
tips: Stir constantly only until the first boil; after that the yogurt is stable and will not curdle.
Use genuinely sour yogurt or add a squeeze of lemon at the end, since flat kadhi tastes incomplete.
Boil the potatoes just short of falling apart so they hold shape in the long simmer.
variations.servingSuggestion: Ladle over a mound of steamed rice with a spoon of ghee and a side of crunchy papad and mango pickle.

variations.name: Punjabi Dhaba Aloo Kadhi
variations.description: A thick, deep-yellow Punjabi kadhi cooked low and slow in mustard oil with baby potatoes that soak up the robust masala. Onion and a garlicky base give it a dhaba heartiness quite unlike the delicate UP version. It clings to rice and only gets better the next day.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: kachi ghani mustard oil gives the Punjabi kadhi its characteristic pungent base

steps: Whisk the sour yogurt, besan, turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder and salt with 4 cups water into a smooth, thin batter.
Heat the Anveshan Mustard Oil in a kadhai until it lightly smokes, then lower the heat and crackle the cumin and fenugreek seeds for 20 seconds.
Add the sliced onion and crushed garlic and fry over medium heat until deep golden, about 6 minutes, so the base is well caramelised.
Pour in the yogurt batter, bring to a rolling boil while stirring, then simmer uncovered on low heat for 25 minutes until thick and glossy.
Meanwhile shallow-fry the peeled baby potatoes in a little mustard oil until golden, then drop them into the simmering kadhi and cook 12 more minutes until soft.
Rest the kadhi off heat for 5 minutes so the potatoes soak up the masala before serving.
tips: Heat the mustard oil to smoking first to tame its sharpness before the tempering goes in.
The longer this kadhi simmers the better it tastes, so do not rush the 25-minute cook.
Prick the fried baby potatoes with a fork so they absorb more gravy.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve thick over jeera rice with a raw onion-and-green-chilli salad and a wedge of lemon on the side.

variations.name: Sindhi-Style Aloo Kadhi
variations.description: A yogurt-free Sindhi take where besan is dry-roasted to a deep brown, then loosened into a tangy tamarind broth loaded with potato and vegetables. The sourness comes from tamarind and tomato rather than curd, giving a rich amber curry with a smoky, roasted aroma. Hearty, tart and completely different from a dahi kadhi.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed groundnut oil roasts the besan without burning and adds nutty depth

steps: Heat the Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a heavy pot, add cumin, fenugreek seeds, curry leaves, slit green chilli and grated ginger and let them crackle for 30 seconds.
Lower the heat, tip in the besan and dry-roast it in the oil, stirring constantly, for 5 to 6 minutes until it turns nut-brown and smells toasty.
Whisk in 4 cups of water in a slow stream to avoid lumps, then add turmeric, red chilli powder, chopped tomato and salt and bring to a boil.
Add the cubed potato and cluster beans and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the curry thickens.
Stir in the tamarind pulp and simmer another 8 minutes until the raw sourness mellows and the kadhi turns glossy amber.
Check the balance of tang and salt, adding a splash of hot water if it has thickened too much, then serve.
tips: Roast the besan patiently on low heat; a deep brown colour is what gives Sindhi kadhi its signature flavour.
Add tamarind only after the vegetables are cooked, as acid slows down softening.
Cluster beans are traditional but green beans or drumsticks work equally well.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve Sindhi-style over plain boiled rice with a spoon of aloo tuk (twice-fried potato) and papad on the side.

variations.name: South-Indian Coconut Aloo Kadhi
variations.description: A coastal reimagining where the besan-yogurt curry is enriched with fresh coconut paste and tempered in coconut oil with mustard seeds and curry leaves. The potatoes simmer in a mellow, faintly sweet gravy that leans Udupi rather than north Indian. Light, aromatic and lovely with steamed rice or appam.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: cold-pressed coconut oil gives the tempering its unmistakable coastal fragrance

steps: Grind the fresh coconut, cumin, green chilli and ginger with a little water into a smooth paste.
Whisk the yogurt and besan with 2.5 cups water and turmeric until lump-free, then blend in the coconut paste and salt.
Pour the mixture into a pot and bring to a boil while stirring constantly so it does not split, then simmer on low for 12 minutes until it thickens slightly.
Add the cubed potatoes and cook covered on low heat for 12 minutes until tender and infused with the coconut curry.
Heat the Anveshan Coconut Oil in a small pan, splutter the mustard seeds, dried red chillies and curry leaves for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Pour the sizzling coconut-oil tempering over the kadhi and cover for 2 minutes before serving.
tips: Do not let this kadhi boil hard after the coconut paste goes in, or the gravy turns grainy.
Use fresh grated coconut for the sweetest result; desiccated coconut needs soaking first.
A pinch of sugar rounds the tang beautifully in this southern style.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with soft appam or steamed matta rice and a side of stir-fried beans thoran.

variations.name: Classic Anjeer Halwa
variations.description: A luscious fig halwa where soaked dried figs are pureed and slow-cooked in ghee until they turn into a glossy, jammy fudge. Naturally sweet from the figs themselves, it needs little added sugar and carries a deep caramel richness studded with fried nuts.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: the halwa is roasted in generous ghee until glossy and it leaves the sides of the pan

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: a little jaggery lifts the figs' natural sweetness with a warm caramel depth

steps: Soak 300 g dried figs in 1 cup warm water for 1 hour until soft, then blend them with a little of the soaking water into a thick puree.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a heavy kadhai and fry 12 cashews and 12 almonds until golden, then set them aside.
Add the fig puree to the ghee and cook on medium-low for 10 minutes, stirring constantly, until it darkens and thickens.
Pour in 0.5 cup milk and 0.33 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder and cook 6 minutes until the sugar melts and the halwa turns glossy.
Drizzle in the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee with 0.5 tsp cardamom and cook until the halwa leaves the sides of the pan.
Fold in most of the fried nuts and serve warm, topped with the rest.
tips: Soften the figs well before blending, or the halwa stays fibrous and grainy.
Figs are already very sweet, so taste before adding all the jaggery and adjust to your liking.
It firms up on cooling, so take it off the heat while still slightly soft.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm topped with slivered almonds, or press into a tray and cut into fudgy squares once cool.

variations.name: Anjeer Dry-Fruit Barfi Halwa
variations.description: A sugar-free set version where the fig puree is cooked with a medley of ground dry fruits into a dense mixture that firms into sliceable barfi. Bound entirely by the natural sugars of figs and dates, it makes a wholesome, energy-rich sweet for gifting.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: binds the fig and dry-fruit mixture into a glossy mass that sets firm for slicing

steps: Soak 250 g dried figs and 150 g seedless dates in 0.75 cup warm water for 45 minutes until soft, then blend to a thick paste.
Dry-roast 1 cup mixed nuts for 3 minutes until fragrant, cool, and pulse to a coarse crumble.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a heavy pan and cook the fig-date paste on medium-low for 10 minutes, stirring, until it thickens and darkens.
Fold in the crushed nuts, 0.5 tsp cardamom and 0.25 tsp nutmeg and cook 5 minutes until the mixture holds together as a mass.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, cook until it leaves the sides of the pan, then press the hot mixture into a greased, poppy-seed-dusted tray.
Smooth the top, scatter 1 tbsp poppy seeds, cool for 30 minutes until firm, and cut into barfi squares.
tips: Cook until the mass cleanly leaves the pan, which is the sign it will set firm enough to slice.
Press the mixture down hard while hot so the barfi holds clean edges once cool.
Being sugar-free and rich in nuts, this keeps for over a week and travels well as a healthy gift.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve the sliced barfi squares in a gifting box, an ideal naturally sweetened treat for diabetics and children alike.

variations.name: Anjeer Semolina Halwa
variations.description: A textured halwa that folds the fig puree into ghee-roasted semolina for a soft, grainy sooji-halwa carrying the fig's sweetness. The rava soaks up the fig, milk and ghee into fluffy grains, giving a heartier, more traditional halwa.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the semolina to a nutty gold and keeps this halwa's grains rich and non-sticky

steps: Soak 200 g dried figs in 1.5 cups warm water for 45 minutes, then blend with the soaking water into a smooth puree.
Simmer the fig puree with 1 cup milk and 0.33 cup sugar on low for 6 minutes into a warm, pourable fig syrup and keep it hot.
Heat 4 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a kadhai and roast 0.5 cup fine semolina on medium-low for 5 minutes until nutty and pale gold.
Pour the hot fig syrup into the roasted rava in a slow stream while stirring hard to avoid lumps, then cook covered on low for 4 minutes until the grains swell soft.
Fold in 2 tbsp raisins and 0.5 tsp cardamom and drizzle in the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, stirring until glossy and fluffy.
Roast 0.25 cup walnuts for a minute, fold most in, and serve the halwa warm topped with the rest.
tips: Always pour the hot fig syrup, never cold, onto the roasted rava so the semolina does not clump.
Roast the semolina until it smells nutty; under-roasted rava tastes raw and pasty.
Keep it slightly loose off the heat as the semolina keeps drinking in liquid as it sits.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm and fluffy, garnished with walnuts, a comforting winter halwa after a simple meal.

variations.name: Anjeer Khoya Halwa
variations.description: A decadent mithai-shop style halwa where the fig puree is cooked down with khoya into a dense, milk-rich fudge topped with a shower of pistachios. The mawa lends a creamy, caramelised depth that turns anjeer into a shop-window barfi-halwa.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: binds the khoya and fig into a glossy fudge that can be spooned soft or set to slice

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: steeped in warm milk to perfume and colour this richer fig halwa

steps: Soak 250 g dried figs in 0.75 cup warm water for 45 minutes, then blend into a thick puree.
Crumble 150 g khoya and roast it in 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on low for 5 minutes until it softens and smells nutty and caramelised.
Add the fig puree, 0.33 cup sugar and 0.5 cup milk and cook on medium-low for 10 minutes, stirring, until the mixture thickens and darkens.
Steep 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk and stir it in with 0.5 tsp cardamom.
Drizzle in the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and cook until the halwa turns glossy and pulls from the sides of the pan.
Fold in half the pistachios and serve warm, or set in a tray and slice, topping with the rest.
tips: Roast the khoya well before adding the fruit, as raw-tasting mawa flattens the whole halwa.
For a spoonable halwa keep it soft; for barfi cook until it cleanly leaves the pan and then set it.
A pinch of saffron makes this festive version look and smell truly special.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm in bowls or as set squares showered with pistachios, a rich sweet for Diwali and Eid platters.

variations.name: Classic Rajasthani Bajre Ka Churma
variations.description: The beloved Marwari sweet where thick pearl-millet dumplings are slow-fried in ghee, cooled, coarsely crushed and folded with more ghee and jaggery into a warm, nutty crumble. Earthy and rich, it is winter comfort food traditionally served alongside dal-baati or eaten on its own by the spoonful.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Bilona ghee both fries the muthiya and binds the crumble, giving churma its signature richness

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: Natural jaggery sweetens the crumble with a deep, mineral warmth that suits earthy bajra

steps: Mix 1.5 cups bajra flour, 0.5 cup wheat flour, 2 tbsp semolina and 0.25 tsp salt, rub in 3 tbsp of the ghee until crumbly, then knead with warm water into a stiff, tight dough and rest 10 minutes.
Shape the dough into 6 to 8 thick flattened dumplings and press a dent in the centre so they cook through evenly.
Heat the remaining ghee for frying in a deep pan and slow-fry the dumplings on low for 15 to 18 minutes, turning often, until deep golden-brown and cooked to the core, then drain and cool completely.
Break the cooled dumplings into chunks and grind in batches to a coarse, sandy crumble, sieving out any hard bits and regrinding them.
While the crumble is still warm, mix in 0.75 cup jaggery powder, 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and 10 chopped almonds, tossing well so the jaggery melts slightly into the churma.
Drizzle 2 tbsp of warm ghee over the top, fold through until glossy and fragrant, and serve warm or at room temperature.
tips: Fry the muthiya on low heat for a long time so the centre cooks fully; a raw core makes lumpy churma.
Add the jaggery while the crumble is warm so it melts just enough to bind without turning sticky.
Grind the churma coarse for texture, or finer if you plan to shape it into ladoos later.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm with dal-baati and a bowl of extra ghee, or on its own after a winter meal.

variations.name: Bajra Churma Ladoo
variations.description: The festive hand-rolled form of churma, where the warm ghee-and-jaggery millet crumble is bound with melted jaggery and shaped into firm round ladoos studded with nuts. Portable and long-keeping, these earthy ladoos are made for Makar Sankranti and winter celebrations.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee fries the dumplings and binds the ladoos so they hold a firm, glossy shape

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: Melted jaggery is the binder that sets these earthy bajra ladoos firm

steps: Rub 3 tbsp ghee into 1.5 cups bajra flour, 0.5 cup wheat flour and 0.25 tsp salt, then knead with warm water into a stiff dough and shape into 6 thick dumplings.
Slow-fry the dumplings in the remaining ghee on low for 16 to 18 minutes until deep golden and cooked through, then cool and grind to a fine crumble.
Chop 10 cashews and lightly toast them with 2 tbsp raisins and 1 tbsp poppy seeds in 1 tbsp ghee until fragrant.
Melt 1 cup jaggery powder with 2 tbsp water in a pan on low, stirring, until it forms a thick syrup that reaches a soft-ball stage where a drop holds shape in cold water.
Working quickly, mix the fine crumble, 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and the toasted nuts into the warm jaggery syrup until it clumps together.
While still warm enough to handle, grease your palms with ghee and roll the mixture into tight round ladoos, then cool completely so they firm up.
tips: Grind the crumble fine for ladoos so they bind smoothly without cracking.
Take the jaggery syrup only to soft-ball stage; overcooked syrup makes hard, dry ladoos.
Shape the ladoos while the mixture is warm, as it becomes too crumbly to roll once cold.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve as a winter festival sweet with masala chai, and store in an airtight tin for up to two weeks.

variations.name: Dry-Fruit and Gond Bajra Churma
variations.description: A strengthening winter version enriched with puffed edible gum (gond) and a generous handful of fried dry fruits, in the spirit of a new-mother's tonic. The crisp gond and toasted nuts give the earthy churma extra crunch, warmth and nourishment.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee puffs the gond, fries the nuts and binds this rich winter-tonic churma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: Jaggery sweetens the tonic churma with warming, iron-rich depth

steps: Rub 3 tbsp ghee into 1.5 cups bajra flour, 0.5 cup wheat flour and 0.25 tsp salt, knead stiff with warm water, shape into thick dumplings and slow-fry in ghee on low for 16 minutes until deep golden; cool and grind to a coarse crumble.
Heat 3 tbsp ghee in a small pan on medium and fry 3 tbsp gond in batches for about 1 minute each until they puff up like popcorn, then drain and crush lightly.
In the same ghee toast 12 almonds and 12 cashews until golden, chop them, and warm 0.25 cup chopped dates until soft.
Fold the crushed gond, toasted nuts and dates into the warm bajra crumble with 0.5 tsp cardamom and 0.5 tsp dry ginger powder.
Mix in 0.75 cup jaggery powder while the crumble is still warm so it melts slightly and binds the churma.
Drizzle over 2 tbsp warm ghee, toss until glossy, and serve warm or press into rough mounds.
tips: Fry the gond on medium heat so each piece puffs fully; underfried gond stays hard and chewy.
Dry ginger powder adds warmth and makes this a genuinely restorative winter sweet.
Store cool and reheat gently, as the ghee firms up when cold.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm on cold mornings with a glass of hot milk, especially through the winter months.

variations.name: Til-Coconut Bajra Churma with Khandsari
variations.description: A Sankranti-inspired take where toasted sesame and desiccated coconut are folded into the millet crumble, sweetened with mild unrefined khandsari for a lighter, paler finish. The nutty sesame and coconut make it fragrant and festive without the deep molasses note of jaggery.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee fries the muthiya and carries the toasted sesame and coconut through the crumble

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari Sugar
ingredients.note: Unrefined khandsari gives a mild, pale sweetness that lets the sesame and coconut shine

steps: Rub 3 tbsp ghee into 1.5 cups bajra flour, 0.5 cup wheat flour and 0.25 tsp salt, knead stiff with warm water, shape into thick dumplings and slow-fry in ghee on low for 16 minutes until golden; cool and grind to a coarse crumble.
Dry-roast 3 tbsp sesame seeds in a pan on low for 2 minutes until they pop and smell nutty, then roast 0.33 cup desiccated coconut for 1 minute until pale gold.
Powder 0.75 cup khandsari sugar fine in a grinder so it blends smoothly into the warm crumble.
Fold the toasted sesame, coconut, powdered khandsari and 0.5 tsp cardamom into the warm bajra crumble until evenly mixed.
Drizzle 2 tbsp warm ghee over the top and toss until the churma turns glossy and holds together lightly.
Scatter 10 chopped pistachios over the top and serve warm or at room temperature.
tips: Powder the khandsari before adding, as its crystals are coarser than boora and will not dissolve on their own.
Roast the sesame just until it pops; over-roasting turns it bitter.
Since khandsari is milder than jaggery, taste and add a little more if you like it sweeter.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve as a Sankranti sweet alongside til-gud ladoo, with a cup of ginger chai.

variations.name: Classic Rajasthani Bajre Ki Khichdi
variations.description: A rustic desert one-pot of coarsely pounded pearl millet cooked soft with moong dal and finished with a lavish cumin-ghee tempering. Warming and grounding, it is the winter staple of Rajasthani and Haryanvi homes, traditionally topped with a puddle of melting ghee and eaten with buttermilk.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Bilona ghee makes the cumin tempering and the generous finishing pool that defines this khichdi

steps: Coarsely crush 1 cup bajra in a mortar to loosen the husk, winnow or rinse well, then soak with 0.5 cup moong dal in plenty of water for 30 minutes and drain.
Add the drained grains to a pressure cooker with 4 cups water, 0.5 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt, and cook on medium for 5 to 6 whistles until the bajra is soft and porridge-like.
Open the cooker after the pressure drops, stir in another 0.5 cup hot water if it is too thick, and mash lightly to a creamy consistency.
Heat 4 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a small pan on medium, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds and 0.25 tsp hing for 20 seconds, then add 1 inch grated ginger and 2 slit green chillies and fry for 30 seconds.
Pour the sizzling tempering into the khichdi with the remaining 0.25 tsp salt and 0.5 tsp black pepper, and stir through for 2 minutes on low.
Simmer for 3 minutes more until everything is glossy and well combined, then serve hot with an extra spoon of ghee on top.
tips: Crush the bajra coarsely to help remove the husk and speed up cooking to a soft, creamy texture.
Bajra khichdi thickens fast as it cools, so keep it looser than you want and loosen with hot water before serving.
Do not skimp on the ghee; the richness balances the earthy, slightly bitter millet.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve piping hot with a bowl of cold buttermilk or plain curd, a spoon of white butter and a side of jaggery.

variations.name: Lehsuni Bajra Khichdi with Garlic Tadka
variations.description: A bold Haryanvi-Marwari version finished with a smoking garlic and red-chilli tempering in mustard oil that pours over the soft millet in a fiery red slick. The pungent garlic cuts the earthiness of the bajra, making a robust winter comfort bowl.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Sharp wood-pressed mustard oil carries the smoking garlic tadka poured over the khichdi

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: A finishing spoon of ghee rounds the pungent garlic tadka into the millet

steps: Coarsely crush 1 cup bajra, rinse well, soak with 0.5 cup moong dal for 30 minutes and drain.
Pressure-cook the grains with 4 cups water, 0.5 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt for 5 to 6 whistles until soft, then mash lightly to a creamy khichdi and keep warm.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil in a small pan until it just smokes, then lower the heat to tame its sharpness.
Add 1 tsp cumin seeds, 12 sliced garlic cloves and 3 broken dried red chillies and fry for 1 to 2 minutes until the garlic turns deep golden and fragrant.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder so it colours the oil red without burning, then pour the sizzling tadka over the khichdi with the remaining 0.25 tsp salt.
Add 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, fold everything through on low for 2 minutes until glossy and aromatic, and serve at once.
tips: Slice the garlic rather than crush it so it fries into golden, visible slivers on top.
Add the chilli powder off the heat to keep the tadka red and prevent a burnt, bitter taste.
Bring the mustard oil to a light smoke first to mellow its raw pungency before the garlic goes in.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with cold buttermilk, a wedge of jaggery and a raw onion to match the garlicky punch.

variations.name: Bajra Vegetable Khichdi
variations.description: A wholesome winter one-pot where soft pearl millet and moong dal are cooked with diced seasonal vegetables and warm spices into a nourishing meal-in-a-bowl. Peas, carrot and beans add colour, sweetness and body, turning the rustic khichdi into a complete dinner.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee tempers the whole spices and enriches this vegetable-laden khichdi

steps: Coarsely crush 1 cup bajra, rinse, soak with 0.5 cup moong dal for 30 minutes and drain; dice 1 carrot and 8 beans and keep 0.5 cup peas ready.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pressure cooker on medium, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds, add 1 chopped onion and fry for 3 minutes until golden, then add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
Add 1 chopped tomato, 0.5 tsp turmeric, 0.75 tsp red chilli powder and the diced vegetables and saute for 3 minutes.
Stir in the drained bajra and dal, 4.5 cups water and 1.25 tsp salt, close the cooker and cook on medium for 5 to 6 whistles until the millet is soft.
Once the pressure drops, open and mash lightly to a creamy consistency, loosening with hot water if needed.
Stir in 0.5 tsp garam masala, simmer for 2 minutes on low, and serve hot with a spoon of ghee on top.
tips: Cut the vegetables small and even so they cook through in the same time as the millet.
Add hot water, not cold, when loosening the khichdi so it stays smooth and does not go gluey.
A squeeze of lemon at the table lifts the earthy millet and sweet vegetables.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve as a one-dish dinner with plain curd, pickle and a crisp papad on the side.

variations.name: Gujarati Bajra Khichdi with Peanuts
variations.description: A Kathiawadi-style bajra khichdi brightened with crunchy peanuts, a mild green-chilli-ginger paste and a sweet-savoury balance. Softer and lighter than the Rajasthani bowl, it is finished with fresh coriander and eaten with a spoon of chaas.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee fries the peanuts and tempers the spices for this Kathiawadi khichdi

steps: Coarsely crush 1 cup bajra, rinse, soak with 0.5 cup moong dal for 30 minutes and drain.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pressure cooker on medium and fry 0.33 cup raw peanuts for 2 minutes until they turn nutty, then push them aside.
In the same ghee splutter 1 tsp cumin seeds, 0.5 tsp mustard seeds, 0.25 tsp hing and 10 curry leaves for 20 seconds, then add 1 tbsp ginger-green chilli paste and fry 30 seconds.
Add the drained bajra and dal, 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1.25 tsp salt and 4.5 cups water, close the cooker and cook on medium for 5 to 6 whistles until soft.
After the pressure drops, open and mash lightly to a soft, creamy khichdi, adding hot water if it is thick.
Fold in 3 tbsp chopped coriander, simmer 2 minutes on low, and serve hot with the fried peanuts studded through.
tips: Fry the peanuts first and keep them slightly crunchy so they hold texture in the soft khichdi.
Use fresh ginger-green chilli paste rather than powder for the bright Gujarati flavour.
This khichdi is meant to be soft and loose, so err on the side of more water.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm with a tall glass of spiced chaas and a spoon of mango chundo on the side.

variations.name: Classic Beetroot Halwa
variations.description: Beetroot halwa is the ruby-red cousin of gajar halwa, made by slow-cooking grated beetroot in full-fat milk until it reduces to a soft, glistening mass, then sweetening and enriching it with ghee-fried nuts. The earthy sweetness of the beet turns jewel-bright and fragrant with cardamom.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: sautes the grated beetroot and fries the nuts for a glossy, aromatic halwa

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: sweetens the reduced beetroot cleanly without dulling its bright colour

steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the Anveshan Ghee in a heavy kadhai and fry 3 tbsp cashews and 2 tbsp raisins over medium heat until golden and plump, then lift out.
Add 4 cups grated beetroot to the same pan and saute over medium heat for 5 minutes until it softens and smells earthy.
Pour in 2.5 cups full-fat milk and simmer over medium-low heat, stirring often, for 18 to 20 minutes until the milk is almost fully absorbed.
Stir in 0.5 cup Anveshan Khandsari, which loosens the mixture, and cook for 6 to 8 minutes more until it thickens again.
Add the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and cook, stirring, until the halwa turns glossy and pulls from the sides of the pan.
Fold in 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and the fried nuts, then serve the beetroot halwa warm.
tips: Grate the beetroot fine so it cooks down evenly; coarse shreds stay firm and stringy in the halwa.
Add the sweetener only after the milk has reduced, as sugar released early makes the beetroot watery and slow to thicken.
Wear gloves while grating if you want to keep the beet stain off your hands.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm in bowls as a winter dessert, garnished with extra fried cashews, or chill and top with a scoop of vanilla for a striking contrast.

variations.name: Beetroot Mawa Halwa
variations.description: A quicker, richer halwa that swaps long milk-reduction for crumbled mawa, giving a dense, grainy, barfi-like texture in half the time. The khoya lends a deep milky richness that balances the beet's earthiness, making it a favourite for festive platters.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the beetroot and melts into the mawa for a dense, festive halwa

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: sweetens the mawa-rich halwa without overpowering the beetroot

steps: Heat 4 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a heavy pan, add 4 cups grated beetroot and saute over medium heat for 8 minutes until softened and glossy.
Pour in 0.5 cup milk and cook for 6 to 7 minutes until it is fully absorbed and the beetroot looks dry.
Add 1 cup crumbled mawa and stir over low heat for 4 to 5 minutes until it melts into the beetroot and the mixture turns grainy.
Stir in 0.5 cup Anveshan Khandsari and cook for 4 minutes more until the sugar dissolves and the halwa thickens to a dense mass.
Fold in 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and half the slivered almonds and mix well.
Spoon into bowls, scatter the remaining almonds on top and serve the mawa halwa warm.
tips: Roast the mawa gently and keep the flame low, as khoya catches and browns fast once it starts melting.
For a firmer, cuttable halwa, press it into a greased tray while warm and slice into diamonds once set.
Use fresh, soft mawa; hard, dry khoya stays lumpy and refuses to blend into the beetroot.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm on festive thalis, or set it firm and cut into barfi diamonds garnished with a sliver of edible silver leaf.

variations.name: Vegan Beetroot Coconut Halwa
variations.description: A dairy-free halwa that simmers grated beetroot in coconut milk and jaggery, cooked in coconut oil for a wholesome, earthy sweet with a faint tropical note. The jaggery deepens the beet's colour to a dark ruby and adds a mineral-rich caramel edge.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: sautes the beetroot and keeps this halwa completely plant-based

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: melts into the beetroot to sweeten it with earthy caramel depth

steps: Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil in a pan and toast 3 tbsp chopped cashews over medium heat until golden, then set aside.
Add 4 cups grated beetroot to the oil and saute for 6 to 7 minutes until it softens and loses its raw smell.
Pour in 1.5 cups thick coconut milk and simmer over medium-low heat for 18 to 20 minutes until it is mostly absorbed.
Lower the heat, stir in 0.5 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder off the boil so it does not split, and cook for 5 minutes until melted and thick.
Mix in 0.25 cup desiccated coconut and cook for 3 minutes more until the halwa turns glossy and holds together.
Fold in 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and the toasted cashews, then serve warm.
tips: Add the jaggery off the boil and on a low flame, as pouring it into fiercely bubbling coconut milk can curdle it.
Full-fat coconut milk gives the richest body; thin carton coconut milk leaves the halwa watery.
A pinch of dry ginger powder alongside the cardamom makes this a warming winter version.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm as a vegan festive dessert, garnished with toasted coconut flakes and cashews.

variations.name: Beetroot Carrot Halwa
variations.description: A two-toned halwa that marbles grated beetroot with red carrots so the ruby of the beet meets the orange of the gajar in one pan. Slow-cooked in milk and ghee, it balances the beet's earthiness with the carrot's mellow sweetness for a livelier, festive-looking pudding.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: sautes both roots and fries the pistachios for a glossy two-toned halwa

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: sweetens the mixed roots with a warm, earthy caramel note

steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the Anveshan Ghee and fry 3 tbsp chopped pistachios and 2 tbsp raisins over medium heat until golden and plump, then set aside.
Add 2 cups grated beetroot and 2 cups grated red carrots to the pan and saute over medium heat for 6 minutes until softened.
Pour in 2.5 cups full-fat milk and simmer over medium-low heat for 18 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until the milk is nearly absorbed.
Add the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and cook for 4 minutes until the roots turn glossy and dry.
Take the pan off the boil, stir in 0.5 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder and cook on low for 5 minutes until it melts and the halwa thickens.
Fold in 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and the fried nuts and raisins, then serve the halwa warm.
tips: Keep the beetroot and carrot in equal measure so neither colour nor flavour overwhelms the other.
Stir the jaggery in off the heat so the milk in the halwa does not split against the acidity.
Delicate red Delhi carrots give the sweetest result; thick woody carrots stay fibrous even after long cooking.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm in winter as a festive halwa, garnished with chopped pistachios, or layer it with the plain versions for a colourful dessert.

variations.name: Classic Beetroot Tikki
variations.description: Beetroot Tikki is a jewel-toned patty of grated beetroot and boiled potato, spiced with cumin and chaat masala and shallow-fried till crusty. The beetroot lends an earthy sweetness and a stunning magenta hue that makes these tikkis a favourite party starter.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: shallow-frying in bilona ghee gives the tikki a crisp, nutty golden crust

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sattu
ingredients.note: roasted sattu soaks up the beetroot's moisture and binds the tikki with a protein boost

steps: Boil the 3 potatoes until soft, peel and mash them smooth while still warm in a large mixing bowl.
Squeeze the 2 cups grated beetroot firmly to remove excess juice, then add it to the mashed potato so the mix does not turn watery.
Dry-roast 3 tbsp Anveshan Sattu for a minute until fragrant and stir it in to absorb any remaining moisture and bind the tikki.

Mix in the grated ginger, 2 finely chopped green chillies, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1 tsp chaat masala, 0.5 tsp red chilli powder, 3 tbsp coriander and 1 tsp salt, then knead into a firm dough and shape into 10 round patties.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on a griddle over medium heat and shallow-fry the tikkis in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side until a deep crust forms.
Add the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee as needed between batches and drain the cooked tikkis on paper before serving hot.
tips: Squeeze the grated beetroot really well, as its juice is the main cause of tikkis that refuse to hold together.
If the dough still feels wet, add another spoonful of roasted sattu rather than potato to firm it up.
Fry on steady medium heat so the crust sets slowly and the beetroot cooks through without burning.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with mint-coriander chutney and thin onion rings, or tuck into a slider bun for a beetroot burger.

variations.name: Beetroot Quinoa Tikki
variations.description: A wholesome, gluten-free take that binds grated beetroot with cooked quinoa and mashed chickpeas instead of potato, for a nutty, protein-rich patty. Shallow-fried in wood-pressed olive oil, it stays hearty and satisfying while keeping the beetroot's earthy sweetness front and centre.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Olive Oil
ingredients.note: cold-pressed olive oil shallow-fries these healthy tikkis with a clean, light finish

steps: Mash the 1 cup boiled chickpeas coarsely with a fork so some texture remains for bite.
Squeeze the 2 cups grated beetroot dry and combine it with the mashed chickpeas and 1 cup cooked quinoa in a bowl.
Add 0.33 cup powdered oats to soak up moisture, then mix in grated ginger, 2 chopped green chillies, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp amchur, 3 tbsp coriander and 1 tsp salt.
Knead the mixture into a firm dough, adding a little extra powdered oats if needed, and shape into 10 patties.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Olive Oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat and shallow-fry the tikkis for 4 minutes per side until crisp and set.
Cook the remaining batch in the rest of the Anveshan Olive Oil and drain briefly on paper before serving warm.
tips: Cook the quinoa until just tender and let it cool fully so it does not add extra moisture to the mix.
Powdered oats are the key binder here, so add them gradually until the dough feels firm enough to shape.
These are more delicate than potato tikkis, so flip them gently with a wide spatula.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve on a green salad with a dollop of hung-curd dip for a light, protein-packed meal.

variations.name: Cheese-Corn Stuffed Beetroot Tikki
variations.description: A cafe-style indulgence where the crimson beetroot patty hides a molten pocket of sweet corn and cheese that oozes when you cut in. The savoury, gooey centre plays gorgeously against the earthy-sweet beetroot shell for a real crowd-pleaser.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: griddling in ghee crisps the shell while the stuffed cheese melts inside

steps: Boil, peel and mash the 3 potatoes, then mix in the firmly squeezed 2 cups grated beetroot to form the coloured outer dough.
Add 0.5 cup bread crumbs, 2 chopped green chillies, 1 tsp chaat masala, 3 tbsp coriander and 1 tsp salt and knead into a firm, shapeable dough.
For the filling, mix 0.75 cup sweet corn with 0.75 cup grated mozzarella, 0.5 tsp black pepper and a pinch of salt.
Flatten a portion of the beetroot dough in your palm, place a spoon of the corn-cheese filling in the centre, seal the edges and shape into 8 stuffed patties.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on a griddle over medium heat and cook the stuffed tikkis for 4 minutes per side until the crust is deep and crisp.
Fry the remaining tikkis in the rest of the Anveshan Ghee and serve immediately while the cheese is still molten inside.
tips: Seal the stuffed edges tightly and chill the tikkis for 15 minutes so the cheese does not leak while frying.
Use enough bread crumbs in the dough so the shell stays firm around the soft, melting filling.
Cut one open at the table so guests see the cheese pull against the bright beetroot casing.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve halved to show the molten centre, with a smoky tomato salsa or garlic dip on the side.

variations.name: Baked Beetroot Beans Tikki
variations.description: A guilt-free oven-baked patty where beetroot meets mashed green beans and nutty khapli atta for extra fibre and a rustic crumb. Brushed with ghee and baked till the edges crisp, these tikkis feel wholesome without the deep-fry.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: nutty khapli atta binds the tikki and browns beautifully in the oven

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: brushed over the tikkis so they crisp and turn golden while baking

steps: Preheat the oven to 200C and line a baking tray with parchment brushed lightly with a little Anveshan Ghee.
Steam the 1 cup chopped French beans for 4 minutes until just tender, then mash them coarsely with the 1 cup boiled sweet potato.
Squeeze the 2 cups grated beetroot dry and mix it into the bean-sweet potato mash along with 0.5 cup Anveshan Khapli Atta to bind.
Stir in grated ginger, 2 chopped green chillies, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 3 tbsp coriander and 1 tsp salt, then shape into 10 patties.
Arrange the tikkis on the tray, brush the tops generously with Anveshan Ghee, and bake for 15 minutes.
Flip each tikki, brush again with ghee, and bake another 12 to 15 minutes until firm and crisp at the edges, then rest 2 minutes before serving.
tips: Toast the khapli atta lightly before mixing if you want an even deeper nutty aroma in the tikkis.
Brush ghee on both bakes, as this is what gives the oven-baked tikkis their golden colour.
Chop the beans very fine so they cook through fully and do not leave hard bits in the patty.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm with a beetroot-hued raita and a scatter of toasted sesame for a wholesome starter.

variations.name: Classic Rajasthani Sukhe Besan Ke Gatte
variations.description: The dry, snacky avatar of Marwari gatte, where steamed gram-flour logs are sliced into coins and tossed in a bright ghee tempering of cumin, hing and dry masala. With no gravy at all, every coin turns glossy and spice-coated, eaten as a teatime bite or a travel food that keeps for days.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Bilona ghee coats each gatta coin and blooms the dry masala the classic Marwari way

steps: Mix 1.5 cups besan with 0.5 tsp ajwain, 0.25 tsp turmeric, 0.5 tsp salt, 1 tbsp of the ghee, 2 tbsp yogurt and a pinch of hing, then add water little by little to knead a stiff, smooth dough, about 5 minutes.
Roll the dough into 3 finger-thick ropes and steam or boil them in salted water for 10 to 12 minutes until firm and floating; cool and slice into 1 cm coins.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a kadai on medium and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds and 0.25 tsp hing for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Lower the heat, add 0.25 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder and 1.5 tbsp coriander powder and stir for 15 seconds, adding 1 tbsp water so the spices do not scorch.
Add the gatta coins and 0.5 tsp salt and toss on medium for 5 to 6 minutes until every coin is coated and the edges catch a little golden colour.
Sprinkle 0.75 tsp amchur, 0.5 tsp garam masala and 3 tbsp chopped coriander, toss for 1 minute more, and serve warm or at room temperature.
tips: Knead the dough stiff and smooth; a soft or cracked dough gives crumbly gatte that break while tossing.
Slice the boiled logs only after they cool fully, or warm gatte tear instead of cutting into neat coins.
Save the gatta boiling water to loosen the masala if it dries out while tossing.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve as a dry side with dal-rice and phulka, or pack as a spiced snack with a cup of masala chai.

variations.name: Lehsuni Chilli Fried Gatte
variations.description: A punchy dry gatte where boiled coins are shallow-fried crisp, then tossed in a garlicky red-chilli tempering with browned garlic slivers. Sharp, hot and moreish, it eats like a spicy dry snack rather than a mild sabzi.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A clean wood-pressed oil crisps the gatta coins and carries the garlic-chilli tadka

steps: Knead 1.5 cups besan with 0.5 tsp ajwain, 0.25 tsp turmeric, 0.5 tsp salt and 1 tbsp of the oil into a stiff dough, roll into ropes and boil in salted water for 12 minutes until firm; cool and cut into 1 cm coins.
Heat 4 tbsp Anveshan Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil in a pan on medium and shallow-fry the gatta coins for 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp at the edges, then lift out.
In the same oil crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds, add 12 sliced garlic cloves and 4 broken dried red chillies and fry for 1 to 2 minutes until the garlic turns golden and aromatic.
Lower the heat, add the remaining 0.25 tsp turmeric, 1.5 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder and 1 tbsp sesame seeds and stir for 20 seconds until the sesame pops.
Return the fried gatte with 0.5 tsp salt and toss on medium for 3 minutes until every coin is coated in the sticky garlic-chilli masala.
Finish with 1 tbsp lemon juice and 3 tbsp chopped coriander, toss once, and serve hot.
tips: Fry the gatte until genuinely crisp so they stay firm against the moist garlic tadka.
Take care not to burn the garlic; pull it to golden, since browner garlic turns bitter.
Add the lemon only off the heat to keep its fresh sourness bright.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve as a spicy dry starter with drinks, or alongside plain dal and rice to cut the heat.

variations.name: Methi Besan Ke Gatte
variations.description: A winter-style dry gatte where fresh fenugreek leaves are kneaded straight into the besan dough, giving a faintly bitter, herby coin that is pan-tossed in a simple ghee masala. The methi makes these gatte greener, softer and more fragrant than the plain version.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee mellows the fresh methi and glosses the herby gatte in the dry masala

steps: Chop and wash 1 cup fresh methi leaves, then knead into 1.5 cups besan with 2 tbsp yogurt, 0.25 tsp turmeric, 0.75 tsp fennel seeds, 0.5 tsp salt, 1 tsp ginger paste and 1 tbsp ghee, adding water slowly to a stiff smooth dough.
Roll into 3 finger-thick ropes and steam or boil in salted water for 12 minutes until firm; cool and slice into 1 cm coins.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a kadai, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds and 0.25 tsp hing for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Lower the heat, add the remaining 0.25 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder and 1 tbsp coriander powder and stir for 15 seconds with a splash of water so they do not burn.
Add the methi gatta coins and 0.5 tsp salt and toss on medium for 5 to 6 minutes until they are evenly coated and lightly crisped at the edges.
Rest for 3 minutes off the heat so the fenugreek aroma settles, then serve warm.
tips: Squeeze the washed methi dry before kneading so the dough does not turn slack and sticky.
A little fennel in the dough rounds off the fenugreek's bitterness beautifully.
If the methi is very bitter, sprinkle a little salt on the chopped leaves, rest 5 minutes and squeeze before use.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with plain paratha or bajra roti and a bowl of curd to offset the gentle bitterness.

variations.name: Tawa Peanut-Masala Dry Gatte
variations.description: A street-style dry gatte griddled on a hot tawa with crushed roasted peanuts and a smoky pav-bhaji-like masala. The nuts add crunch and the tawa char gives a roadside sizzle, making this the most snackable take of all.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee on the hot tawa gives these gatte their glossy roadside char and aroma

steps: Knead 1.5 cups besan with 0.5 tsp ajwain, 0.25 tsp turmeric, 0.5 tsp salt and 1 tbsp ghee into a stiff dough, roll into ropes and boil in salted water for 12 minutes; cool and cut into 1 cm coins.
Coarsely crush 0.5 cup roasted peanuts, keeping some texture.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on a flat tawa on medium-high, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds, add 1 finely chopped onion and fry for 3 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the remaining 0.25 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp pav bhaji masala and 0.75 tsp red chilli powder and stir for 20 seconds with a splash of water.
Add the gatta coins and 0.5 tsp salt and griddle-toss on the hot tawa for 5 to 6 minutes, pressing gently, until they catch charred spots and take on the masala.
Scatter the crushed peanuts, 0.75 tsp chaat masala, 1 tbsp lemon juice and 3 tbsp coriander, toss for 1 minute, and serve sizzling.
tips: Keep the tawa hot and press the coins lightly so they develop the roadside char.
Add the peanuts near the end so they stay crunchy rather than turning soft.
Chaat masala and lemon go in only at the finish for a fresh, tangy street-food hit.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot off the tawa as a chaat-style snack with green chutney and a sprinkle of sev.

variations.name: Classic Boondi Kadhi
variations.description: A quick, elegant kadhi where crisp besan boondi pearls are dropped into a smooth soured yogurt gravy, soaking up the tang until they turn soft and juicy. Far faster than pakora kadhi yet just as satisfying, with a fragrant cumin-and-curry-leaf ghee tempering. A weekday favourite across UP and Rajasthan.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee carries the cumin and curry-leaf tempering into the kadhi

steps: Whisk the sour yogurt with besan, turmeric, red chilli powder and salt into 3.5 cups water until completely smooth and lump-free.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pot, crackle cumin, fenugreek seeds and grated ginger for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the yogurt batter and bring to a boil while stirring continuously so the yogurt does not split.
Lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 18 minutes until the kadhi thickens and loses its raw besan taste.
Meanwhile soak the boondi in warm water for 2 minutes and gently squeeze, then add to the simmering kadhi and cook 4 minutes until plump.
Finish with a tempering of the remaining ghee sizzled with dried red chillies and curry leaves poured over the top.
tips: Soak store-bought boondi briefly so it turns soft and sheds excess oil before going in.
Add the boondi close to serving; left too long it dissolves into the gravy.
Use tangy yogurt or add a squeeze of lemon so the kadhi has a lively sourness.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve over steamed rice with a spoon of ghee, papad and a sharp lemon pickle.

variations.name: Rajasthani Masala Boondi Kadhi
variations.description: A bolder Marwari version using spiced masala boondi and a thinner, pourable kadhi soured sharply with extra yogurt. Cooked in a garlicky asafoetida tempering, it is meant to be soupy and tangy, ladled generously over rice or khichdi. The spiced boondi adds pockets of heat throughout.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed groundnut oil carries the garlic-asafoetida tempering typical of Marwari kadhi

steps: Whisk the sour yogurt, besan, turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder and salt into 4 cups water until smooth and thin.
Heat the Anveshan Groundnut Oil, crackle mustard and cumin seeds, then add crushed garlic and asafoetida and fry for 30 seconds until the garlic is golden.
Pour in the yogurt batter and bring to a rolling boil while stirring so it stays smooth.
Simmer uncovered on low heat for 18 minutes, keeping the kadhi deliberately thin and pourable.
Add the masala boondi and simmer just 3 minutes so it swells but keeps a little bite.
Taste and adjust the sourness and salt, then rest off heat for 2 minutes before serving.
tips: Keep this kadhi thin as Rajasthanis like to drink it alongside bajra roti.
Add masala boondi last since its spices bleed quickly into the gravy.
A double hit of garlic and hing is essential to the Marwari character here.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve soupy over hot rice or with bajra roti and a dollop of white butter on the side.

variations.name: Gujarati Sweet Boondi Kadhi
variations.description: A silky, thin Gujarati-style kadhi balanced with jaggery for the signature sweet-sour note, tempered in ghee with cinnamon, clove and green chilli-ginger paste. Boondi is folded in for texture in a gravy that is delicate, aromatic and only lightly thickened. A gentle, almost drinkable curry.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee tempers the whole spices for the fragrant Gujarati base

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: jaggery gives the signature Gujarati sweet-sour balance without refined sugar

steps: Whisk the yogurt, besan, turmeric and salt into 3.5 cups water until very smooth and thin.
Heat the Anveshan Ghee in a pot, temper cumin, cinnamon, cloves, curry leaves and the ginger-green chilli paste for 40 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the yogurt batter and bring to a boil while stirring constantly to keep it silky.
Add the Anveshan Jaggery Powder and simmer uncovered on low for 15 minutes until the kadhi is lightly thickened and glossy.
Soak the boondi in warm water for 2 minutes, squeeze gently and stir into the kadhi for the last 3 minutes.
Check the sweet-sour balance, adjusting jaggery or a squeeze of lemon, then serve warm.
tips: Keep this kadhi thin and pourable, as Gujarati kadhi is meant to be almost soupy.
Balance jaggery against the yogurt's sourness by tasting, since curd tanginess varies.
Whole spices give aroma but fish out the cinnamon and cloves before serving if you prefer.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve alongside steamed rice and a dry aloo sabzi, or sip it warm on its own as Gujaratis often do.

variations.name: Dahi Boondi Raita Kadhi
variations.description: A chilled, no-simmer take that blurs the line between raita and kadhi, where soaked boondi floats in a lightly spiced, roasted-cumin yogurt loosened to a spoonable consistency and finished with a quick sizzling tarka. Cooling and instant, it is perfect for summer when a hot kadhi feels heavy. Tangy, creamy and refreshing.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: a small ghee tarka lifts the chilled yogurt with warm aromatics

steps: Whisk the thick yogurt with 1 cup chilled water, roasted cumin powder, black salt and salt until smooth and pourable.
Soak the boondi in warm water for 3 minutes, squeeze gently and fold into the yogurt along with finely chopped green chilli and coriander.
Heat the Anveshan Ghee in a small pan and splutter mustard seeds, the dried red chilli and curry leaves for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Pour the hot tarka over the chilled yogurt-boondi mixture and stir once so the warm aromatics streak through.
Chill for 10 minutes to let the boondi soften fully and the flavours meld.
Stir gently and adjust salt before serving cold.
tips: This dish is not simmered, so use fresh, non-sour yogurt for a cool, mild flavour.
Add the boondi close to serving so it keeps a little texture instead of dissolving.
Loosen with extra chilled water just before serving if it thickens on standing.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve chilled as a cooling side with jeera rice, hot parathas or a spicy pulao on a summer afternoon.

variations.name: Classic Cabbage Kofta
variations.description: Grated cabbage bound with besan and spices fries into light, savoury dumplings that soak up a homely onion-tomato gravy. A clever way to turn humble cabbage into a satisfying main, the koftas stay soft inside with a lacy crisp edge.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: builds the onion-tomato masala and lends the gravy a homely richness

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: fries the cabbage koftas to a crisp golden edge without turning greasy

steps: Grate the 3 cups cabbage, sprinkle with 0.25 tsp salt, rest for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the water and mix with 0.75 cup besan, chopped green chillies and 0.5 tsp salt into a thick batter.
Drop spoonfuls into the hot Anveshan Groundnut Oil and deep-fry over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and crisp, then drain on paper.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pan over medium heat, add the finely chopped onions, and saute for 6 minutes until golden brown.

Stir in 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute, then add the pureed tomatoes with 1 tsp chilli powder, 1.5 tsp coriander powder, 0.5 tsp turmeric and 0.5 tsp salt, and cook for 8 minutes until the ghee separates.
Add 1.5 cups water and simmer for 5 minutes until the gravy thickens, then stir in 0.5 tsp garam masala.
Add the koftas to the simmering gravy just 2 minutes before serving so they warm through yet keep a little bite.
tips: Squeeze the salted cabbage well, or the extra moisture makes the koftas absorb oil and turn soggy.
Keep the batter thick enough to hold shape; add a spoon more besan if it spreads in the oil.
Add the koftas to the gravy at the last moment so they stay intact instead of dissolving.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with phulka roti or steamed rice and a bowl of boondi raita to offset the spice.

variations.name: Bengali Cabbage Kofta in Poppy Gravy
variations.description: A Bengali-style bandhakopir kofta where cabbage dumplings simmer in a delicate posto gravy of ground poppy seeds and mustard. The nutty white sauce, mellow and faintly sweet, is a world apart from the fiery northern gravy and pairs beautifully with steamed rice.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: the defining pungent oil of Bengali cooking that carries the posto gravy

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sunflower Oil
ingredients.note: a neutral medium to deep-fry the koftas without overpowering the mild posto

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: adds the subtle sweetness Bengali gravies are known for

steps: Soak the 3 tbsp poppy seeds and 1 tsp mustard seeds in warm water for 15 minutes, then grind with 2 green chillies into a smooth white paste.
Squeeze the grated 3 cups cabbage dry, mix with 0.5 cup besan, 2 tbsp rice flour and 0.5 tsp salt, and shape into small koftas.
Deep-fry the koftas in the hot Anveshan Sunflower Oil over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until golden, then drain.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil until it smokes, lower the heat, and temper 0.5 tsp kalonji, 1 bay leaf and 1 slit green chilli for 20 seconds.
Add the poppy-mustard paste with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 0.75 tsp salt and 0.5 tsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder, and cook for 5 minutes on low, stirring, until the raw smell fades.
Pour in 1.5 cups water, simmer for 6 minutes until the posto gravy thickens, then fold in the koftas just before serving so they stay soft.
tips: Grind the poppy seeds with as little water as possible for a thick, luscious posto paste.
Cook the mustard-poppy paste on low heat only, as high heat turns the mustard bitter.
Add a slit green chilli whole at the end for aroma without extra heat, in true Bengali style.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with hot steamed rice and a wedge of lime, the way posto dishes are enjoyed in a Bengali meal.

variations.name: Baked Cabbage Kofta Makhani
variations.description: A lighter take where cabbage-oats koftas are baked instead of fried, then folded into a creamy tomato makhani gravy. You get all the indulgence of the classic with far less oil, and the oats give the dumplings a pleasant, hearty bite.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: enriches the makhani gravy and glazes the baked koftas before serving

ingredients.name: Anveshan Olive Oil
ingredients.note: brushed over the koftas so they crisp in the oven without deep-frying

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: balances the tang of the tomato makhani with natural sweetness

steps: Squeeze the grated 3 cups cabbage dry, mix with 0.5 cup oats, 0.25 cup besan and 0.5 tsp salt, and shape into 12 small balls.
Brush the koftas with 1 tbsp Anveshan Olive Oil and bake in a preheated oven at 200 C for 18 minutes, turning once, until firm and golden.
Boil the 5 tomatoes and 12 cashews in a cup of water for 8 minutes, cool, blend, and strain into a smooth puree.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pan over medium heat, add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, and saute for 30 seconds.
Pour in the strained tomato-cashew puree with 0.75 tsp salt and 1 tsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder, and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring, until glossy and thick.
Crush 1 tsp kasuri methi in, stir 3 tbsp cream off the heat, and gently fold in the baked koftas 2 minutes before serving.
tips: Bake the koftas until firm before saucing so they hold together in the gravy.
Strain the tomato puree for a silky makhani finish without any seeds or skin.
Toss the baked koftas in a spoon of the gravy first so they absorb flavour without going mushy.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a multigrain roti or steamed brown rice, drizzled with cream and a pinch of kasuri methi.

variations.name: Kolhapuri Cabbage Kofta
variations.description: A fiery Maharashtrian version where cabbage koftas plunge into a dark, coconut-based Kolhapuri masala crackling with dry red chillies and roasted spices. Bold, earthy and unapologetically hot, it is for those who love their kofta curry with a proper kick.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: fries the koftas and, reused, carries the pungent Kolhapuri masala

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: finishes the fiery gravy with a rounding richness

steps: Squeeze the grated 3 cups cabbage dry, mix with 0.5 cup besan and 0.5 tsp salt, and shape into small koftas.
Deep-fry the koftas in the hot Anveshan Groundnut Oil over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden, then drain and reserve the oil.
Dry-roast the 0.25 cup dry coconut, 4 red chillies, 1 tbsp coriander seeds and 1 tbsp sesame seeds until dark and fragrant, cool, and grind with a little water into a coarse dark paste.
Heat 3 tbsp of the reserved oil in a pan over medium heat, add the chopped onions, and fry for 6 minutes until browned, then add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute.
Stir in the ground Kolhapuri paste with 1 tsp goda masala, 0.5 tsp turmeric and 0.75 tsp salt, and cook for 6 minutes until the oil separates and the masala darkens.
Pour in 2 cups water, simmer for 6 minutes, finish with 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, and add the koftas just before serving so they hold their shape.
tips: Roast the coconut and spices to a deep brown for the authentic dark colour and smoky Kolhapuri flavour.
Reduce the dry red chillies if you prefer a milder heat, as this masala is traditionally very spicy.
Add the koftas at the very end so the thin, spicy gravy does not break them apart.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with jowar bhakri or plain rice, with sliced raw onion and lime to cool the fiery gravy.

variations.name: Classic Corn Palak Tikki
variations.description: Corn Palak Tikki pairs sweet crushed corn with vibrant blanched spinach in a spiced potato patty that fries up crisp and golden. The corn brings juicy pockets of sweetness while the spinach lends colour and a mellow, wholesome flavour that appeals to every age.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: shallow-frying in bilona ghee gives the tikki a crisp, nutty crust

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sattu
ingredients.note: roasted sattu soaks up the corn and spinach moisture and binds the tikki

steps: Blanch 1.5 cups spinach in boiling water for 30 seconds, refresh in cold water, squeeze dry and chop it fine.
Crush the 1.5 cups sweet corn coarsely, leaving some whole kernels, then boil and mash the 3 potatoes smooth.
Dry-roast 3 tbsp Anveshan Sattu for a minute and combine it with the potato, corn and spinach to bind and absorb moisture.
Mix in grated ginger, 2 chopped green chillies, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp chaat masala, 3 tbsp coriander and 1 tsp salt, then knead firm and shape into 10 patties.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on a griddle over medium heat and shallow-fry the tikkis for 3 to 4 minutes per side until crisp and golden.
Fry the remaining tikkis in the rest of the Anveshan Ghee and drain on paper before serving hot.
tips: Squeeze the blanched spinach really dry so the tikkis do not turn soggy or fall apart while frying.
Crush only part of the corn so you keep juicy whole kernels for texture in every bite.
Add extra roasted sattu a spoon at a time if the mix feels wet from the vegetables.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with mint-coriander chutney and a squeeze of lemon, or slide into a burger bun.

variations.name: Cheese Corn Palak Tikki
variations.description: A rich cafe-style version where grated cheese melts through the corn and spinach for a gooey, kid-friendly patty. Oregano and chilli flakes give it a continental accent while the crisp shell keeps the molten centre contained.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: ghee crisps the shell as the cheese melts through the tikki

steps: Blanch 1 cup spinach for 30 seconds, refresh, squeeze dry and chop it fine, then boil and mash the 3 potatoes.
Crush the 1.5 cups sweet corn coarsely and combine it with the mashed potato and chopped spinach.
Add 0.5 cup bread crumbs, 1 tsp oregano, 1 tsp chilli flakes, 0.5 tsp black pepper, 3 tbsp coriander and 1 tsp salt, and knead into a firm dough.
Fold 0.75 cup grated mozzarella gently through the dough, then shape into 10 patties, pressing so the cheese stays enclosed.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on a griddle over medium heat and cook the tikkis for 4 minutes per side until crisp with a golden crust.
Fry the rest in the remaining Anveshan Ghee and serve at once while the cheese is still stretchy inside.
tips: Chill the shaped tikkis for 15 minutes so the cheese does not ooze out the moment they hit the pan.
Bread crumbs keep the dough firm around the melting cheese, so do not reduce them.
Fold the cheese in gently rather than mashing it so you get clear molten pockets.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a tangy schezwan or salsa dip and a sprinkle of extra oregano for a party platter.

variations.name: Baked Corn Palak Oats Tikki
variations.description: A lighter oven-baked patty that binds corn and spinach with rolled oats instead of potato for extra fibre and a hearty chew. Brushed with olive oil and baked till the edges crisp, these are a wholesome after-school snack.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Olive Oil
ingredients.note: brushed over the tikkis so they crisp and brown evenly in the oven

steps: Preheat the oven to 200C and line a tray with parchment brushed lightly with a little Anveshan Olive Oil.
Dry-roast 1 cup rolled oats for 2 minutes, then grind two-thirds of them to a coarse flour and keep the rest whole.
Blanch 1.5 cups spinach briefly, squeeze dry and chop, then mix it with the crushed 1.5 cups corn, 0.5 cup grated carrot and the oats.
Add grated ginger, 2 chopped green chillies, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 3 tbsp coriander and 1 tsp salt, rest 10 minutes, then shape into 10 patties.
Arrange on the tray, brush the tops well with Anveshan Olive Oil, and bake for 15 minutes.
Flip, brush again with oil, and bake another 12 to 15 minutes until firm and golden at the edges, then rest 2 minutes before serving.
tips: Rest the mixture so the ground oats absorb moisture and bind the tikkis firmly before shaping.
Keep some oats whole for a satisfying, hearty texture in the baked patty.
Squeeze the spinach thoroughly, as excess water will keep the tikkis from crisping in the oven.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm with a yogurt-garlic dip and a crunchy salad for a light, wholesome bite.

variations.name: Corn Palak Paneer Tikki
variations.description: A protein-rich take that folds crumbled paneer through the corn and spinach for a soft, satisfying patty with a restaurant-style richness. Kasuri methi and a touch of cream cheese give it a lush, aromatic finish.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: ghee gives these rich paneer tikkis a golden, aromatic crust

steps: Blanch 1 cup spinach for 30 seconds, refresh, squeeze dry and chop it fine.
Crush the 1.5 cups corn coarsely and mix it with the spinach and 1 cup crumbled paneer in a bowl.
Add 3 tbsp cornflour, 1 tbsp crushed kasuri methi, grated ginger, 2 chopped green chillies, 1 tsp garam masala, 3 tbsp coriander and 1 tsp salt.
Knead into a soft but shapeable dough and form into 10 patties, adding a little extra cornflour if it feels loose.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on a griddle over medium heat and shallow-fry the tikkis for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and set.
Fry the remaining tikkis in the rest of the Anveshan Ghee and serve hot so the paneer stays soft inside.
tips: Use fresh, soft paneer and crumble it fine so it binds smoothly with the corn and spinach.
Cornflour is the binder here since there is no potato, so add enough to hold the tikkis together.
Crush the kasuri methi between your palms before adding to release its full aroma.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a mint raita and thin onion rings as a hearty, protein-packed starter.

variations.name: Classic Dahi Bhindi
variations.description: A North Indian home favourite of shallow-fried okra folded into a lightly spiced, tangy yogurt gravy. Frying the bhindi first keeps it non-slimy and lets it soak up the mild curd sauce, giving a comforting sabzi that is sour, soft and gently warming.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Bilona ghee fries the okra clean and gives the yogurt gravy a rounded homestyle richness

steps: Wash 400 g okra, wipe every piece completely dry, trim the ends and cut into 2 cm lengths so they crisp rather than turn slimy.

Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a wide pan on medium and saute the okra for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the edges turn golden and the stickiness disappears, then lift out and set aside.
Whisk 1 cup yogurt smooth with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 0.75 tsp red chilli powder and 1.5 tbsp coriander powder so it will not split when heated.

In the same pan add the remaining 1 tbsp ghee, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds and 0.25 tsp hing for 20 seconds, then add 1 finely chopped onion and 1 tsp ginger paste and fry for 4 to 5 minutes until soft and golden.
Lower the heat to minimum, pour in the spiced yogurt and stir continuously for 4 minutes until it comes to a gentle simmer and thickens slightly without curdling, adding 0.5 cup water and 1 tsp salt.
Fold in the fried okra, simmer uncovered on low for 5 minutes until the gravy coats the pieces, finish with 0.5 tsp garam masala and 3 tbsp chopped coriander, and rest 3 minutes before serving.
tips: Dry the okra thoroughly before cutting and never cover it while frying, or trapped steam brings back the sliminess.
Keep the flame low and stir without stopping while the yogurt cooks, otherwise the curd splits into grains.
Use slightly sour set curd for the classic tang; if it is too sharp add a pinch of sugar to balance.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with hot phulka or jeera rice and a wedge of lemon, with sliced onions and green chilli on the side.

variations.name: Punjabi Dhaba Dahi Bhindi Masala
variations.description: A robust dhaba-style take where the okra rests in a thick onion-tomato masala enriched with beaten curd. Wood-pressed mustard oil and kasuri methi build a bold, restaurant-like gravy that clings to each piece, far heartier than the light homestyle version.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Pungent wood-pressed mustard oil gives this bhindi its unmistakable Punjabi dhaba depth

steps: Wipe 400 g okra dry, trim and slit each into halves lengthwise so the masala clings well.
Heat 4 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil in a kadai until it just smokes, lower the heat and shallow-fry the okra for 8 minutes until seared and non-sticky, then remove and reserve.

In the same oil crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds, add 2 finely chopped onions and fry on medium for 6 minutes until deep golden, then stir in 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and 2 slit green chillies for 1 minute.
Add 3 pureed tomatoes with 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder and 1 tbsp coriander powder and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until the oil separates and the masala darkens.
Lower the heat, whisk in 0.5 cup yogurt a spoon at a time, stirring constantly for 3 minutes so it blends without splitting, then add 0.5 cup water and 1.25 tsp salt.
Return the fried okra, simmer for 6 minutes until the thick gravy coats it, then crush in 1 tsp kasuri methi and 0.75 tsp garam masala and rest 3 minutes before serving.
tips: Slitting rather than dicing the okra keeps it intact in the heavier gravy and gives a dhaba-style look.
Add the curd off the boil and one spoon at a time so the rich tomato masala stays smooth.
For extra dhaba aroma, place a live charcoal ember in a bowl over the finished sabzi with a drop of ghee and cover for 2 minutes to smoke it.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with butter naan, laccha paratha or tandoori roti and a raw onion-and-lemon salad.

variations.name: South Indian Mor Bhindi with Coconut
variations.description: A Tamil-style buttermilk okra curry where fried bhindi simmers in a ground coconut, cumin and green-chilli curd sauce, finished with a curry-leaf and mustard tempering. Light, coconut-sweet and gently soured, it eats beautifully with plain rice.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: Wood-pressed coconut oil carries the tempering and echoes the ground coconut base

steps: Wipe 350 g okra dry, trim and cut into 3 cm pieces, then saute in 1 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil on medium for 8 minutes until the edges brown and the stickiness goes.
Grind 0.5 cup grated coconut with 2 green chillies, 1 tsp cumin seeds and 1 inch ginger to a smooth paste using a little water.
Whisk 1.25 cups yogurt smooth with the coconut paste, 0.25 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt to make the mor base.
