Pour the buttermilk mixture into a pan over the lowest heat and warm it gently for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring constantly, just until it steams and thickens slightly, never letting it boil.
Fold in the fried okra and simmer very gently for 4 minutes until heated through and the sauce clings lightly.

In a small pan heat the remaining 2 tbsp coconut oil, splutter 0.5 tsp mustard seeds, 2 dried red chillies and 12 curry leaves for 20 seconds, then pour this sizzling tempering over the curry and cover for 2 minutes before serving.
tips: Keep the buttermilk base below a simmer at all times, as boiling curd in this thin sauce curdles instantly.
Grind the coconut fresh and fine so the sauce is smooth and naturally sweet.
Use slightly sour curd and thin with a splash of water if the mor becomes too thick on standing.
variations.servingSuggestion: Ladle over hot steamed rice with a spoon of ghee, alongside a crisp papad and a simple stir-fry.

variations.name: Rajasthani Crispy Besan Dahi Bhindi
variations.description: A crunchy Marwari treatment where okra is tossed in spiced gram flour and pan-crisped, then bathed in a tangy hing-tempered curd gravy just before serving. The besan coating stays crisp against the sour sauce for a lively contrast of textures.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee tempers the tangy curd gravy with a nutty Rajasthani aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A clean wood-pressed oil crisps the besan-coated okra without heaviness

steps: Wipe 350 g okra dry, slit lengthwise and toss with 0.5 cup besan, 0.5 tsp ajwain, 0.25 tsp turmeric, 0.5 tsp red chilli powder and 0.5 tsp salt so the flour clings in a thin coat.
Heat 4 tbsp Anveshan Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil in a pan on medium and pan-crisp the coated okra in batches for 6 to 7 minutes, turning, until golden and crunchy, then drain on paper.
Whisk 1 cup yogurt smooth with the remaining 0.25 tsp turmeric, 0.5 tsp red chilli powder, 0.5 tsp amchur and 0.5 tsp salt.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a small kadai, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds and 0.25 tsp hing for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Lower the heat to minimum, pour in the spiced yogurt and stir constantly for 4 minutes until it simmers and thickens without splitting, loosening with 0.25 cup water.
Just before serving, spread the crisp besan okra over the warm curd gravy or fold it in at the last moment so it keeps its crunch, and serve immediately.
tips: Coat the okra in besan just before frying so the flour does not turn pasty from the vegetable's moisture.
Add the fried okra to the gravy only at the table, or the coating softens within minutes.
Amchur brightens the curd; increase it slightly if your yogurt is mild rather than sour.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve straight away with bajra roti or steamed rice, keeping extra crisp okra aside to scatter on top.

variations.name: Classic Dahi Ke Kabab
variations.description: A Lucknawi delicacy of thick hung curd bound with roasted gram, spiced gently and pan-seared into crisp-edged, custard-soft kababs. The contrast of a golden crust against a cool, melting centre makes these an elegant vegetarian starter that feels indulgent yet light.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: shallow-fries the kababs to a fragrant golden crust without them sticking

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sattu
ingredients.note: roasted gram sattu binds the soft curd and adds a nutty depth without any raw taste

steps: Hang 3 cups of curd in muslin for 2 to 3 hours until it yields 1.5 cups of thick, dry hung curd.
Dry-roast the 4 tbsp Anveshan Sattu in a pan on low heat for 2 minutes until warm and fragrant, then let it cool completely.

Mix the hung curd with the sattu, 3 tbsp grated paneer, finely chopped chillies and ginger, chopped cashews, 0.25 tsp cardamom powder, 0.5 tsp white pepper, coriander and 0.75 tsp salt into a soft, shapeable mixture.
Chill the mixture for 20 minutes, then shape into 8 flat round patties with lightly greased palms so they hold together.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on a flat griddle over medium heat and place the kababs, cooking for 2 to 3 minutes per side until a deep golden crust forms.
Lift them carefully with a wide spatula and drain briefly on paper, serving hot while the centre is still soft.
tips: Use very thick hung curd; any moisture will make the kababs collapse on the griddle.
Chill the mixture well before shaping so the delicate patties firm up and hold their round form.
Turn the kababs only once, gently, as they are soft and break if flipped repeatedly.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with mint chutney and thin onion rings, with a squeeze of lemon just before eating.

variations.name: Hyderabadi Dahi Ke Kabab
variations.description: A Deccani version studded with golden fried onions, mint and a whisper of roasted spice, giving the melting curd kababs a sweet-savoury depth. The birista folded through the mixture perfumes every bite in true Hyderabadi style.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: shallow-fries the kababs to a rich golden crust with a Hyderabadi aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: fries the onions into crisp golden birista for the kabab mixture

steps: Hang 3 cups of curd in muslin for 2 to 3 hours to get 1.5 cups of thick hung curd.
Thinly slice the 2 onions and fry them in the hot Anveshan Groundnut Oil over medium heat for 5 minutes until crisp and golden, then drain into birista.
Mix the hung curd with 4 tbsp roasted gram flour, crushed birista, chopped chillies, ginger, mint, 0.5 tsp roasted cumin, 0.5 tsp chaat masala and 0.75 tsp salt into a soft mixture.
Chill for 20 minutes, then shape into 8 flat patties with greased palms so they stay intact.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on a griddle over medium heat and cook the kababs for 2 to 3 minutes per side until a crisp golden crust forms.
Drain briefly on paper and serve hot, dusted with a little extra chaat masala.
tips: Crush the fried onions slightly so they distribute evenly through the soft mixture.
Keep the roasted gram flour lump-free by sieving it into the curd before mixing.
Fry the birista to a deep gold, not brown, or it turns bitter in the kababs.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a tangy imli-date chutney and sliced cucumber, garnished with a few whole mint leaves.

variations.name: Beetroot Dahi Ke Kabab
variations.description: A vibrant magenta version where grated beetroot lends colour, earthiness and a natural sweetness to the melting curd kababs. As striking to look at as they are delicious, these rosy patties bring a modern flourish to a classic starter.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: shallow-fries the beetroot kababs to a crisp edge while keeping the centre soft

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sattu
ingredients.note: roasted gram sattu soaks up the beetroot moisture and binds the kababs firmly

steps: Hang 3 cups of curd in muslin for 2 to 3 hours to yield 1.5 cups of thick hung curd.
Grate the 1 cup beetroot finely, then dry-roast it in a pan on medium heat for 4 minutes to drive off its moisture, and cool.
Dry-roast the 4 tbsp Anveshan Sattu on low heat for 2 minutes until fragrant, then let it cool.
Mix the hung curd, roasted beetroot, sattu, 3 tbsp grated paneer, chopped chillies and ginger, 0.5 tsp roasted cumin, 0.5 tsp black pepper, coriander and 0.75 tsp salt into a firm, rosy mixture.
Chill for 20 minutes and shape into 8 flat patties with greased palms.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on a griddle over medium heat and cook the kababs for 2 to 3 minutes per side until crisp and set, then drain and serve hot.
tips: Dry-roast the grated beetroot first so it does not leak water and weaken the kababs.
Add a little extra sattu if the beetroot makes the mixture too moist to shape.
Handle gently while flipping, as the soft magenta patties are fragile.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a cooling mint-yogurt dip and a scatter of pomegranate seeds for colour and crunch.

variations.name: Baked Dahi Ke Kabab
variations.description: A guilt-free version where the melting curd kababs are baked to a golden crust instead of pan-frying, using just a light brush of oil. All the creamy, spiced softness of the original with a fraction of the fat, perfect for a lighter starter.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Olive Oil
ingredients.note: brushed over the kababs so they crisp in the oven without deep-frying

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: glazes the baked kababs at the end for a rich finishing aroma

steps: Hang 3 cups of curd in muslin for 2 to 3 hours to get 1.5 cups of very thick hung curd.
Mix the hung curd with 5 tbsp roasted gram flour, 0.25 cup grated paneer, chopped chillies and ginger, 0.25 tsp cardamom powder, 0.5 tsp white pepper, coriander and 0.75 tsp salt into a firm mixture.
Chill for 20 minutes, then shape into 8 flat patties and place them on a lined baking tray.
Brush both sides generously with the 2 tbsp Anveshan Olive Oil so they crisp evenly.
Bake in a preheated oven at 200 C for 20 minutes, turning once halfway, until golden and set on both sides.
Brush the hot kababs with 1 tbsp melted Anveshan Ghee for a rich finish and serve immediately.
tips: Use extra roasted gram flour compared to the fried version so the kababs hold firm while baking.
Line the tray with parchment and oil it well so the delicate patties lift off cleanly.
Finish with a ghee brush after baking to bring back the flavour lost by skipping the fry.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a fresh coriander-mint chutney and a crisp kachumber salad on the side.

variations.name: Classic Rajasthani Dahi Ki Sabzi
variations.description: A quick Marwari curry born of scarcity, where whisked curd is thickened with a little gram flour and tempered with cumin and hing into a light, tangy sauce. With no vegetables at all, it leans entirely on the sourness of the yogurt and a warm spice tadka, ready in minutes for everyday meals.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Bilona ghee makes the cumin-hing tadka that defines this bare-bones Marwari curd curry

steps: Whisk 1.5 cups yogurt smooth with 2 tbsp besan, 0.5 tsp turmeric, 0.75 tsp red chilli powder and 1 tbsp coriander powder until there are no lumps, then stir in 1.5 cups water to make a thin buttermilk.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a kadai on medium and crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds, 0.5 tsp mustard seeds, 2 dried red chillies and 0.25 tsp hing for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add 1 tsp ginger paste and fry for 30 seconds until the raw smell goes.
Lower the heat to minimum, pour in the yogurt mixture and stir continuously for 5 to 6 minutes as it heats, so the besan cooks and the curd does not split.
Add 1 tsp salt and simmer gently on low for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce thickens to a light pouring consistency and loses its raw besan taste.
Finish with 2 tbsp chopped coriander and rest 3 minutes before serving so the tempering flavours settle in.
tips: Keep stirring without a break until the curd comes to a simmer, as this is the moment it is most likely to curdle.
Cook the besan for at least 8 minutes so the sauce loses its raw, floury edge.
If the curd is very sour, add a pinch of jaggery; if too mild, a squeeze of extra whisking brightens it.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve piping hot over steamed rice or with bajra roti, topped with a spoon of fresh ghee.

variations.name: Boondi Dahi Ki Sabzi
variations.description: A festive Marwari version where crisp gram-flour boondi is dropped into the tangy curd curry, soaking up the sauce until soft and pillowy. The boondi adds body and a savoury bite, turning the plain curd curry into something special for guests.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee tempers the curd base and warms the boondi so they turn soft and flavourful

steps: Whisk 1.5 cups yogurt with 1.5 tbsp besan, 0.5 tsp turmeric and 0.75 tsp red chilli powder until smooth, then thin with 1.5 cups water.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a kadai on medium and splutter 1 tsp cumin seeds, 0.25 tsp hing, 10 curry leaves and 2 slit green chillies for 30 seconds.
Lower the heat to minimum, pour in the yogurt mixture and stir constantly for 5 to 6 minutes until it heats through and the besan cooks without the curd splitting.
Add 0.75 tsp salt and simmer on low for 6 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce thickens to a light gravy.
Stir in 1 cup boondi and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes only, just until they swell and soften but still hold a little bite.
Finish with 0.5 tsp garam masala and 2 tbsp chopped coriander, then serve within a few minutes while the boondi are plump.
tips: Add the boondi at the very end, as they turn mushy if left in the hot sauce too long.
If your boondi are very oily, soak them in warm water for 2 minutes and squeeze gently before adding.
Season the sauce a touch lighter because the salted boondi bring their own salt.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with hot phulka or plain rice, ladled generously so each spoon carries a few soft boondi.

variations.name: Aloo Dahi Ki Sabzi (No-Onion No-Garlic)
variations.description: A satvik potato-and-curd curry made without onion or garlic, ideal for fasting days and temple-style meals. Boiled potato cubes simmer in a gently spiced yogurt sauce brightened only with ginger, green chilli and a clean cumin tadka.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Pure ghee suits this satvik curry and carries the cumin-ginger tempering

steps: Boil 3 potatoes until just tender, peel and cut into 2 cm cubes.
Whisk 1.25 cups yogurt smooth with 1.5 tbsp besan, 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp coriander powder and 0.5 tsp red chilli powder, then loosen with 1 cup water.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a kadai on medium, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds for 20 seconds, then add 1 inch grated ginger and 2 slit green chillies and fry for 30 seconds.
Lower the heat to minimum, pour in the yogurt mixture and stir continuously for 5 minutes until it heats through and the besan cooks without splitting.
Add the potato cubes and 1 tsp salt and simmer gently on low for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce thickens and coats the potatoes.
Finish with 0.5 tsp garam masala and 2 tbsp chopped coriander and rest 3 minutes before serving.
tips: Slightly undercook the potatoes when boiling so they hold their shape in the simmering curd.
Mash one potato cube into the sauce if you want a naturally thicker, clingier gravy.
For a strict fasting version, swap coriander and chilli powders for rock salt and crushed black pepper.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with samvat rice, kuttu puri or plain paratha, with a wedge of lemon on the side.

variations.name: Lehsuni Tadka Dahi Ki Sabzi
variations.description: A bold garlic-forward curd curry finished with a second smoking tempering of sliced garlic and red chilli in mustard oil. The double tadka gives a pungent, aromatic sauce with real punch, a rustic Marwari-Haryanvi favourite for the winter table.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Sharp wood-pressed mustard oil makes the smoking garlic tadka that crowns this curry

steps: Whisk 1.5 cups yogurt with 2 tbsp besan, 0.5 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp coriander powder and 0.5 tsp of the Kashmiri chilli powder until smooth, then thin with 1.5 cups water.

Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil in a kadai until it just smokes, lower the heat and add 1 tsp cumin seeds, 0.25 tsp methi seeds and 6 crushed garlic cloves, frying for 1 minute until the garlic turns golden.
Lower the heat to minimum, pour in the yogurt mixture and stir continuously for 6 minutes until it simmers and the besan cooks through without curdling.
Add 1 tsp salt and simmer on low for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce thickens to a light gravy, then pour it into a serving bowl.
For the finishing tadka, heat the remaining 2 tbsp mustard oil until smoking, lower the heat and add 4 sliced garlic cloves and 3 dried red chillies, frying for 40 seconds until deep golden.
Stir in the remaining 0.5 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder off the heat and immediately pour the sizzling garlic tadka over the curry, cover for 1 minute, and serve.
tips: Bring the mustard oil to a light smoke first to mellow its raw sharpness before the garlic goes in.
Slice the garlic for the top tadka so it crisps and stays visible on the sauce.
Take the final tadka off the heat before adding chilli powder so it colours the oil without burning.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with hot bajra or makki roti and a knob of white butter, with raw onion on the side.

variations.name: Classic Chana Dal Ke Kabab
variations.description: Dal Ke Kabab is the North-Indian griddle kabab built from coarsely ground soaked chana dal, spiced and shaped into patties before a slow ghee sear. The dal gives a nutty, grainy body that crisps beautifully at the edges while staying moist within.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: sears the kababs to a crisp golden crust and carries the spices

steps: Soak 1.5 cups chana dal for 4 hours, drain fully, then pressure-cook with just 0.5 cup water for 2 whistles so it turns soft but not mushy.
Cool and coarsely grind the cooked dal without water into a thick, grainy paste that still holds texture.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, crackle 1 tsp cumin for 20 seconds, add the chopped onion, grated ginger and 2 green chillies and saute 3 minutes until soft, then mix into the dal.
Add 1 tsp coriander powder, 0.75 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 3 tbsp coriander leaves and 1 tsp salt, and knead into a firm, shapeable dough.
Shape into round patties and rest for 10 minutes so they hold together.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on a flat tawa on medium heat and sear the kababs for 4 minutes each side, adding ghee as needed, until deep golden and crisp, then serve hot.
tips: Grind the cooked dal coarse and without water so the kababs stay grainy and do not turn pasty.
If the mixture feels loose, dry-roast it in a pan for a few minutes to evaporate moisture before shaping.
Sear on steady medium heat so the crust crisps before the inside overcooks.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with sliced onions, green chutney and a lemon wedge, or tuck into a pav for a filling snack.

variations.name: Shami-Style Kaali Dal Kabab
variations.description: Inspired by the classic shami kabab, this version uses black urad and chana dal cooked with whole spices until dry, then ground fine for a smooth, dense kabab. Stuffed with a tangy onion-mint filling, it delivers a soft, richly spiced bite.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: sears the shami kababs to a smooth golden crust

steps: Drain the soaked 1 cup chana dal and 0.5 cup urad dal, then cook with 1 tbsp whole garam masala, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 3 dry red chillies, 1 cup water and 0.5 tsp salt until the dal is soft and completely dry, about 20 minutes.
Cool the mixture, discard the large whole spices, and grind it to a smooth, stiff paste without adding water.
Knead in 1 tsp roasted cumin and 0.5 tsp salt, then divide into balls.
Mix the chopped onion, 3 tbsp mint and 1 tbsp lemon juice into a tangy filling.
Flatten each ball, place a little onion-mint filling in the centre, seal into a smooth patty and rest for 10 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on a tawa on medium heat and shallow-fry the kababs for 3 minutes each side, adding ghee as needed, until golden and crisp, then serve warm.
tips: Cook the dal until truly dry, as any moisture makes the smooth shami paste too soft to shape.
Grind fine and without water for the dense, melt-in-mouth texture that defines a shami kabab.
Seal the tangy filling well so it stays as a surprise centre rather than leaking out.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with sirke wale pyaaz and a mint-yogurt dip, with lemon wedges on a mezze platter.

variations.name: Mixed Sprouts Dal Kabab
variations.description: A wholesome, protein-packed griddle kabab made from steamed mixed sprouts and moong dal, mashed with roasted spices for an earthy, nutritious bite. Lighter than the classic yet full of texture, it is a nourishing snack or light-meal patty.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: shallow-fries the kababs crisp and light without a heavy aftertaste

steps: Steam 1.5 cups mixed sprouts for 8 minutes until tender, then coarsely mash them with the 0.75 cup cooked moong dal.
Mix in the chopped onion, 1 tbsp ginger-green chilli paste, 1 tsp roasted cumin, 1 tsp chaat masala, 3 tbsp coriander and 1 tsp salt.
Add 3 tbsp powdered oats to bind and knead into a firm dough, resting it 10 minutes so the oats absorb moisture.
Shape into small round patties, pressing them firm so they hold on the griddle.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil on a tawa on medium heat and shallow-fry the kababs for 3 to 4 minutes each side, adding oil as needed, until crisp and golden.
Drain on paper and serve warm while crisp.
tips: Steam rather than boil the sprouts so they stay firm and the mixture is not watery.
Powdered oats bind the loose sprout mix without weighing it down like heavy flour.
Mash only coarsely to keep a pleasant bite of whole sprouts in each kabab.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a tangy tamarind-date chutney and a fresh cucumber salad for a light, nourishing plate.

variations.name: Masala Dal Kabab Chaat
variations.description: A street-style makeover where crisp dal kababs are broken over a plate and loaded with curd, tangy chutneys, onions and sev. It layers the nutty kabab with cool yogurt and sweet-sour tamarind for a full-on chaat experience.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: sears the dal kababs crisp before they are topped for chaat

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: sweetens the tamarind chutney with a deep, mellow warmth

steps: Soak 1.5 cups chana dal for 4 hours, drain, pressure-cook with 0.5 cup water for 2 whistles until soft, then coarsely grind without water.
Knead the ground dal with the chopped onion, 2 green chillies, 1 tsp roasted cumin and 1 tsp salt, and shape into small patties.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on a tawa on medium heat and sear the kababs for 4 minutes each side, adding ghee as needed, until crisp and golden.
Simmer 3 tbsp tamarind pulp with 2 tbsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder, 0.5 tsp roasted cumin and a pinch of salt for 4 minutes into a pourable sweet-tangy chutney, then cool.
Break the warm kababs onto a serving plate, spoon over the whisked yogurt, and drizzle generously with the tamarind chutney.
Dust with 1 tsp chaat masala and the remaining cumin, scatter 0.5 cup sev and 3 tbsp coriander, and serve at once.
tips: Assemble the chaat just before serving so the kababs stay crisp under the toppings.
Chill the whisked yogurt so the hot kabab and cool curd contrast comes through.
Keep the tamarind chutney pourable so it coats every piece evenly.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve on a wide plate topped with pomegranate seeds for colour, as a hearty chaat-counter special.

variations.name: Classic Dates Halwa
variations.description: Dates halwa is a naturally sweetened pudding of soft Medjool dates blended to a paste and slow-cooked in ghee with milk until it turns dark, glossy and fudgy. It needs no added sugar, carrying the deep toffee sweetness of the fruit alone, and is finished with fried cashews and almonds for crunch.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: slow-cooks the date paste to a glossy fudge and fries the nuts for the halwa

steps: Warm 1 cup full-fat milk, add 2 cups soft pitted dates and soak for 10 minutes, then blend to a smooth thick paste.
Heat 5 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a heavy kadhai and fry 3 tbsp cashews and 3 tbsp chopped almonds over medium heat until golden, about 2 minutes, then lift them out.
Pour the date paste into the same ghee and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, for 10 to 12 minutes until it darkens and thickens.
Keep stirring until the halwa turns glossy and pulls away from the sides of the pan, releasing ghee at the edges, about 4 minutes more.
Stir in 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and 1 pinch nutmeg powder along with most of the fried nuts and mix through.
Spoon the halwa into bowls, scatter the reserved nuts on top and serve warm.
tips: Choose soft Medjool or Kimia dates; dry, fibrous dates need extra milk and never blend to a silky paste.
Cook the paste on a low flame throughout, as the natural sugars in dates scorch quickly on high heat.
For a firmer set, press the cooked halwa into a greased tray, chill and cut into barfi-like squares.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm as a wholesome no-sugar dessert, or chill and slice into squares for a lunchbox sweet, topped with slivered pistachios.

variations.name: Vegan Dates and Coconut Halwa
variations.description: A dairy-free take that simmers date paste in creamy coconut milk and coconut oil instead of ghee, folding in desiccated coconut for a soft, tropical chew. The coconut rounds off the toffee notes of the dates and gives the halwa a fudgy, almost laddoo-like body.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: replaces ghee to cook the date paste and keep this halwa fully plant-based

steps: Soak 2 cups soft pitted dates in 0.75 cup thick coconut milk for 10 minutes, then blend to a smooth paste.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil in a non-stick pan and lightly toast 3 tbsp chopped walnuts over medium heat until fragrant, about 1 minute, then set aside.
Add the date and coconut-milk paste to the same oil and cook over low heat, stirring, for 8 to 10 minutes until it thickens and darkens.
Stir in 0.5 cup desiccated coconut and 1 pinch salt and keep cooking for 4 to 5 minutes until the mass turns glossy and leaves the pan.
Fold in 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and most of the toasted walnuts, mixing until evenly combined.
Serve the halwa warm in bowls, garnished with the remaining walnuts and a light dusting of coconut.
tips: Use full-fat canned coconut milk rather than diluted carton milk so the halwa sets to a proper fudge.
Toast the desiccated coconut for a minute before adding if you want a deeper, nuttier flavour.
This mixture rolls easily into laddoos while still warm if you prefer bite-sized sweets.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm as a dairy-free festive sweet, or roll into small laddoos and coat in extra desiccated coconut for gifting.

variations.name: Kesar Dates and Almond Halwa
variations.description: A celebration-grade version enriched with ground almonds, reduced milk and bloomed saffron for a creamy, saffron-gold halwa that is softer and more fragrant than the everyday one. The almond flour thickens the pudding while the saffron perfumes every spoonful.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: cooks the almond and date paste together for a plush, glossy festive halwa

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: bloomed in warm milk to colour and perfume this rich dates halwa

steps: Soak 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp of warm milk taken from the 1.25 cups and set aside to bloom.
Blend 2 cups soft pitted dates with the remaining warm milk to a smooth, pourable paste.
Heat 4 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a heavy pan, add 0.5 cup almond flour and roast over low heat for 3 minutes until it smells nutty.
Pour in the date paste and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, for 8 to 10 minutes until it thickens and turns glossy.
Stir in the bloomed saffron milk and 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and cook for 3 minutes more until the halwa deepens to a rich gold.
Fold in half the slivered pistachios, spoon into bowls and finish with the rest on top before serving warm.
tips: Bloom the saffron in warm, not hot, milk so its colour and aroma spread evenly through the pudding.
Keep the halwa slightly loose off the heat, as almond flour and milk continue to thicken it as it cools.
A tablespoon of khoya stirred in at the end makes this even richer for wedding-style feasts.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve this saffron dates halwa warm at festivals in small bowls, crowned with slivered pistachios and a few saffron strands.

variations.name: Khajur Anjeer Halwa
variations.description: A dense, sugar-free dry-fruit halwa in which dates and figs are cooked down together and bound with dry-fruit paste for an intensely fruity, chewy sweet. Studded with walnuts and pistachios, it doubles as an energy-rich winter tonic that keeps for days.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: binds the date and fig paste into a glossy, chewy dry-fruit halwa

ingredients.name: Anveshan Dry Fruit Paak
ingredients.note: stirred in to deepen the nutty richness and body of this fruit halwa

steps: Soak 1.5 cups soft pitted dates and 0.75 cup dried figs in 0.5 cup warm water for 15 minutes, then blend to a coarse thick paste.
Heat 4 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a kadhai and dry-roast 3 tbsp walnuts and 2 tbsp pistachios over medium heat for 1 minute, then set most aside.
Add the date and fig paste to the ghee and cook over low heat, stirring often, for 10 to 12 minutes until it thickens and turns sticky.
Stir in 3 tbsp Anveshan Dry Fruit Paak and cook for 3 minutes more until the halwa is glossy and pulls away from the pan.
Fold in 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and the roasted nuts, mixing until evenly distributed.
Serve warm, or press into a greased tray, chill and cut into chewy dry-fruit squares.
tips: Snip the hard stem tips off the figs before soaking so the paste blends smooth and grit-free.
This halwa is stiffer than milk-based ones by design; add a splash of warm water if it feels too dry to stir.
Stored airtight in the fridge, these fruit squares keep for up to two weeks as a travel-friendly energy bite.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve as bite-sized energy squares with evening tea, or warm as a winter dessert topped with extra chopped walnuts.

variations.name: Classic Double Ka Meetha
variations.description: The iconic Hyderabadi wedding dessert of ghee-fried bread slices soaked in fragrant saffron-cardamom sugar syrup and drenched in reduced, thickened milk. Named for the fluffy 'double roti' loaf it uses, it sits somewhere between shahi tukda and a rich bread pudding, crowned with fried nuts.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: shallow-fries the bread to a rich golden crisp and gives the dessert its unmistakable royal aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: steeped in warm milk to perfume the reduced milk and lend a soft amber glow

steps: Bring 1 litre full-fat milk to a boil in a heavy pan, then simmer on medium-low for 20 minutes, stirring often, until it reduces by nearly half to a thick, creamy rabri; steep 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp of it.
Meanwhile make the syrup by boiling 1 cup sugar with 0.75 cup water and 0.25 tsp cardamom for 5 minutes until slightly sticky but not thread-like, then keep it warm.
Trim the crusts off 8 bread slices and cut each in half; heat 4 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pan and shallow-fry the pieces in batches on medium until deep golden and crisp on both sides.
Dip each fried bread piece into the warm syrup for just 10 to 15 seconds so it drinks in the sweetness without turning soggy, then arrange the pieces in a single layer in a serving dish.
Stir the saffron milk and remaining 0.25 tsp cardamom into the reduced milk and pour it evenly over the soaked bread so every piece is bathed.
Fry 10 cashews, 10 almonds and 10 pistachios in the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee until golden, scatter them over the top, and rest for 15 minutes before serving so the bread absorbs the milk.
tips: Use day-old bread; slightly stale slices fry crisper and hold their shape better in the syrup and milk.
Dip the fried bread in syrup only briefly, or it collapses into mush instead of staying plump and layered.
Reduce the milk properly to a rabri thickness; thin milk leaves the dessert watery rather than luscious.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve slightly warm or chilled, topped with extra slivered pistachios and a few saffron strands, as the grand finale to a Hyderabadi biryani feast.

variations.name: Khoya Double Ka Meetha
variations.description: A richer nawabi rendition where the fried bread is layered with grated khoya and finished with a thicker, mawa-enriched milk for an almost cake-like density. This is the version served at grand Hyderabadi shaadis, deeply sweet and unapologetically indulgent.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: fries the bread and enriches the khoya layer for a truly royal texture

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: colours and perfumes the mawa milk that binds this denser version together

steps: Crumble 150 g khoya into a pan with 500 ml milk and warm on low, stirring, for 8 minutes until the khoya melts into a smooth, thick mawa-milk; steep 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp of it.
Boil 1 cup sugar with 0.75 cup water and 0.25 tsp cardamom for 5 minutes into a slightly sticky syrup, then stir in 1 tsp rose water and keep warm.
Trim and halve 8 bread slices, then shallow-fry them in 5 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on medium until deep golden and crisp.
Dip each fried piece in the warm syrup for 10 seconds and arrange half of them in a layer in a dish.
Spread half the saffron mawa-milk over this layer, place the remaining bread on top, and pour over the rest of the mawa-milk with the remaining 0.25 tsp cardamom.
Fry 0.33 cup sliced mixed nuts in the last 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee until golden, scatter over the top, and rest for 20 minutes so the layers set before serving.
tips: Grate the khoya finely so it melts evenly into the milk without leaving lumps.
Layering with khoya makes this version very rich, so serve it in small portions.
A little rose water in the syrup lifts the heavy mawa and adds a floral nawabi note.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve chilled in small squares dusted with edible silver leaf for a genuinely regal wedding-style dessert.

variations.name: Khapli Whole-Wheat Double Ka Meetha
variations.description: A wholesome reinvention using slices of khapli whole-wheat bread and jaggery syrup in place of white bread and refined sugar. The nutty ancient-grain bread holds the milk beautifully and the jaggery lends a caramel warmth that suits its earthier crumb.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta Bread Slices
ingredients.note: nutty ancient-grain wheat bread replaces refined white bread and soaks up the milk without going pasty

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: fries the wholewheat slices to a crisp golden edge and adds richness

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: melted into a syrup, its caramel depth complements the earthy khapli bread far better than white sugar

steps: Simmer 1 litre full-fat milk on medium-low for 20 minutes, stirring often, until reduced to a thick rabri, then stir in 0.5 tsp cardamom and 0.25 tsp dry ginger powder.
Melt 0.75 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder with 0.5 cup water on low heat, strain out any grit, and simmer 3 minutes into a light syrup.
Trim and halve 8 slices of Anveshan Khapli Atta bread and shallow-fry them in 4 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on medium until crisp and golden on both sides.
Dip each fried slice briefly in the warm jaggery syrup so it soaks up the caramel sweetness, then lay the pieces in a serving dish.
Pour the spiced reduced milk evenly over the bread so every piece is covered and glossy.
Fry 0.25 cup walnuts and 0.25 cup chopped dates in the last 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee for a minute, scatter over the top, and rest 15 minutes before serving.
tips: Strain the melted jaggery before using it so no grit or sediment ends up in the dessert.
Khapli bread is denser than white, so dip it in syrup a few seconds longer to soak through.
The dates add natural sweetness, so keep the jaggery syrup on the lighter side.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm as a nourishing winter pudding, topped with extra toasted walnuts for crunch.

variations.name: Air-Fried Light Double Ka Meetha
variations.description: A lighter everyday version where the bread is brushed with ghee and air-fried instead of deep-fried, then soaked in a lighter honey-sweetened milk. It keeps the saffron-cardamom soul of the classic while cutting the heaviness, so it can be enjoyed any weeknight.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: brushed lightly over the bread so it crisps in the air fryer without deep-frying

ingredients.name: Anveshan Honey
ingredients.note: sweetens the milk soak naturally in place of a heavy sugar syrup

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: keeps the signature colour and aroma of double ka meetha in this lighter form

steps: Simmer 750 ml low-fat milk with 0.5 tsp cardamom on medium for 10 minutes, then whisk 1 tbsp cornflour into a little cold milk and stir it in to thicken the milk to a creamy pour; steep 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp of it.
Take the milk off the heat, let it cool for 5 minutes, then stir in the saffron milk and 4 tbsp Anveshan Honey so the honey stays raw and fragrant.
Trim and halve 8 brown bread slices, brush both sides lightly with 3 tbsp melted Anveshan Ghee, and air-fry at 180C for 6 to 8 minutes until crisp and golden, turning once.
Arrange the crisp air-fried bread in a single layer in a shallow dish.
Pour the warm honey-saffron milk evenly over the bread so each piece soaks it up while staying intact.
Scatter 3 tbsp slivered almonds and 1 tsp dried rose petals on top and chill for 20 minutes before serving.
tips: Add the honey only after the milk cools a little, as boiling honey loses its aroma and health benefits.
Air-frying keeps this version far lighter, but brush the bread evenly so it crisps rather than dries out.
The cornflour gives body to the low-fat milk so it still coats the bread like the classic rabri.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve well chilled in individual bowls, garnished with rose petals, as a guilt-free finish to a rich meal.

variations.name: Classic Farali Chevdo
variations.description: Farali chevdo is the Gujarati fasting mixture eaten during Navratri and ekadashi, a moreish tangle of crisp fried potato straws, puffed tapioca and roasted peanuts tossed with a sweet-salty-tangy fasting seasoning. Light, crunchy and free of grains and regular salt, it keeps for days in a jar.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed oil for frying the potato straws and sabudana to a light, clean crisp

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: powdered fine to give the chevdo its signature sweet-salty fasting balance

steps: Soak the potato straws in cold water for 10 minutes, then drain and pat completely dry on a cloth.
Heat 2 cups Anveshan Groundnut Oil to 180C and fry the potato straws in batches until pale gold and crisp, about 3 minutes each, then drain.
Lower the heat and fry 0.5 cup sabudana until each pearl puffs white in seconds, then fry 0.75 cup peanuts, 0.25 cup cashews and 3 tbsp raisins to golden and drain all on paper.
In 1 tbsp of the hot oil, crisp 3 slit green chillies and 15 curry leaves for 30 seconds until they stop spluttering.
In a large bowl toss the fried potato straws, sabudana, nuts, chillies and curry leaves with 1.5 tsp rock salt, 1 tbsp powdered Anveshan Khandsari, 0.5 tsp black pepper and 1 tbsp lemon juice.
Cool the chevdo completely, then store airtight so it stays crunchy for up to two weeks.
tips: Dry the potato straws thoroughly before frying, as any water makes the oil splutter and the straws turn soggy.
Fry the sabudana in very hot oil for just a few seconds; overcooked pearls turn hard instead of airy.
Toss the seasoning only when everything is fully cool, or trapped steam will soften the whole mix.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve as a dry fasting namkeen with tea, or sprinkle over a bowl of fasting curd for extra crunch.

variations.name: Roasted Rajgira Farali Chevdo
variations.description: A lighter, mostly roasted chevdo built around puffed amaranth and roasted peanuts, with only a whisper of ghee instead of a deep fry. Nutty, airy and far lower in oil, it is the wholesome fasting mix for those who want crunch without the kadhai.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the makhana and tempers the spices for this light, low-oil fasting mix

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: adds a warm sweet edge that offsets the rock salt in the roasted mix

steps: Dry-roast 0.75 cup raw peanuts in a pan over medium heat for 5 minutes until the skins crackle, then rub off the skins and set aside.
Heat 4 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and roast 1 cup makhana over low heat for 5 minutes until crisp, then roast 0.25 cup slivered almonds for 1 minute and remove.
In the same ghee crisp 2 slit green chillies and 15 curry leaves for 30 seconds until fragrant and no longer spluttering.
Warm 2 cups puffed amaranth briefly in a dry pan to freshen its crunch, then tip it into a large bowl with all the roasted items.
Sprinkle over 1 tbsp powdered Anveshan Jaggery Powder, 1.5 tsp rock salt and 0.5 tsp black pepper and toss until evenly coated.
Cool the mixture fully and store airtight so the puffed grains stay crisp.
tips: Freshen the puffed amaranth in a dry hot pan for a minute if it has gone slightly limp in the packet.
Roast the makhana until it snaps cleanly, as underdone foxnuts turn chewy once the mix cools.
Keep this mix extra dry and skip lemon juice, since moisture quickly softens puffed amaranth.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve as a light, roasted fasting snack with fruit or fasting tea, ideal for those avoiding deep-fried food.

variations.name: Sweet Potato Farali Chevdo
variations.description: A vividly orange chevdo where crisp-fried sweet potato straws replace regular potato, lending a gentle caramel sweetness that plays beautifully against the salty-tangy seasoning. Coconut slivers and cashews make it a richer, more festive fasting mix.

ingredients.name: Sweet Potatoes, cut into thin straws
Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed oil that fries the sweet potato straws crisp while keeping their colour bright

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: balances the salt and lemon so the sweet potato's own sweetness stays subtle

steps: Soak the sweet potato straws in cold water for 10 minutes, then drain and pat them thoroughly dry.
Heat 2 cups Anveshan Groundnut Oil to 180C and fry the sweet potato straws in small batches for 2 to 3 minutes until crisp, then drain on paper.
In the same oil fry 0.3 cup sliced dried coconut and 0.25 cup cashews to pale gold, then fry 0.75 cup peanuts until crisp and drain all.
Crisp 3 slit green chillies and 15 curry leaves in 1 tbsp of the hot oil for 30 seconds, then remove.
In a large bowl toss the fried straws, coconut, nuts, chillies and curry leaves with 1.5 tsp rock salt, 1 tbsp powdered Anveshan Khandsari, 0.5 tsp black pepper and 1 tbsp lemon juice.
Let the chevdo cool completely before storing airtight to keep it crunchy.
tips: Fry the sweet potato straws in small batches and at a steady heat, as they brown faster than regular potato.
Slice the sweet potato as thin as possible so the straws crisp through instead of staying leathery.
The coconut can turn bitter if over-fried, so pull it out the moment it turns pale gold.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve as a festive fasting namkeen, its orange colour and sweet-salty crunch a bright change from the classic mix.

variations.name: Makhana Dry Fruit Farali Chevdo
variations.description: A rich, no-fry-potato chevdo built almost entirely on ghee-roasted foxnuts and a generous mix of nuts and seeds, seasoned in the classic sweet-salty fasting style. Crunchy, filling and protein-rich, it is the premium version to keep for long fasting days.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the makhana to a deep crisp and carries the fasting spices through the mix

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: powdered fine for the warm sweet note that balances the rock salt

steps: Heat 3 tbsp of the Anveshan Ghee in a wide pan and roast 3 cups makhana over low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until they snap crisp, then set aside.
In the remaining ghee roast 0.5 cup peanuts, 0.3 cup almonds and 0.3 cup cashews over medium heat for 4 minutes until golden, then add 2 tbsp melon seeds for the last minute.
Crisp 2 slit green chillies and 15 curry leaves in the same ghee for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Tip the roasted makhana, nuts, seeds, chillies and curry leaves into a large bowl.
Sprinkle over 1 tbsp powdered Anveshan Jaggery Powder, 1.5 tsp rock salt and 0.5 tsp black pepper and toss until evenly coated while still warm.
Cool the chevdo completely and store airtight to preserve its deep crunch.
tips: Roast the makhana low and slow until it snaps with a clean crack, or it will turn chewy on cooling.
Toss the seasoning while the mix is still warm so it clings to the ghee-coated makhana.
This mix is drier and keeps longer than fried chevdo; store it away from any moisture.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve as a rich, protein-packed fasting snack that satisfies through long vrat days, on its own or with fruit.

variations.name: Classic Gil E Firdaus
variations.description: A royal Hyderabadi pudding whose poetic name means 'clay of paradise', made from grated bottle gourd simmered in reduced milk with a little rice or sago for body. Enriched with khoya, saffron and cardamom, it is a silky, mildly sweet dessert that hides its humble lauki base entirely.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: sauteing the grated gourd in ghee removes its raw smell and enriches the pudding

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: steeped in warm milk to give this paradise pudding its glow and delicate aroma

steps: Peel and grate 500 g bottle gourd, squeeze out the excess water, and soak 3 tbsp sabudana in water for 20 minutes until softened.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a heavy pan and saute the grated gourd on medium for 6 to 7 minutes until it wilts and loses its raw smell.
Pour in 1 litre full-fat milk and simmer on medium-low for 20 minutes, stirring often, until the gourd is soft and the milk reduces and thickens.
Add the drained sabudana and cook 8 minutes until the pearls turn translucent and give the pudding body.
Stir in 0.75 cup sugar, 100 g crumbled khoya and 0.5 tsp cardamom and cook 5 minutes until the khoya melts in and the pudding is creamy.
Steep 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk, stir it through, fold in the chopped almonds and pistachios, and serve warm or chilled.
tips: Squeeze the grated gourd well before cooking so the pudding does not turn watery.
Saute the lauki thoroughly in ghee first; this single step removes the raw vegetable smell that puts people off.
Add the sugar only after the gourd is soft, as sugar added early stops it from cooking down properly.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve chilled in small bowls topped with saffron strands and slivered pistachios, a refined finish to a nawabi meal.

variations.name: Vermicelli Gil E Firdaus
variations.description: A festive variation that swaps the sago for roasted vermicelli, giving the bottle-gourd pudding delicate strands and a seviyan-like richness. Popular at Hyderabadi Eid tables, the toasted vermicelli lends a nutty aroma and a fuller body to the creamy base.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: sauteing the gourd and toasting the vermicelli in ghee builds this version's rich seviyan aroma

steps: Peel, grate and squeeze 450 g bottle gourd, then saute it in 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on medium for 6 minutes until wilted and raw-smell free.
Pour in 1 litre full-fat milk and simmer on medium-low for 18 minutes, stirring, until the gourd is soft and the milk thickens.
Lightly crush 0.5 cup roasted vermicelli, add it to the pudding, and cook 6 minutes until the strands soften and swell.
Stir in 0.75 cup sugar and 0.5 tsp cardamom and cook 4 minutes until the pudding turns creamy.
In the remaining 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee fry 10 cashews golden and 2 tbsp raisins until they plump, then stir them in with 3 tbsp chopped dates.
Finish with 1 tsp rose water off the heat and serve warm or chilled.
tips: Crush the vermicelli lightly so the strands stay short and spoonable in the pudding.
Do not overcook the vermicelli or it turns mushy and loses its distinct texture.
Chopped dates add natural sweetness, so you can reduce the sugar slightly if you like.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm for Eid, garnished with fried cashews and raisins, or chill it for a set seviyan-style pudding.

variations.name: Jaggery Coconut Gil E Firdaus
variations.description: A rustic, earthier take that sweetens the bottle-gourd pudding with jaggery and folds in coconut milk for a subtle tropical richness. The jaggery lends a caramel depth and warm colour that gives this humbler version a homely, festive character.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: sauteing the gourd in coconut oil layers in a gentle coastal aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: melted and strained to sweeten the pudding with a warm caramel depth in place of sugar

steps: Peel, grate and squeeze 500 g bottle gourd, and soak 3 tbsp sabudana for 20 minutes until soft.
Saute the grated gourd in 2 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil on medium for 6 minutes until wilted, then add 700 ml full-fat milk and simmer 18 minutes until soft and thickened.
Add the drained sabudana and cook 8 minutes until the pearls turn translucent.
Melt 0.75 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder with 0.25 cup water on low, strain out grit, and stir the syrup into the pudding with 0.5 tsp cardamom.
Pour in 1 cup coconut milk off high heat, stirring gently so it does not split, and warm through for 3 minutes.
Fold in 3 tbsp grated coconut and 3 tbsp chopped cashews and serve warm or chilled.
tips: Always melt and strain the jaggery separately, and add it after the milk has thickened so the milk does not curdle.
Add the coconut milk on low heat right at the end to keep it smooth and prevent splitting.
This version tastes even better the next day once the jaggery and coconut mellow together.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve chilled topped with toasted coconut flakes for a rustic, coastal-inflected dessert.

variations.name: Makhana Gil E Firdaus
variations.description: A nourishing modern take that folds ghee-roasted foxnuts into the bottle-gourd pudding for extra protein and a soft, dumpling-like bite. The makhana soaks up the saffron milk and adds wholesome body, turning the paradise pudding into a lighter, more filling dessert.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the makhana crisp and sautes the gourd, enriching the whole pudding

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: steeped in milk to perfume and colour this superfood version of the paradise pudding

ingredients.name: Anveshan Honey
ingredients.note: sweetens the pudding naturally, added off the heat to keep its aroma

steps: Roast 1 cup makhana in 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on low for 5 minutes until crisp, then coarsely crush half and keep the rest whole.
Peel, grate and squeeze 450 g bottle gourd and saute it in the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee for 6 minutes until wilted.
Add 1 litre full-fat milk and simmer on medium-low for 18 minutes, stirring, until the gourd softens and the milk thickens.
Add both the crushed and whole makhana and cook 8 minutes until they soften and swell into the pudding, then stir in 0.5 tsp cardamom.
Steep 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk and stir it through, then take the pan off the heat and cool for 5 minutes.
Stir in 5 tbsp Anveshan Honey so it stays raw and fragrant, fold in the almonds and walnuts, and serve warm or chilled.
tips: Roast the makhana until fully crisp so they hold a soft bite rather than turning slimy in the milk.
Add the honey only after the pudding cools a little, since boiling honey loses its aroma and benefits.
Leave some makhana whole for texture and crush the rest to naturally thicken the pudding.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm as a protein-rich dessert, topped with a few crisp roasted makhana and chopped walnuts.

variations.name: Classic Govind Gatta
variations.description: The showpiece of a Jaipur banquet: thick besan logs stuffed with a spiced dry-fruit and coconut filling, deep-fried golden and simmered in a robust onion-tomato gravy. Sliced open, each piece reveals a jewelled centre, making this the grandest of all Rajasthani gatta dishes.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee binds the rich stuffing and finishes the gravy with a nutty Rajasthani aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A clean wood-pressed oil deep-fries the stuffed logs crisp without a heavy aftertaste

steps: Knead 1.5 cups besan with 0.25 tsp turmeric, 0.75 tsp salt, 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and enough water into a firm pliable dough and rest it covered for 10 minutes.
Chop 10 cashews and 1 tbsp raisins fine and mix with 2 tbsp desiccated coconut, 0.25 tsp garam masala and a pinch of salt to make the sweet-spiced stuffing.
Divide the dough into 6 balls, flatten each, place a spoon of stuffing in the centre, seal into a smooth thick log, then steam the logs for 10 minutes until firm; cool and cut into 2 cm pieces.
Heat 2 cups Anveshan Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil to 170C and fry the pieces in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and crisp, then drain on paper.

In a kadai heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds, add 2 chopped onions and fry until golden, then add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and 2 pureed tomatoes and cook until the ghee separates, about 8 minutes.

Add the remaining 0.25 tsp turmeric, 1.5 tbsp coriander powder, 1 tsp chilli powder and 2 cups water with the remaining salt, simmer 5 minutes, slide in the fried gatte and simmer 6 to 8 minutes until they drink up the gravy; finish with 0.5 tsp garam masala.
tips: Seal the stuffing with no cracks, or the filling leaks out while steaming and frying.
Fry the logs only to golden; too dark and they turn hard inside the gravy.
Add the gatte to the gravy just 8 minutes before serving so they stay slightly firm and hold their shape.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with saffron pulao or laccha paratha, slicing each piece at the table to reveal the stuffing.

variations.name: Shahi Makhani Govind Gatta
variations.description: A royal wedding-style Govind gatta bathed in a velvety cashew-tomato makhani gravy finished with cream and kasuri methi. The stuffed logs stay soft and rich, and the mild, buttery sauce turns this into pure festive indulgence.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Generous ghee keeps the stuffed gatte tender and enriches the makhani gravy

steps: Knead 1.5 cups besan with 0.25 tsp turmeric, 0.5 tsp salt and 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee into a firm dough and rest 10 minutes.

Make the rich stuffing by mixing 3 tbsp crumbled khoya with 8 chopped almonds, a pinch of garam masala and a little salt, then flatten dough balls, fill and seal into smooth logs and steam for 10 minutes; cool and cut into 2 cm pieces.
Soak 15 cashews in warm water for 10 minutes, then grind with 4 tomatoes and 3 cardamom pods to a smooth puree.

Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a kadai, add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and fry for 1 minute, then pour in the cashew-tomato puree and cook on medium-low for 12 minutes, stirring, until the ghee separates.
Add the remaining 0.25 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, 1.25 tsp salt and 1.5 cups water and simmer for 5 minutes into a glossy makhani gravy.
Slide in the steamed gatte, simmer gently for 6 minutes, then stir in 4 tbsp cream off the boil, 1 tsp crushed kasuri methi and 0.5 tsp garam masala and warm through for 2 minutes before serving.
tips: Steam rather than fry these gatte so they stay soft and soak up the creamy makhani.
Strain the cashew-tomato puree for an ultra-smooth restaurant-style gravy.
Add the cream on the lowest heat so the makhani stays silky and does not split.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with butter naan or saffron pulao, finished with a swirl of cream and a few slivered almonds.

variations.name: Paneer-Stuffed Govind Gatta
variations.description: A protein-rich twist where the besan logs hide a spiced paneer and green-chilli filling instead of dry fruit, simmered in a tangy tomato-yogurt gravy. The soft paneer centre melts slightly against the firm gatta shell for a comforting, homely richness.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee tempers the tomato-yogurt gravy and lends the stuffed gatte a homely richness

ingredients.name: Anveshan Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A clean wood-pressed oil fries the paneer-filled logs crisp and golden

steps: Knead 1.5 cups besan with 0.25 tsp turmeric, 0.75 tsp salt and 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee into a firm dough and rest 10 minutes.

Mix 0.75 cup grated paneer with 2 finely chopped green chillies, 0.25 tsp garam masala and a pinch of salt, then flatten dough balls, fill with the paneer mixture, seal into logs and steam for 10 minutes; cool and cut into 2 cm pieces.
Heat 2 cups Anveshan Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil to 170C and fry the pieces for 3 minutes until light golden, then drain.

Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a kadai, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds, add 2 chopped onions and fry until golden, then add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and 2 pureed tomatoes and cook 8 minutes until the ghee separates.
Add the remaining 0.25 tsp turmeric, 1.5 tbsp coriander powder and 1 tsp chilli powder, then lower the heat and whisk in 0.5 cup yogurt slowly, stirring for 3 minutes so it does not split.
Add 1.5 cups water and the remaining salt, simmer 5 minutes, slide in the fried gatte and simmer 6 minutes, then finish with 0.5 tsp garam masala.
tips: Grate the paneer fine and press the filling well so it does not crumble out while sealing.
Fry the logs only lightly, as the paneer inside softens further in the gravy.
Whisk the yogurt smooth and add it off high heat so the tangy gravy stays creamy.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with tandoori roti or jeera rice, garnished with coriander and a few paneer crumbs.

variations.name: Achari Govind Gatta in Yogurt Gravy
variations.description: A tangy Shekhawati take where the stuffed gatte rest in a pickle-spiced curd gravy built on browned onions and a fresh five-seed achari tempering in mustard oil. Fennel, nigella and fenugreek give it the sharp perfume of Rajasthani pickle around the rich stuffed centre.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: Pungent wood-pressed mustard oil is the soul of the achari masala around these stuffed gatte

steps: Knead 1.5 cups besan with 0.25 tsp turmeric, 0.75 tsp salt and 1 tbsp of the mustard oil into a firm dough, fill flattened balls with a mix of 10 chopped cashews and 2 tbsp desiccated coconut, seal into logs and steam 10 minutes; cool and cut into 2 cm pieces.
Coarsely crush 1 tsp fennel, 0.5 tsp nigella, 0.5 tsp mustard and 0.25 tsp methi seeds into an achari spice mix.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil in a kadai until it just smokes, lower the heat and splutter the crushed achari spices for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add 2 finely chopped onions and fry on medium for 7 minutes until deep golden, then add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.

Lower the heat to minimum, whisk 1 cup yogurt with the remaining 0.25 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp chilli powder, pour it in and stir constantly for 4 minutes until it simmers without splitting, then add 1.5 cups water and the remaining salt.
Slide in the steamed gatte and simmer uncovered on low for 8 minutes until the tangy pickle gravy clings to them, then rest 5 minutes so the achari spices bloom before serving.
tips: Bring the mustard oil to a light smoke first, then lower the flame before the achari spices go in.
Crush the achari seeds coarse, not powder, so you get bursts of fennel and nigella in each bite.
Steam the gatte rather than fry so the pickle gravy soaks into the shell around the sweet stuffing.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with plain paratha or bajra roti and a spoon of mango pickle to echo the achari notes.

variations.name: Classic Hara Bhara Kabab
variations.description: Hara Bhara Kabab is the vibrant green tea-time patty made from spinach, green peas and potato bound with roasted gram flour. Pan-fried till crisp outside and soft inside, its fresh green colour and mild spicing make it a wholesome, popular vegetarian snack.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: pan-fries the kababs to a crisp golden crust without a greasy finish

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sattu
ingredients.note: roasted gram flour that binds the moist green mix and keeps it light

steps: Blanch 2 cups spinach for 1 minute, refresh in cold water to keep it bright green, then squeeze dry and chop fine.
Coarsely mash 0.75 cup boiled peas and mix with the 2 mashed potatoes, chopped spinach, 2 green chillies and grated ginger.
Add 3 tbsp Anveshan Sattu, 0.75 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp roasted cumin, 0.75 tsp amchur and 1 tsp salt, and knead into a firm, non-sticky dough.
Shape into round patties and press a cashew half into the centre of each for the classic garnish.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on a flat tawa on medium heat until it shimmers.
Shallow-fry the kababs for 3 to 4 minutes each side, adding the remaining ghee as needed, until crisp and golden, then drain and serve hot.
tips: Squeeze the blanched spinach thoroughly dry, as excess water makes the kababs soggy and hard to bind.
Roasted sattu binds better and stays lighter than raw besan, which can taste doughy.
If the mix feels sticky, chill it for 15 minutes or add a spoon more sattu before shaping.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with mint-coriander chutney and tomato ketchup, alongside a cup of masala chai.

variations.name: Cheese-Stuffed Hara Bhara Kabab
variations.description: A kid-friendly upgrade where each green kabab hides a molten cube of cheese that oozes at the first bite. The crisp spinach shell and gooey centre make it an irresistible party and lunchbox snack.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: shallow-fries the stuffed kababs to a crisp golden shell

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sattu
ingredients.note: roasted gram flour binder that keeps the shell firm around the cheese

steps: Blanch 2 cups spinach for a minute, refresh in cold water, squeeze dry and chop fine to keep the colour vivid.

Mash 0.75 cup peas and 2 potatoes together, then mix with the spinach, 2 green chillies, grated ginger, 3 tbsp Anveshan Sattu, 1 tsp chaat masala, 0.5 tsp garam masala and 1 tsp salt into a firm dough.
Take a portion, flatten it on your palm, place a cheese cube in the centre, and seal it into a smooth stuffed patty.
Roll each stuffed kabab lightly in bread crumbs for an extra-crisp coat.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on a tawa on medium heat and shallow-fry the kababs for 3 minutes each side, adding ghee as needed, until golden and crisp.
Serve immediately while the cheese centre is hot and molten.
tips: Seal the cheese completely inside the patty so it does not leak out during frying.
Serve straight away, as the cheese firms up quickly once the kababs cool.
Chill the stuffed kababs for 10 minutes before frying so they hold their shape.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with schezwan sauce and ketchup as a party platter or after-school treat.

variations.name: Air-Fried Oats Hara Bhara Kabab
variations.description: A wholesome, low-oil version where rolled oats replace some binder and the kababs are air-fried instead of pan-fried. It keeps the fresh green flavour while cutting the fat, ideal for a health-conscious snack.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: brushed lightly over the kababs so they crisp in the air fryer

steps: Blanch 2 cups spinach for a minute, refresh in cold water, squeeze dry and chop fine.

Coarsely mash 1 cup boiled peas, then mix with the spinach, 100 g grated paneer, 0.5 cup powdered oats, 2 green chillies, grated ginger, 1 tsp roasted cumin, 3 tbsp coriander, 0.75 tsp amchur and 1 tsp salt into a firm dough.
Rest the mix for 10 minutes so the oats absorb moisture and bind, then shape into flat patties.
Brush both sides of each kabab lightly with Anveshan Groundnut Oil and arrange in a single layer.
Preheat the air fryer to 190C, air-fry the kababs for 10 minutes, flip and brush again with oil, then air-fry another 8 minutes until golden and crisp.
Rest for 2 minutes so the crust firms up, then serve warm.
tips: Powdered oats bind moisture well and add fibre while keeping the kababs light.
Do not overcrowd the air-fryer basket so each kabab crisps evenly.
Rest the mix before shaping so the oats swell and hold the patties together.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a hung-curd dip and a squeeze of lemon for a light, guilt-free tea-time plate.

variations.name: Hara Bhara Kabab Roll
variations.description: A satisfying street-style meal where crisp hara bhara kababs are wrapped in a soft khapli-atta roti with onions, chutney and a tangy slaw. It turns the humble snack into a portable, filling roll perfect for lunch on the go.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khapli Atta
ingredients.note: kneaded into soft, nutty rotis that wrap the kababs without cracking

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: cooks the rotis and pan-fries the kababs golden and crisp

steps: Knead 1.5 cups Anveshan Khapli Atta with about 0.66 cup water and 0.25 tsp salt into a soft, non-sticky dough and rest it for 15 minutes.

Blanch and squeeze 2 cups spinach dry, chop fine, then mix with 0.75 cup mashed peas, 2 mashed potatoes, 3 tbsp roasted chana powder, 2 green chillies, 1 tsp chaat masala and 1 tsp salt, and shape into oblong kababs.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on a tawa on medium heat and pan-fry the kababs for 3 minutes each side until crisp and golden.
Roll the dough into rotis and cook each on the tawa with a little ghee for 1 minute per side until soft with light brown spots.
Toss the shredded cabbage and sliced onion with a pinch of chaat masala into a quick slaw.
Spread mint chutney on each roti, lay two kababs and a handful of slaw, roll tightly, and serve warm.
tips: Keep the khapli rotis soft and slightly thick so they wrap without tearing.
Shape the kababs oblong rather than round so they sit neatly along the roll.
Wrap the base in paper or foil so the roll holds together and stays warm on the go.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve the rolls halved on a diagonal with extra mint chutney and a wedge of lemon for lunch on the go.

variations.name: Classic Kaddu Ki Kheer
variations.description: A comforting North Indian kheer of grated pumpkin simmered in reduced milk until it melts into a soft, fragrant pudding. Lightly sweetened and scented with cardamom, it turns the humble kaddu into a silky, saffron-flecked dessert studded with ghee-fried nuts.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: sautes the grated pumpkin to remove its raw edge and fries the nut garnish

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: steeped in warm milk to give the kheer its golden hue and floral aroma

steps: Peel and grate enough pumpkin to give 3 cups, and squeeze out any excess moisture.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a heavy pan and saute the grated pumpkin on medium for 7 minutes until it softens and its raw smell disappears.
Pour in 1 litre full-fat milk and simmer on medium-low for 20 minutes, stirring often, until the pumpkin melts in and the milk reduces and thickens.
Stir in 0.75 cup sugar and 0.5 tsp cardamom and cook 5 minutes until the sugar dissolves and the kheer turns creamy.
Steep 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk and stir it through for colour and aroma.
Fry 10 cashews, 10 almonds and 2 tbsp raisins in the remaining 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee until golden, fold most in, and serve warm or chilled with the rest on top.
tips: Squeeze the grated pumpkin before cooking so the kheer does not turn watery.
Saute the pumpkin properly in ghee first, which is the key to losing its raw vegetable smell.
Add the sugar only after the pumpkin is soft, as early sugar keeps it from cooking down.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve chilled in bowls topped with saffron strands and fried nuts, a lovely festive or vrat-friendly dessert.

variations.name: Jaggery Coconut Kaddu Kheer
variations.description: A South Indian style kaddu payasam sweetened with jaggery and finished with coconut milk for a fragrant, caramel-rich pudding. Coconut-oil-fried cashews and a hint of dry ginger give it the distinct aroma of a Kerala festival sweet.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: melted and strained to sweeten the payasam with deep caramel notes instead of sugar

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: sautes the pumpkin and fries the cashews for an authentic coastal aroma

steps: Saute 3 cups grated pumpkin in 1 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil on medium for 7 minutes until it softens and loses its raw smell.
Add 600 ml full-fat milk and simmer on medium-low for 18 minutes until the pumpkin melts in and the milk thickens.
Melt 1 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder with 0.25 cup water on low, strain out grit, and stir the syrup into the kheer with 0.5 tsp cardamom and 0.25 tsp dry ginger powder.
Pour in 1 cup coconut milk off high heat, stirring gently so it does not split, and warm through for 3 minutes.
Fry 12 cashews and 3 tbsp grated coconut in the remaining 1 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil until golden.
Fold the fried cashews and coconut in and serve the payasam warm.
tips: Add the jaggery only after the milk has thickened, and off a rolling boil, so the milk does not curdle.
The pinch of dry ginger powder is a traditional Kerala touch that aids digestion and adds warmth.
Stir in the coconut milk gently on low heat to keep the payasam smooth.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm as a temple-style payasam, ideally on a banana leaf, garnished with toasted coconut.

variations.name: Roasted Pumpkin Rabri Kheer
variations.description: A decadent version where the pumpkin is roasted to concentrate its sweetness, then folded into a thick, khoya-enriched rabri. Slow reduction and mawa give this kheer a luxurious, almost fudgy density fit for a wedding dessert table.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the pumpkin cubes and enriches the thick rabri base

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: steeped in milk to colour and perfume this richer rabri-style kheer

steps: Peel and cube 400 g pumpkin, toss with 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, and roast in the pan or oven for 12 minutes until caramelised and soft, then mash coarsely.
Bring 1 litre full-fat milk to a boil and simmer on medium-low for 22 minutes, stirring and scraping the sides, until it reduces to a thick rabri.
Crumble in 100 g khoya and cook 4 minutes until it melts smoothly into the rabri.
Fold in the mashed roasted pumpkin with 0.75 cup sugar and 0.5 tsp cardamom and cook 6 minutes until thick and creamy.
Steep 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk, stir it through, and finish with the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee for a glossy sheen.
Fold in half the pistachios and almonds and serve warm or chilled topped with the rest.
tips: Roasting the pumpkin instead of boiling it deepens the flavour and stops the kheer from turning watery.
Keep scraping the sides of the pan while reducing the milk so the dried cream folds back in as rabri.
This kheer is very rich, so serve it in small portions.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve chilled in kulhads topped with slivered pistachios, a festive rabri-style dessert for celebrations.

variations.name: Vegan Almond-Milk Kaddu Kheer
variations.description: A light, dairy-free kheer where the pumpkin simmers in almond milk and is sweetened with honey for a delicate, nutty pudding. Naturally lighter than the milk version, it keeps the cardamom and saffron soul of the classic while suiting plant-based diets.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: sautes the pumpkin and fries the nuts in this dairy-free version

ingredients.name: Anveshan Honey
ingredients.note: sweetens the kheer naturally, stirred in off the heat to keep its aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: steeped in warm almond milk to keep the kheer's signature colour and scent

steps: Saute 3 cups grated pumpkin in 1 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil on medium for 7 minutes until soft and free of its raw smell.
Pour in 900 ml almond milk and simmer on medium-low for 15 minutes, stirring, until the pumpkin melts in and the kheer thickens slightly.
Steep 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp warm almond milk and stir it in with 0.5 tsp cardamom.
Take the pan off the heat and cool for 5 minutes, then stir in 5 tbsp Anveshan Honey so it stays raw and fragrant.
Fry 3 tbsp slivered almonds and 2 tbsp cashews in the remaining 1 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil until golden.
Fold most of the nuts in and serve warm or chilled topped with the rest.
tips: Almond milk thickens less than dairy, so simmer a little longer or add a spoon of ground almonds for body.
Add the honey only after cooling slightly, since boiling honey loses its aroma.
Use unsweetened almond milk so you can control the sweetness with the honey.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve chilled as a light vegan dessert, topped with toasted slivered almonds and a saffron strand.

variations.name: Classic Rajasthani Kadhi Vada
variations.description: Soft urad-dal vadas simmered in a tangy, hing-tempered besan-and-curd kadhi. The fried vadas soak up the sour yellow gravy until pillowy, making this a beloved Marwari one-pot that turns humble pantry staples into a satisfying meal.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Bilona ghee makes the cumin-hing tempering that gives this Rajasthani kadhi its signature aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A clean wood-pressed oil fries the vadas light and golden without heaviness

steps: Soak 0.75 cup urad dal for 4 hours, drain and grind to a thick fluffy batter with minimal water, then whisk in 0.5 tbsp of the ginger-green chilli paste and 0.5 tsp salt and beat well until light.

Heat 2 cups Anveshan Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil to 170C and drop in small spoonfuls of batter, frying in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until golden, then soak the vadas in warm water for 10 minutes and gently squeeze.
For the kadhi, whisk 1.5 cups sour yogurt with 0.5 cup besan, 0.5 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp red chilli powder until lump-free, then stir in 3 cups water.

Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a deep pot on medium, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds, 2 dried red chillies and 0.25 tsp hing for 30 seconds, then add the remaining ginger-green chilli paste and fry 30 seconds.

Lower the heat to minimum, pour in the yogurt-besan mixture and stir continuously for 6 minutes until it comes to a simmer without splitting, then add 1 tsp salt and cook on low for 15 to 18 minutes, stirring often, until it thickens and loses the raw besan taste.
Slide in the squeezed vadas and simmer gently for 5 minutes so they drink up the kadhi, finish with 3 tbsp chopped coriander, and rest 5 minutes before serving.
tips: Beat the vada batter until a small dollop floats in water, which guarantees light, airy vadas.
Soak the fried vadas in warm water and squeeze gently so they turn soft and absorb the kadhi.
Cook the kadhi low and slow for at least 15 minutes; a rushed kadhi tastes raw and floury.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot over steamed rice with a spoon of ghee and a side of garlic chutney or mango pickle.

variations.name: Gujarati Sweet-Sour Kadhi Vada
variations.description: A thin, silky Gujarati kadhi balanced between sweet and sour with jaggery and curd, holding soft moong-dal vadas. Curry leaves, ginger and a whisper of cinnamon and clove make it fragrant and delicate rather than fiery.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee carries the delicate curry-leaf tempering typical of a Gujarati kadhi

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: Natural jaggery gives the gentle sweetness that balances the sour curd in Gujarati kadhi

steps: Soak 0.75 cup moong dal for 3 hours, grind to a smooth thick batter, beat in 0.5 tbsp ginger-green chilli paste and 0.5 tsp salt until fluffy, then fry small vadas in ghee or hot oil until golden and soak them in warm water for 10 minutes.
Whisk 1.5 cups yogurt with 3 tbsp besan and 0.25 tsp turmeric until smooth, then add 3.5 cups water to make a thin kadhi base.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pot on medium and splutter 1 tsp cumin seeds, 0.5 tsp mustard seeds, 1 inch cinnamon, 2 cloves and 12 curry leaves for 30 seconds until fragrant.

Add the remaining ginger-green chilli paste, fry 30 seconds, then lower the heat to minimum and pour in the yogurt-besan mixture, stirring continuously for 6 minutes until it simmers without curdling.
Add 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder and 1.25 tsp salt and simmer on low for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until the kadhi is thin, glossy and balanced sweet-sour.
Gently squeeze the soaked vadas and add them to the kadhi, warm through for 4 minutes, garnish with 2 tbsp coriander and serve.
tips: Gujarati kadhi is meant to be thin and pourable, so do not over-thicken it with extra besan.
Add the jaggery only after the curd has come to a simmer so it dissolves evenly without splitting the kadhi.
Grind the moong batter smooth rather than coarse for the softest vadas in this delicate kadhi.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with soft steamed rice or khichdi, drizzled with a little extra ghee.

variations.name: Punjabi Onion Pakora Kadhi Vada
variations.description: The hearty Punjabi kadhi, thick and deeply tangy, studded with crisp onion pakora vadas that turn spongy in the golden gravy. A long, patient simmer gives the besan its characteristic toasty depth, finished with a fiery red-chilli ghee tadka.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: Ghee makes the fiery red-chilli tadka poured over the finished Punjabi kadhi

ingredients.name: Anveshan Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: A clean wood-pressed oil fries the onion pakoras crisp and golden

steps: Make the pakora batter by mixing 0.5 cup besan with 2 thinly sliced onions, 0.5 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, a pinch of turmeric and 0.5 tsp salt, adding a little water to a thick clinging batter.
Heat 2 cups Anveshan Wood-Pressed Groundnut Oil to 175C and fry small clusters for 4 minutes until deep golden and crisp, then drain on paper.
For the kadhi, whisk 1.5 cups very sour yogurt with the remaining 0.5 cup besan, 0.75 tsp turmeric and 1 tbsp coriander powder until smooth, then add 4 cups water.

Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a deep pot, crackle 1 tsp cumin seeds and 0.5 tsp methi seeds, add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and fry 1 minute, then lower the heat and pour in the yogurt-besan mixture, stirring constantly for 6 minutes until it simmers.
Add 1 tsp salt and simmer on low for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often, until the kadhi turns thick, glossy and golden-brown, then drop in the pakoras and cook 8 more minutes until spongy.
For the tadka heat the remaining 1 tbsp ghee, add 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder off the heat, and pour the red sizzling ghee over the kadhi before serving.
tips: Use the most sour curd you have; Punjabi kadhi depends on a sharp tang that mellows over the long simmer.
Add the pakoras only in the last 8 minutes so they stay soft-spongy and do not dissolve.
The kadhi thickens as it sits, so keep it a little looser than final and reheat with a splash of water.
