variations.servingSuggestion: Serve over a mound of steamed rice with a raw onion salad and a dab of green chilli pickle.

variations.name: South Indian Majjige Kadhi Vada with Coconut
variations.description: A Karnataka-style buttermilk kadhi where soft vadas rest in a ground coconut, cumin and green-chilli curd sauce, crowned with a mustard and curry-leaf tempering in coconut oil. Light, fragrant and coconut-sweet, it is a cooling southern cousin of the northern kadhi.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: Wood-pressed coconut oil ties the tempering to the ground coconut kadhi base

steps: Soak 0.75 cup urad dal for 4 hours, grind fluffy with little water, beat in a pinch of salt, fry small vadas in hot oil until golden, then soak in warm water for 10 minutes and squeeze gently.
Grind 0.5 cup grated coconut with 3 green chillies, 1 tsp cumin seeds and 1 inch ginger to a smooth paste.
Whisk 1.5 cups yogurt with the coconut paste, 1 tbsp besan and 1.25 tsp salt, then thin with 2.5 cups water to a light kadhi.
Pour the buttermilk kadhi into a pot over the lowest heat and warm it gently for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring constantly, until it steams and thickens slightly but never boils.
Add the squeezed vadas and simmer very gently for 4 minutes so they soften and absorb the coconut sauce.

In a small pan heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil, splutter 0.5 tsp mustard seeds, 2 dried red chillies and 12 curry leaves for 20 seconds, then pour this tempering over the kadhi and cover for 2 minutes before serving.
tips: Keep this coconut kadhi below a boil throughout, as the thin buttermilk sauce curdles the instant it bubbles hard.
Grind the coconut paste very fine so the kadhi is silky rather than grainy.
Add the vadas just before serving so they stay soft without disintegrating in the delicate sauce.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm with steamed rice and a spoon of ghee, alongside a crisp papad.

variations.name: Classic Kaju Halwa
variations.description: Kaju halwa is a luxurious cashew pudding made by cooking freshly ground cashew paste in ghee and milk until it turns into a soft, ivory-coloured fudge that melts on the tongue. Delicately scented with cardamom, it is the halwa of festivals and gift boxes, richer than any grain-based version.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: cooks the cashew paste to a smooth, glossy fudge and keeps it from sticking

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: sweetens the cashew halwa cleanly while keeping its pale ivory colour

steps: Soak 1.5 cups cashews in warm water for 15 minutes, drain, then blend with just enough of the 1 cup milk to a smooth thick paste.
Heat 3 tbsp of the Anveshan Ghee in a non-stick pan, add the cashew paste and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, for 6 to 7 minutes.
Pour in the remaining milk and 0.6 cup Anveshan Khandsari and keep stirring for 5 minutes until the sugar dissolves and the mixture loosens.
Add the rest of the ghee a spoon at a time and cook for 5 to 6 minutes more until the halwa thickens and leaves the sides of the pan.
Stir in 0.5 tsp cardamom powder until the halwa is glossy and holds a soft shape.
Spoon into bowls, scatter 2 tbsp slivered almonds over the top and serve the kaju halwa warm.
tips: Grind the cashews to a smooth paste but stop before they turn oily, or the halwa will feel greasy.
Cook only on low heat, as cashew paste scorches and turns grainy the moment the flame rises.
For a firmer barfi-like set, spread the hot halwa in a greased tray and cut once cooled.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm in small bowls as a festive dessert, or set firm and cut into diamonds topped with edible silver leaf for gifting.

variations.name: Kesar Kaju Malai Halwa
variations.description: A saffron-gilded version enriched with cream and reduced milk for an extra-plush, malai-soft cashew halwa. Bloomed saffron paints it a warm gold and lends a floral fragrance that turns this into a wedding-grade sweet.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: cooks the cashew paste to a plush, glossy malai halwa

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: bloomed in warm milk to colour and perfume this rich kaju halwa

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: sweetens the halwa while keeping the saffron gold clear and bright

steps: Soak 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk from the 1 cup and set aside to bloom.
Soak 1.5 cups cashews in warm water for 15 minutes, drain and blend with a little milk to a smooth paste.
Heat 4 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a non-stick pan, add the cashew paste and cook over low heat, stirring, for 6 minutes until it smells nutty.
Pour in the remaining milk, 0.25 cup fresh cream and 0.6 cup Anveshan Khandsari and cook for 6 to 7 minutes until it thickens.
Stir in the bloomed saffron milk and 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and cook for 4 minutes more until the halwa turns a soft gold and leaves the pan.
Fold in half the slivered pistachios, spoon into bowls and finish with the rest before serving warm.
tips: Add the cream off a high flame so it enriches the halwa without splitting.
Bloom the saffron in warm milk first so its colour spreads evenly instead of streaking.
This halwa stays soft and spoonable even when chilled, thanks to the cream.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve this saffron malai kaju halwa warm at weddings and festivals, garnished with slivered pistachios and a few saffron strands.

variations.name: Kaju Pista Rose Halwa
variations.description: A pretty pink-and-green halwa where cashew paste meets ground pistachios and a whisper of rose water, giving a fragrant, floral fudge flecked with green. The pistachio adds bite and colour while the rose keeps it delicate and festive.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: cooks the cashew and pistachio paste to a fragrant, glossy fudge

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: sweetens the halwa without masking the delicate rose and pistachio

steps: Soak 1 cup cashews and 0.5 cup pistachios in warm water for 15 minutes, drain, then blend with a little of the milk to a smooth paste.
Heat 3 tbsp of the Anveshan Ghee in a non-stick pan, add the nut paste and cook over low heat, stirring, for 6 to 7 minutes.
Pour in the remaining milk and 0.6 cup Anveshan Khandsari and keep stirring for 5 minutes until the sugar melts and the mixture loosens.
Add the remaining ghee gradually and cook for 5 minutes more until the halwa thickens and pulls from the sides of the pan.
Take it off the heat, stir in 1 tsp rose water quickly so the aroma does not cook off, and mix until glossy.
Spoon into bowls, scatter 1 tbsp dried rose petals over the top and serve the kaju pista halwa warm.
tips: Blanch and peel the pistachios if you want the brightest green colour in the finished halwa.
Add the rose water only after the pan is off the flame, as heat destroys its fragrance.
Keep the pistachio proportion under a third of the nuts, or its oil can make the halwa heavy.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm as a fragrant festive sweet, or set firm and cut into squares topped with a single rose petal for gifting.

variations.name: Vegan Kaju Coconut Halwa
variations.description: A dairy-free cashew halwa cooked in coconut milk and coconut oil and sweetened with jaggery, giving a soft fudge with warm caramel and coconut notes. It proves kaju halwa needs no dairy to stay rich and melt-in-the-mouth.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: cooks the cashew paste and keeps this halwa entirely plant-based

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: sweetens the cashew halwa with a warm, earthy caramel note

steps: Soak 1.5 cups cashews in warm water for 15 minutes, drain and blend with a little coconut milk to a smooth paste.
Heat 3 tbsp of the Anveshan Coconut Oil in a non-stick pan, add the cashew paste and cook over low heat, stirring, for 6 to 7 minutes.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk and cook for 4 minutes until the mixture loosens and turns creamy.
Lower the heat, stir in 0.6 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder off the boil so it does not split, and cook for 4 minutes until melted.
Add the remaining coconut oil and 0.25 cup desiccated coconut and cook for 4 minutes more until the halwa thickens and leaves the pan.
Fold in 0.5 tsp cardamom powder, spoon into bowls and serve the vegan kaju halwa warm.
tips: Stir the jaggery in off the boil so the coconut milk stays smooth and does not curdle.
Use fresh, unsalted cashews, as roasted or salted ones throw off both the colour and the flavour.
A tablespoon of coconut oil rubbed on your palms lets you roll leftovers into neat laddoos.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm as a vegan festive dessert, garnished with toasted coconut, or roll into laddoos coated in desiccated coconut.

variations.name: Classic Kathal Kabab
variations.description: Raw jackfruit boiled soft, mashed and bound with roasted gram, then shallow-fried into meaty, smoky patties that fool everyone at the table. The stringy texture of kathal mimics kebab meat while whole and ground spices lend an old-Delhi seekh-house depth. Crisp at the edges, moist within.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sattu
ingredients.note: roasted sattu binds the mash and adds a nutty backbone without egg

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed groundnut oil for shallow-frying gives a clean, aromatic crust

steps: Rub your palms and knife with a little oil, then chop the raw jackfruit into 2-inch chunks; pressure-cook with 1 cup water and ½ tsp salt for 4 whistles until fork-soft, about 15 minutes.
Drain thoroughly and squeeze out every drop of water, then mash the kathal with the boiled potato into a coarse, fibrous paste while still warm.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a pan and sauté the finely chopped onion, green chilli and ginger-garlic paste over medium heat until golden, about 4 minutes.

Mix the sautéed masala into the mash along with 3 tbsp Anveshan Sattu, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp red chilli powder, coriander and remaining salt; knead into a firm, non-sticky dough.
Shape into 10 flat oval patties and rest them in the fridge for 10 minutes so they hold together while frying.
Heat the remaining Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a flat pan over medium heat and shallow-fry the kababs 3 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp-edged.
tips: If the mixture feels wet and refuses to hold, add another tablespoon of sattu rather than breadcrumbs to keep it gluten-light and nutty.
Chill the shaped patties before frying; cold kababs stay intact and brown more evenly.
Boil the kathal a little under-done rather than mushy so the finished kabab keeps its meaty bite.
variations.servingSuggestion: Pile onto a platter with rings of raw onion, lemon wedges and a bowl of mint-coriander chutney, and tuck leftovers into a pav with sliced tomato for a next-day kabab roll.

variations.name: Awadhi Galouti-Style Kathal Kabab
variations.description: A Lucknawi tribute where the jackfruit is mashed silk-smooth and perfumed with kewra, mace and a whisper of saffron ghee, then melted on a griddle until it dissolves on the tongue. Unlike the crisp classic, these are deliberately soft, rich and fragrant. The hallmark galouti tenderness comes from a fine paste and gentle low-heat searing.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee both binds the paste and sears the kababs for that melt-in-mouth Awadhi finish

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: a few strands bloomed in warm ghee give the royal amber aroma

steps: Pressure-cook the oiled, chopped jackfruit with 1 cup water for 4 whistles until completely soft, then drain and squeeze bone-dry.
Warm 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, drop in the Anveshan Saffron strands off the heat and let them bloom for a minute until the ghee turns golden and fragrant.
Blend the jackfruit with fried onion, cashew paste, roasted chana dal powder, ginger-garlic paste and the saffron ghee into a very smooth, pipe-able paste.
Fold in mace, cardamom, white pepper, kewra water and salt, then rest the mixture covered for 15 minutes so the flavours settle and firm up.
Wet your palms with a little ghee and pat the paste into small thick discs, handling them gently as they are soft.
Heat the remaining Anveshan Ghee on a flat tawa over low heat and sear the kababs 3 to 4 minutes each side until a fragile golden crust forms while the centre stays melting.
tips: Keep the heat low; galouti kababs scorch fast because of the ghee and cashew richness.
If the paste is too loose to shape, chill it for 20 minutes and add an extra spoon of roasted chana dal powder.
Make the birista fresh and crush it fine, as it is the main source of sweet depth here.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve two per person on warm ultra-thin rumali roti or sheermal with a squeeze of lime and thinly sliced onions dusted with chaat masala.

variations.name: Tandoori Kathal Tikka Kabab
variations.description: Here the jackfruit stays in bite-size chunks, marinated in a smoky hung-curd masala and charred rather than mashed, so each piece keeps its meaty pull. A coal-smoked dhungar finish delivers the tandoor perfume without an oven. Bright, tangy and blistered at the edges, it eats like a paneer tikka's heartier cousin.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: kachi ghani mustard oil gives the marinade its pungent tandoori edge

steps: Oil your hands and knife, cut the jackfruit into 1.5-inch cubes and parboil with ½ tsp salt for 8 minutes until just tender but still firm, then drain well.

Dry-roast the besan for 2 minutes until nutty, then whisk it into the hung curd with 2 tbsp Anveshan Mustard Oil, tandoori masala, Kashmiri chilli, ginger-garlic paste, crushed ajwain, kasuri methi, lemon juice and salt.
Fold the jackfruit cubes into the marinade and rest, covered, for 20 minutes so the tangy masala soaks the fibres.
Thread the cubes onto skewers and cook in a preheated 220C oven or on a griddle for 12 to 15 minutes, brushing with the remaining mustard oil and turning until charred at the edges.
For the smoke, set a heated charcoal piece in a small bowl in the centre of the tikkas, drizzle a few drops of mustard oil over it and cover the pan for 3 minutes to trap the dhungar aroma.
Dust the hot tikkas with 1 tsp chaat masala and toss once before serving.
tips: Keep the parboiled cubes firm; over-soft jackfruit falls off the skewer during charring.
The dhungar smoking step is what fakes the tandoor, so do not skip covering the pan.
Roasting the besan first removes its raw smell and keeps the marinade from turning pasty.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve sizzling on a bed of sautéed onions and capsicum with mint chutney and lemon, or slide the tikkas into a kathi-roll paratha with pickled onions.

variations.name: Chatpata Street-Style Kathal Kabab
variations.description: A tangy, sweet-hot bazaar version studded with chopped onion, mint and a jaggery-tamarind kick, shallow-fried and finished with a shower of chaat masala. Coarser and more textured than the classic, it is built for eating off a paper plate with chutney. Every bite balances sour, spicy and a gentle caramel sweetness.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sunflower Oil
ingredients.note: light wood-pressed sunflower oil keeps the street-style crust crisp and neutral

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: a spoon of jaggery balances the tamarind for that chatpata sweet-sour hit

steps: Pressure-cook the oiled, chopped jackfruit with 1 cup water for 4 whistles until soft, drain fully and squeeze out the moisture, then mash coarse.
Soak the poha in a little water for 2 minutes, squeeze dry and mix into the mash to soak up excess moisture and add body.
Stir in the tamarind pulp, Anveshan Jaggery Powder, finely chopped onion, mint, green chilli, roasted cumin, 1 tsp chaat masala, black salt and salt until the mixture tastes sharp and sweet-sour.
Knead into a firm mass and shape into 10 thick tikkis, pressing a mint leaf onto each top.
Heat the Anveshan Sunflower Oil in a flat pan over medium heat and shallow-fry the tikkis 3 minutes per side until crisp and browned.
Dust the hot kababs with the remaining ½ tsp chaat masala just before serving.
tips: Squeeze the boiled jackfruit really dry; the tamarind and onion add moisture back, so a wet mash will not crisp up.
Adjust jaggery and tamarind together, tasting as you go, until the chatpata balance is right for you.
Add the raw onion last and fry soon after so it stays crunchy inside the kabab.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with green chutney and a swirl of sweet tamarind chutney, sliced onions and a sprinkle of sev for a full chaat-counter effect.

variations.name: Classic Khubani Halwa
variations.description: A rich, spoonable apricot halwa where soaked dried apricots are pureed and slow-cooked in ghee until they darken into a glossy, fudge-like mass. Unlike the loose qubani compote, this is cooked down thick and pudding-dense, its natural fruit sweetness deepened with a little sugar and cardamom.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: the halwa is roasted in generous ghee until it turns glossy and leaves the sides of the pan

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: deepens the apricot's caramel notes and sweetens the halwa without refined sugar

steps: Soak 300 g dried apricots in 2.5 cups water for 4 hours or overnight until soft and plump, then destone them.
Blend the soaked apricot flesh with a little of the soaking water into a smooth, thick puree.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a heavy kadhai, fry 12 cashews and 12 almonds until golden, and set them aside.
In the same ghee add the apricot puree and cook on medium-low for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until it darkens and thickens.
Stir in 0.5 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder and 0.25 cup milk and keep cooking for 8 minutes until the sugar melts and the halwa turns glossy.
Drizzle in the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee with 0.5 tsp cardamom, cook until the halwa leaves the sides of the pan, then fold in the fried nuts and serve warm.
tips: Puree the apricots smoothly for a fudge-like halwa, or leave it slightly coarse if you prefer some fruit texture.
Cook patiently on low heat; rushing on high scorches the natural fruit sugars and turns it bitter.
It firms up considerably on cooling, so take it off the heat while still a touch soft.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm in bowls topped with slivered almonds, or press into a tray and cut into barfi-like squares once cool.

variations.name: Apricot Semolina Halwa
variations.description: A more textured halwa that combines the apricot puree with ghee-roasted semolina for a grainy, sooji-halwa body carrying the fruit. The rava soaks up the apricot and ghee into soft, distinct grains, giving a heartier dessert than the smooth fruit-only version.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the semolina to a nutty gold and gives this halwa its rich, non-sticky grains

steps: Soak 250 g dried apricots in 2.5 cups water for 4 hours, destone, and blend the flesh with the soaking water into a puree.
Simmer the apricot puree with 0.5 cup sugar and 0.5 cup milk on low for 6 minutes into a warm, pourable apricot syrup and keep it hot.
Heat 4 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a kadhai and roast 0.5 cup fine semolina on medium-low for 5 minutes, stirring, until nutty and pale gold.
Pour the hot apricot syrup into the roasted rava in a slow stream while stirring hard to avoid lumps, then cook covered on low for 4 minutes until the grains swell soft.
Fold in 2 tbsp raisins and 0.5 tsp cardamom and drizzle in the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee, stirring until the halwa turns glossy and fluffy.
Roast 0.25 cup walnuts in a dry pan for a minute, fold most in, and serve the halwa warm topped with the rest.
tips: Always pour hot apricot syrup, never cold, onto the roasted rava or the semolina clumps into lumps.
Roast the semolina until it smells nutty; under-roasted rava tastes raw and pasty.
Keep it slightly loose off the heat as the semolina keeps absorbing liquid as it sits.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm and fluffy, garnished with walnuts and a few soaked apricot slivers for a festive touch.

variations.name: Apricot Almond Halwa
variations.description: A luxurious flourless halwa that binds the apricot puree with freshly ground almond meal for a moist, marzipan-like richness. The almonds add protein and a mellow nuttiness that pairs naturally with the tangy apricot, making it a wholesome festive sweet.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: cooks the almond and apricot together into a soft, glossy, marzipan-like halwa

ingredients.name: Anveshan Honey
ingredients.note: sweetens the nutty halwa gently and keeps it soft and moist

steps: Soak 250 g dried apricots in 2 cups water for 4 hours, destone, and blend the flesh into a smooth puree.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a heavy pan and lightly roast 1 cup ground almonds on low for 3 minutes until fragrant but not browned.
Add the apricot puree and 0.5 cup milk and cook on medium-low for 8 minutes, stirring, until the mixture thickens and pulls together.
Steep 1 pinch saffron in a spoon of warm milk and stir it in with 0.5 tsp cardamom, cooking 4 more minutes until glossy.
Take the halwa off the heat, cool for 3 minutes, then fold in 3 tbsp Anveshan Honey and the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee so the honey stays fragrant.
Fold in half the pistachios and serve warm or set, topped with the rest.
tips: Roast the almond meal only briefly, as it browns and turns bitter very quickly on high heat.
Add the honey off the heat so it keeps its aroma and does not turn the halwa grainy.
For a firmer set, chill it and cut into diamonds like a soft barfi.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve at room temperature dusted with pistachios, a rich yet nourishing sweet for Eid or Diwali platters.

variations.name: Apricot Khoya Halwa
variations.description: A decadent mithai-shop style halwa where the apricot puree is cooked down with khoya into a dense, milk-rich fudge that sets firm enough to slice. The mawa lends a creamy, caramelised depth that turns the humble apricot into a shop-window barfi.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: binds the khoya and apricot into a glossy fudge that sets firm for slicing

steps: Soak 250 g dried apricots in 2 cups water for 4 hours, destone, and blend into a thick puree.
Crumble 150 g khoya and roast it in 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on low for 5 minutes until it softens and smells nutty and caramelised.
Add the apricot puree and 0.5 cup sugar and cook on medium-low for 10 minutes, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens and darkens.
Drizzle in the remaining 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee with 0.5 tsp cardamom and cook until the halwa turns glossy and leaves the sides of the pan.
Fold in 0.25 cup chopped cashews, then press the hot mixture into a greased tray and smooth the top.
Scatter 2 tbsp desiccated coconut, cool for 30 minutes until set, and cut into squares.
tips: Roast the khoya well before adding the fruit; raw-tasting mawa flattens the whole halwa.
Cook until the mass cleanly leaves the pan, which is the sign it will set firm enough to slice.
Grease the tray well and press the halwa down hard so the squares hold clean edges.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve the sliced squares on a festive platter dusted with coconut, an apricot barfi for gifting boxes.

variations.name: Classic Kuttu Ki Puri
variations.description: Kuttu Ki Puri is the beloved fasting-day flatbread of buckwheat flour bound with boiled potato, rolled and deep-fried until it puffs golden. Gluten-free buckwheat needs the potato to hold together, giving a soft, earthy puri eaten during Navratri and Ekadashi vrat.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: a fasting-friendly wood-pressed oil for deep-frying that keeps the puris light

steps: Boil, cool and grate 2 medium potatoes finely so there are no lumps to tear the delicate dough.
In a bowl, mix 2 cups kuttu atta with the grated potato, 1 tsp sendha namak, 0.5 tsp cumin seeds and 0.5 tsp black pepper.
Knead into a firm, smooth dough adding only up to 3 tbsp water a little at a time, as the potato already brings moisture, then rest it covered for 10 minutes.
Grease your palms with a little oil and roll portions between two greased sheets of plastic into thick 4-inch discs, since buckwheat dough cracks under a dry pin.
Heat 3 cups Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a kadai to about 180C, until a pinch of dough sizzles up at once.
Slide in one puri at a time, press gently with a slotted spoon so it puffs, fry about 1 minute per side until golden and crisp, then drain and serve hot.
tips: Roll between greased plastic sheets rather than on a floured board, as buckwheat has no gluten and cracks easily.
Keep the dough firm; a wet, sticky dough will disintegrate the moment it hits the oil.
Fry on steady medium-high heat so the puris puff and stay crisp instead of drinking oil.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with vrat ke aloo or sweetened curd for a satisfying Navratri fasting meal.

variations.name: Singhara Kuttu Puri
variations.description: This version blends water chestnut flour (singhara atta) into the buckwheat for a smoother, less earthy puri that rolls more easily. The singhara lightens the flavour and gives a paler, crisper crust prized by fasting cooks.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: for deep-frying the blended-flour puris to a light, even gold

steps: Grate 1 boiled potato finely and finely chop 1 green chilli.
Combine 1.5 cups kuttu atta and 0.5 cup singhara atta with the potato, 1 tsp sendha namak, 0.5 tsp ajwain and the chilli in a bowl.
Knead to a firm pliable dough with up to 4 tbsp water added gradually, then cover and rest 10 minutes.
Grease your palms and roll small portions between two oiled sheets into thick 4-inch rounds without dusting flour.
Heat 3 cups Anveshan Groundnut Oil to about 180C so a scrap of dough rises briskly.
Fry the puris one by one, nudging them under the oil to puff, about 1 minute each side until pale gold and crisp, then drain on paper.
tips: Singhara flour makes the dough smoother, but it can turn slack, so add the water in careful splashes.
Toast the ajwain lightly between your palms before adding to release its aroma into the dough.
Roll these a touch thinner than pure kuttu puris, as the blend crisps beautifully when not too thick.
variations.servingSuggestion: Pair with a bowl of vrat aloo curry or a cooling lauki raita made with rock salt.

variations.name: Palak Kuttu Puri
variations.description: A vibrant green fasting puri where blanched spinach puree is worked into the buckwheat dough, adding iron, colour and moisture. The spinach keeps the puris softer and gives a mild savoury note to the earthy buckwheat.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: deep-fries the green puris crisp while keeping them light

steps: Blanch a handful of spinach for 1 minute, cool in ice water, and blend to a smooth 0.5 cup puree; grate 1 boiled potato.
Mix 2 cups kuttu atta with the potato, 1 tsp sendha namak, 0.5 tsp roasted cumin powder and 0.5 tsp ginger paste.
Add the spinach puree and knead to a firm green dough, using no extra water unless it feels dry, then rest 10 minutes covered.
Grease your palms and roll portions between two oiled sheets into thick 4-inch discs, handling gently to avoid cracks.
Heat 3 cups Anveshan Groundnut Oil to about 180C, testing with a pinch of dough that should sizzle up.
Slide in each puri, press to puff, and fry about 1 minute per side until the green crust is set and crisp, then drain and serve warm.
tips: Squeeze the blanched spinach well before pureeing, as excess water will make the dough sticky and hard to roll.
Use the potato only for binding here; the spinach already adds moisture, so keep the dough firm.
Fry soon after rolling, since the spinach dough softens if it sits too long and can tear.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve these emerald puris with sweetened yogurt or a peanut-potato sabzi for a colourful vrat thali.

variations.name: Ghee-Roasted Kuttu Puri
variations.description: A lighter shallow-cooked take where the buckwheat discs are roasted in ghee on a tawa like a puri-paratha instead of deep-frying. It uses far less fat and gives crisp, golden-flecked flatbreads with a rich ghee aroma.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: brushed onto the tawa and the puris so they roast crisp and golden without deep-frying

steps: Grate 2 boiled potatoes finely and chop 2 tbsp coriander leaves.
Mix 2 cups kuttu atta with the potato, 1 tsp sendha namak, 0.5 tsp crushed black pepper and the coriander into a firm dough, adding up to 2 tbsp water only if needed, then rest 10 minutes.
Roll portions between two greased sheets into thick 5-inch discs, keeping them slightly thicker than fried puris.
Heat a tawa on medium and lay a disc on it, cooking for about 1 minute until the base sets and pale spots appear.
Flip, brush the top generously with Anveshan Ghee, then turn again and brush the other side, pressing lightly so it crisps and browns for about 2 minutes total.
Roast until both sides are golden with crisp edges, then serve hot straight off the tawa.
tips: Keep these discs a little thicker than deep-fry puris so they hold together while flipping on the tawa.
Press gently with a spatula while roasting to encourage crisp golden spots without tearing the buckwheat.
Add the ghee only after the first flip, so the base sets firm before it meets the fat.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve these ghee-roasted flatbreads with cool cucumber raita and a wedge of lemon for a lighter fasting plate.

variations.name: Classic Kuttu Aloo Pakora
variations.description: Kuttu Pakora is the crispy fasting fritter of potato slices dipped in a spiced buckwheat batter and deep-fried golden. Made with rock salt and gluten-free kuttu atta, it is a Navratri favourite that turns humble aloo into an irresistible vrat snack.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: a fasting-friendly wood-pressed oil for deep-frying the pakoras crisp

steps: Whisk 1 cup kuttu atta with 1 tsp sendha namak, 0.5 tsp cumin, 0.5 tsp black pepper, 2 finely chopped green chillies and 2 tbsp coriander, adding up to 0.75 cup water to a thick coating batter.
Rest the batter for 10 minutes while you peel and slice 3 potatoes into thin 3 mm rounds and pat them dry.
Heat 3 cups Anveshan Groundnut Oil in a kadai to about 180C, until a drop of batter rises steadily.
Dip each potato slice fully in the batter, letting the excess drip, then slide it into the hot oil.
Fry 6 to 8 pakoras at a time for about 4 minutes, turning until the coating is deep golden and the potato inside is cooked through.
Drain on paper and serve the pakoras hot and crisp with a sprinkle of extra rock salt.
tips: Slice the potatoes thin and even so they cook through in the time the batter takes to turn golden.
Keep the batter thick enough to cling; kuttu has no gluten, so a runny batter slides off the potato.
Fry at a steady medium-high, as too-hot oil browns the coating before the potato softens.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with green coriander chutney made with rock salt and a cup of masala chai during fasting.

variations.name: Kuttu Paneer Pakora
variations.description: A richer fasting fritter where cubes of fresh paneer are coated in the buckwheat batter and fried until the crust crackles over the soft, molten cheese. These protein-packed pakoras feel indulgent enough to be a party starter, not just vrat food.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: deep-fries the paneer fritters to a crisp golden shell

steps: Cut 250 g paneer into thick fingers and toss them with 1 tsp lemon juice, a pinch of rock salt and 0.5 tsp crushed pepper to marinate for 10 minutes.
Whisk 1 cup kuttu atta with 1 tsp sendha namak, 2 chopped green chillies and 1 tsp ginger paste, adding up to 0.66 cup water to a thick, smooth batter.
Heat 3 cups Anveshan Groundnut Oil to about 180C, so a drop of batter sizzles and rises at once.
Coat each paneer finger fully in the batter and lower it gently into the oil.
Fry in small batches for about 3 minutes, turning until the shell is crisp and deep gold while the paneer stays soft inside.
Drain on paper and serve the paneer pakoras immediately while the centre is warm and tender.
tips: Marinate the paneer briefly so it carries flavour, but pat it dry before battering or the coating will slip.
Fry only until golden; overcooking makes the paneer rubbery and squeaky.
Use fresh soft paneer for a melting centre, and cut the fingers thick so they do not dry out.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with a sweet-tangy date chutney or plain sweetened curd as a festive fasting starter.

variations.name: Kuttu Kele Ke Pakore
variations.description: This Maharashtrian-inspired vrat fritter uses slices of raw banana, which turn wonderfully creamy inside a crackly buckwheat crust. The mild banana takes on the peppery batter beautifully and makes a change from the usual potato pakora.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: deep-fries the raw banana fritters to a crisp golden finish

steps: Peel 3 raw bananas, slice into 4 mm rounds, and drop them into water with 1 tsp lemon juice to stop browning.
Whisk 1 cup kuttu atta with 1 tsp sendha namak, 0.5 tsp cumin powder, 2 chopped green chillies and 2 tbsp crushed peanuts, thinning with up to 0.75 cup water to a thick batter.
Heat 3 cups Anveshan Groundnut Oil to about 180C, until a bit of batter puffs up immediately.
Pat the banana slices dry, dip each in the batter, and slip them into the hot oil.
Fry in batches for about 4 minutes, turning until golden and crisp while the banana inside turns soft and creamy.
Lift onto paper and serve the pakoras hot with a squeeze of lemon.
tips: Keep the sliced banana in acidulated water until battering, as it discolours fast once peeled.
The crushed peanuts in the batter add a lovely crunch and fasting-friendly protein.
Test one slice first; if the banana is still firm, slice the rest a touch thinner for even cooking.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a cooling peanut-curd dip and slices of cucumber for a light vrat evening snack.

variations.name: Kuttu Palak Bhajiya
variations.description: Whole spinach leaves are cloaked in the seasoned buckwheat batter and fried into lacy, crisp bhajiyas that shatter at a bite. The leaves stay tender and grassy inside the crackly coating, a refreshing green vrat fritter.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: deep-fries the leaf bhajiyas to a lacy, crisp gold

steps: Wash and pat dry 20 large spinach leaves, keeping the stems on as handles for dipping.
Whisk 1 cup kuttu atta with 1 tsp sendha namak, 2 chopped green chillies, 1 tsp ginger paste and 0.5 tsp ajwain, adding up to 0.75 cup water to a thick coating batter.
Heat 3 cups Anveshan Groundnut Oil to about 180C, so a drop of batter rises briskly.
Hold each leaf by the stem, draw it through the batter to coat one side generously, and lower it into the oil.
Fry 4 to 5 leaves at a time for about 3 minutes, turning until the coating is crisp, lacy and golden.
Drain on paper and serve the palak bhajiyas hot and crackling.
tips: Coat the leaves thinly on just one side so they fry into crisp lace rather than a heavy fritter.
Dry the leaves completely, as any water on them makes the hot oil spit dangerously.
Serve at once; the thin coating softens quickly once the bhajiyas cool.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve immediately with sweetened yogurt or a tangy tamarind-date chutney for the perfect crunch-and-cool bite.

variations.name: Classic Makhana Kheer
variations.description: Makhana Kheer is a luscious North Indian pudding of ghee-roasted foxnuts simmered in reduced milk until they turn soft and creamy. Lightly sweetened and scented with cardamom, it is a festive, fasting-friendly dessert that feels indulgent yet wholesome.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: an unrefined sugar that sweetens the kheer without curdling the milk

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the makhana crisp so they stay springy in the milk

steps: Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a heavy pan and roast 1.5 cups makhana on low heat for about 6 minutes until they turn crisp and snap easily.
Set aside a third of the roasted makhana whole, and coarsely crush the rest for body.
Bring 4 cups full-fat milk to a boil in the same pan, then lower the heat and simmer for 8 minutes, stirring, until it reduces slightly.
Add all the makhana and simmer for 10 minutes until the crushed ones soften and thicken the kheer while the whole ones stay springy.
Turn the heat to low and stir in 0.5 cup Anveshan Khandsari until fully dissolved, then add 0.5 tsp cardamom and the chopped almonds and pistachios.
Simmer for 2 more minutes, then serve warm or chilled as you prefer.
tips: Roast the makhana until they crackle, so they hold a pleasant bite instead of going soggy in the milk.
Add the khandsari only after the kheer is off a hard boil, so the milk stays smooth.
Keep the kheer a little thin on the stove, as it thickens considerably once it cools.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm in winter or chilled in summer, garnished with slivered pistachios and a few whole roasted makhana.

variations.name: Kesar Makhana Kheer
variations.description: A regal version infused with saffron and a hint of rose that turns the kheer a warm golden hue with a heady aroma. Extra reduced milk and a generous pinch of saffron make this the celebration-worthy take served at weddings and festivals.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: steeped in warm milk to give the kheer its golden colour and luxurious aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: sweetens the saffron kheer cleanly without masking the delicate spice

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the foxnuts to a crisp, aromatic base

steps: Warm 2 tbsp milk and steep 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in it for 10 minutes until it turns bright gold.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and roast 1.5 cups makhana on low for 6 minutes until crisp, then crush two-thirds and keep the rest whole.
Boil the remaining milk and simmer for 12 minutes, stirring often, until it reduces and thickens noticeably.
Add the makhana and simmer for 10 minutes until the kheer is creamy, then pour in the saffron milk.
On low heat, stir in 0.5 cup Anveshan Khandsari, 0.5 tsp cardamom and the chopped almonds until the sugar dissolves.
Turn off the heat, stir in 0.5 tsp rose water, and serve the golden kheer warm or chilled.
tips: Steep the saffron in warm milk rather than adding it dry, which draws out far more colour and aroma.
Reduce the milk a little more than the classic for a richer, thicker celebration kheer.
Add rose water only at the very end and sparingly, as its perfume fades and overpowers if boiled.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve chilled in small kulhads topped with saffron strands and rose petals for a festive dessert.

variations.name: Makhana Rabri Kheer
variations.description: An extra-thick, decadent version where the milk is reduced hard to a rabri-like consistency studded with clotted cream flakes before the foxnuts go in. Jaggery gives it a deep caramel note, making it the richest, most spoon-coating kheer of the set.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: stirred in off the heat to give the rabri kheer a deep caramel sweetness

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the makhana crisp before they meet the thickened milk

steps: Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and roast 1 cup makhana on low for 6 minutes until crisp, then crush them coarsely.
Boil 5 cups full-fat milk in a wide heavy pan, then simmer on medium-low for about 25 minutes, scraping the cream from the sides back in, until it reduces by nearly half to a rabri thickness.
Add the crushed makhana and simmer for 8 minutes until the kheer is very thick and creamy.
Stir in 0.5 tsp cardamom, a pinch of nutmeg, and the chopped cashews and almonds.
Take the pan fully off the heat and let it cool for 5 minutes, then stir in 0.5 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder until dissolved.
Warm gently for a minute without boiling, then serve this rich rabri kheer warm or well chilled.
tips: Never add jaggery to hot boiling milk; cool the kheer a few minutes first so the milk does not split.
Scrape the cream layer back into the pan as the milk reduces for that authentic rabri texture.
Use a wide heavy pan for faster reduction and to prevent the thick milk from scorching.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve chilled in shallow bowls topped with slivered nuts and a dusting of cardamom for a festive feast finale.

variations.name: Vegan Coconut Makhana Kheer
variations.description: A dairy-free take that swaps milk for creamy coconut milk and sweetens with jaggery for a tropical, wholesome pudding. Roasted in coconut oil, the foxnuts pick up a fragrant coastal aroma that sets this plant-based kheer apart.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: roasts the foxnuts and lends the kheer its fragrant coastal aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: stirred in off the heat to sweeten the coconut kheer naturally

steps: Heat 1.5 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil in a heavy pan and roast 1.5 cups makhana on low for 6 minutes until crisp, then crush two-thirds and keep the rest whole.
In the same pan, warm 4 cups coconut milk on low heat, stirring so it does not catch, and simmer gently for 8 minutes.
Add all the makhana and simmer for 8 minutes until the crushed ones thicken the kheer to a creamy consistency.
Stir in 0.5 tsp cardamom and the chopped cashews, then take the pan fully off the heat.
Let it cool for 4 minutes, then stir in 0.5 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder until dissolved so the coconut milk does not split.
Warm through gently without boiling, garnish with 2 tbsp grated coconut, and serve warm or chilled.
tips: Keep coconut milk on low heat throughout, as it splits and turns grainy if boiled hard.
Cool the kheer before adding jaggery so the acidity of the sugar does not curdle the coconut milk.
Thin with a little warm water or extra coconut milk if it thickens too much on cooling.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve chilled topped with toasted coconut flakes for a refreshing, dairy-free festive dessert.

variations.name: Classic Makhane Ki Kheer
variations.description: A beloved North Indian fasting kheer of ghee-roasted foxnuts simmered in reduced milk until they turn soft and pillowy. Lightly sweetened and scented with cardamom and saffron, makhane ki kheer is a wholesome, protein-rich pudding often made for vrat and festivals.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the makhana crisp so they stay soft yet distinct in the kheer

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: steeped in warm milk for the kheer's golden colour and delicate aroma

steps: Roast 2 cups makhana in 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on low for 6 minutes, stirring, until crisp and lightly golden, then coarsely crush half and keep the rest whole.
Bring 1 litre full-fat milk to a boil and simmer on medium-low for 12 minutes, stirring, until it reduces slightly and thickens.
Add both the crushed and whole makhana and cook 8 minutes until they soften and swell and the kheer thickens further.
Stir in 0.5 cup sugar and 0.5 tsp cardamom and cook 4 minutes until the sugar dissolves and the kheer is creamy.
Steep 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk and stir it through for colour and aroma.
Fold in the chopped almonds and pistachios, keeping a few for the top, and serve warm or chilled.
tips: Roast the makhana until properly crisp so they hold a soft bite instead of going slimy in the milk.
Crushing half the makhana naturally thickens the kheer while whole ones give texture.
The kheer thickens a lot on cooling, so keep it slightly loose while cooking.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm or chilled in bowls topped with saffron strands and slivered pistachios, a perfect vrat dessert.

variations.name: Makhana Rabri Kheer
variations.description: A festive, indulgent version where the foxnuts simmer in a thick khoya-enriched rabri rather than plain milk. Slow reduction and mawa give the kheer a dense, creamy body and a caramelised richness suited to celebration tables.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the makhana and enriches the thick rabri base

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: steeped in milk to deepen the colour of this richer rabri kheer

steps: Roast 2 cups makhana in 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on low for 6 minutes until crisp, then crush half and keep the rest whole.
Bring 1.2 litres full-fat milk to a boil and simmer on medium-low for 20 minutes, scraping the sides, until it reduces to a thick rabri.
Crumble in 100 g khoya and cook 4 minutes until it melts smoothly into the rabri.
Add all the makhana and cook 8 minutes until they soften into the thick base, then stir in 0.66 cup sugar and 0.5 tsp cardamom.
Steep 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk, stir it in, and finish with the remaining 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee for gloss.
Stir in 1 tsp rose water off the heat, fold in 3 tbsp chopped cashews, and serve warm or chilled.
tips: Keep scraping the pan sides while reducing the milk so the cream folds back in as rabri.
Add the khoya on low heat and stir until smooth to avoid grainy lumps.
A little rose water lifts the heavy rabri and adds a fragrant nawabi note.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve chilled in matka cups topped with cashews and saffron, a rich dessert for weddings and Diwali.

variations.name: Jaggery Makhana Coconut Kheer
variations.description: A dairy-free take that simmers the foxnuts in coconut milk and sweetens them with jaggery for a warm, caramel-toned pudding. Coconut-oil-roasted makhana and a hint of nutmeg give it a fragrant, wholesome coastal character.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Coconut Oil
ingredients.note: roasts the makhana crisp and lends a coastal aroma to this dairy-free kheer

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: melted and strained to sweeten the kheer with warm caramel notes instead of sugar

steps: Roast 2 cups makhana in 2 tbsp Anveshan Coconut Oil on low for 6 minutes until crisp, then crush half and keep the rest whole.
Simmer 800 ml coconut milk on medium-low for 8 minutes, stirring so it does not catch, until it warms and thickens slightly.
Add all the makhana and cook 8 minutes until they soften and swell into the coconut milk.
Melt 0.75 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder with 0.25 cup water on low, strain out grit, and stir the syrup in with 0.5 tsp cardamom and 0.25 tsp nutmeg.
Warm through for 3 minutes on low so the coconut milk does not split, then fold in 3 tbsp chopped walnuts.
Finish with 2 tbsp desiccated coconut and serve warm or chilled.
tips: Keep the heat low once the coconut milk and jaggery are together so the milk stays smooth and does not split.
Always strain the melted jaggery to keep the kheer free of grit.
This vegan kheer thickens fast as makhana absorbs the coconut milk, so loosen with a splash if needed.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm as a dairy-free festive pudding, topped with toasted coconut and walnuts.

variations.name: Makhana Kheer with Sabudana
variations.description: A heartier fasting kheer that combines the roasted foxnuts with translucent sabudana pearls for extra body, honey-sweetened for a vrat-friendly finish. The soft sago and pillowy makhana together make a filling, energising pudding for festival fasts.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the makhana crisp so they stay soft yet distinct in the vrat kheer

ingredients.name: Anveshan Honey
ingredients.note: sweetens the fasting kheer naturally, stirred in off the heat

steps: Soak 0.25 cup sabudana in water for 30 minutes until softened, then drain.
Roast 1.5 cups makhana in 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on low for 6 minutes until crisp, then crush half and keep the rest whole.
Bring 1 litre full-fat milk to a boil, add the drained sabudana, and simmer on medium-low for 10 minutes until the pearls turn translucent.
Add all the makhana and cook 8 minutes until they soften and the kheer thickens, then stir in 0.5 tsp cardamom.
Take the pan off the heat, cool for 5 minutes, and stir in 5 tbsp Anveshan Honey so it stays raw and fragrant.
Fold in 3 tbsp chopped almonds and 2 tbsp raisins and serve warm or chilled.
tips: Soak the sabudana fully so the pearls cook through and turn glassy rather than staying hard in the centre.
Add the honey only after cooling slightly, since boiling honey loses its aroma and benefits.
It thickens fast as both makhana and sabudana swell, so loosen with warm milk if needed.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm as a filling vrat dessert, garnished with almonds and raisins for Navratri or Ekadashi fasts.

variations.name: Classic White Malai Kofta
variations.description: Soft paneer-and-potato dumplings resting in a pale, cashew-cream gravy that stays deliberately white with no tomato or chilli powder. The koftas melt on the tongue while the mild, milky sauce carries only the perfume of cardamom and a whisper of sweetness.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: fries the cashew paste gently so the gravy gains richness while staying snow-white

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: its clean neutral flavour deep-fries the koftas golden without masking the paneer

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: rounds off the gravy with a mellow sweetness that refined sugar cannot match

steps: Boil the 2 potatoes until soft, then grate them along with the 200 g paneer and mash together with 2 tbsp cornflour and 0.5 tsp salt into a smooth, non-sticky dough.
Roll the mixture into 10 walnut-sized balls, then deep-fry them in the hot Anveshan Groundnut Oil over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until pale golden, and drain on paper.
Boil the 2 onions and 18 cashews in a cup of water for 8 minutes, cool completely, then blend to a silky white paste without any water discolouring it.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pan over low heat, add 4 lightly crushed cardamoms and 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, and saute for 1 minute until fragrant but not browned.
Pour in the cashew-onion paste with 0.5 tsp salt and 0.5 tsp white pepper, and cook gently for 6 minutes, stirring so it never catches colour, until the ghee just separates.
Add 1 cup water and 0.5 tsp Anveshan Jaggery Powder, simmer for 4 minutes, then stir in 4 tbsp cream off the boil and slip in the koftas only at serving time so they stay soft.
tips: Add the fried koftas to the gravy just before serving, or they soak up the sauce and fall apart.
Keep the flame low the entire time so nothing browns, which is the secret to a truly white gravy.
If the kofta dough feels sticky, add another spoon of cornflour so the balls hold their shape while frying.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with butter naan or a mild jeera pulao, garnished with a swirl of cream and a few slivered pistachios for contrast.

variations.name: Shahi Saffron Malai Kofta
variations.description: A regal Mughlai take where khoya-enriched koftas hide a nutty surprise and float in a saffron-tinted white gravy thickened with melon seeds and khoya. Richer and more aromatic than the everyday version, it carries the golden glow and banquet fragrance of a wedding kitchen.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: essential for a shahi gravy, it fries the melon-seed paste and enriches the royal sauce

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sunflower Oil
ingredients.note: light and neutral, it fries the delicate khoya koftas to an even golden crust

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: steeped in warm milk it lends the gravy its royal golden hue and heady aroma

steps: Soak the 0.25 tsp Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk and set aside so it releases its colour and fragrance.
Grate the 150 g paneer with half the khoya, mix with 2 tbsp cornflour and 0.5 tsp salt, then shape into 10 balls each stuffed with a pinch of the 3 tbsp chopped nuts.
Deep-fry the stuffed koftas in the hot Anveshan Sunflower Oil over medium heat for 3 minutes until golden all over, and drain gently on paper.
Boil the 2 onions and 3 tbsp melon seeds in a cup of water for 7 minutes, cool, then blend to a smooth pale paste.

Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pan over low heat, add 4 crushed cardamoms and 1 tbsp ginger paste, saute for 1 minute, then add the melon-seed paste with 0.5 tsp salt and 0.25 tsp mace and cook for 6 minutes until the ghee separates.
Stir in the remaining khoya with a cup of water, simmer for 4 minutes, then fold in 3 tbsp cream and the saffron milk off the heat and add the koftas just before serving.
tips: Grate the khoya finely so it melts smoothly into the gravy without forming lumps.
Seal the nut stuffing well inside each kofta so it does not burst open in the hot oil.
Brush a little extra saffron milk over the plated dish to deepen both the colour and the aroma.
variations.servingSuggestion: Pair with sheermal or a zafrani pulao, scattered with fried raisins and slivered almonds for a festive table.

variations.name: Restaurant-style White Malai Kofta
variations.description: The pristine dhaba-buffet favourite built on a no-tomato curd and cashew base that stays milky white and glossy. Lauki lightens the koftas so they stay tender, while the tangy-mild gravy clings to every dumpling like the versions ladled out at banquet counters.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: keeps the gravy pale while lending the clean richness a restaurant korma is known for

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: fries the grated-lauki koftas crisp without weighing them down

steps: Grate the 1 cup lauki, squeeze out all its water, then mix with the 150 g grated paneer, 3 tbsp besan and 0.5 tsp salt into a firm dough.
Roll into 10 small balls and deep-fry in the hot Anveshan Groundnut Oil over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and set, then drain.
Boil the 2 onions, 20 cashews and 2 green chillies in a cup of water for 8 minutes, cool fully, and blend to a completely smooth white paste.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pan over low heat, add 1 bay leaf, then pour in the cashew-onion paste with 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook for 6 minutes without browning.
Whisk the 0.5 cup curd until smooth, lower the flame and stir it in slowly with 0.5 tsp salt and 0.5 tsp white pepper so it does not split, then add 1 cup water.
Simmer the gravy for 5 minutes until it turns glossy, then arrange the koftas in the sauce just before serving so they stay whole and soft.
tips: Squeeze the grated lauki thoroughly, or the koftas will absorb oil and disintegrate while frying.
Add the whisked curd only on low heat and keep stirring to prevent the white gravy from curdling.
Make the koftas and gravy ahead but combine them only at the last minute for the best texture.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with laccha paratha or steamed basmati, finished with a drizzle of cream and a dusting of dried fenugreek leaves.

variations.name: Lucknowi Chironji Malai Kofta
variations.description: An Awadhi rendition where the white gravy is thickened with chironji and poppy seeds for a subtly grainy, nutty body. The koftas hide a jewel of raisins and chironji, and the sauce is scented with kewra and green cardamom in true Lucknowi style.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: the soul of Awadhi cooking, it toasts the poppy-chironji paste into a fragrant white base

ingredients.name: Anveshan Sunflower Oil
ingredients.note: a light frying medium that crisps the koftas without tinting them dark

steps: Soak 1 tbsp chironji and the 2 tbsp poppy seeds in warm water for 15 minutes, then blend with the boiled 2 onions into a smooth pale paste.
Grate the 180 g paneer, knead with 2 tbsp cornflour and 0.5 tsp salt, and shape into 10 balls each stuffed with a few raisins and remaining chironji.
Deep-fry the koftas in the hot Anveshan Sunflower Oil over medium heat for 3 minutes until pale gold, then lift out and drain.
Heat 3 tbsp Anveshan Ghee in a pan over low heat, add 4 crushed cardamoms and 1 tbsp ginger paste, and saute for 1 minute until aromatic.
Add the poppy-chironji paste with 0.5 tsp salt and cook gently for 7 minutes, stirring constantly so it thickens without catching any colour.
Pour in 1 cup water and simmer for 4 minutes, then stir in 3 tbsp cream and 0.5 tsp kewra water off the heat and add the koftas just before serving.
tips: Soak the poppy seeds and chironji well so they grind into a smooth paste rather than a gritty one.
Add kewra water sparingly at the very end, as its aroma turns harsh if it is boiled.
Warm leftover gravy gently with a splash of water, adding fresh-fried koftas so they never go soggy.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with warm rumali roti or a delicate yakhni pulao, garnished with a sprinkle of chironji and rose petals.

variations.name: Classic Methi Pakora Kadhi
variations.description: Fresh fenugreek leaves folded into crisp besan fritters and simmered in a tangy yogurt kadhi, where the pleasant bitterness of methi balances the sourness beautifully. A winter special from north Indian kitchens, finished with a cumin-and-red-chilli ghee tarka. Wholesome, aromatic and deeply comforting over rice.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed groundnut oil fries the methi pakoras crisp and clean

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee for the finishing cumin and red-chilli tarka

steps: Mix half the chopped methi leaves with ½ cup besan, ajwain, a pinch of salt and a little water into a thick batter, then deep-fry spoonfuls in Anveshan Groundnut Oil at 180C for 3 minutes until golden and crisp.
Whisk the sour yogurt with the remaining ½ cup besan, turmeric, red chilli powder, grated ginger and salt into 5 cups water until smooth.
Heat 1 tbsp of the frying oil in a pot, crackle cumin and fenugreek seeds for 30 seconds, then pour in the yogurt batter.
Bring to a boil while stirring so the yogurt does not split, then simmer uncovered on low for 25 minutes until thick.
Stir in the remaining raw chopped methi and cook 5 minutes so its bitterness mellows into the gravy.
Add the pakoras 6 minutes before serving and finish with a tarka of Anveshan Ghee, cumin and red chilli powder.
tips: Sprinkle a little salt on the chopped methi and squeeze out its water to reduce bitterness.
Add the pakoras near the end so they turn soft without disintegrating.
A long simmer deepens the tang and cooks out the raw besan; do not rush it.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve over steamed rice with a spoon of ghee, or with hot phulkas and a wedge of lemon.

variations.name: Punjabi Methi Pyaaz Pakora Kadhi
variations.description: A robust Punjabi version where the fritters combine fenugreek and plenty of sliced onion for sweetness and crunch, set in a thick garlicky mustard-oil kadhi. The onion softens the methi's bitterness and adds body to the pakoras. Rich, dhaba-style and made for slow winter lunches.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Mustard Oil
ingredients.note: kachi ghani mustard oil fries the pakoras and gives the kadhi its pungent Punjabi base

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee for the finishing garlic tarka

steps: Mix the chopped methi and sliced onion with ½ cup besan, a pinch of salt and a little water into a thick batter, then deep-fry in Anveshan Mustard Oil at 180C for 3 minutes until golden.
Whisk the sour yogurt with the remaining ½ cup besan, turmeric, red chilli powder and salt into 5 cups water until smooth.
Heat 1 tbsp of the frying oil, crackle cumin and fenugreek seeds with crushed garlic for 40 seconds until golden.
Pour in the yogurt batter, bring to a boil while stirring, then simmer uncovered on low for 30 minutes until thick and deep yellow.
Slide in the methi-onion pakoras and simmer 8 minutes so they plump and soften.
Finish with a tarka of Anveshan Ghee sizzled with extra sliced garlic poured sizzling over the top.
tips: Slice the onions thin so the pakoras cook through and stay crisp.
Heat the mustard oil to smoking before frying to mellow its sharpness.
The garlic double-hit, in the base and the tarka, is what makes this Punjabi.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve thick over jeera rice or with tandoori roti, sliced onion and green chilli on the side.

variations.name: Kasuri Methi Baked Pakora Kadhi
variations.description: A lighter version using dried kasuri methi in the batter and oven-baked pakoras instead of deep-fried, set in a low-fat yogurt kadhi tempered in minimal ghee. The kasuri methi lends a concentrated fenugreek aroma without the seasonal wait for fresh leaves. All the comfort with far less oil.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: a little bilona ghee for the tempering keeps this baked version light yet aromatic

ingredients.name: Anveshan Olive Oil
ingredients.note: a light brush of olive oil helps the baked pakoras crisp without deep-frying

steps: Soak 2 tbsp kasuri methi in warm water for 5 minutes, squeeze, and mix with ½ cup besan, chopped onion, a pinch of salt and enough water for a thick batter.
Shape small fritters onto an oiled tray, brush with Anveshan Olive Oil and bake in a preheated 200C oven for 18 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Whisk the yogurt with the remaining ½ cup besan, turmeric, red chilli powder, grated ginger and salt into 5 cups water until smooth.
Heat the Anveshan Ghee, crackle cumin and fenugreek seeds for 30 seconds, then pour in the yogurt batter and bring to a boil while stirring.
Simmer uncovered on low for 25 minutes, then crush the remaining 1 tbsp kasuri methi in and cook 3 minutes for a deeper aroma.
Add the baked pakoras 5 minutes before serving so they keep a little bite.
tips: Brushing the fritters with oil before baking gives them a crisp exterior with minimal fat.
Crushing kasuri methi between your palms before adding releases its full fragrance.
Add the baked pakoras late as they soften faster than fried ones.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve over brown rice or with a jowar roti and a fresh kachumber salad for a lighter meal.

variations.name: Gujarati Methi Muthia Kadhi
variations.description: A Gujarati spin where steamed then pan-tossed methi muthia dumplings replace fried pakoras, simmered in a thin, jaggery-sweetened kadhi. The steamed muthia are lighter and studded with fenugreek and spices, and the gravy carries the classic sweet-sour Gujarati balance. Elegant, wholesome and less oily than the fried classic.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: bilona ghee tempers the whole spices and tosses the steamed muthia

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: jaggery gives the signature Gujarati sweet-sour note to the thin kadhi

steps: Mix the chopped methi with ½ cup besan, the wheat flour, half the ginger-green chilli paste, a pinch of turmeric, salt and a little water into a soft dough.
Shape into logs, steam for 12 minutes until firm to the touch, cool and slice into ½-inch muthia pieces.
Heat 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee and toss the muthia with sesame seeds until golden on the edges, about 4 minutes, then set aside.
Whisk the yogurt with the remaining ¼ cup besan, turmeric and salt into 4 cups water until smooth and thin.
Heat the remaining Anveshan Ghee, crackle cumin, curry leaves and the rest of the ginger-green chilli paste for 30 seconds, then pour in the yogurt batter and bring to a boil while stirring.
Add the Anveshan Jaggery Powder and simmer 15 minutes, then slip in the muthia and cook 5 minutes until they soak up the sweet-sour gravy.
tips: Steam the muthia only until firm; over-steaming makes them dense.
Pan-tossing the steamed muthia in ghee adds flavour without deep-frying.
Keep the kadhi thin and balance the jaggery against the yogurt's tang by tasting.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with steamed rice or khichdi and a spoon of ghee for a classic Gujarati comfort meal.

variations.name: Classic Moong Dal Sheera
variations.description: Moong dal sheera is the labour-of-love halwa of North Indian weddings, made by slow-roasting soaked, ground yellow moong dal in generous ghee until it turns golden and grainy, then swelling it with sweet milk. Patient roasting is everything, giving a nutty, melt-in-the-mouth halwa that pools ghee.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the ground dal low and slow until golden and deeply aromatic

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: dissolved into the hot milk to sweeten the sheera cleanly

steps: Soak 1 cup yellow moong dal for 3 hours, drain well and grind to a coarse, thick paste without adding water.
Heat 0.75 cup Anveshan Ghee in a heavy kadhai, add the dal paste and roast over low heat, stirring without pause, for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and grainy.
Meanwhile heat 2 cups milk with 1 cup water and 0.75 cup Anveshan Khandsari until the sugar dissolves, then keep it hot.
Pour the hot sweet milk very slowly into the roasted dal, standing back from the splutter, and stir hard to break every lump.
Cook on low heat for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring constantly, until the sheera thickens and ghee pools at the edges.
Fold in 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and 3 tbsp chopped almonds and cashews, then serve the sheera warm.
tips: Grind the dal coarse and paste-like without water; a watery grind gums up and never roasts to that signature grainy texture.
The roast is long and cannot be rushed; a pale, under-roasted dal leaves a raw, beany taste in the finished sheera.
If the sheera stiffens on standing, loosen it with a splash of hot milk and a spoon of ghee before serving.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm as a festive or wedding dessert, garnished with fried nuts and a few strands of saffron.

variations.name: Rajasthani Mawa Moong Dal Halwa
variations.description: The royal Rajasthani rendition enriched with crumbled mawa and a blush of saffron, giving a denser, darker halwa fit for winter feasts and Holi tables. The khoya deepens the milkiness while saffron perfumes the whole pan a warm gold.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the dal deep and slow for the rich, grainy Rajasthani halwa

ingredients.name: Anveshan Saffron
ingredients.note: bloomed in warm milk to give the halwa its royal gold colour and aroma

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: sweetens the mawa-rich halwa while keeping the saffron gold clear

steps: Soak 1 cup moong dal for 3 hours, drain and grind to a coarse thick paste, and bloom 1 pinch Anveshan Saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk.
Heat 0.75 cup Anveshan Ghee in a kadhai, add the dal paste and roast over low heat, stirring, for 20 minutes until golden and fragrant.
Add 0.75 cup crumbled mawa and roast for 5 minutes more until it melts into the dal and the mixture turns rich brown.
Heat 2 cups milk with 0.5 cup water and 0.75 cup Anveshan Khandsari until dissolved, then pour it slowly into the dal, stirring hard to avoid lumps.
Add the bloomed saffron milk and cook on low heat for 8 minutes until the halwa thickens and ghee separates at the sides.
Fold in 3 tbsp slivered pistachios and almonds and serve the halwa warm.
tips: Add the mawa only after the dal is well roasted, so the khoya does not brown and turn bitter too early.
Keep the flame low throughout; moong dal halwa scorches easily once the mawa goes in.
This halwa reheats beautifully with a spoon of hot milk and tastes even better the next day.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm at winter feasts and Holi, garnished with slivered pistachios, almonds and a pinch of saffron.

variations.name: Jaggery Moong Dal Sheera
variations.description: A more rustic, wholesome sheera sweetened with jaggery instead of sugar, giving an earthier, caramel-brown halwa with a mineral depth. Cooked in ghee with a little dry ginger, it is the kind of sheera made as a nourishing prasad and winter tonic.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the dal to a golden grain for this earthy jaggery sheera

ingredients.name: Anveshan Jaggery Powder
ingredients.note: melted into the milk to sweeten the sheera with warm caramel depth

steps: Soak 1 cup moong dal for 3 hours, drain and grind to a coarse, thick paste without water.
Heat 0.7 cup Anveshan Ghee in a heavy pan, add the dal paste and roast over low heat, stirring constantly, for 20 to 22 minutes until golden.
Melt 0.75 cup Anveshan Jaggery Powder in 1 cup water over low heat, strain out any grit, then combine with 1.5 cups warm milk.
Pour the warm jaggery milk slowly into the roasted dal off a high flame, stirring hard so it stays lump-free and does not split.
Cook on low heat for 7 to 8 minutes, stirring, until the sheera thickens to a glossy caramel-brown mass that releases ghee.
Fold in 0.25 tsp dry ginger powder, 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and 3 tbsp chopped walnuts, then serve warm.
tips: Always melt and strain the jaggery first, as its grit and the acidity of raw jaggery can curdle the milk.
Add the jaggery milk off the boil to protect the milk from splitting against the heat.
The pinch of dry ginger makes this a warming winter tonic; leave it out for a milder, everyday sweet.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm as a nourishing winter prasad or tonic, topped with chopped walnuts and a drizzle of ghee.

variations.name: Coconut Moong Dal Sheera
variations.description: A South Indian spin that folds fresh coconut and a splash of coconut milk into roasted moong dal for a lighter, fragrant sheera with a mellow tropical sweetness. Fried cashews and raisins give the finish, making it a gentle, everyday festival sweet.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: roasts the dal and fries the cashews for this coconut-scented sheera

ingredients.name: Anveshan Khandsari
ingredients.note: sweetens the sheera cleanly, letting the coconut flavour stay forward

steps: Soak 1 cup moong dal for 3 hours, drain and grind to a coarse thick paste without adding water.
Heat 0.6 cup Anveshan Ghee in a kadhai, fry 3 tbsp cashews and raisins until golden, then lift out and reserve.
Add the dal paste to the same ghee and roast over low heat, stirring, for 18 to 20 minutes until golden and grainy.
Stir in 0.5 cup fresh grated coconut and roast for 3 minutes until it smells sweet and toasty.
Heat 1 cup coconut milk with 1 cup water and 0.75 cup Anveshan Khandsari until dissolved, then pour it slowly into the dal, stirring hard.
Cook on low heat for 5 to 6 minutes until the sheera thickens, then fold in 0.5 tsp cardamom powder and the fried nuts and serve warm.
tips: Add the coconut milk warm and off the boil so the sheera stays smooth and does not split.
Fresh grated coconut gives the best fragrance; if using frozen, thaw and squeeze it dry first.
This lighter sheera thickens fast as it cools, so serve it while still soft and spoonable.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm as a South Indian festival sweet, garnished with fried cashews and a sprinkle of grated coconut.

variations.name: Classic Moong Dal Tikki
variations.description: Moong Dal Tikki is a North Indian patty made from soaked yellow moong dal coarsely ground with ginger, chilli and crushed coriander, then shallow-fried till crusty and cooked through. It has a lightly grainy interior and a savoury, protein-rich bite reminiscent of moong dal pakoda in patty form.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: shallow-frying in bilona ghee cooks the dal through and crisps the crust

steps: Soak 1.5 cups yellow moong dal in plenty of water for 4 hours, then drain it completely.
Grind the drained dal to a thick, coarse paste with grated ginger and 2 green chillies, using as little water as possible so it stays stiff.
Transfer to a bowl and mix in the finely chopped onion, 1 tsp crushed coriander seeds, 0.25 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 0.25 tsp asafoetida, 3 tbsp coriander and 1 tsp salt.
Whisk the batter for a minute to lighten it, then shape into 10 thick patties with moistened palms.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on a griddle over medium-low heat and shallow-fry the tikkis for 4 to 5 minutes per side so the dal cooks through and the crust turns deep golden.
Cook the remaining tikkis in the rest of the Anveshan Ghee, keeping the heat gentle so the centres are not raw, and drain on paper before serving.
tips: Grind the dal thick with minimal water, as a runny batter will spread on the pan instead of holding a patty shape.
Fry on medium-low heat so the inside cooks fully before the crust darkens too much.
Whisking the ground dal aerates it and makes the tikkis lighter rather than dense.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve hot with green chutney and a cup of masala chai on a cool evening.

variations.name: Moong Dal Palak Tikki
variations.description: A greener, more wholesome version where fresh spinach is ground into the moong dal for colour and iron, sharpened with garlic and cumin. A spoon of rice flour keeps the edges extra crisp while the spinach keeps the inside moist and tender.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Groundnut Oil
ingredients.note: wood-pressed groundnut oil fries these spinach tikkis crisp and light

steps: Soak 1.5 cups yellow moong dal for 4 hours, then drain thoroughly.
Grind the dal to a thick coarse paste with 1.5 cups chopped spinach, 4 garlic cloves, 2 green chillies and 1 inch ginger, using minimal water.
Stir in 3 tbsp rice flour, 1 tsp cumin powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 3 tbsp coriander and 1 tsp salt to make a stiff, bright-green batter.
Whisk briefly to lighten, then shape into 10 patties with wet hands.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Groundnut Oil on a griddle over medium-low heat and fry the tikkis for 4 to 5 minutes per side until crisp and cooked through.
Cook the remaining tikkis in the rest of the Anveshan Groundnut Oil and drain on paper before serving hot.
tips: Add the rice flour to keep the spinach batter from spreading and to give a shatteringly crisp edge.
Do not over-water the grind; the spinach already adds moisture to the dal.
Fry gently so the thick tikkis cook to the centre without the outside burning.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve with a garlicky yogurt dip and lemon wedges for a nourishing green snack.

variations.name: Paneer-Stuffed Moong Dal Tikki
variations.description: A festive, indulgent tikki where a spiced paneer and cashew filling is tucked inside the crisp moong dal shell. The soft, mildly sweet paneer centre contrasts beautifully with the savoury, grainy dal crust for a starter that feels special.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: ghee crisps the shell while keeping the paneer filling soft inside

steps: Soak 1.5 cups moong dal for 4 hours, drain, and grind to a thick coarse paste with 2 green chillies and minimal water.
Mix the ground dal with the finely chopped onion, 2 tbsp cornflour, 1 tsp garam masala and 0.5 tsp salt into a shapeable outer dough.
For the filling, combine 1 cup crumbled paneer with 3 tbsp chopped cashews, 0.5 tsp black pepper, 3 tbsp chopped mint and the remaining 0.5 tsp salt.
Flatten a portion of the dal dough in your palm, place a spoon of the paneer filling in the centre, seal well and shape into 8 stuffed patties.
Heat 2 tbsp Anveshan Ghee on a griddle over medium-low heat and cook the tikkis for 4 to 5 minutes per side so the dal cooks through and the crust crisps.
Fry the rest in the remaining Anveshan Ghee and serve hot so the paneer stays soft in the centre.
tips: Seal the stuffed edges carefully so the paneer does not spill while the dal crust cooks.
Keep the heat medium-low, since a thick stuffed tikki needs time for the dal shell to cook fully.
Toast the cashews lightly first for a deeper crunch against the soft paneer.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve halved to reveal the paneer centre, with a drizzle of mint chutney and pomegranate.

variations.name: Baked Sprouted Moong Tikki
variations.description: A high-protein, oven-baked patty made from whole green moong sprouts mashed with boiled potato and bound with oats. Chaat masala and amchur give it a tangy street-food flavour while baking keeps it light and gut-friendly.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Olive Oil
ingredients.note: brushed over the tikkis so they crisp and brown while baking

steps: Preheat the oven to 200C and line a tray with parchment brushed lightly with a little Anveshan Olive Oil.
Steam the 2 cups green moong sprouts for 6 minutes until soft, then coarsely mash them, keeping some texture.
Boil and mash the 2 potatoes, then combine with the mashed sprouts and 0.5 cup powdered oats to bind.
Mix in grated ginger, 2 chopped green chillies, 1 tsp chaat masala, 1 tsp amchur, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 3 tbsp coriander and 1 tsp salt, and shape into 10 patties.
Arrange on the tray, brush the tops well with Anveshan Olive Oil, and bake for 15 minutes.
Flip, brush again with oil, and bake another 12 to 15 minutes until golden and crisp, then rest 2 minutes before serving.
tips: Steam the sprouts until fully tender so the tikkis are easy to digest and mash smoothly.
Powdered oats are the key binder, so add a little more if the mixture feels loose.
Brush oil on both bakes for an even golden colour without any deep-frying.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve warm with a tangy tamarind-date chutney and a sprinkle of chaat masala.

variations.name: Classic Mushroom Tikka
variations.description: Mushroom Tikka takes plump button mushrooms marinated in spiced hung curd and char-grilled until juicy inside with smoky, blistered edges. The mushrooms drink up the tandoori marinade like little sponges, giving a meaty, satisfying bite in every skewer.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: brushes the mushrooms for a golden grill and keeps them from drying out

steps: Wipe 400 g button mushrooms clean with a damp cloth rather than washing, so they do not soak up water and turn soggy on the grill.

Roast 1 tbsp besan on a dry pan for 1 minute until nutty, then whisk it into 0.5 cup hung curd with 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1.5 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, 1 tsp tandoori masala, 1 tbsp lemon juice and 0.75 tsp salt.
Fold in the whole mushrooms, capsicum squares and onion petals, coat evenly, and marinate for 20 minutes so the curd soaks in.
Thread them onto skewers and grill on a hot tawa brushed with 1 tbsp Anveshan Ghee for 8 minutes, turning until charred and the mushrooms release their juices.
Brush with the remaining ghee and grill 2 more minutes until the edges blister and turn glossy brown.
Dust with 0.5 tsp chaat masala and serve hot straight off the skewer.
tips: Choose medium, tightly closed mushrooms of even size so they grill at the same rate.
Do not over-marinate beyond 30 minutes, as the salt draws out too much water and softens the mushrooms.
Grill on high heat quickly so the mushrooms char before they steam and shrink.
variations.servingSuggestion: Serve as a starter with mint chutney and onion rings, or skewer with grilled pineapple for a party platter.

variations.name: Malai Mushroom Tikka
variations.description: A creamy, mild version where mushrooms are bathed in a cheese-and-cream marinade spiced only with white pepper and green chilli, keeping them pale and delicate. The malai coat caramelises into a rich golden crust that contrasts the juicy mushroom within.

ingredients.name: Anveshan Ghee
ingredients.note: grills the malai-coated mushrooms to a rich golden crust
